audubon-birds-88-autumnal-warbler: What Audubon described as the Autumnal Warbler is now recognized as the non-breeding plumage of the Bay-breasted Warbler, an instructive example of the seasonal variation that confused early American ornithology. Hand-coloured aquatint from the double-elephant folio.
audubon-birds-89-nashville-warbler: Two Nashville Warblers move among the leaves and red berries of a leafy branch, their olive-green upperparts and yellow underparts shown in active foraging poses. Plate 89 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, hand-coloured aquatint engraved by Robert Havell Jr., held at the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-9-selby-s-flycatcher: What Audubon named Selby's Flycatcher in honour of British ornithologist Prideaux John Selby is now generally regarded as a Hooded Warbler. Hand-coloured aquatint from the double-elephant folio, recording one of several taxonomic redeterminations made after the work's initial publication.
audubon-birds-90-black-white-creeper: A Black-and-white Warbler clings to a black larch branch bearing green cones, the bold zebra striping characteristic of the species clearly rendered. Plate 90 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, hand-coloured aquatint demonstrating Audubon's interest in characteristic foraging posture as a diagnostic field mark, held at the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-91-broad-winged-hawk: An adult and juvenile Broad-winged Hawk perch together on a branch, paired to show the contrasting plumages of the small forest raptor known for its enormous autumnal kettling migrations. Hand-coloured aquatint engraving from the double-elephant folio.
audubon-birds-92-pigeon-hawk: A male and female Merlin (Pigeon Hawk) perch on a leafy branch, shown in the plate Audubon labelled Falco columbarius. The darker, brown-backed male sits above the streaked, buff-breasted female, wings partially fanned. Plate 92 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, held by the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-93-sea-side-finch: Two Seaside Sparrows perch among rose-like flowering plants and tall reeds, the olive-grey plumage and pale supercilium carefully rendered as diagnostic field marks. The plate, from Audubon's Birds of America, uses the botanical setting to frame both birds in characteristic postures. Plate 93 of the double-elephant folio, credited to the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-94-grass-finch-or-bay-wing: A single Vesper Sparrow (Grass Finch or Bay-winged Bunting) stands on a rocky surface before a blooming prickly pear cactus, its streaked brown plumage blending with the warm tones of the stone. Plate 94 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, from the double-elephant folio held at the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-95-yellow-poll-warbler: A single male Yellow-poll Warbler clings to a leafy branch from which hangs a drooping raceme of pale blue-white flowers, its lemon-yellow plumage set against the green foliage. The plate label identifies the subject as the male. Plate 95 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, from the double-elephant folio held at the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-96-columbia-jay: A male and female Columbia Jay (Corvus bullockii) display their rich blue plumage and long, graduated tail feathers as they perch on leafy branches in this striking double-page composition. The birds' prominent crests and elongated tails give the plate an ornamental quality unusual among Audubon's passerine plates. Plate 96 of John James Audubon's Birds of America, held at the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-97-little-screech-owl: Three Eastern Screech-Owls illustrate the species' striking colour polymorphism, with red-morph and grey-morph individuals shown together on a single branch. Hand-coloured aquatint engraved by Robert Havell Jr., emphasizing the small owl's prominent ear tufts and yellow eyes.
audubon-birds-98-white-bellied-swallow: A male and female White-bellied Swallow are shown in mid-air against a light sky, the male's iridescent blue-green upperparts contrasting with the clean white underparts of both birds. The composition captures the species in characteristic flight, a device Audubon used to portray aerial insectivores in motion. Plate 98 of Birds of America, held at the University of Pittsburgh.
audubon-birds-99-cow-pen-bird: A male and female Brown-headed Cowbird stand on a mossy, rocky ground surface, the male's glossy dark plumage contrasting with the streaked brown female beside him. Plate 99 of John James Audubon's Birds of America depicts the species — then known as the Cow-pen Bird — in a ground-level setting, from the double-elephant folio held at the University of Pittsburgh.
collection-of-beauty-0-entrevue-du-roi-e: Part of Rubens's twenty-four-canvas Marie de' Medici cycle commissioned for the Luxembourg Palace and now in the Louvre. The royal meeting at Lyons is staged as an allegorical pageant, with personifications of the city, putti and a chariot drawn by lions glorifying a politically uneasy marriage.
collection-of-beauty-0-le-sultan-mulay-a: Rubens reworks an earlier portrait by Jan Cornelisz Vermeyen of the Hafsid sultan, lending the Tunisian ruler the broad shoulders, ruddy flesh and lustrous turban he reserved for noble sitters. Such copies after Vermeyen fed Rubens's lifelong fascination with cosmopolitan dress and the wider Mediterranean world.
collection-of-beauty-01-ichikobu-bridge: Sheet from Hiroshige's late series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, showing Edo's Ikkoku Bridge with the sacred peak rising behind the city's tiled rooftops. The print uses the deep cobalt bokashi gradation Hiroshige favoured for sky and water, contrasting urban bustle below with serene distance.
collection-of-beauty-07leucip: A vehement Baroque mythology in which Castor and Pollux carry off the daughters of Leucippus, the rearing horses and twisting nudes locked into Rubens's signature swirling diagonal. Painted in Antwerp at the height of his powers, the picture exemplifies the warm, pearly flesh and muscular drama that defined his manner.
collection-of-beauty-09-the-teahouse-wit: From Hiroshige's Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, travellers pause at a roadside teahouse while the snow-tipped volcano floats beyond. The graded blue sky and crisp foreground figures show the woodblock master's command of bokashi printing and his eye for the everyday rhythms of Edo travel.
collection-of-beauty-10-the-prodigal-son: Dürer's celebrated early engraving sets the parable in a meticulously observed German farmyard, the kneeling youth surrounded by snouting pigs and timber outbuildings. The print, made soon after his first Italian journey, fuses Northern realism with new Renaissance ideas of psychological inwardness.
collection-of-beauty-100-views-edo-063: A giant black carp streamer hoisted for the Boys' Festival fills the foreground of this Summer sheet from Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo (1857), a hallmark of his daring close-up framing. Far below, travellers cross Suido Bridge over the Kanda River while smaller streamers fly above the rooftops of Surugadai, with the snow-capped cone of Mount Fuji on the horizon.
collection-of-beauty-100-views-edo-076: An Autumn sheet from Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo (1857). The timber arch of Kyobashi spans the foreground beneath a full moon as pilgrims carrying banners cross the bridge, while bamboo poles stacked upright in the riverside yards rise in jagged silhouette behind it. Below, a lone boatman poles a loaded skiff across the dark water.
collection-of-beauty-11-wild-goose-hill-: From Hiroshige's vertical Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (1858), the view looks out from the pine-studded bluffs of Konodai — Wild Goose Hill — across the broad, islanded course of the Tone River. White sails thread the channels between grassy banks, and Mount Fuji's snow-covered cone rises on the horizon above a band of red sky.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-arcimboldo-w: From Arcimboldo's Four Seasons cycle painted for the Habsburg court, Winter is a gnarled tree-stump head with bark for skin, ivy for hair and a lemon and orange hanging from broken branches. The conceit flattered the emperor as the season that endures and rules over all others.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-de-schovenbi: Painted at the asylum in Saint-Rémy after a Millet print, part of Van Gogh's series translating the older peasant painter into his own thick, rhythmic brushwork. The stooping woman and golden sheaves are reworked in the saturated yellows and ultramarines of his final Provençal year, now in the Van Gogh Museum.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-eugene-ferdi: An Orientalist subject typical of Delacroix's late career, depicting a North African horseman tending to his mount. The painter draws on sketches from his 1832 Moroccan journey, deploying loose, energetic brushwork and a warm, dust-toned palette to evoke movement and Mediterranean light.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-gericault-th: A Romantic head study of a long-haired youth, painted in the years surrounding the Raft of the Medusa. Géricault works in rapid, sculptural brushstrokes against a darkened ground, using strong chiaroscuro to model the face with a directness drawn from his admiration of Caravaggio and the Old Masters.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-gerome-black: A study of an Ottoman irregular soldier, painted after Gérôme's travels through Egypt and the Levant. The figure's embroidered silks and weaponry are rendered with the polished, almost photographic finish that defined French academic Orientalism, set against a neutral studio ground that isolates costume and pose.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-giuseppe-arc: Summer rendered as a profile head built from ripe produce — peach cheeks, a cucumber nose, garlic teeth, with a straw collar inscribed with the artist's signature. Part of the Four Seasons series for Maximilian II, it pairs Mannerist invention with sharp still-life observation.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-gustave-cail: Painted in the family garden at Yerres, the picture shows the artist's brother Martial reading beneath potted orange trees while a woman strolls in dappled sun. Caillebotte combines Impressionist light with the steep, photographically cropped perspective that distinguishes his contribution to the movement.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-ingres-mme-v: A graphite portrait drawing of Madame Baltard with her young daughter, wife of the architect of Les Halles. Ingres lavishes precise, wiry contour on the heads while leaving the dresses summarily indicated, in keeping with the Neoclassical portrait drawings he produced throughout his Roman and Parisian careers.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-jean-leon-ge: An allegory of Truth, nude and enraged, climbing from the well into which liars have cast her — painted at the height of the Dreyfus Affair and widely read as Gérôme's bitter comment on public deceit. The polished academic surface gives the mythic figure unsettling photographic immediacy.

A slave auction in ancient Rome, set in a vaulted brick hall: an auctioneer in a yellow toga presents a nude woman on a raised platform while bidders' arms reach up from the crowd below, and other captives wait behind him. Painted in 1884, the work applies the same archaeological precision and enamelled finish Gérôme brought to his Orientalist subjects, here turned on classical antiquity.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-john-constab: A panoramic view down the Stour Valley toward Dedham church and the Suffolk coast, the heart of Constable's native country. Painted late in his life, the picture distils decades of plein-air study into a richly worked oil, with broken touches of white — his signature "snow" — flickering across foliage and sky.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-nihon-fukei-: A view of Uchisange in Okayama, issued in Hasui's series Selected Views of Japan. Working in the shin-hanga revival of ukiyo-e, he uses graded bokashi printing and a quiet, twilight palette to capture a fleeting weather effect over the streetscape.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-peter-paul-r: A nocturnal genre piece in which an elderly woman shields a single flame as a boy lights his candle from hers. Rubens borrows the candlelit motif from Northern tradition and from his Italian study of Caravaggio, modelling the warm, ruddy flesh in fluid Baroque brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-pierre-puvis: Three pensive nymphs are arranged in a frieze along a pale shore, an Arcadian reverie rather than a specific place. Puvis de Chavannes paints in the chalky, fresco-like matte tonality that made him a touchstone for Symbolists and for the young Picasso and Seurat.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-rocky-landsc: A study of the Neurathen rock formation in Saxon Switzerland, with weathered sandstone pillars rising against a pale sky. Friedrich drew repeatedly from this region near Dresden, translating direct observation into the meditative, vertical compositions characteristic of his mature Romantic landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-suzuki-harun: A polychrome woodblock print from Harunobu's Zashiki hakkei (Eight Parlour Views), a series that recasts the classical "Eight Views" landscape themes as domestic interior scenes. A woman with a pipe sits beside a lacquered dome draped with white silk floss — its unprinted, embossed relief standing in for evening snow — while a girl dozes against her side. Made around 1765, when Harunobu was pioneering full-colour nishiki-e printing; this impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-the-chess-ga: Two men hunched over a chessboard in a tiled Cairene interior, a favourite subject of the Austrian Orientalist Ludwig Deutsch. The picture displays his trademark microscopic finish, with carpets, brass trays and mashrabiya screens recorded in jewel-like detail under cool, even daylight.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-theodore-ger: A monumental Roman aqueduct spans an Italianate river valley at dusk, hill-top towers catching the last light while small figures bathe in the stream below. One of the large decorative landscapes depicting times of day that Géricault painted in 1818, it shows him adopting the heroic, Poussin-derived classical landscape mode at the threshold of Romanticism. The painting is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-van-gogh-das: A view of a suburban café-restaurant on the banks of the Seine, painted during Van Gogh's Paris years when he frequented the riverside towns with Bernard and Signac. The lightened palette and short, divisionist-inflected strokes register his rapid absorption of Impressionist and Neo-Impressionist colour theory.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-van-gogh-gar: A view into the walled garden of the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum, where Van Gogh was a voluntary patient between 1889 and 1890. A solitary figure passes between trees rendered in writhing, rope-like strokes; the picture is one of many in which the cloister grounds become both subject and consolation.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-van-gogh-wei: Painted from a vantage above Arles in the productive summer of 1888, the canvas reads as a tapestry of yellow stubble, ripening crops and red roofs gathered around the town's spires. Van Gogh works in dense, directional brushstrokes that translate Provençal heat into structured pattern.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-vincent-van-: A small, mordant memento mori produced during Van Gogh's studies at the Antwerp academy, where students were drilled in anatomy from articulated skeletons. The flippant cigarette has been read as a sardonic jab at academic propriety as much as a meditation on mortality.

One of several portraits Van Gogh painted of Joseph Roulin, the postal employee he befriended in Arles. Roulin appears bust-length in his blue, gilt-buttoned uniform and "POSTES" cap, his long forked beard set off against a green ground patterned with swirling blossoms. Oil on canvas, painted in 1888; now in the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-vittore-carp: Hunters draw bows at waterbirds from flat-bottomed boats on the still Venetian lagoon, rendered with the crystalline detail typical of Carpaccio's narrative cycles. The panel was originally the upper portion of a larger work: its lower half is the Two Venetian Ladies in the Museo Correr, and the lily at the bottom edge once continued into a vase beside the seated women. Oil on panel, about 1490–1495, J. Paul Getty Museum; the verso carries a trompe-l'oeil letter rack.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-wilhelm-von-: Two riders pause with a pair of riderless horses on a pale track at the shore of the Tegernsee, dogs at their feet and country women passing to the right, while rain streaks from heavy clouds over the mountains beyond. Painted in 1832, the small picture shows the crisp, sharply lit Biedermeier finish for which Kobell is known. It is held in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-1280px-zelfportret-: Painted in Paris, the artist confronts the viewer at his easel with palette and brushes in hand, dressed in a workman's blue smock. The dense, divisionist touches of complementary colour absorbed from Seurat and Signac mark a decisive break from the dark Dutch palette of his earlier self-portraits.

Painted during Van Gogh's Paris years, this self-portrait shows the artist absorbing Impressionist and Pointillist colour theory. Short, hatched strokes of complementary blue and orange radiate from his head, turning the felt hat into a halo of pure pigment. Now in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-15-qian-xuan-eight-: A handscroll by the thirteenth-century painter Qian Xuan, spacing eight flowering sprays — narcissus, blossoming branches and garden flowers among them — across a plain paper ground. Qian Xuan, a Song loyalist who declined to serve the Mongol court, renders each specimen in fine outline filled with pale colour washes, in his deliberately refined, archaistic manner. The scroll is held in the Palace Museum, Beijing.
collection-of-beauty-1520-portrait-of-a-: A woman in a dark gown and broad white linen headdress gazes past the viewer from behind a painted arch with marbled columns, one ringed hand holding open a small prayer book at the lower edge. Painted around 1520, the portrait is characteristic of the sober likenesses Quinten Metsys produced for burgher patrons in Antwerp.
collection-of-beauty-1522-holbein-d-a-an: Half-length portrait of a clean-shaven young man in a broad black hat and patterned damask robe, identified as a member of the Weiss family of Augsburg. He holds a sprig of red carnations and an inscribed metal object before a dark foliate ground. Hans Holbein the Elder painted the portrait in 1522, two years before his death.
collection-of-beauty-1529-cranach-allego: A programmatic Lutheran image divided down the middle: on the left, Death and the Devil drive a sinner toward Hell beneath the Tablets of the Law; on the right, John the Baptist directs the same figure to the crucified Christ. Cranach worked closely with Luther in Wittenberg, and this composition became a template for Reformation visual theology.
collection-of-beauty-1595-wtewael-die-si: The Genesis flood overtakes humanity in Wtewael's 1595 canvas: contorted nude figures scramble up trees and rocky outcrops as the waters rise, the doomed crowding every ledge of the darkening landscape behind. The Utrecht Mannerist favoured such teeming figure compositions for biblical and Ovidian subjects; the painting is in the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Nuremberg.
collection-of-beauty-1596-caravaggio-the: An early half-length picture from Caravaggio's years in the household of Cardinal del Monte, showing an androgynous youth absorbed in playing a lute. The still life of violin, recorder and open sheet music is rendered with the same forensic light that became the artist's signature, the figure pulled forward against a dark wall. Caravaggio treated the subject more than once: this version, with its red oriental carpet and spinet keyboard, was painted for Cardinal del Monte and is the canvas long exhibited at the Metropolitan Museum from the Wildenstein Collection. The closely related version in the Hermitage, made for the Marchese Vincenzo Giustiniani, sets flowers, fruit and a violin on a marble table in their place.
collection-of-beauty-1627-rubens-maria-m: A Nursing Madonna: the Virgin, in a red gown, suckles the standing Christ Child while steadying an open illuminated book beside her. Climbing roses fill the upper left and a still life of fruit spills over the ledge at the right, opening onto a wooded landscape. Painted in 1627, the picture joins warm Rubensian figures to finely observed Flemish flower and fruit painting in the devotional manner cultivated in Counter-Reformation Antwerp; it hangs in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-1665-girl-with-a-pe: A tronie rather than a portrait: an anonymous young woman turns over her shoulder, lips parted, against a deep glazed-black ground. Vermeer reserves his most expensive pigments, ultramarine and lead-tin yellow, for the turban, and renders the famous teardrop earring with two soft dabs of lead white. In the Mauritshuis, The Hague.
collection-of-beauty-17-the-sea-off-the-: From Hiroshige's late Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, published shortly before his death. A foreground of dark, choppy water frames the distant cone of Fuji across the bay; the woodblock printer's bokashi gradients soften sky and sea into bands of graded blue.
collection-of-beauty-1770-fragonard-maed: A girl lies on her back amid tumbled bedclothes beneath a golden canopy, balancing a small white dog on her raised legs, her chemise fallen back. Painted around 1770, the canvas belongs to Fragonard's intimate group of boudoir scenes, set down with rapid, broken brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-1777-west-benjamin-: Two officers pause with their horses in a rocky landscape: one, in scarlet regimentals, gestures with his hat toward the distant valley, while his companion in a pale uniform rests a boot on a boulder; their groom waits with the mounts at the left. West, born in Pennsylvania and by then historical painter to George III in London, painted the canvas in 1777, in the midst of the American Revolution. Oil on canvas, 101.6 by 127 cm; Princeton University Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-1794-stuart-gilbert: The New York merchant William Bayard sits in three-quarter view at a writing table, papers in one hand and an inkstand at his elbow, his sage-green coat and white stock set against a backdrop of crimson drapery. Stuart painted the portrait in 1794, during his New York period and shortly before he moved to Philadelphia to begin the presidential portraits that would define his career.
collection-of-beauty-18-the-sagami-river: Plate eighteen of Hiroshige's late vertical Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858. Raftsmen pole timber rafts down the Sagami River in Sagami Province, seen through a screen of tall reeds in the foreground; beyond, birds cross the sky above low hills as the snow-capped cone of Fuji rises in the distance.
collection-of-beauty-1813-schinkel-blick: Better remembered as Berlin's neoclassical architect, Schinkel was also a Romantic landscape painter. Here a high Alpine valley with a humble farmstead is dwarfed by the snow mass of Mont Blanc, the staffage and outbuildings supplying scale for the sublime geology beyond.
collection-of-beauty-1815-schinkel-mitte: An imagined medieval city rises in tiers of Gothic spires above a river, lit by a low theatrical sun. Schinkel uses architecture as nationalist allegory in the wake of the Napoleonic wars, the cathedral silhouette standing in for a recovered German past.
collection-of-beauty-1832-brullov-vsadni: Giovannina Pacini reins in a black horse while her younger sister Amazilia watches wide-eyed from the steps of a villa, both wards of Countess Yulia Samoilova. Commissioned by Samoilova in Milan and exhibited at the Brera Academy in 1832, the picture earned Bryullov comparisons to Rubens and Van Dyck before it passed to Pavel Tretyakov in 1893.
collection-of-beauty-1836-heimkehr-des-p: A Berlin contribution to European Philhellenism: a palikar, one of the irregular fighters of the Greek War of Independence, returns to his family on the shore at sunset, bending over the infant in his arms while his wife shoulders his rifle and two children press around him. Magnus, a Berlin portraitist, treats the costume and embroidery with ethnographic precision while keeping the emotional register restrained. Painted in 1836; Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-1841-millet-jean-fr: A bust-length likeness of Louis-Alexandre Marolles, the sitter turned slightly and set against a dark ground. Millet painted this portrait in 1841 during his early Cherbourg years, well before the rural subjects that made his name; the canvas is now in the Princeton University Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-1859-menzel-student: Menzel records a Berlin student torchlight procession with his characteristic reportorial eye, the crowd compacted into a flickering frieze of faces and smoking brands. He was the great chronicler of Prussian public life, equally at ease with court ceremonies and street gatherings.
collection-of-beauty-1866-gustave-courbe: A reclining nude exhibited at the Salon of 1866, where Courbet's frank naturalism, tousled hair and unidealised flesh, scandalised critics expecting an academic Venus. The bird perched on her outstretched hand provides the slim mythological pretext. Now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-1869-courbet-die-wo: One of a series of stormy seascapes Courbet painted at Étretat in 1869, the breaking wave thickly built up with the palette knife. He treated water as solid matter, layering grey-green pigment against a leaden sky to register the weight rather than the glitter of the Channel.
collection-of-beauty-1871-vereshchagin-a: A pyramid of human skulls rises on a scorched plain before a ruined city, crows wheeling overhead. Vereshchagin, a veteran of the Russian campaigns in Turkestan, dedicated the canvas "to all conquerors, past, present and to come"; it is the closing image of his Turkestan series.
collection-of-beauty-1872-vereshchagin-p: Part of the Turkestan series, the painting shows the Emir of Bukhara receiving a heap of severed Russian heads as battle trophies in a tiled courtyard. Vereshchagin's archaeological precision in the architecture sharpens, rather than softens, the indictment of war.
collection-of-beauty-1872-vereshchagin-t: Set in Samarkand's Registan square, a victory ceremony unfolds before the great madrasa portals while Russian soldiers' heads stand impaled on poles in the foreground. Vereshchagin pairs the splendour of Timurid tilework with documentary atrocity, a recurring strategy of his Turkestan cycle.
collection-of-beauty-1873-monet-houses-a: Painted in the Paris suburb where Monet lived from 1871 to 1878, the heart of the early Impressionist project. A row of villas behind a flowering garden is rendered in broken touches of green, rose and violet, light flickering across stucco walls.
collection-of-beauty-1878-vereshchagin-s: From Vereshchagin's Balkan series, painted after his service in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-78. Lines of Russian troops throw their caps in the air as a general on a white horse gallops past in salute, while the snow-covered field at Shipka Pass is strewn with the frozen dead of both armies. The canvas hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-1880-frederic-leigh: Leighton shown bearded in the red robe and President's chain of the Royal Academy, a fragment of the Parthenon frieze behind him. Oil on canvas painted in 1880 by invitation for the Uffizi collection of artists' self-portraits in Florence, where it remains.
collection-of-beauty-1885-1889-birkenhai: Sunlight filters between the white trunks of a young birch wood, the grass below flecked with light, shadow and scattered wildflowers. Levitan worked on the small picture for four summers, beginning it at Babkino near Moscow in 1885 and finishing it at Plyos on the Volga in 1889; it is now in the Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-1887-renoir-nu-dans: A small late-1880s nude from Renoir's so-called "manière aigre", when he tightened his contours under the influence of Ingres and Italian Renaissance drawing. The pearly figure is set against a lightly brushed landscape, oil on canvas, now on long-term loan from the Pearlman Foundation to the Princeton University Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-1890s-frederick-lei: Psyche stands nude beside a reflecting pool, drawing aside a length of drapery as she prepares to bathe, framed by two fluted columns. Leighton exhibited the oil at the Royal Academy in 1890; it was bought under the Chantrey Bequest and passed to the Tate. The narrow vertical format echoes a marble caryatid, the figure's weight set on one leg in contrapposto.
collection-of-beauty-1893-levitan-portra: Isaac Levitan sits in a dark suit, one arm draped along the back of a wicker-patterned chair, his bearded face turned in three-quarter view with a calm, reserved gaze against a dark interior. Valentin Serov painted his friend and fellow painter in 1893; the portrait is in the Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-19-the-seven-ri-bea: Plate nineteen of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting Shichirigahama, the seven-ri stretch of coast in Sagami Province. Enoshima crouches on the horizon while Fuji floats beyond, the printer using bokashi gradient to fade sea into sky.
collection-of-beauty-1901-portrait-of-iv: The illustrator Ivan Bilibin sits with long dark hair and a pointed beard, a white ruffled shirt-front and a red flower in the lapel of his dark coat, painted in broad, fluid strokes against a dark green interior. Kustodiev portrayed him in 1901, when Bilibin was producing the illustrated Russian fairy-tale books that made his name.
collection-of-beauty-1902-monet-die-wate: From Monet's London series, painted from his rooms at the Savoy Hotel overlooking the Thames. Waterloo Bridge dissolves into morning mist, its arches reduced to violet silhouettes while factory chimneys smoke on the far bank; the canvas, signed and dated 1902, is in the Hamburger Kunsthalle.
collection-of-beauty-1913-malevich-portr: Malevich disperses the head of the composer and painter Mikhail Matyushin into intersecting metallic planes, with a band of piano keys and a fragment of neatly parted hair standing in for the sitter's likeness. The Cubo-Futurist oil on canvas was painted in 1913, the year the two men collaborated with Aleksei Kruchenykh on the Futurist opera Victory over the Sun, for which Matyushin wrote the music and Malevich the designs. It is held by the State Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-1915-kustodiev-die-: A stout nude with reddish-blond hair sits upright on the edge of her bed, one hand resting on the pink satin quilt and her feet on a small embroidered footstool, framed by rose-patterned blue wallpaper, lace-trimmed pillows and a chest painted with bright flowers. Kustodiev painted The Beauty in 1915 with the Moscow Art Theatre actress Faina Shevchenko as his model; the canvas is in the Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-1993-151-1-pma2018: A Monet of 1888, catalogued as Wildenstein 1191 and now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art. By this date the artist was working in extended series, breaking form into mosaics of high-keyed colour to record a single motif under shifting light.
collection-of-beauty-1stearlofclare: Gilbert Stuart's full-length portrait shows John FitzGibbon, 1st Earl of Clare, standing in the black robes of the Lord Chancellor of Ireland, heavy with gold embroidery, wearing a full-bottomed wig and lace cravat; the ceremonial mace and embroidered purse of state rest beside him. Stuart painted the portrait in 1789, the year FitzGibbon was appointed Lord Chancellor.
collection-of-beauty-20-the-entrance-gat: Plate twenty of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, showing pilgrims passing through the bronze torii at Enoshima with Fuji floating across Sagami Bay. The composition is built from flat overlapping silhouettes, a hallmark of late-Edo ukiyo-e landscape design.
collection-of-beauty-2021-nyr-19739-0043: An elderly man with a bald crown and a long white beard turns toward the viewer, dressed in a plain dark coat and holding a white handkerchief in his right hand, set against a warm brown ground. The portrait is attributed to Domenikos Theotokopoulos, called El Greco, whose sober Toledan likenesses stand apart in register from his visionary religious compositions.
collection-of-beauty-2022-06-24-at-13-35: Five peaches, two of them halved to expose the stone, lie on a bed of dark green leaves against a warm orange-brown ground. The feathery brushwork and close-keyed orange and pink tones are characteristic of Monet's small still lifes, and the picture is catalogued as Wildenstein 952.
collection-of-beauty-2022-06-24-at-13-41: A bare lane leads into the village of Giverny under winter light, with leafless trees and pale fields rendered in muted blues and ochres. Painted shortly after Monet settled in Giverny, the canvas catalogued as Wildenstein 967 belongs to a small group of winter views recording his new surroundings.
collection-of-beauty-21-lake-at-hakone: Mount Fuji rises beyond the ring of mountains enclosing Lake Ashi at Hakone, where a pine-topped green headland and jagged ochre crags meet the pale water. The sheet is numbered twenty-one in Hiroshige's vertical-format Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858.
collection-of-beauty-23-the-sea-off-satt: Plate twenty-three of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Big stylised waves curl in the foreground off Satta Point on the Tōkaidō road, with Fuji rising serenely behind, an answer to Hokusai's earlier Great Wave composition.
collection-of-beauty-24-the-pine-forest-: From Hiroshige's late Mount Fuji series, the spit of pines at Miho-no-Matsubara curls into Suruga Bay with Fuji on the far shore. The site is bound up with the noh play Hagoromo, and Hiroshige uses bokashi blues and the dense black of pine needles to set its quiet mood.
collection-of-beauty-25-fuji-on-the-left: Travellers move along the Tokaido highway as Mount Fuji rises to the left, a print from Hiroshige's posthumously published Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The composition layers near figures against a flattened distance, exploiting the woodblock medium's graded skies and crisp silhouettes.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-bonaparte-an: Napoleon, mounted on a dark horse, halts before the half-buried Great Sphinx during the 1798 Egyptian campaign, his army drawn up on the desert plain behind him. Gérôme, the leading Orientalist of the Paris Salon, painted the encounter in 1886 — the picture is also known by the subtitle 'Œdipe' — casting it as one civilisational riddle posed to another. The canvas now hangs at Hearst Castle.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-courbet-late: A monumental allegory of seven years of Courbet's artistic life, gathering critics, patrons, and anonymous figures around the painter at his easel, with a nude muse and small boy looking on. Rejected from the 1855 Exposition Universelle, it became the centrepiece of his self-organised Pavilion of Realism in Paris.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-de-heuvel-va: Painted shortly after the artist's arrival in Paris, this view of the working windmills and gypsum quarries on Montmartre still uses the muted, earth-toned palette he carried over from his Dutch period. The brushwork is loose and matter-of-fact, predating his encounter with Impressionist colour.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-finches-and-: Two finches perch on a slender bamboo branch, rendered in delicate ink and colour on silk. Attributed to the artist-emperor Huizong, the painting exemplifies the Northern Song court's pursuit of meticulous bird-and-flower observation, where each feather and leaf vein is individually described.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-gustave-cour: A small landscape of the Roman bridge over the Vidourle in Languedoc, oil on paper later mounted on panel. Courbet builds the stonework and riverbank with the heavy palette knife and earthy tonal range that defined his realist treatment of provincial French scenery.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-hiroshi-yosh: A woodblock print of cherry blossoms at Kumoi, made in the shin-hanga revival style that Yoshida helped lead. He personally supervised the carvers and printers, layering many impressions of subtly graded pink to capture diffuse spring light.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-hiroshige-fi: Descending Geese at Katata, from the Eight Views of Ōmi, depicting boats and a flock settling onto Lake Biwa at dusk. Hiroshige distils the classical Chinese-derived theme into broad bands of graded indigo bokashi, a printing technique that became his signature.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-hiroshige24-: Shimada Station from Hiroshige's celebrated series The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, showing travellers being carried across the unbridged Ōi River. The print is reproduced from a later miniature edition by the Takamizawa workshop in Tokyo.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-jean-leon-ge: A reconstruction of a race in the Circus Maximus, with quadrigas thundering past the spina under the gaze of a packed Roman crowd. Gérôme drew on archaeological sources to render every harness, obelisk, and statue with the meticulous polish that made him a star of Salon history painting.

Two deer pause amid golden autumn bracken beneath an orange-leafed tree, with hazier woodland and tall slender trees beyond under a soft sky. Gérôme painted Souvenir of Achères in 1903, the year before his death, setting aside his Orientalist subjects for a quiet record of the French countryside. The canvas is held by the Columbus Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-jean-louis-t: Four thoroughbreds stretched into the rocking-horse 'flying gallop' pose then conventional in sporting art, set against a low storm-bruised English sky. Géricault painted it in London, where his fascination with horseflesh and equestrian sport reshaped his late Romantic style.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-ndl-dc-25865: Sun setting over the rooftops of Ichinokura at Ikegami, from Hasui's series Twenty Views of Tōkyō. The shin-hanga print uses long horizontal bands of graded orange and indigo to fix a single, melancholic moment of urban dusk.

On a rain-puddled quay, a dog stands beside a water pump and looks out across the harbour, where sailing vessels and a steamer ride at anchor and the lights of the far shore streak the still water. Akashi-chō after Rain belongs to Hasui's series Twenty Views of Tokyo, published in 1928 (Shōwa 3); this impression is from the National Diet Library Digital Collections.

Jagged rock pinnacles, caught red by the low sun, rise from a teal sea off Ryūga Island on the Oga Peninsula in Akita, grassy slopes climbing behind them beneath a bank of grey cloud. The woodblock print comes from Hasui's series Souvenirs of Travel III, published in 1926; this impression is held in the National Diet Library Digital Collections.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-nihon-fukei-: An early Hasui woodblock from Selected Views of Japan, showing thatched roofs at Kazusa village in former Hizen Province on the Kyūshū coast. The print already shows the publisher Watanabe's house style: precise architecture, soft skies, and water rendered in layered indigo wash.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-ondergesneeu: A bleak field at Auvers with a discarded harrow under fresh snow, freely after a black-and-white print by Jean-François Millet. Van Gogh translated Millet's earthbound peasant subjects into his own thicker, colour-saturated impasto throughout his last year.

A bleak field at Auvers with a discarded harrow under fresh snow, freely after a black-and-white print by Jean-François Millet. Van Gogh translated Millet's earthbound peasant subjects into his own thicker, colour-saturated impasto throughout his last year.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-pieter-brueg: Returning hunters and their lean dogs trudge across a snowy ridge above frozen ponds where villagers skate, the panel that anchors Bruegel's celebrated cycle of the months commissioned by the Antwerp merchant Niclaes Jonghelinck. Now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, it set the template for European winter landscape painting.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-saint-franci: The saint swoons into the arms of an angel after receiving the stigmata on Mount La Verna, a nocturnal vision lit by a single raking source. It is generally taken to be Caravaggio's earliest religious commission of consequence, painted for his patron Cardinal Francesco Maria del Monte in Rome.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-saint-jerome: The aged hermit-scholar bends over his Vulgate translation, his bald head and the skull on the table almost mirrored across the strong diagonal of his outstretched arm. Painted in Rome for Cardinal Scipione Borghese, the work is now in the Galleria Borghese.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-the-big-wave: A page from Hokusai's later, more contemplative woodblock series One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji, in which a curling wave frames the distant sacred peak. Printed in monochrome ink with discreet grey gradations, it reprises in book form the motif of his earlier Great Wave.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-the-langlois: The Langlois drawbridge spans the canal south of Arles, a lone woman with a parasol crossing as a small boat sits by the bank below and a pair of dark cypresses rise behind. Van Gogh painted the bridge repeatedly in spring 1888, drawn to its echo of the Dutch canals of his youth. This oil on canvas, catalogued F570, is now in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, Cologne.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-the-taking-o: Judas's kiss seals Christ's arrest as armoured soldiers surge in from the right, their polished steel catching the lantern held by a self-portrait of the painter at the edge of the scene. Lost for nearly two centuries, the canvas was rediscovered in a Jesuit residence in Dublin in 1990 and is now on long-term loan to the National Gallery of Ireland.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-thumbnail: An unattributed image from the collection. Without a reliable title, artist, or date, no descriptive label can be drawn from the historical record.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-van-dyck-sir: A posthumous portrait of Venetia Stanley, Lady Digby, propped on her pillows in the dawn following her sudden death in 1633. Commissioned by the grieving Sir Kenelm Digby and now at Dulwich Picture Gallery, the picture is unusually intimate among Van Dyck's English court portraits.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-van-gogh-ack: A Provençal field worked by oxen and ploughman, painted while Van Gogh was a voluntary patient at the asylum of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole near Saint-Rémy. The furrows roll across the canvas in his characteristic ribbon-like impasto, an homage to the peasant labour Millet had pictured a generation earlier.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-van-gogh-the: Gnarled olives churn in the foreground while the limestone Alpilles rise behind under a clouded sky, painted from the grounds of Saint-Paul asylum. Now at MoMA, it belongs to the group of about fifteen olive-grove canvases Van Gogh devoted to the trees during his Saint-Rémy year.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-vincent-van-: A still life of grapes, lemons, pears, and apples banked across the table, painted in Paris under the influence of Adolphe Monticelli's heavy paint and the Impressionists' fruit studies. Now at the Art Institute of Chicago, it shows Van Gogh testing a brighter, complementary-colour palette.

A field of green wheat and tall flowering grasses fills the foreground, with a white house half-hidden behind a low wall and dark trees on the rise beyond. Van Gogh painted it in 1890 at Auvers-sur-Oise, where he spent his last weeks under the care of Dr Paul Gachet. The canvas now belongs to The Phillips Collection, Washington.

Two harvesters nap in the shade of a haystack at noon, freely copied from a Millet print Van Gogh kept in his Saint-Rémy studio. He translated Millet's grey original into a pairing of complementary blue shadows and golden yellow stubble.

Rows of vines descend the slope toward the white walls and orange-tiled roofs of Auvers-sur-Oise, with wooded hills closing the horizon and red blossoms edging the foreground. Painted in June 1890, weeks before Van Gogh's death, the canvas is now in the Saint Louis Art Museum.

Beached fishing smacks on the Mediterranean sand at Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, their masts and rigging picked out in clean primary colour. Made on a five-day excursion from Arles in June 1888, the picture marks Van Gogh's first encounter with the sea in the South of France.

A reaper bends to his work amid sun-bleached fields under a churning sky, painted in the final months of Van Gogh's life at Auvers-sur-Oise. Thick parallel strokes of yellow and ochre carry the artist's recurring theme of the harvester as a figure of mortality and quiet acceptance.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-william-holm: A goat staggers across the salt flats of the Dead Sea, its horns bound with the red wool of the Yom Kippur ritual. Hunt painted the scene on site in 1854, hauling his easel to the shore of Oosdoom in pursuit of the Pre-Raphaelite ideal of truth to nature, sharpened by Christian symbolism.
collection-of-beauty-26-the-oi-river-bet: Porters ford the broad shallows of the Oi River, with Fuji's cone framed beyond. Hiroshige drew the design for the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji issued by Tsutaya Kichizo, deploying the bokashi gradient technique to suggest mist rising off the water.
collection-of-beauty-2895-1-modigliani-0: A seated female nude faces the viewer with hands folded in her lap, the elongated neck and almond-shaped eyes characteristic of Modigliani's late figures set against a cool blue-grey ground. Painted around 1918, the canvas is held by the Honolulu Museum of Art under accession 2895.1.
collection-of-beauty-31-the-otsuki-plain: A stream meanders through the Ōtsuki plain past clumps of autumn grasses and wildflowers, with Fuji a pale silhouette above the mist-veiled hills. The design is plate 31 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858.
collection-of-beauty-32-dog-eye-pass: Hiroshige's view from Inume Pass in Kai Province looks down on a sea of cloud broken by Fuji's summit, plate 32 of his Thirty-six Views series. The composition compresses foreground rocks and distant peak into a single graphic plane, a hallmark of late-Edo landscape design.
collection-of-beauty-33-kogane-plain: A grazing horse, cropped by the frame, dominates the foreground while a second stands further off in the grassy plain; Fuji rises small and pale on the horizon between scattered pines. Plate 33 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, published around 1858, with red wildflowers dotting the green expanse.
collection-of-beauty-34-kuroto-bay: Boats drift in Kuroto Bay with Fuji visible across the water, plate 34 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The flat blue expanses and economical drawing of sails reflect the woodblock vocabulary that would soon enthral European Japonisme.
collection-of-beauty-3415-maria-magdalen: The Magdalene rests her cheek on her hand in the conventional pose of melancholia, jar of ointment beside her. Painted during Gentileschi's Roman years, the work fuses Caravaggesque chiaroscuro with the artist's signature interest in solitary, introspective female protagonists.
collection-of-beauty-35390682010-4609909: A landscape catalogued as Wildenstein 1449 in Monet's oeuvre. The artist's standard practice in such canvases is to dissolve form into broken touches of complementary colour, recording transient light with a saturated, high-keyed palette.
collection-of-beauty-36-the-hoda-coast: The closing print of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows the rocky Hoda coast in Awa Province, Fuji floating across Edo Bay. Crisp keyblock outlines and indigo seas give the design the graphic clarity that defined his late style.
collection-of-beauty-4344-vis-print-1476: An oil sketch on oak panel of an elderly woman, made as preparatory study for figures populating Rubens's larger religious and mythological compositions. The loose, economical handling typifies the head-studies the Antwerp workshop produced from life models.
collection-of-beauty-500px-gipsen-vrouwe: A plaster cast of a female torso seen from behind, set against a pale blue ground. Van Gogh painted a group of such plaster-cast studies in Paris, using the neutral academic subject to work through problems of modelling and colour. This 1887 example is in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam (inv. s0199V1962).
collection-of-beauty-500px-kuniyoshi-uta: A hawk poised in profile, its plumage detailed in the layered keyblock and colour blocks of an ukiyo-e print. Hawks were a favoured subject of late Edo print designers, the bird's predatory stillness suiting the medium's graphic economy.

A tiger paces against a wind-blown ground, its striped coat picked out in dense keyblock lines. Kuniyoshi, never having seen a live tiger, drew on imported Chinese painting models and his own taste for muscular animal subjects in the warrior-print tradition.
collection-of-beauty-7222-adoracion-de-l: The Magi present their gifts to the Virgin and Child before classical columns, a camel and horses crowding in at the left and a crown laid on the steps. An early work by El Greco of 1568-69, made shortly after the young painter left Crete for Italy, it is now in the Museo Soumaya, Mexico City.
collection-of-beauty-9: A Southern Song album leaf depicting a spring tide laden with rain, attributed to the court painter Li Di. Soft ink wash and atmospheric distance reflect the lyrical small-format landscape tradition cultivated at the Hangzhou academy.
collection-of-beauty-960px-03-sukiyagahs: The Sukiyagashi district of Edo with Fuji rising beyond rooftops, plate three of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The print balances the dense urban foreground against the calm geometric mountain that recurs throughout the series.
collection-of-beauty-960px-13-the-tama-r: The Tama River flows beneath a pale Fuji in this thirteenth design from Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views. Rafts and figures animate the middle distance, while bokashi gradients carry the eye from green water to blue mountain.
collection-of-beauty-960px-evening-snow-: Snow settles on the eaves of Terajima village at dusk, a print from Hasui's revival of landscape woodblock under the shin-hanga movement. Hasui worked closely with publisher Watanabe Shozaburo, prizing atmospheric weather and quiet rural corners over the bustle of the old Edo school.
collection-of-beauty-960px-fox-hunt-1893: A red fox flounders through deep snow as a flock of crows descends, the predator suddenly become prey. Painted at Prouts Neck on the Maine coast, this is the largest canvas of Homer's late career, its compressed Japonist composition and bleak palette signalling the harshness of the northern winter.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hanagami-danj: The warrior Hanagami Danjo grapples with a colossal salamander in the Tonta River of Izumo, a scene of legendary heroism. Kuniyoshi delights in muscular anatomy and reptilian texture, characteristic of the musha-e warrior prints that made his reputation.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-fut: The wedded rocks of Meoto Iwa stand off the Futami shore, joined by the sacred shimenawa rope, with Fuji visible across the bay. Plate twenty-seven of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the design pairs Shinto pilgrimage iconography with Hiroshige's signature distant cone.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-ii-: The Kintai Bridge arches in five wooden spans over the Nishiki at Iwakuni, a celebrated feat of Edo carpentry. The print belongs to Hiroshige II's One Hundred Famous Views of the Provinces, continuing the meisho tradition his teacher had popularised.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-mt-: From the Misaka Pass in Kai Province, Fuji is doubled by its reflection in Lake Kawaguchi below. Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views design exploits the symmetry as a graphic device, layering pine-clad slopes against the still water.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-sun: Red maples frame a view of Fuji from the slopes of Meguro at sunset, plate ten of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views. Printed by Tsutaya Kichizo, the design uses heavy bokashi in the sky to evoke the dying autumn light.
collection-of-beauty-960px-jean-leon-ger: Napoleon on horseback before the Sphinx and pyramids, a meditation on power and antiquity tied to the 1798 Egyptian campaign. Gerome's polished academic finish and ethnographic eye made him the leading French Orientalist of the Second Empire.
collection-of-beauty-960px-lofty-mt-lu-b: Towering peaks of Mount Lu rise in vertically stacked planes of ink, a hanging scroll painted by Shen Zhou as a birthday tribute to his teacher Chen Kuan. A founder of the Wu School of Ming literati painting, Shen here pays homage to the Yuan master Wang Meng's dense, crinkled brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-960px-museo-del-pra: An artist slumps over his desk as bats and owls swarm from the dark behind him, plate forty-three of Goya's Caprichos. The etching with aquatint, issued in Madrid in 1799, became the central emblem of the series' attack on Spanish superstition and unreason.
collection-of-beauty-960px-pieter-bruege: Hunters and their hounds trudge home over a snowbound ridge, looking down on skaters scattered across frozen ponds. The winter panel of Bruegel's series of months, commissioned by the Antwerp merchant Niclaes Jonghelinck, hangs today in Vienna's Kunsthistorisches Museum.
collection-of-beauty-960px-robert-delaun: The Eiffel Tower surges upward as if seen from its base, its lattice splayed against interlocking planes of saturated colour. Delaunay returned to the monument repeatedly across his career, fragmenting it through the Orphism he developed with Sonia Delaunay; this 1926 oil on canvas is in the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris.
collection-of-beauty-960px-sesshutoyo: An autumn landscape built from firm contours and axe-cut texture strokes, a temple compound rising beyond rocky bluffs while a lone sail crosses the water at left. Sesshū studied Ming Chinese ink painting at first hand during his 1467-69 journey to China; this work, dated 1496, is in the Tokyo National Museum.
collection-of-beauty-960px-tokyo-junidai: A cherry tree in full bloom spreads over a dark wooden building on Atagoyama, petals drifting down toward children playing on the paved ground below. The woodblock print, from Hasui's series Twelve Scenes of Tokyo (1921), shows the shin-hanga movement's pairing of traditional craftsmanship with atmospheric naturalism.
collection-of-beauty-960px-van-gogh-le-m: The windmill of the Moulin de la Galette stands on its mound beneath a windswept blue sky, a stooping figure working in the foreground. Van Gogh painted the Montmartre landmark — also depicted by Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec — several times in 1886, soon after moving in with his brother Theo in Paris; this version is in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-a-colored-version-o: A reworked echo of the famous Kanagawa wave, drawn from the later One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji. Hokusai mirrors the composition, removes the fishing boats, and turns the spume into a flock of birds — a meditation on transformation rendered in his late, more graphic woodblock manner.
collection-of-beauty-a-female-martyr-sai: A young woman in a mauve robe leans on a stone ledge, her arms resting on a book with a martyr's palm beside her, her gaze turned toward a distant landscape. Painted by Artemisia Gentileschi around 1640 and tentatively identified as Saint Catherine of Alexandria, the painting is in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
collection-of-beauty-a-foolish-virgin-in: A young woman with elaborately knotted braids is shown half-length, turning her oil lamp upside down to show that it is empty — the mark of the foolish virgins of the parable in Matthew 25, who let their lamps run dry before the bridegroom came. The engraving relates to Schongauer's series of the Wise and Foolish Virgins and bears his monogram. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-a-friendly-call: Two women sit in conversation in Chase's summer studio at Shinnecock, Long Island — a visitor in crisp white, parasol still in hand, faces her hostess across a long cushion-strewn divan, with framed prints and a tall gilt mirror filling the wall behind them. A leading American Impressionist and influential teacher, Chase painted the interior in 1895; the canvas hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-a-hippopotamus-and-: One of four exotic hunts Rubens painted around 1615 for Maximilian I of Bavaria, blending Flemish pictorial drama with antique pathos. Spear-wielding riders, snarling hounds, and writhing reptiles crash together in a swirling diagonal composition that became a touchstone for Baroque action painting.
collection-of-beauty-a-kitchenmaid-by-jo: A young kitchenmaid in a white cap and ruff raises a spitted fowl in one hand and holds a plucked bird in the other, surrounded by shelves of earthenware and metal vessels, a laid table with bread and fish, and a foreground basket of cabbages, cucumbers, and a joint of meat. Through the opening behind her, Christ appears in the house of Mary and Martha. The oil on canvas, signed by Joachim Wtewael and dated 1620–1625, measures roughly 103 by 72 centimetres and belongs to the Centraal Museum, Utrecht.
collection-of-beauty-a-parisian-lady-edo: A near-life-size portrait of the actress Ellen Andrée in fashionable street dress, her black silhouette set against a flat ground in Manet's signature manner. The picture pursues the figure of the modern Parisienne championed by Baudelaire rather than a sitter's likeness.
collection-of-beauty-a-sketch-of-the-mit: Hokusai frames the snow-capped cone of Mount Fuji between the tiled roofs of the Mitsui dry-goods house on Suruga Street in Edo, kites climbing the sky on long strings while tilers work on a roof at right. The design is number 2 in the woodblock series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, first published around 1830; an impression is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-a-sunday-on-la-gran: Seurat's manifesto of Neo-Impressionism, built over two years from countless oil sketches and conté studies. Bourgeois Parisians promenade along the Seine in frieze-like stillness, their forms assembled from tiny dots of contrasting pigment — the optical method he called divisionism.
collection-of-beauty-a-view-of-the-archb: Submitted to the Royal Academy in April 1790, the month Turner turned fifteen, this was his exhibition debut. The watercolour shows a topographical precision learned from Thomas Malton, the architecture set at sharp angles to flaunt the teenager's grasp of perspective.
collection-of-beauty-a-view-of-the-mount: A horseman crosses the V of Crawford Notch in the New Hampshire White Mountains, dwarfed by twisted pines and the bleached skeletons of trees torn from the slope. Cole painted the gorge in 1839, drawing on memories of the 1826 avalanche that wiped out the Willey family and their farmhands; it hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-a-woman-bathing-in-: A woman in a white shift gathers the hem above her knees as she wades into dark water, rich gold and red garments piled on the bank behind her. Painted on a small oak panel in the mid-1650s and signed at the lower left, the picture in the National Gallery, London, is rendered in strikingly free, loaded brushwork and is often thought to depict Hendrickje Stoffels.
collection-of-beauty-a-woman-whose-face-: A young woman bows her head into her shawl, mouth set and eyes downcast in unconcealed grief. Etching in the crayon manner by W. Hebert, around 1770, the print belongs to the Wellcome Collection's holdings of physiognomic studies that imitated red-chalk drawing through stippled etched dots.
collection-of-beauty-a-woman-with-a-rose: A woman in a wide-brimmed hat and ribbon choker stands in profile, a rose held in her lowered hand against the folds of her full skirts. The drawing dates from around 1763–1765, during Gainsborough's Bath years, and is catalogued in the British Museum's online database as entry 749307.
collection-of-beauty-a-young-lady-s-adve: A wide-eyed young woman with streaming hair strides in profile through a murky tangle of plant forms, bird-like creatures, and floating signs, a red arrow zigzagging near her feet. Klee made the work in 1922, during his early years teaching at the Bauhaus in Weimar; it is held by Tate Modern.
collection-of-beauty-abigail-adams-by-gi: The former First Lady sits with hands folded, wearing a rose-red dress under a sheer embroidered lace overlay and a white lace cap tied with ribbon. Gilbert Stuart painted Abigail Smith Adams between 1810 and 1815 as a companion to his portrait of John Adams; the portrait is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-accolade-by-edmund-: A medieval-revival fantasy of a queen knighting a young warrior with the flat of a sword, set in a sun-streaked palace hall. The picture is by Edmund Blair Leighton, a late Victorian academic painter whose chivalric scenes drew on Pre-Raphaelite costume study and theatre design.
collection-of-beauty-adachi-moor: A pregnant woman hangs bound and upside down from the rafters of a darkened house while a gaunt old woman crouches below, sharpening a knife — Yoshitoshi's treatment of the legend of the cannibal hag of Adachigahara. Published in September 1885, the vertical-format colour woodblock diptych, known as The Lonely House on Adachi Moor, is held by the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-adam-and-eve-uk-cia: Cranach returned to Adam and Eve dozens of times after 1509, refining a courtly Reformation iconography of the Fall. Eve hands the apple across the Tree of Knowledge while a serpent watches and a menagerie of stag, sheep, and roe gather symbolically around the first couple.
collection-of-beauty-adameveparadisecran: An early treatment of the Fall by the Wittenberg court painter, set within a paradise teeming with stags, lions, and small game. Cranach's slender, mannerist nudes and crisp linear drawing reflect his proximity to Luther's circle, where the subject carried fresh theological weight.
collection-of-beauty-admiral-of-the-whit: A swagger portrait of Admiral Lord Rodney, victor over the French at the 1782 Battle of the Saintes, the captured ensign of the Ville de Paris draped behind him. Gainsborough's feathery brushwork and silvery palette soften the formal demands of state portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-baupl: Menzel turns a humble Berlin construction site, fringed by drooping willows, into a study of weather and labour. The unposed subject and freshly observed light anticipate the realist vein the Prussian painter would pursue across decades of obsessive sketching from life.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-das-b: An empty room, white curtains billowing at the open balcony door, a sofa half-glimpsed in a wall mirror. Menzel made the small oil for himself, capturing transient sunlight with the immediacy of a snapshot decades before plein-air Impressionism reached Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-eisen: A grimy panorama of the Königshütte rolling mill in Upper Silesia, with workers wrestling glowing iron under shafts of furnace light. Menzel spent months on site making hundreds of drawings, producing one of the first ambitious European paintings to take heavy industry as its subject.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-flote: Menzel reconstructs an evening concert at Sanssouci, with Frederick the Great playing flute beside C.P.E. Bach at the harpsichord and Quantz, Benda, and the Margravine Wilhelmine listening. Painted under Friedrich Wilhelm IV, it crowns the artist's long Prussian historical project.
collection-of-beauty-adoration-of-the-ma: A Neapolitan-period altarpiece in which the Magi crowd around the Virgin and Child by torchlight. Gentileschi pushes the figures close to the picture plane and stages the gift-giving in heavy raking light, drawing on the Caravaggism she had carried south from Rome.
collection-of-beauty-adoration-of-the-sh: Shepherds gather around the Virgin and the naked Christ Child in a manger, bringing offerings including a lamb and a basket of eggs. A bull stands to the left and a rooster pecks at the foreground, grounding the holy scene in the rural world of the visitors. Painted around 1650 and now in the Museo del Prado, the work reflects Murillo's early naturalist manner, indebted to the Spanish Tenebrist tradition in its warm, earth-toned palette and unpretentious figure types.
collection-of-beauty-aeltje-uylenburgh-b: An elderly woman in a flat white collar and plain white linen cap meets the viewer's gaze with quiet composure, her face modelled in Rembrandt's characteristic warm chiaroscuro. Signed and dated 1632, this portrait of Aeltje Pietersdr. Uylenburgh belongs to the early Amsterdam years when Rembrandt was working in the studio of Hendrick Uylenburgh. The work is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-afganets: A standing portrait of an Afghan man in regional dress. Oil painting from Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, made in 1867 to 1868 after the artist joined General Kaufman's expedition to Central Asia. Vereshchagin combined ethnographic portraits of this kind with the battle scenes drawn from the same campaign.
collection-of-beauty-after-benjamin-west: A young man in a broad-brimmed black hat and blue coat rests his chin on one hand while holding drawing implements, in a pose that signals his identity as an artist. This circa 1776 work is a copy after a self-portrait by Benjamin West, the Pennsylvania-born painter who served as historical painter to George III and later as President of the Royal Academy. The original is attributed to West himself; this version is recorded at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-after-rubens-anne-o: An early seventeenth-century studio copy of a lost Rubens portrait of Anne of Austria, queen consort of Louis XIII. The Spanish-born queen wears stiff court dress and an elaborate ruff, recorded with the smooth porcelain finish typical of Rubens's diplomatic likenesses of European royalty.
collection-of-beauty-after-the-attack-pl: Vereshchagin painted the carnage of the Russo-Turkish siege of Plevna from first-hand experience as a war correspondent attached to the Russian army. The unsentimental documentary realism he made his trademark exposes the human cost behind official communiqués of imperial conquest.
collection-of-beauty-after-the-battle-of: From the twenty-canvas Slav Epic that Mucha worked on for nearly two decades, this scene shows the aftermath of the 1410 Polish-Lithuanian victory over the Teutonic Knights. The Art Nouveau poster designer here deploys monumental tempera-and-oil composition to advance a pan-Slavic political mythology.
collection-of-beauty-aivasovsky-i-c-ship: The warship Twelve Apostles ploughs through a heavy swell under billowing sail, her dark hull and tiered gun decks rendered with Aivazovsky's characteristic luminous seascape technique. Painted in 1897, the canvas depicts the celebrated Black Sea Fleet ship of the line that figured prominently in mid-nineteenth-century Russian naval history. Aivazovsky returned throughout his career to subjects drawn from the Imperial fleet, and this work belongs to the large body of maritime paintings produced at his studio in Feodosia.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-bosporus: Sailing vessels and a small rowing boat drift on the hazy waters of the Bosporus, their reflections dissolving in a pearly morning mist, while figures rest on the waterfront quay of Constantinople at the right. Aivazovsky painted this canvas in 1878, during one of several extended stays in the Ottoman capital where his marine panoramas attracted considerable patronage. The composition exemplifies his mastery of atmospheric light over water, a quality that made his Bosphorus views among the most sought-after of his later career.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-brig-mer: The 18-gun Russian brig Mercury fires from between two towering Ottoman ships of the line off the Bosphorus in May 1829, smoke and wind shredding the sails. Aivazovsky returned to the legendary encounter repeatedly, this 1892 canvas painting the small brig as a luminous wedge between dark hulls.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-by-bolot: Ivan Aivazovsky sits in three-quarter view in a dark coat, his broad side-whiskers framing a clean-shaven chin, a pencil poised over the drawing board resting on his lap. Dmitry Mikhailovich Bolotov painted the portrait in 1876, when Aivazovsky, official painter to the Russian Navy since 1844, was among the most celebrated artists in the empire.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-catholic: Catholicos Mkrtich Khrimian, patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church, walks the dusty road near the cathedral of Echmiadzin with Mount Ararat rising beyond. Aivazovsky, himself Armenian, painted the elderly Khrimian Hayrik in 1895 shortly after his election to the Catholicosate.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-chaos-18: An angel of God hovers in cruciform pose above the dark turbulent waters of creation, light tearing the cloud apart behind him. Aivazovsky painted Chaos in Rome in 1841, his early twenties; it earned him a gold medal from Pope Gregory XVI and now hangs at the Mechitarist monastery of San Lazzaro degli Armeni in Venice.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-gibralta: A three-masted ship runs under full sail through heavy swell at sunset, the Rock of Gibraltar rising in the haze behind a second vessel to the right; in the foreground a crowded open boat lifts on the crest of a turquoise wave. Aivazovsky, principal painter of the Russian Navy, painted the canvas in 1873, identifying the shipping in its title as American.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-look-to-: The Grand Cascade tumbles down its gilded terraces toward the Marine Canal at Peterhof, the Samson fountain throwing its jet high at the left while the long facade of the Great Palace stretches along the upper terrace; two strollers pause at the water's edge below. Aivazovsky painted the view in 1837, his final year as a student of the Imperial Academy of Arts in Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-passage-: The Israelites crowd the far shore as Moses, white-robed, raises his arm toward the sea closing over Pharaoh's army at the left, horses and spearmen vanishing beneath a great green wave while light breaks through the storm cloud above. Aivazovsky painted the biblical subject in 1891, bringing to it the marine effects of a half-century of seascape painting on the Black Sea coast.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-portret-: Anna Nikitichna Burnazyan-Sarkisova, the painter's second wife, gazes out from a semi-transparent veil that softens the dark ground behind her. Aivazovsky married Anna in 1882, nearly forty years his junior; the portrait hangs in the Aivazovsky Art Gallery in Feodosia, a rare exercise in formal portraiture from a painter best known for storms at sea.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-sea-coas: Moonlight breaks through heavy cloud over a quiet shore where a lighthouse rises above the rocks; a sailing vessel lies beached and heeled over at the right, a rowboat rests on the sand, and ships ride offshore in the silvery light. Aivazovsky painted the nocturne in 1837, the year he completed his studies at the Imperial Academy of Arts with a gold medal.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-self-por: Aivazovsky, in his late fifties and at the height of his European reputation, turns his head sharply to the side, his dark side-whiskers and formal dress set against a grey-green ground. He painted the self-portrait in 1874 for the Uffizi's collection of artists' self-portraits in Florence, following Orest Kiprensky as only the second Russian artist so honoured.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-view-of-: Caïques and sailing ships line the Bosphorus shore at sunset, the quay busy with figures beneath a domed mosque flanked by twin minarets, the city's skyline of masts and minarets dissolving into golden haze beyond. Aivazovsky painted the view in 1856, drawing on visits to Constantinople in the 1840s and 1850s that made the Bosphorus panorama one of his recurring subjects.
collection-of-beauty-akashi-strand-akash: A solitary pine bends over the moonlit waters of Akashi Bay as sailboats drift in the distance. Tsuchiya Kōitsu designed the print for the Watanabe Shin-hanga workshop, which carried the lyric landscape tradition of Hiroshige into the twentieth century.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1910: A woman sits with bowed head amid faceted planes of grey, green, and buff, her hands resting in her lap and one arm raised to the drapery behind her, a vase of phlox standing at the left. Gleizes showed the canvas in Room 41 of the 1911 Salon des Indépendants, the public debut of group Cubism, and again at the 1913 Armory Show. The oil, 81.6 by 100.2 cm, belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1911: The writer Jacques Nayral sits with legs crossed and an open book on his lap, his grey-suited figure set among the faceted foliage of Gleizes's garden at Courbevoie. The 161.9 by 114 cm canvas was shown at the 1911 Salon d'Automne and reproduced in Du Cubisme, the manifesto Gleizes wrote with Metzinger in 1912. Tate acquired the picture in 1979.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1912: Cubist footballers lunge across the canvas in a tangle of jersey stripes, limbs, and faceted ground plane. Oil on canvas, 225.4 x 183 cm, the work entered the National Gallery of Art in Washington as one of Gleizes's largest Salon-scale figure compositions of 1912-13.

Cubist bathers stand and recline along a river bank rendered as a shallow stage of interlocking planes. Oil on canvas, 105 x 171 cm, Les Baigneuses entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris after being shown at the 1912 Salon de la Section d'Or, the exhibition that defined the Puteaux group.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1913: A reclining figure in a straw hat is assembled from interlocking Cubist planes of ochre, brown, grey, and blue, with text fragments — including a reference to Alexandre Mercereau — embedded in the composition. Oil on canvas, 130 x 155.5 cm, the painting is held at the Albright-Knox Art Gallery, Buffalo, New York. Gleizes dated and signed the canvas in 1913.

The publisher Eugène Figuière sits behind a desk stacked with books and journals, surrounded by Cubist planes that name his most important authors. Oil on canvas, 143.5 x 101.5 cm, the portrait was painted to mark Figuière's publication of Gleizes and Metzinger's manifesto Du Cubisme in 1912; it hangs at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1914: Faceted planes assemble a dynamic standing figure in this Cubist portrait of the composer Florent Schmitt. Gleizes executed the work between 1914 and 1915 at 36 by 27 centimetres; the black-and-white photographic reproduction preserves a pastel that was inscribed to Josep Maria Junoy and published in the Catalan avant-garde review Troços.

A seated figure is fragmented into bold Cubist planes of green, blue, red, and ochre alongside animal forms — at least one cat-like creature is discernible in the lower composition. Gleizes finished the nearly two-metre canvas in February 1914; it is held at the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice. The title 'Woman with Animals' and the record dimensions (196.4 x 114.1 cm) are confirmed by the museum's own catalogue.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1915: A spare linear sketch of a standing figure — inscribed 'Pour J.M. Junoy, amicalement, Albert Gleizes, 1915' — serves as a preparatory study for a portrait of the poet Jean Cocteau. The work was published in Troços, the Catalan avant-garde review edited by Josep Maria Junoy, in its second series, no. 2, October 1917. Medium and dimensions are unrecorded; the work is known through its printed reproduction.

A Cubist musician holding a banjo occupies the centre of this square composition, surrounded by interlocking planes of ochre, red, yellow, grey, and black. Gleizes painted the work in 1915 on cardboard, 73 x 73 cm; it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York. The title links the composition to the jazz music that animated New York's avant-garde circles during the artist's wartime visits.

A returning poilu, rifle and pack flattened into Cubist scaffolding, appears in this wood engraving captioned 'Retour de Bois-le-Prêtre'. Gleizes contributed the print to issue 20 of Le Mot on 1 July 1915, the wartime Parisian weekly co-edited by Paul Iribe and Jean Cocteau, while the artist was himself serving at Toul.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1920: A seated figure is reduced to bold interlocking planes of orange, red, yellow, and black, the black glove of the title prominent against the warm ground. Painted in 1920 and measuring 126 by 100 centimetres, the canvas belongs to a private collection and is reproduced in the 1998 Gleizes catalogue raisonné. The work belongs to the post-war phase in which Gleizes reformulated Cubism into the rhythmic system later set out in his treatise La Peinture et ses lois.

Two Cubist figures — a woman and a child — are assembled from bold interlocking planes of red, orange, blue, yellow, and black. Published in 1921, the composition belongs to Gleizes's early-twenties efforts to integrate the figure into the rhythmic translation-rotation system he codified in La Peinture et ses lois. The work is reproduced in the 1998 Gleizes catalogue raisonné.

A Cubist composition of a mother and child built from interlocking curving planes, surviving only through a black-and-white photographic reproduction. The painting was shown at the Exposition Internationale d'Art Moderne in Geneva in the winter of 1920-21 as catalogue number 185; its dimensions and present location remain unknown.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-l-ho: A monumental Cubist figure dominates this tall, narrow canvas, the surrounding urban and industrial landscape dissolved into stacked facets of ochre, grey, and green. Oil on canvas, 195.6 x 114.9 cm, the painting entered the Philadelphia Museum of Art via the Louise and Walter Arensberg Collection. Gleizes painted L'Homme au Balcon in 1912, the same year it was exhibited at the Salon de la Section d'Or.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-port: Broad overlapping planes and intersecting diagonals reassemble a uniformed military doctor in this Cubist portrait. Gleizes painted the canvas between 1914 and 1915 while serving in the French army; it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York. The record title is Portrait of an Army Doctor (Portrait d'un médecin militaire).
collection-of-beauty-albinus-skeleton-w-: A plate from Bernhard Siegfried Albinus's Tables of the Skeleton and Muscles of the Human Body (1749), engraved by Jan Wandelaar. The skeleton is set in a poetic landscape with a rhinoceros, marrying anatomical exactitude to Enlightenment-era pictorial staging. The series was produced at the University of Leiden and was prized for the proportional rigour of its figures.
