Another plate from Albinus's Tabulae sceleti et musculorum, in which Wandelaar layers the superficial muscles over the skeleton in a posed standing figure. The series was prized for its proportional accuracy, achieved with grids and double-perspective drafting unusual for medical illustration of the period.
collection-of-beauty-albinus-tabulae-sce: An engraving from Tabulae sceleti et musculorum corporis humani (Tables of the Skeleton and Muscles of the Human Body, 1747), the anatomical atlas of the Leiden anatomist Bernhard Siegfried Albinus, with plates drawn and engraved by Jan Wandelaar. The second table presents a full-length male ecorche displaying the superficial layer of muscles, posed with one arm extended before a parkland backdrop where a big cat watches from behind a masonry wall; Wandelaar's pictorial settings were meant to lend the figures depth and life. This impression is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-altdorfer-: Commissioned by Duke William IV of Bavaria, Altdorfer compresses Alexander's 333 BC victory over Darius III into thousands of tiny figures swarming under a cosmic sky. The Danube School master treats landscape and weather as protagonists, the curving horizon and apocalyptic sun lifting the battle into world-historical drama.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-adam: Dürer's celebrated copperplate engraving applies the canon of human proportion he had absorbed from Jacopo de' Barbari in Nuremberg. Adam and Eve flank the Tree of Knowledge amid a forest stocked with elk, ox, rabbit, and cat — emblems of the four humours soon to be unbalanced by the Fall.

Two life-size oil panels showing the first humans isolated against black grounds, Dürer's first attempt to model nudes in the Italian manner after his second Venice trip. Each figure is treated as a study in idealized anatomy, paired across the diptych held by the Prado.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-barb: A charcoal portrait of the artist's mother drawn weeks before her death, capturing her gaunt cheekbones and sunken eye in unsparing detail. Dürer's inscription records her age and condition, turning the sheet into a private memorial as much as a likeness.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-der-: A watercolor and gouache study of a severed roller's wing, its ultramarine, turquoise, and rust feathers laid out with near-scientific precision. The sheet exemplifies Dürer's habit of treating natural specimens as objects of sustained, meditative observation.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-druc: The only surviving printing plate from Dürer's hand, preserved in the Bamberg State Library. It bears his 1515 composition of Christ praying on the Mount of Olives, an angel appearing above while the disciples sleep in the foreground.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-hare: A young hare crouches alert against a blank ground, its fur built up in fine watercolour and bodycolour strokes that distinguish guard hairs from softer underfur. Among the most exacting nature studies of the Northern Renaissance, the sheet even records the cross-barred reflection of a studio window in the animal's eye.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-head: A brush drawing heightened with white on prepared paper, recording a bearded man of ninety-three whom Dürer met in Antwerp during his Netherlandish journey. The head served as a study for his 1521 painting of Saint Jerome, and the sheet is held by the Albertina in Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-mele: An engraving from Dürer's so-called Master Prints in which a winged figure broods amid scattered tools of geometry, a polyhedron, and a magic square. The image has been read as an emblem of artistic genius stalled by melancholic temperament.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-pray: A brush study in white and grey on blue prepared paper, drawn as a detail for an apostle in the Heller Altarpiece. The folded hands have since detached from their context to become one of the most reproduced devotional images in Western art.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-selb: Painted shortly after his first Italian journey, the twenty-six-year-old Dürer presents himself as a gentleman scholar in tasselled cap and silk-trimmed jacket rather than a craftsman. The Alpine landscape glimpsed through the window signals his new cosmopolitan ambitions for the German artist.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-the-: A small woodcut from Dürer's Small Passion series, dated 1510 in the block, showing a sword-wielding angel driving the naked Adam and Eve out of Eden beneath the trees of Paradise. Densely cut parallel hatching gives the bodies sculptural weight at this modest scale. This impression is held by the National Gallery of Art.

Christ stands bound to a tall column in a vaulted hall while a crowd of tormentors presses in from every side, scourges raised; a small dog at the foot of the column underlines the casual cruelty of the scene. The woodcut belongs to Dürer's Large Passion, the ambitious series he began around 1496-97 and published as a book in 1511. The dense, swarming composition shows the young Dürer pushing the woodcut toward an expressive power the medium had never carried before.

The four horsemen of the Apocalypse ride down humanity in the most celebrated woodcut from Durer's Apocalypse series of 1498, illustrating the vision of Revelation 6. This impression is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

A watercolour and gouache study of a clump of meadow plants, dandelions and grasses, viewed at ground level with botanical exactitude. The work is a touchstone of Renaissance nature study and prefigures modern ecological imagery.

An early woodcut of six men relaxing around a Nuremberg bathhouse pump, several modelled on Dürer's friends and possibly himself. The crowded composition lets him show male anatomy from multiple angles in a vernacular setting.

A woodcut of an Indian rhinoceros gifted to King Manuel I of Portugal, drawn from a written description and a sketch since Dürer never saw the animal. He sheathes it in armour-like plates, an invented anatomy that dominated European imagery of the species for centuries.
collection-of-beauty-alexander-iii-recep: A wide-format Russian historical scene of Tsar Alexander III addressing village elders gathered in the Petrovsky Palace courtyard during his coronation. Repin orchestrates the crowd with his characteristic eye for individuated peasant types and ceremonial pomp.
collection-of-beauty-alexandra-and-elena: A double portrait of Grand Duchesses Alexandra and Elena Pavlovna, daughters of Paul I, painted soon after Vigée Le Brun's arrival at the Russian court in exile from revolutionary France. Soft pastel-like flesh and silvery silks display the courtly grace that made her Marie Antoinette's preferred portraitist.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1896-a: From the four-panel decorative series The Seasons, an allegorical figure reclines among grape vines, ripening clusters, and warm autumnal foliage, holding a shallow cup. The richly saturated ochre and burgundy palette and the sinuous interplay of figure and plant life are characteristic of Mucha's 1896 Seasons cycle.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1896-s: Part of Mucha's first Seasons cycle, the allegorical figure stands playing an ornate Art Nouveau harp amid flowering cherry blossoms, her auburn hair flowing freely. The pale, delicate palette and sinuous arabesque line are hallmarks of his early decorative work.

From the Seasons quartet, a languid woman wearing a poppy-blossom crown sits among summer vegetation near water, her bare feet resting at the water's edge. Mucha's warm, sun-bleached palette and the serpentine outlines of the figure and foliage give the composition its characteristic fin-de-siècle languor.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1896-w: Closing the 1896 Seasons set, a woman wrapped in a flowing teal-green cloak cradles small birds against her chest among snow-laden branches. The warm amber background contrasted with the cold white snowfall and her verdant wrap demonstrates Mucha's command of decorative colour in this lithographic series.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1898-d: Part of The Arts panel series, an entranced female personification swirls through flowing rose-pink drapery within a large circular medallion, flower petals drifting around her. Mucha treats movement itself as ornament, threading sinuous line through the figure in continuous arabesques characteristic of his 1898 decorative panels.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1898-t: From the four-panel Flowers series, a virginal figure rises among towering white lilies in a symmetrical decorative niche. Mucha equates the woman with the bloom, fusing botanical study and Art Nouveau allegory.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-the-mo: Titled 'Clair de Lune', this panel shows a partially draped woman standing before a crescent moon, wrapped in a dark star-strewn shawl and crowned with flowers, set within an elaborate floral border. Mucha works in a nocturnal, dream-laden register, with deep olive and gold tones enriching the atmospheric night scene.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-018: The Seine at Bougival, low banks and a pale sky reflected in still water. Sisley painted the riverside in 1876 during the years he worked the villages downstream of Paris, oil on canvas, the broken touch typical of his mature landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-020: Two haystacks stand in a stubble field at Moret under a wide sky, casting long shadows across the cut ground. Sisley painted the pair in 1895, working the thatch in broken strokes of gold and russet. The horizon sits low, giving most of the canvas to the changing light overhead.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-023: The cast-iron suspension bridge across the Seine at Villeneuve-la-Garenne, with a stone pier at its centre and rowing boats below. Sisley painted the span during a campaign in the Argenteuil district in 1872, oil on canvas, now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (gift of Mr. and Mrs. Henry Ittleson Jr., 1964).
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-038: The church of Notre-Dame at Moret-sur-Loing seen close up, its Gothic buttresses and stonework filling the upper canvas above a row of low houses. Sisley painted a series of views of the church between 1893 and 1894, varying the light across its west front. He worked the masonry in short strokes of cream, ochre and grey-blue.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-050: Sailing boats and spectators on the Thames at Molesey, bright bunting strung along the bank for the local regatta. Sisley painted the scene during a four-month stay in England in 1874, oil on canvas, bequeathed by Gustave Caillebotte and now in the Musée d'Orsay (R.F. 2787).
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-057: A still life of black grapes and walnuts spread on a white cloth, a knife laid across the table edge. Sisley rarely painted still life, making the 1876 canvas unusual in his output, which is dominated by river and village landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-062: Floodwater standing in the streets of Port-Marly, a wine merchant's house rising from the inundated quay with a rowing boat alongside. Sisley returned to the flooded village several times in 1876, producing a small series of canvases of the high Seine.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-064: The banks of the river Loing at Moret-sur-Loing, with low buildings and a stand of trees mirrored in the slow water. Sisley settled in the Moret district from 1880 and painted the Loing repeatedly until his death in 1899. The sky occupies the upper half of the canvas, worked in pale blue and grey above the green riverbank.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-065: The bank of the Seine under autumn foliage, reflections breaking across the water in short horizontal strokes. Sisley painted the riverside subject in 1876, oil on canvas, working in the loose touch he developed alongside Monet in the villages west of Paris.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-the-l: The Canal du Loing at Moret recedes between rows of bare poplars whose trunks are doubled in the still water. Oil on canvas of 1892, given to the Musée du Luxembourg by friends of the painter led by Claude Monet after his death and now in the Musée d'Orsay (INV 20723). Sisley kept to the canal's straight perspective lines through many canvases of the early 1890s.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-the-r: A road running past garden walls towards Hampton Court, figures walking under a high, clouded sky. Painted during Sisley's 1874 stay near London, when he produced a series of nearly twenty views of the non-tidal Thames, oil on canvas, now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-women: Figures on the main street of Marlotte, a village at the edge of the Fontainebleau forest, the women setting out to gather firewood. Oil on canvas, about 65 by 92 cm, painted in 1866. Sisley showed it at the Paris Salon that year, the first time the jury accepted his work.
collection-of-beauty-allee-de-chataignie: An avenue of chestnut trees in the woods at La Celle-Saint-Cloud, the path running back between heavy trunks toward a clearing. Among Sisley's earliest plein-air canvases, painted in the mid-1860s alongside Bazille in the same woods. Oil on canvas, in his pre-Impressionist Barbizon-inflected manner.
collection-of-beauty-allegory-of-paintin: In this Allegory of Painting attributed to Gerard van Honthorst (1648), a seated woman holds palette and brushes while painting a male portrait, a winged putto leaning over the canvas behind them. The controlled chiaroscuro and intimate grouping are characteristic of Honthorst's mature Dutch Baroque style.
collection-of-beauty-almina-daughter-of-: Almina Wertheimer is depicted seated in elaborate Oriental costume — an embroidered robe and feathered turban — resting a long-necked stringed instrument across her lap and gazing directly at the viewer. Painted in 1908, this is among the last of Sargent's celebrated series of Wertheimer family portraits, bequeathed to the British nation and now in Tate.
collection-of-beauty-along-the-river-dur: A Qing court reinterpretation of the celebrated Song handscroll documenting Qingming festivities along the Bian River. Shen Yuan, an academician under the Qianlong emperor, executes the panorama in fine ink line touched with sparing ochre washes.
collection-of-beauty-altaarstuk-van-het-: The altarpiece of the Antwerp joiners' guild, with the Lamentation at centre flanked by wing scenes of the martyrdoms of John the Baptist and John the Evangelist. Completed by Quinten Metsys in 1511 for the cathedral of Our Lady, the triptych is now held by the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp under inventory numbers 245-248.
collection-of-beauty-alte-nationalgaleri: Wilhelm Gentz's monumental oil on canvas, more than two and a half meters wide, records the entry of Crown Prince Friedrich Wilhelm of Prussia, the future Emperor Frederick III, into Jerusalem in November 1869, a visit made on his journey to the opening of the Suez Canal. The prince rides a white horse at the center of a teeming procession outside the city walls, surrounded by dignitaries, onlookers in Ottoman and Arab dress and waving palm fronds, with the domes of Jerusalem beyond. Gentz, a specialist in Orientalist subjects, completed the painting in 1876, when it was acquired by the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin.

Franz Kruger records a military parade held on Berlin's Opernplatz in 1822, with cavalry drawn up before the opera house and a dense crowd of recognisable Berliners given as much attention as the royal party, which includes Frederick William III of Prussia and the future Tsar Nicholas I. Commissioned by Nicholas, then Grand Duke of Russia, the monumental oil on canvas - roughly 2.5 by 3.7 metres - occupied the painter from 1824 to 1830. It entered the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin in 1928.
collection-of-beauty-amalia-van-solms-ge: This portrait from the workshop of Gerard van Honthorst (1650) depicts Amalia van Solms, widow of Frederick Henry of Orange-Nassau, at knee-length beside a draped curtain and column, an olive branch held in her lowered right hand. Painted as the pendant to her husband's posthumous portrait, the work is held in the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-ambroise-vollard-av: The dealer Ambroise Vollard wrapped in a red headscarf, the bare head and heavy features set against a warm ground. Renoir painted Vollard, who handled much of his work after 1900, in 1906; oil on canvas, now in the Petit Palais, Paris. The close-keyed reds and softened modelling are typical of the artist's late Cagnes years.
collection-of-beauty-ambrosius-and-hans-: Two boys share a single sheet drawn from life by their father: Ambrosius (left) and the young Hans Holbein the Elder's son, later Hans Holbein the Younger (right), with their names inscribed above each head. Executed in silverpoint on white-coated paper, 10.3 × 15.5 cm (1511), the study is preserved in the Kupferstichkabinett of the Berlin State Museums.
collection-of-beauty-amor-vincet-omnia: A naturalistic Cupid in the Berlin Gemäldegalerie, who clambers grinning over scattered emblems of music, war, science, and rule. Caravaggio's tenebrist lighting and the boy's frank nudity made the picture notorious among Roman collectors.
collection-of-beauty-amsterdam-musee-van: Painted during Monet's brief stay in the Dutch bulb fields near Sassenheim, this canvas spreads horizontal bands of red and yellow tulips before distant windmills. The high-keyed palette previews the saturated colour Monet would later push at Giverny.
collection-of-beauty-an-afternoon-stroll: Chase paints his wife and one of their children walking through the dunes at Shinnecock, Long Island, where he ran his summer school of plein-air painting. Loose, sun-bleached brushwork shows his absorption of French Impressionism into an American idiom.
collection-of-beauty-an-experiment-on-a-: A candle-lit demonstration of a vacuum pump, with a cockatoo gasping in its glass globe as a mixed audience reacts in awe, fascination, and dread. Wright transposes religious chiaroscuro onto the new theatre of Enlightenment science.
collection-of-beauty-anatomy-wellcome-l0: A full skeleton stands facing the viewer in a lush river landscape, left arm extended, while a winged putto hovers at its shoulder holding up a billowing drape. The 1747 etching follows the anatomical tables of Bernhard Siegfried Albinus, whose atlas famously set its specimens in living, pastoral scenery to give the bones scale and vitality; this plate was engraved for the English edition by Charles Grignion. The impression comes from the Wellcome Collection, London.

A skeleton seen from behind with the left arm extended, engraved by Gérard Jean-Baptiste Scotin after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Bernhard Siegfried Albinus's anatomical atlas. Albinus's plates, first published in Leiden in 1747, set a new standard of precision by posing the skeleton like a living figure within a measured grid. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.

A standing skeleton in side view with the left arm extended, engraved by Simon François Ravenet after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas of 1747. The plates combined exacting anatomical measurement with the poise of classical statuary, and were widely copied across Europe. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.

An écorché figure seen from the front, engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas. The grazing rhinoceros in the background is Clara, the celebrated Indian rhinoceros who toured Europe in the 1740s — Wandelaar sketched her in Leiden and used her to lend scale and life to the plates. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.

The companion écorché figure seen from behind, engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas, again with the rhinoceros Clara in the background. Pairing the flayed figure with the exotic animal made these among the most recognisable anatomical prints of the eighteenth century. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.
collection-of-beauty-anbetung-der-konige: Bruegel sets the Adoration of the Magi inside a snowbound Flemish village, the Holy Family barely visible amid the crowd, woodcutters, and falling flakes. Painted in oil on wood in 1567, it is among the earliest winter scenes in Western painting and now belongs to the Oskar Reinhart Foundation in Winterthur.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-as: The Virgin ascends on a bank of clouds, hands clasped in prayer, as putti attend her on either side. Below stand four saints — including a warrior saint and a Franciscan friar — set against a rocky Italian landscape. Andrea del Sarto painted this altarpiece in 1530 for the church at Poppi in Tuscany; it is now in the Galleria Palatina at the Palazzo Pitti, Florence.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-he: A young man's face is rendered in chalk on paper, his gaze directed forward and his curly hair loosely framing his features. The drawing, attributed to Andrea del Sarto and dated to around 1523, is now in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington, and exemplifies his sensitive handling of line and tone in preparatory work.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-pi: The dead Christ rests against the Virgin's lap, attended by Mary Magdalene, Saint Peter, Saint Paul and Saint Catherine in a tight pyramidal group. Painted between 1523 and 1524 for the convent of San Pietro a Luco in the Mugello, the altarpiece is now in the Palazzo Pitti in Florence.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-po: A young man in a black doublet turns toward the viewer with one hand resting on a parapet, his face emerging from a darkened ground. Andrea del Sarto painted the sitter around 1517, and the picture was long thought to be a self-portrait; Vasari wrote that had Andrea's spirit matched his judgement he would have been without equal among Florentine painters.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-mantegna-014: Saint Sebastian stands bound to a fragmented classical column, his body bristling with arrows against a ruined ancient cityscape. Mantegna fuses humanist antiquarianism with Christian martyrdom, a recurring preoccupation in his Mantuan years.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-mantegna-the: Christ's body is laid on a marble slab and seen in radical foreshortening from the soles of his pierced feet. Mantegna's hard, sculptural line and reduced palette turn the Lamentation into an exercise in perspectival shock.
collection-of-beauty-anisimov-alexander-: Alexander Ivanovich Anisimov is shown in close-up against a luminous Russian landscape with domed church spires, rivers, and autumn foliage — a backdrop characteristic of Kustodiev's outdoor portraits. Boris Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1915; Anisimov was a leading scholar of medieval Russian icon painting.
collection-of-beauty-ann-fairchild-bowle: Ann Fairchild Bowler, wife of Newport merchant and politician Metcalf Bowler, stands in a blue silk gown, her left hand resting on a birdcage and a fold of pink drapery over her other arm. Copley painted the portrait in 1758 during his early Boston practice; it is now in the Colby College Museum of Art, Waterville, Maine.
collection-of-beauty-anna-alexandrovna-g: Princess Anna Alexandrovna Galitzin, great-granddaughter of the Georgian monarch Vakhtang, is shown reclining on a green chaise longue in an orange-amber gown with a red feathered headdress and gold chains. Vigée Le Brun painted the portrait in 1797 during her Russian years, capturing the opulent informality fashionable in St Petersburg society at the close of the eighteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-anna-hillmayer-1829: Anna Hillmayer, daughter of a Munich game merchant, sat for this picture as part of Ludwig I's Gallery of Beauties. Stieler departs from aristocratic convention to record a tradesman's daughter with the same idealised serenity and porcelain finish he gave his royal sitters.
collection-of-beauty-anna-payne-cutts-by: Dolley Madison's younger sister Anna Payne Cutts, wife of Massachusetts congressman Richard Cutts, sits in a soft white gown against a neutral ground. Stuart painted her in Washington shortly after her marriage, working in the bust-length format he reserved for society wives of the early Republic.
collection-of-beauty-anne-de-cleves-hans: Anne of Cleves is shown frontally in a richly embroidered red and gold gown with layered jewelled chains and a rounded bonnet-style cap, her hands clasped low before her. Holbein painted the small panel in 1539 during his mission to the Continent to assess the Duke of Cleves's sister as a potential bride for Henry VIII; the portrait is now in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-c: An early devotional work from the Bolognese reformer of late-Mannerist painting, the composition tightens onto the suffering Christ as winged attendants steady his body. Carracci leans on the warm chiaroscuro and sculptural drapery he absorbed from Correggio and Venetian sources.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-p: The dead Christ slumps across the Virgin's lap as two grieving angels hold up his arm and a crown of thorns. Carracci's restrained classicism, Bolognese in its rigour, became a key model for seventeenth-century devotional painting.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-r: A wooded river scene in which large trees fill the foreground and a narrow stream winds toward a distant valley and pale hills. A lone figure pauses by the water's edge, dwarfed by the dense canopy. Carracci painted this ideal landscape around 1590, helping establish the classical tradition later developed by Poussin and Claude; the canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-s: The chaste Susanna recoils as two elders intrude on her bath, the biblical pretext for a study of startled flesh against shaded foliage. Carracci stages the assault with the firm contour and idealised anatomy he was simultaneously developing for the Farnese ceiling.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-t: Two aproned butchers work among hanging carcasses and joints of meat, one trimming a cut while the other hangs a side — a small canvas of the early 1580s, the more compact of Carracci's two butcher-shop pictures (the larger is at Christ Church, Oxford), now in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth. Carracci's interest in low-life genre, drawn from northern prints and direct observation, gives the scene an unusually frank realism for its date.
collection-of-beauty-anonymous-brustbild: A bust-length study of a young man, plainly dressed and turned slightly toward the viewer, kept in the Belvedere as part of the German Romantic holdings. Runge favoured this kind of clear, almost severe portrait pared back to face and gaze.
collection-of-beauty-anonymous-ten-thous: An eleven-metre handscroll on silk that travels the Yangtze from its mountain source to the sea, opening section by section in the hand of the viewer. Long attributed to the Southern Song master Xia Gui, it strings together mist, gorges, fishing villages and city walls in characteristic axe-cut brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-anthonis-van-dyck-0: The Genoese noblewoman descends a terrace beneath a parasol held by an African page, the pairing a familiar device in van Dyck's Italian portraits of patrician women. Crimson drapery, towering verticals and a reserved, columnar pose set the template for European court portraiture.

The wine-soaked Silenus, fleshy and unsteady, is supported by a rowdy Bacchic company of satyrs, a maenad, and cherubs bearing grapes. Painted around 1620, when the young van Dyck was absorbing Rubens's workshop practice, the canvas shares the older master's ruddy, full-bodied paint handling and preference for closely pressed, animated flesh. The work is held by the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-anthony-van-dyck-ma: Van Dyck's wife Mary Ruthven is shown in a rich blue satin gown with pearl necklace and gold hair ornament, posed with calm composure against a dark ground. The portrait, dated 1640, is unusually domestic in register for the painter, setting aside the aristocratic trappings of his formal commissions in favour of a quiet, personal likeness.
collection-of-beauty-anthony-van-dyck-ra: Rachel de Ruvigny, Countess of Southampton, is shown in blue and white satin drapery beside a large terrestrial globe, a skull resting at her feet in a Vanitas allusion to worldly transience. The full-length allegorical portrait, painted around 1640, is in the collection of the National Gallery of Victoria, Melbourne, and is among van Dyck's most ambitious English-period compositions.
collection-of-beauty-antoine-coypel-man-: Two nude figures — a reclining man and a woman leaning tenderly over him — are depicted in an amorous embrace in this chalk study, the transfer grid still visible across the sheet. Attributed to Antoine Coypel and dated around 1716, the drawing demonstrates the loose, animated draughtsmanship of his later career.
collection-of-beauty-antoine-coypel-self: Coypel turns toward the viewer in a large powdered wig and a voluminous dark velvet robe, holding an ornate bound volume — attributes befitting his role as First Painter to the King and director of the Académie royale. The self-portrait is dated 1715, seven years before his death in 1722.
collection-of-beauty-anton-van-dyck-anto: The Genoese patron Anton Giulio Brignole-Sale rides forward on a grey horse, raising his hat, beside a tall column draped in crimson — an assertive equestrian formula van Dyck adapted from Rubens and Titian. Painted in 1627 during the artist's Italian sojourn, the canvas remains in Genoa at the Palazzo Rosso.
collection-of-beauty-anton-van-dyck-sams: Delilah leans forward in shock as Philistine soldiers seize the shorn Samson from her lap, the moment of betrayal pitched between sensuality and violence. Van Dyck reworks Rubens's earlier composition with cooler colour and a more refined, elongated drawing.
collection-of-beauty-aphonse-mucha-rose-: A young woman in a cream gown is shown surrounded by and crowned with roses, her hair dressed with blossoms, within the vertical panel format characteristic of Mucha's decorative series. Part of the Flowers series of 1898, the design exemplifies the Art Nouveau idiom Mucha refined in Paris — sinuous line, stylised flora, and the fusion of figure and ornament.
collection-of-beauty-apocalypse-vasnetso: Conquest, War, Famine and Death ride through a turbulent sky above a landscape strewn with the fallen, the Lamb of God faintly visible in the upper register. Vasnetsov completed the oil in 1887, drawing on the Book of Revelation to produce one of the most vivid Russian Symbolist treatments of the Apocalypse theme.
collection-of-beauty-arabian-nights-3-by: An Armenian woman reclines in a sunlit Cairo interior, beside a latticed window and richly coloured carpets, in a scene identified by its full title as 'The Love Missive'. Lewis painted the work in 1855, drawing on the decade he had spent living in Cairo; the jewel-like handling of light across costume and tilework is characteristic of his mature watercolour and oil technique.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldo-air-copy: Birds of every order roost on and form a human profile, one of four allegories of the elements painted for the Habsburg court. Arcimboldo's composite portraits flatter the encyclopaedic ambitions of Maximilian II while showing off the painter's natural-history library.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldo-earth: A bust assembled from terrestrial mammals — stag, leopard, hare, sheep and many others — interlocks to form a human profile in Arcimboldo's allegorical conceit for Earth. Painted possibly in 1566, the composite portrait was part of a series on the four elements produced for the Habsburg court, in which the emperor's dominion is cast as a literal embodiment of the natural world.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldo-les-sais: A male head built from the harvest, with a pear nose, apple cheeks, a pomegranate chin and a crown of grapes and vine leaves bound by a barrel-stave neck. Part of the Seasons series Arcimboldo painted for the Habsburg court in 1573, the version at the Louvre carries the imperial monogram tying the cycle to Emperor Maximilian II.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldowater: A profile fashioned from fish, crustaceans, coral and pearls, completing the Vienna set of the four elements. Arcimboldo treats the composite as both witty courtly device and a serious display of zoological knowledge.
collection-of-beauty-arethusa-by-benjami: A nude nymph turns and looks back over her shoulder in a darkened woodland setting, red and white drapery falling around her as she appears to flee. The work, painted in 1802 and now at the High Museum of Art in Atlanta, depicts Arethusa from Ovid's Metamorphoses in the moment before her transformation. Benjamin West was then serving as President of the Royal Academy.
collection-of-beauty-argenteuil-a14692: A promenade of trees lines the right bank of the Seine at Argenteuil while two sailboats move on the open water in the distance and strollers walk in dappled afternoon light. Monet settled at Argenteuil after the Franco-Prussian War and made it the crucible of Impressionist landscape painting; this canvas, now at the National Gallery of Art, dates from around 1872.
collection-of-beauty-arnaut-and-his-dog-: An Arnaut warrior — Albanian soldiers who served in the Ottoman Egyptian army — reclines on cushions in a richly tiled interior and exhales pipe smoke toward the muzzle of a greyhound lying at his feet. The sourceDescription identifies the figure as fighting under Muhamed Ali, founder of modern Egypt. Gérôme, working in 1882 and employing his characteristic smooth enamel finish, treats the idle soldier with the zoological exactitude typical of his Orientalist studies.
collection-of-beauty-arsene-vigeant-john: Arsène Vigeant sits before a table, one hand resting on a closed book and his gaze directed at the viewer, while a sword stands in the background shadow to his left. Sargent painted the portrait in 1885, linking the fencing master's twin identities as swordsman and bibliographer of the sword. The work is now in the collection of the Metz museum.
collection-of-beauty-artemisia-gentilesc: Cleopatra lies fully reclined across rumpled white and crimson drapery, her eyes closed and one arm raised above her head, a small asp coiled at her wrist. The foreshortened nude composition is attributed to Artemisia Gentileschi, dated 1613 or 1621–1622, and belongs to her series of monumental heroines drawn from antiquity.

Danaë reclines across white and red drapery as a shower of gold falls from the dark upper field, while a servant in blue and white stands behind her holding a cloth. Attributed to Artemisia Gentileschi and dated to around 1612, the work applies Caravaggesque tenebrism to this Ovidian subject. The canvas, measuring approximately 53 by 41 cm, is a relatively intimate treatment of the theme.

Judith and her servant pause in Holofernes's tent, alerted by a sound outside; a single candle throws Judith's shielding hand into silhouette and glances off the discarded gauntlet. The Detroit canvas is among Artemisia's most theatrical exercises in Caravaggesque candle-light.

The Virgin, dressed in a rose-red gown, looks tenderly down at the active Christ Child seated in her lap, who turns toward her holding a small red fruit. Painted around 1609–1610 near the start of Artemisia Gentileschi's Roman career, the work is now in the Galleria Palatina, Florence, and shows her absorbing her father Orazio's cool, silvery palette within a spare Caravaggesque interior.

The penitent Magdalene twists in her chair, gold gown slipping, hand pressed to her breast in conversion. Artemisia gives the Counter-Reformation subject the muscular, psychologically charged female protagonist that is her hallmark.
collection-of-beauty-artlib-gallery-1387: An Orthodox priest holds a censer while a Russian military officer stands beside him on a vast autumnal steppe strewn with the bodies of fallen soldiers, a stormy sky filling most of the canvas. The work's Russian title — Побежденные. Панихида по убитым — translates as The Vanquished: Requiem for the Fallen, and the subtitle dates it to the 1877–1878 Russo-Turkish War. Vereshchagin made the war's human cost his sustained subject throughout this period.
collection-of-beauty-arundel-mill-and-ca: A water mill on the River Arun in the foreground, with Arundel Castle's keep rising through trees on the slope beyond. Constable spent the entire day of 31 March 1837 putting the last touches on the canvas and died unexpectedly that night; his friend C. R. Leslie sent it to the Royal Academy summer exhibition the following year as his final work.
collection-of-beauty-as-the-old-sing-so-: A multi-generational Flemish family bellows around a table while a child blows a pipe, illustrating the proverb inscribed at the top: as the old sing, so the young pipe. Jordaens returned to the boisterous moralised feast many times, this version inscribed Ut genus est genius.
collection-of-beauty-asakusa-honganji-te: The ornate roof of Asakusa Hongan-ji temple fills the right foreground while a kite and its airborne handler drift across the pale sky, with Mount Fuji visible in the distance. Plate four of Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (c. 1830) makes the sacred peak a small, constant presence glimpsed across the rooftops of Edo, held at the Chester Beatty Library.
collection-of-beauty-at-eternity-s-gate-: An old man sits on a plain chair, fists pressed to his eyes in a posture of complete despair. Van Gogh painted the canvas at Saint-Rémy in early May 1890, returning in oil to a lithograph he had made in The Hague in 1882 of the same model, the almshouse pensioner Adrianus Jacobus Zuyderland. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo.
collection-of-beauty-at-first-glance-he-: A glowering giant's face is, on closer look, made up entirely of squirming naked men — a sly anatomical pun on the proverb in the title. Kuniyoshi produced such jigsaw figures to slip past Tempō-era censorship that restricted depictions of named actors and courtesans.
collection-of-beauty-at-the-beer-garden-: Two men occupy the foreground of this small, densely observed beer-garden scene, surrounded by a press of figures whose hats, glasses, and animated faces Menzel records with characteristic exactitude. Painted in 1883, the canvas exemplifies the sharp, sketchbook-trained eye Menzel trained on the social spectacle of modern German urban life.
collection-of-beauty-at-the-stock-exchan: The banker Ernest May, top-hatted and pince-nez'd, listens to a colleague leaning over his shoulder while the trading floor blurs into faceless agitation behind them. Degas painted his collector and admirer in 1878,79, applying Edmond Duranty's call for portraits that read a sitter's profession in his bearing.
collection-of-beauty-at-volga-kustodiev: A woman in a white dress and a reclining man rest on a grassy bluff beside silver birch trees, gazing out over a broad, luminous river stretching to the horizon. Painted in 1922, the canvas belongs to Kustodiev's late series of provincial pastorals — warm, sunlit evocations of Russian riverside life rendered in his characteristic decorative palette.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-a-gi: A small girl in a blue dress and lace-trimmed pinafore stands on a garden path holding a watering can, flowers scattered at her feet. Renoir painted the figure in 1876, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington (Chester Dale Collection).
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-en-e: A dark-eyed young woman sits outdoors in a loose white blouse and striped skirt, her long dark hair pinned back, gazing calmly at the viewer against a lush green background. Painted in 1868 and now at the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin, the work casts Renoir's model Lise Tréhot as a summer bohémienne and retains a solidity of form that still recalls Courbet's influence.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-la-g: Bathers and rowboats cluster around the floating café on the Seine at Bougival, the spot where Renoir and Monet spent the summer of 1869 painting side by side. Broken touches of opaque colour on the water mark one of the foundational moments of Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-the-: A young woman stands on a rope swing in a garden talking with a man seen from behind, sunlight falling in patches of blue and rose through the leaves. Renoir painted it in the summer of 1876 in the gardens below the Moulin de la Galette, oil on canvas, now in the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-youn: Two girls in white and pink dresses lean over an upright piano, one seated and playing while the other follows the score. Renoir painted this version in 1892 as the first of his works acquired by the French state, placed in the Musée du Luxembourg and now in the Musée d'Orsay. He made several oil and drawn repetitions of the composition for dealers and collectors.
collection-of-beauty-augustins-le-christ: Rubens stages the Crucifixion with the two thieves flanking Christ, the muscular bodies twisting against a darkened sky in the dynamic Counter-Reformation idiom. Originally painted for a Flemish religious setting, the altarpiece deploys the diagonal energy and ruddy flesh tones characteristic of his Antwerp workshop, and now hangs in the Musée des Augustins in Toulouse.
collection-of-beauty-autoportrait-au-ber: The painter shown half-length in a soft beret and dark coat, turned slightly from the viewer with a guarded expression. Oil on canvas of about 1898 to 1900, in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. It is among the last of the roughly two dozen self-portraits Cézanne made across his career.
collection-of-beauty-autoportrait-au-tur: Rigaud, the great portraitist of Louis XIV's court, presents himself in an exotic turban, a studio prop conveying artistic vanity and learned cosmopolitanism. The lustrous fabrics and confident chiaroscuro foreshadow the polished grandeur he would soon bring to royal portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-autoportrait-avec-u: A bearded self-portrait set against a dull olive-green wallpaper whose pattern Cézanne echoes in the modelling of the head. Painted in Paris around 1880 to 1881, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery, London. The dome of the skull is built from short oblique patches of white, red and ochre, the ear and crown outlined in blue.
collection-of-beauty-ave-caesar-morituri: Jean-Leon Gerome's academic vision of the Roman arena shows gladiators saluting the emperor with the famous formula "Hail Caesar, those who are about to die salute you." The painting epitomizes the meticulous archaeological detail and theatrical staging of nineteenth-century French history painting.
collection-of-beauty-ayvaz-sredy-voln: Foaming swells crest under a torn, luminous sky in a wholly unpeopled marine. Aivazovsky painted Among the Waves in 1898 at the age of eighty-one, judging it the finest canvas of his late career; it remains in the gallery he founded at Feodosia in Crimea.
collection-of-beauty-ayvazovskiy-gayvazo: A full moon breaks through thin cloud above the Bosphorus, laying a path of light across the strait between anchored sailing ships. On the near shore a domed mosque flanked by slender minarets overlooks a quay where small figures gather by the water's edge. Aivazovsky painted this nocturne in 1894; it is held in the Tretyakov Gallery.

A rainbow arches above a shipwreck and lifeboat tossed in heavy seas, survivors pulling at the oars while the sky breaks open behind them. Painted in 1873 and now in the State Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas is one of Aivazovsky's signature meditations on rescue at sea, salvation hinging on a sliver of coloured light.
collection-of-beauty-ayvazovskiy-i-k-vol: Enormous grey-green waves tower over a stricken sailing ship in the centre of the canvas, its masts and red flag still visible as it is engulfed by the storm, while a lifeboat crowded with survivors struggles in the churning foreground. Aivazovsky painted this large and turbulent seascape in 1889, signing it in the lower right in his characteristic manner. The scale of the waves against the tiny vessel is a hallmark of the Russian marine painter's Romantic drama.
collection-of-beauty-b159-rembrandt: A rare still life from Rembrandt's etched oeuvre, depicting a single cone shell (Conus marmoreus) rendered with delicate cross-hatching and drypoint burr. The print attests to the Dutch fascination with exotic naturalia gathered through global trade.
collection-of-beauty-b320-rembrandt: Rembrandt depicts himself wide-eyed and open-mouthed in this tiny etching from 1630, one of a series of experimental self-portraits in which he pushed his own features into exaggerated expressions to study the physiognomy of emotion. The work, held at the Städel Museum, dates from his Leiden period and demonstrates the graphic virtuosity he was deploying as an advertisement of his skill.
collection-of-beauty-back-view-of-fuji-f: Hiroshige reverses the conventional southern view of Fuji, glimpsing the sacred peak from Kai Province on the mountain's far side. Part of his first Thirty-six Views series, the design uses graduated bokashi printing to layer mist, peak, and foreground.
collection-of-beauty-bad-war: Swiss pikemen and German Landsknechts press into the murderous close-quarters combat known as der schlimme Krieg, where the long pike shafts become unmanageable and halberds and short swords decide the outcome. This engraving by Hans Holbein the Younger, preserved in the Albertina in Vienna, is among the most visceral early sixteenth-century images of infantry battle.
collection-of-beauty-baglione: Baglione's allegory of Sacred and Profane Love, painted in 1602, sets a winged divine figure in armour above a reclining Eros who gazes upward in submission, while a crouching devil recoils at left. The composition directly rivals Caravaggio's treatment of the same subject and reflects the bitter professional rivalry between the two Roman painters in the early seventeenth century.
collection-of-beauty-baigneurs-a-asniere: Seurat's large-scale oil painting of 1884 shows a group of working-class men and boys resting and bathing on the grassy bank of the Seine at Asnières, with sailboats, a railway bridge, and factory chimneys visible across the water. Although Seurat had not yet fully developed his pointillist dot technique, the canvas displays the methodical colour application and monumental stillness that characterise his mature style. The work has been held in the National Gallery, London (NG3908) since 1924.
collection-of-beauty-bakst-self: A young Léon Bakst presents himself in three-quarter view against a neutral ground, the brushwork loose and the modelling kept to essentials. Painted in 1893, well before his Ballets Russes designs reshaped European stage costume, the self-portrait dates from Bakst's early years training in Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-bakst-uhzin1902: Bakst's 'Dinner' of 1902 shows an elegantly dressed woman in a black gown and wide-brimmed black hat seated at a white-clothed restaurant table, a bowl of oranges before her. The restrained palette and confidently simplified forms belong to his St Petersburg period, when he was closely associated with the World of Art circle in the years before his celebrated work for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes.
collection-of-beauty-baldassare-castigli: Raphael portrays his friend, the courtier and author of The Book of the Courtier, in a restrained palette of grey, black, and pearly white. The composed three-quarter pose and steady gaze became a touchstone for European court portraiture, admired and copied by Rembrandt and Rubens.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-apullia-i: An early classical landscape by J. M. W. Turner, exhibited at the British Institution and pointedly modelled on Claude Lorrain to challenge the older master's reputation. Sunlit foliage, distant temples and a literary Ovidian subject mark Turner's ambition to inherit the grand European pastoral tradition.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-lake-luce: A watercolour from Turner's late Swiss tours, when he returned repeatedly to Lake Lucerne in search of atmospheric subjects. From the heights above Brunnen the bay opens in pale washes of blue and pearl, mountains dissolving into the luminous haze that defined his final manner. The sheet belongs to a celebrated group of Swiss studies now held by Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-shipping-: A loose marine sketch from Turner's mature years, when his oils and watercolours of shipping abandoned topographic detail for weather and mood. Hulls and masts emerge from a smear of sea and sky, the kind of working study that fed his later exhibited storm and harbour pictures.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-story-of-: A late mythological landscape by Turner, the Ovidian chase staged across a golden Italianate valley bathed in the swirling light he had brought back from his Roman travels. Figures dwindle beside vast trees and rivers, drama dissolved into atmosphere in the manner of his ageing Claude homages.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-stromy-se: A late Turner oil sketch in which a burning ship is nearly engulfed by towering surf and smoke. Paint is scrubbed and scraped into vortices of orange and lead grey, rendering catastrophe as pure elemental force. The work belongs to the Tate Bequest of unfinished canvases that Turner left in his studio at his death.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-the-lake-: A small oil sketch from the series of sample studies Turner produced during his extended stays at Petworth House as guest of the 3rd Earl of Egremont. The lake dissolves into flat horizontal bands of pink, gold and lavender beneath a low sun, anticipating the radical atmospheric freedom of his late visionary landscapes. The study remained in Turner's studio and entered the Turner Bequest at Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-the-new-m: A small seaside scene from Turner's late period, where two children quarrel over a lost boat and a hoop on a wide tidal shore beneath a pale new moon. The trivial human anecdote is set against an expansive luminous sky and estuary, characteristic of Turner's mature handling of atmosphere and light. The work entered the national collection through the Turner Bequest and is held at Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-barrikade-in-der-br: Gaertner's 1848 painting records a barricade erected in the Breite Strasse in Berlin during the March revolution, a black-red-gold tricolour flag planted at its summit against the façade of a large urban building. Eduard Gaertner was Berlin's foremost topographical painter, and this work stands as one of the few contemporary pictorial records of the street fighting of 18–19 March 1848.
collection-of-beauty-bartlett-cabbage-ma: Bartlett's 1900 watercolour depicts a crowded provincial market square filled with vendors, buyers, and loaded carts, with heaped cabbages and other green vegetables dominating the foreground. The busy scene predates his celebrated shin-hanga print work by more than a decade and was sold at Bonhams Bond Street, London.
collection-of-beauty-bartolome-esteban-m: Murillo depicts Santa Rosa de Lima kneeling in the white habit and dark veil of a Dominican tertiary, extending her hands towards the Christ Child who sits beside a woven basket at her feet; scattered roses and a book complete the scene. Painted around 1670, the work displays the warm tonality and tender sentiment characteristic of Murillo's late religious compositions.
collection-of-beauty-bartolome-esteban-p: The Holy Family is arranged in an intimate domestic interior: the Christ Child reaches upward toward a small bird held or guided by the seated Joseph, while Mary looks on at the left, her spinning frame visible behind her. A small white dog sits at the foreground. The warm chiaroscuro and genre-inflected tenderness are characteristic of Murillo's Sevillian devotional paintings of around 1650, now in the Museo del Prado.
collection-of-beauty-bartolomeo-magagnos: A pencil head-and-shoulders study of Bartolomeo Magagnosco, inscribed Nice, January 1875, when Sargent was nineteen and travelling on the Riviera with his family. Now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the sheet shows the assured contour drawing that underpinned the oil portraits with which Sargent would debut at the Paris Salon two years later.
collection-of-beauty-bartolomeo-nazari-p: The celebrated castrato Carlo Broschi, known as Farinelli, stands in court dress with the score of an operatic aria in hand. Bartolomeo Nazari painted the oil on canvas in 1734, the year the singer arrived in London to join the Opera of the Nobility, the company set up in rivalry to Handel's. The portrait belongs to the Royal College of Music, London.
collection-of-beauty-bartolommeo-nazari-: A full-length standing portrait of an unidentified bewigged man in a grey coat, one hand resting on a cane and the other holding a tricorn hat, set against a plain dark ground with a glimpse of drapery at left. The work is attributed to the Venetian late-Baroque portraitist Bartolomeo Nazari and entered the Fogg Museum at Harvard under accession number 1943.116.
collection-of-beauty-basket-fishing-in-t: From the Oceans of Wisdom series on traditional fishing methods, Hokusai shows villagers wading the Kinu with woven basket traps. The flattened riverbank and tight figural grouping demonstrate his mature handling of genre subjects in the 1830s.
collection-of-beauty-bathsheba-c-1827-by: Hayez depicts Bathsheba seated nude at the edge of a stone pool, her body turned in three-quarter view as she glances back toward the viewer, a blue turban wound about her head and a white cloth draped across her lap. The cool, smooth modelling and classical clarity of form reflect the Italian Romantic painter's debt to academic tradition; the work dates to around 1827 and was sold at Christie's London in 2024.
collection-of-beauty-battle-of-revel: Aivazovsky depicts the naval engagement of May 1790 off Reval, with Russian and Swedish ships of the line exchanging fire amid billowing gunsmoke on a choppy green Baltic Sea, a town skyline faintly visible on the right horizon. Painted in 1846, the canvas is held in the Naval Museum of St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-battle-of-sinope: Aivazovsky shows the Russian attack on the Ottoman fleet at the harbour of Sinope, with burning ships flying Ottoman colours on the left and Russian men-of-war delivering broadsides through dense white smoke under a turbulent daytime sky. Painted in 1853, the year of the engagement, the work commemorates Admiral Nakhimov's victory at the opening of the Crimean War and is held at the Naval School in St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-battle-poitiers: Delacroix renders the Battle of Poitiers of 19 September 1356 as a Romantic mêlée of foot soldiers and cavalry, banners and lances clashing across a wide plain under a stormy sky. A prominent figure in white at the centre, identifiable as King John II of France, stands surrounded by English knights pressing in from all sides. The canvas, dated 1830, is in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-battle-scene-after-: Two dense formations of pike-armed infantry engage head-on in this sixteenth-century work after a design by Hans Holbein the Younger, the long shafts of the weapons forming a lattice across the picture plane. The composition descends from Holbein's Basel-period battle drawings and was likely made to serve as a model for decorative or print commissions. The work is dated to the sixteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-bauakademie-schinke: Eduard Gaertner records Schinkel's Bauakademie on the Spreeinsel in 1868, some three decades after the building's completion, its distinctive red terracotta façade filling the right half of the composition while a horse-drawn carriage and pedestrians animate the street below. A Gothic church tower rises beyond the building on the left. The Bauakademie was damaged in 1945 and subsequently demolished in 1962.
collection-of-beauty-bauernfeind-gustav-: Bauernfeind, the leading German Orientalist of his generation, records a crowded Jerusalem street where pilgrims and traders converge at the gates of Haram al-Sharif. His near-photographic precision rests on sketches gathered during repeated journeys to Palestine.
collection-of-beauty-bayron-s-visit-to-s: Aivazovsky depicts Lord Byron's celebrated visit to the Armenian Mekhitarist monastery on the island of San Lazzaro in the Venetian lagoon, showing Byron on the quayside gesturing toward a gondola while a group of robed monks stands behind him and the panorama of Venice stretches across the distant horizon. The scene is rendered with the luminous open-water treatment typical of Aivazovsky's late work; the painting dates to 1899.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-and-camille: Monet's plein-air study of 1865 shows Frédéric Bazille standing beside Camille Doncieux — Monet's own model and future wife — in a sun-dappled forest clearing, painted in preparation for the ambitious large-format Déjeuner sur l'herbe. The brisk, broken handling of light on foliage and costume anticipates the Impressionist technique Monet would develop in the following decade. The work is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington (inv. 1970.17.41).
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-ai: The medieval ramparts of Aigues-Mortes seen across flat marshland under a wide sky. Oil on canvas, 46 by 55 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille made several views of the walled Camargue town during a summer in the region.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-fl: A dense bouquet rising from a vase set on a console table, catalogued as Vase de fleurs sur une console. Oil on canvas, 130 by 97 cm, painted between 1867 and 1868 and now in the Musée de Grenoble.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-la: A seated nude attended by two servants, one kneeling to dry her foot, the other holding cloth, in a curtained interior. Oil on canvas, 130 by 128 cm, painted between December 1869 and March 1870 and now in the Musée Fabre, Montpellier.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-po: A standing portrait of Alphonse Tissié in the uniform of a cuirassier, his plumed helmet and breastplate set off against a plain ground. Oil on canvas by Bazille, held at the Musée Fabre in Montpellier.

Bazille's friend Edmond Maître seen in full profile, seated and reading a book in his lap, the ground darkening toward the upper left. Oil on canvas painted in 1869, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-su: Young men in swimming costume resting and wrestling along the wooded bank of the Lez near Montpellier. Bazille drew the figures in his Paris studio before placing them in the open-air setting; the oil was shown at the Salon of 1870 and is now in the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg).
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-vi: A young woman in a striped dress seated on a stone ledge above the village of Castelnau-le-Lez, the Hérault landscape spread behind her. Oil on canvas, painted in 1868 at the Bazille family property near Montpellier and now in the Musée Fabre.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-nature-mort: A dead heron and other birds laid on a table, a study in greys and browns. Oil on canvas, 98 by 78 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille painted it in a Paris studio alongside Sisley, who treated the same heron in his own canvas.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-pecheur-a-l: A nude male fisherman casting a circular throw-net at the water's edge, his back to the viewer. Bazille painted the canvas in 1868; it later entered the Rau Foundation for the Third World in Zurich, and stands among his experiments with the open-air male figure.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-sutdio-in-t: A corner of a sparsely furnished studio with two armchairs and a doorway opening onto a bedroom and a grey winter sky. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. The room is the studio at 6 Place de Furstenberg that Bazille shared with Monet, in the building that now houses the Musée national Eugène Delacroix.
collection-of-beauty-beardsley-peacocksk: Beardsley's ink and graphite drawing, made in 1894 as an illustration for Oscar Wilde's Salomé, shows Salome in a vast sweeping skirt patterned with peacock feather-eyes, facing a slender attendant in white. The extreme contrast of black silhouette against white ground and the integration of decorative Art Nouveau ornament with Japanese-influenced line exemplify Beardsley's graphic style. The original drawing is held in the Harvard Art Museums.
collection-of-beauty-bellini-madonna-and: Giovanni Bellini's Madonna and Child of around 1510 presents the Virgin in a blue mantle and rose dress, the infant Christ seated on her lap raising his right hand in a gesture of blessing, set before an open landscape with trees, hills, and scattered buildings. The intimate frontal composition and luminous palette reflect Bellini's late Venetian manner.
collection-of-beauty-bellini-madonna-mit: The Virgin holds the Christ Child in a half-length sacra conversazione, flanked by a long-haired John the Baptist on the left and an elderly Elizabeth on the right, set against a luminous blue sky. Signed 'IOANNES BELLINUS', the panel dates from between 1490 and 1500 and is held at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt.
collection-of-beauty-bellini-pieta-marti: The dead Christ lies in the arms of the grieving Virgin in a sunlit landscape, the two figures alone in a composition of extraordinary stillness and tenderness. Towns and a river wind through the hilly background. Known as the Pietà Martinengo, the work is attributed to Giovanni Bellini and is among the most celebrated of his devotional panels.
collection-of-beauty-bellows-cliffdwelle: Tenement crowds spill from fire escapes, stoops, and laundry-strung windows on a sweltering summer evening on Manhattan's Lower East Side. Painted in May 1913 and now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, the canvas belongs to Bellows's Ashcan record of immigrant New York.
collection-of-beauty-bemberg-fondation-t: Monet paints fishing boats hauled up beneath the chalk cliffs of Étretat, a Norman coast he returned to repeatedly in the 1880s. The pale beach and overcast sea are built from short, broken strokes that record shifting weather rather than narrative incident. The canvas now resides at the Bemberg Foundation in Toulouse.

A brooding early self-portrait showing the artist in three-quarter profile, his gaze cast slightly downward against a deep, almost black ground. Painted in 1860 or 1861 and now at the Fondation Bemberg in Toulouse, the work reflects Fantin-Latour's close study of seventeenth-century Dutch and Flemish portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-waterhouse: Benjamin Waterhouse sits three-quarter length before an open book, his right hand raised to his cheek in a pose of relaxed thoughtfulness. Stuart painted the portrait in 1775 and it is now held at the Redwood Library and Athenaeum in Newport, Rhode Island.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-005: British General James Wolfe lies dying among his officers on the Plains of Abraham after the 1759 capture of Quebec, a Mohawk scout watching at his side. West broke history-painting decorum by showing his subjects in contemporary uniform rather than classical dress, and the canvas at the National Gallery of Canada was widely copied in engraving.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-1738-: Edward III leads his army across the tidal ford at Blanchetaque in August 1346, mounted knights pressing forward as French defenders contest the far bank. Part of the Windsor history cycle commissioned by George III, West's canvas was painted in 1788 and is catalogued in the Royal Collection as RCIN 404566.

Edward III embraces his sixteen-year-old son the Black Prince on the field of Crecy in August 1346, French dead heaped at their feet. The 1788 canvas belongs to West's eight-picture chivalric cycle for the Audience Chamber at Windsor Castle, where it remains as RCIN 407523.

Double portrait of the future George IV in state robes alongside his younger brother Prince Frederick, later Duke of York, painted in 1777 for George III. West executed the canvas (RCIN 403399, Royal Collection) while serving as historical painter to the king, a post he had held since 1772.

Joseph Banks stands full-length in a Maori flax cloak, with a taiaha and other Polynesian objects arranged beside him, presenting the naturalist as the celebrated voyager he had become after Cook's first Pacific expedition. West painted the portrait between 1771 and 1772 in London; it is now in the collection of the Usher Gallery in Lincoln.

The six leading citizens of Calais approach Edward III bearing the city keys, as Queen Philippa intercedes on their behalf, the figures standing in a scene of formal submission. West's 1789 canvas illustrates the chronicle of Froissart and forms part of the Windsor history cycle for George III, catalogued in the Royal Collection as RCIN 404927.

The French knight Bayard, mortally wounded by an arquebus shot during the retreat from the Sesia in 1524, leans against a tree to receive the rites as his enemy the Constable de Bourbon kneels beside him. West painted the canvas in 1772 for George III; it remains in the Royal Collection.

The Roman consul Marcus Atilius Regulus tears himself from his wife and children to return to certain torture in Carthage, having kept his oath to the enemy. The first picture George III commissioned from West, RCIN 405416, established the painter's role as history painter to the King and now hangs in the Royal Collection.

Edward III invests the founding knights of the Order of the Garter in 1348, the Black Prince kneeling at the centre of a crowded hall hung with banners. West painted the picture for George III's Audience Chamber at Windsor as part of a chivalric history cycle; it remains in the Royal Collection as RCIN 407521.

The young Hannibal kneels at an altar before his father Hamilcar Barca, swearing the lifelong oath of enmity against Rome. Painted as a pendant to The Departure of Regulus for George III, RCIN 405417 in the Royal Collection, the picture pairs Carthaginian and Roman exemplars of stoic resolve.

Thusnelda, wife of the Cheruscan chief Arminius, stands captive with her son before the Roman general Germanicus after the campaigns of 15 AD. West painted the Tacitean episode in 1773 for George III as part of the Windsor history series, in oil on canvas. It remains in the Royal Collection.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-agrip: The widow Agrippina disembarks at the Italian port of Brundisium carrying the urn that holds her husband Germanicus's ashes, flanked by mourners and her children. Commissioned by Archbishop Robert Hay Drummond after a passage in Tacitus, the picture launched West's Neoclassical history practice in London and now hangs at Yale.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-alexa: Colin Fitzgerald seizes the stag by the antlers to protect King Alexander III, whose white horse rears at the left, while the hunt party scatters across a dramatic Highland landscape. Benjamin West painted the medieval Scottish episode in 1786 for Francis Humberston Mackenzie, who wished to honour his clan's legendary descent from Fitzgerald. The picture, known also as The Death of the Stag, applies the heroic compositional energy West had established in his earlier history paintings.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-by-gi: Benjamin West sits in three-quarter view, a quill and open books before him and a sketch or canvas visible behind, conveying his identity as a practitioner of the intellectual arts. Gilbert Stuart painted his teacher and patron around 1785, during the years Stuart spent under West's roof in London after arriving from America. The portrait is recorded in the collection of the Athenaeum.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-cleom: Leonidas II points his son-in-law Cleombrotus toward exile while the younger man's wife pleads at his feet with their children. West drew the episode from Plutarch's Life of Agis, treating Spartan civic duty in the friezelike arrangement that marked his Neoclassical history pictures of the late 1760s.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-cupid: Cupid enfolds the conscious Psyche in his winged embrace, both figures gazing at one another against an open, cloud-filled sky, while putti attend in the middle distance. West painted the canvas in 1808, during his presidency of the Royal Academy, drawing on the Apuleius myth for one of his late mythological commissions. The work is now in the collection of Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-danie: Daniel gestures emphatically as he interprets the divine writing to Belshazzar, the Babylonian king, who recoils on his throne amid alarmed courtiers; a scroll bearing the inscription is displayed at the left. West painted the canvas in oil on canvas in 1775, drawing on the Book of Daniel for an early biblical history. The Saint Louis Art Museum acquired the work in 2018.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-engli: Benjamin Franklin sits on a cloud, surrounded by putti operating the kite-and-key apparatus of his 1752 lightning experiment, while a thunderhead breaks overhead. West painted the apotheosis around 1816 in London, knowingly framing his late countryman as a deified Promethean figure in the manner of Rubens or Reni.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-gentl: A group of gentlemen fish from a flat-bottomed boat moored against a dense reed bank, with ships and a distant tower visible on the horizon under a partly cloudy sky. West painted the small cabinet picture in 1794, a rare excursion into the genre of sporting and leisure scenes away from his grand-manner history practice. The signature and date appear at lower left.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-helen: A seated Paris gazes toward Helen, who is presented to him by a winged Cupid and a second female figure — likely Venus — against a luminous sky with a red curtain at the left. West painted the Homeric subject in 1776, during his tenure as historical painter to George III. No institutional credit is confirmed in the available record.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-isaac: Abraham's servant Eliezer fastens the gold bracelet on Rebecca's wrist at the well, marking her as the chosen bride for Isaac. West painted the Genesis episode in 1775 in oil on canvas. The composition belongs to a series of Old Testament subjects he produced for English patrons in the 1770s.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-john-: Lawyer John Eardley Wilmot sits at a writing desk, a quill in hand and an allegorical group of dispossessed American Loyalists behind him on the wall. West painted the 1812 canvas as a homage to Wilmot, who had chaired the British commission that compensated refugees from the Revolution, the picture-within-a-picture summarising the sitter's public service.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-king-: Lear rages bareheaded on the heath as the Fool and disguised Edgar shelter against a wind-torn hovel, the storm tearing across a black sky. Painted in 1788 for John Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, West's canvas illustrates Act III, scene 4; it now belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-maria: Maria Hamilton Beckford sits in a blue gown, a guitar and an open book of music in her lap, with a classical column, a floral arrangement, and a country house in a landscaped park visible behind her. Benjamin West painted the portrait in 1799 and it is now in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The guitar and open score identify the sitter as an accomplished musician.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-mary-: Mary Hopkinson sits in a pink silk dress against a dark curtained ground, holding a lute in her right hand and glancing toward the viewer. West painted this three-quarter-length portrait in 1764, shortly after settling in London, and it entered the Smithsonian American Art Museum (accession 1926.6.1).
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-milkm: Milkmaids sell pails of fresh milk to passers-by in the open ground of St James's Park, the towers of Westminster Abbey rising in the haze beyond. West painted the London genre scene in 1801, now at the Yale Center for British Art, joining royal pastoral subjects with a documentary view of city trade.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-omnia: A winged Eros stands triumphant amid clouds, holding a flaming torch and a leash that subdues a lion reclining at his feet, while Venus with a flaming sceptre, putti, and a dark horse attended by further putti fill the allegorical scene. West signed the canvas in 1809, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (accession 95.22.1), as one of his late London allegories illustrating Virgil's phrase that love conquers all.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-pylad: Pylades and Orestes stand bound before the priestess Iphigenia at the altar of Diana at Tauris, the moment before she recognises Orestes as her brother. Painted by West in 1766 from Euripides, the canvas was a key statement of the new neoclassical history painting and is held by Tate.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-self-: Benjamin West portrays himself in old age wearing a red cloak and black top hat, leaning over a table with a pen in hand. Painted in 1819, the year before his death, it records the American-born artist who succeeded Joshua Reynolds as President of the Royal Academy in 1792 and held the post until the end of his life.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-the-b: Admiral George Rooke stands sword aloft in a boat amid the wreckage of the French fleet during the 1692 engagement off La Hogue, with the Soleil Royal running aground in the distance. West began this version in 1778, then his pupil John Trumbull completed it in 1785 and West retouched it in 1806, now at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-the-d: The scene shows William Pitt the Elder, Earl of Chatham, collapsing among peers in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778 after speaking against the surrender of the American colonies. West, history painter to George III, painted this version of the subject in 1778; the more celebrated rendering of the scene was ultimately executed by his contemporary John Singleton Copley.

Vice-Admiral Nelson collapses on the quarterdeck of HMS Victory at Trafalgar, surrounded by officers and ratings in a tightly compressed crowd. West composed the 1806 canvas, now at the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool, in deliberate echo of his own Death of General Wolfe, applying his epic modern-history formula to a second imperial martyr.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-venus: Venus stands upright on swans amid waves while two female figures above her hold billowing drapery, and a winged putto hovers to one side. The work belongs to West's late mythological output and is recorded through a Sotheby's auction catalogue; no firm date or medium is established in available sources.
collection-of-beauty-besneeuwde-ochtend-: Hokusai's woodblock print shows a snow-covered tea-house pavilion in the Koishikawa district of Edo, with visitors sheltering inside as Mount Fuji rises beneath a clear blue sky on a winter morning. Scene 11 of his celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji (c. 1830–35), the print is held at the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (AK-MAK-1588).
collection-of-beauty-bewening-van-christ: The dead Christ lies stretched out on a white shroud over blue drapery, his head fallen back toward the Virgin, who throws her arms wide in grief while Saint John and weeping angels gather around the body beneath a darkened sky. Anthony van Dyck painted this horizontal Lamentation in oil on canvas around 1635, after his return to Antwerp from England. It hangs in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), inventory number 404.
collection-of-beauty-bibliotekarien-kons: Arcimboldo's composite portrait assembles a human bust entirely from stacked and open books: an open volume with fanned pages forms the top of the head, volumes of varying sizes build the face and torso, and loose bookmarks suggest beard and fingers. Painted in 1562 and now at Skokloster Castle, Sweden, the panel is traditionally identified as a satirical likeness of the Habsburg court scholar Wolfgang Lazius, made for the court of Maximilian II.
collection-of-beauty-blaas-eugen-die-was: The Italian-Austrian painter de Blaas specialised in genteel scenes of Venetian life, here a young woman pausing with her copper water vessel. His glossy academic finish made such picturesque subjects popular with late-nineteenth-century international collectors.
collection-of-beauty-blaas-eugen-von-an-: A young Venetian woman pauses over the white linen piled in her lap, laughing and gesturing mid-conversation toward someone beyond the edge of the picture — the interesting story of the title. Her red kerchief, coral necklace, and yellow skirt supply the bright local color that made de Blaas's scenes of Venetian working girls hugely popular with collectors. The oil painting is a characteristic example of the genre subjects he produced in Venice through the late nineteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-blauwe-irissen-rp-p: Ohara Koson's woodblock print presents three large dark-blue irises with slender green leaves rising against a pale ground, the blooms rendered with bold flat colour and fine detail. The print was made in Tokyo between 1900 and 1930 and is held at the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (RP-P-1999-419), donated by J. Perrée of Eindhoven.
collection-of-beauty-bodhidharmayoshitos: Yoshitoshi depicts the Zen patriarch Bodhidharma wrapped in a red robe, seated on rocks beneath a full moon amid autumn foliage, his fierce gaze fixed outward. Published in 1887 as part of the series One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, the woodblock print exemplifies Yoshitoshi's expressive naturalistic shading and is one of the defining works of late-nineteenth-century Japanese printmaking.
collection-of-beauty-bogatyy-kirgizskiy-: A wealthy Kyrgyz hunter on horseback with a hooded falcon on his gloved fist, dressed in a heavy embroidered robe. Vereshchagin painted the subject in 1871 from observations made on his Central Asian travels for the Turkestan series.
collection-of-beauty-boilly-incroyable-p: An 'incroyable', one of the foppish young men of the post-Revolutionary Directory, shown in exaggerated dress with cravat and high collar. Oil on canvas in a private collection, painted in 1797. Boilly satirised the muscadin fashions then on display along the Parisian boulevards.
collection-of-beauty-boilly-louis-leopol: A sleeping woman waking in disarranged bedclothes, the subject of Boilly's 'Le Doux Réveil' (The Gentle Awakening). Oil on canvas, catalogued J 7 in the Musée Cognacq-Jay, Paris. The boudoir scene is one of the lightly erotic interiors Boilly produced in the 1790s.
collection-of-beauty-bonneville-savoy-by: An Alpine view from Turner's first Continental tour following the Peace of Amiens, recording the town of Bonneville against the Mont Blanc range. The classical compositional structure recalls Claude Lorrain, whom Turner studied closely as a young Royal Academician.
