collection-of-beauty-boris-kustodiev-por: The bass Fyodor Chaliapin in a long fur coat stands on a hillside above a winter fairground, with sledges, posters, and onion-domed churches spread out below. Painted in 1922 and now divided between versions at the Russian Museum and the Theatre Museum in Saint Petersburg, the picture frames the singer against the same provincial holiday world Kustodiev had been imagining throughout his late career.
collection-of-beauty-boris-kustodiev-sel: Kustodiev portrays himself as a young man in a flat cap and light outdoor coat, holding a palette and brushes before an open rural landscape of golden fields and fir trees. Painted in 1905 and titled Self-Portrait (On the Hunt), the canvas is held at the State Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-boris-kustodiev-shr: Snow-blanketed Russian rooftops, blue-domed churches and frost-white birches frame troikas and revellers celebrating Maslenitsa beneath a luminous pink and green sky. Kustodiev painted this 1916 canvas from his wheelchair following spinal surgery, drawing on the bold, flat colour of the lubok print tradition.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-04-louvr: Botticelli treats the popular Florentine subject of the infant Christ greeted by the young John the Baptist, a tondo-like intimacy enclosed within a vertical panel. The crisp contour drawing and Mary's downcast features are hallmarks of his Quattrocento workshop.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-a-virgem: The Madonna stands holding the Christ Child while a kneeling angel in a blue robe looks up in adoration, a composition typical of Botticelli's early years in the orbit of Filippo Lippi. The soft modelling and delicate linearity announce the Florentine grace of his mature style. The panel, dated 1465, is held at the Musée Fesch in Ajaccio.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-allegori: A standing female personification of Abundance is accompanied by children carrying and clutching bunches of fruit and grapes, executed in pen, ink and chalk on tinted paper. Datable to between 1480 and 1485, the sheet is one of Botticelli's most finished surviving drawings and is held in the British Museum.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-annuncia: Gabriel kneels before a swaying Virgin whose body bends in a pronounced S-curve, the two figures separated by an opening onto a Tuscan landscape. Botticelli painted the panel for the Cestello convent in Florence between 1489 and 1490; the bold red-and-white tiled floor grounds the composition in his late, austere manner.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-incorona: A predella scene from the San Marco altarpiece, showing John the Evangelist receiving his vision on the rocky island of Patmos. The miniature format allowed Botticelli's workshop to compress dramatic landscape and visionary light into a narrow horizontal panel.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-prado-49: The third panel of Botticelli's Story of Nastagio degli Onesti depicts the crucial banquet scene: an armoured horseman on a white horse bursts in among shocked guests at an outdoor table as hounds pursue a fleeing nude woman, the ghostly vision appearing before the assembled company. The courtly pageantry of the feast, richly dressed figures, and open pine-grove setting reflect the refined humanist taste of the Florentine commission.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-leda-lacma: Two nude women are seated together in a wooded landscape, one gesturing outward while the other inclines toward the swan at her side, in Boucher's characteristically pale, warm palette of peach and ivory. The 1742 canvas, now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, treats the myth with the playful sensuality typical of his Rococo mythologies.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-marquise-de: Madame de Pompadour reclines in an elaborate teal silk gown embroidered with floral motifs, holding an open book, surrounded by further volumes and writing implements that signal her role as intellectual patron. Signed and dated 1756 and now in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich, the full-length portrait presents Louis XV's official mistress as an educated champion of the Enlightenment.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-par-gustav-: Gustaf Lundberg portrays François Boucher in a three-quarter turn, wearing a grey coat with lace jabot and a powdered wig, against a neutral ground. Presented as Lundberg's reception piece to the Académie royale de peinture on 28 January 1741, the pastel secured his admission as an academician.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-vulcan-pres: In this large 1757 mythological canvas, Vulcan presents Venus with armour he has forged for her son Aeneas, after the eighth book of the Aeneid; the muscular smith god reclines at lower right amid weapons and tools while Venus and attendant figures fill the luminous centre. Boucher deploys his characteristic theatrical clouds, cupids and warm flesh tones across the ambitious composition.
collection-of-beauty-bouquet-of-mallows: Pink and lilac mallows fill a dark vase set on a pale surface, recorded in the rapid, comma-like brushwork Monet developed during his Vétheuil years around 1880. The loose, broken surface anticipates the enveloping all-over touch of his later garden paintings.
collection-of-beauty-boy-skifov-so-slavy: Mounted warriors locked in combat, lances raised and horses entangled across the steppe. Vasnetsov painted this Battle of the Slavs and Scythians in 1881, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. The subject draws on the Primary Chronicle and the artist's interest in early Russian legend.
collection-of-beauty-boy-with-a-basket-o: An early Roman work made soon after Caravaggio entered the household of Cardinal del Monte, the youth offers a basket spilling with grapes, peaches, and figs. The naturalistic still life, with its bruised leaves and worm-eaten apples, helped found a new Italian tradition of painting fruit from life.
collection-of-beauty-boys-in-a-dory-met-: Four boys in straw hats drift in a flat-bottomed dory on still harbor water, one perched on the bow with bare legs dangling, while schooners ride at anchor in the haze beyond. Homer painted the sheet in watercolor and gouache during the summer of 1873 at Gloucester, Massachusetts — his first sustained campaign in the medium that would become central to his art. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-brjullov: Bryullov turns to face the viewer in a dark coat, his arm resting against a red cushioned support, the pallor of illness evident in his gaunt features. He painted this self-portrait in Rome in 1848 during convalescence, and it now hangs in the State Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-brjullov-italianski: A young Italian woman reaches into a sun-shot vine to pluck a heavy cluster of grapes, her white blouse loosened in the midday heat. Painted in 1827 during Bryullov's residency in Italy on a stipend from the Society for the Encouragement of Artists, the picture now belongs to the State Russian Museum.
collection-of-beauty-brjullov-italiansko: A young woman bathes her face at a stone fountain in dappled morning light. Bryullov painted the canvas in Rome in 1823 as part of his pensioner programme for the Society for the Encouragement of the Arts, who sent it to Tsar Alexander I; it remains one of his earliest Italian successes.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-jun: A sunlit summer landscape opens across a broad meadow, a shallow stream catching the light in the foreground and tall trees casting deep shadow across the grass. Inness signed and dated the canvas 1882, and it entered the collection of the Brooklyn Museum. The freely handled atmosphere and Barbizon-inflected tonality are characteristic of his mature American manner.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-sno: Three figures in richly patterned kimonos dance or move through a snow-covered landscape beneath flowering plum branches, their overlapping forms conveying animated motion. The woodblock print is a product of the Utagawa school and carries the seal of Kunisada (Utagawa Toyokuni III), held today in the Brooklyn Museum. The densely printed textile patterns and speckled snow ground demonstrate the expanded colour range available to nineteenth-century Edo publishers.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-stu: Chase, the leading American Impressionist teacher, captures a young model in a borrowed kimono with rapid, fluid brushwork. Such japoniste studio subjects were fashionable in Gilded Age New York and reveal his admiration for Whistler and Sargent.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-sun: Crashing surf dominates the foreground under a stormy amber sky, the setting sun glowing orange through heavy cloud on the horizon. Inness painted this energetic marine in 1887 and the canvas is now in the collection of the Brooklyn Museum. The warm, suffused light and loosely worked surface show his characteristic merging of atmospheric luminism with expressive handling.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-tab: A wooden onsen inn sits in darkness under a driving rain, its windows glowing amber against the surrounding mountains and deep blue-black sky. This print is from Hasui's first Souvenirs of Travel series (1919), depicting the Tsuta hot spring in the Mutsu region, published with Watanabe Shozaburo as part of the shin-hanga landscape revival. The nocturnal palette of dark indigo and warm light exemplifies Hasui's atmospheric range.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-wil: The Philadelphia sculptor William Rush works at his studio bench, carving an allegorical female figure of the Schuylkill River from a wooden block while the nude model stands posed nearby. Eakins returned to the 1877 composition in 1908, the only subject he is known to have reworked in his career. The canvas is in the Brooklyn Museum.
collection-of-beauty-brullovkp-osadapsko: Russian defenders led by clergy carrying Orthodox icons and banners surge against armoured Polish-Lithuanian troops in this monumental depiction of Stefan Batory's 1581 siege of Pskov. The canvas, dated 1843 in the catalogue record, was left unfinished at Bryullov's death and represents one of his most ambitious historical compositions. The confrontation of faith and force — priests and banners on one side, helmeted soldiers on the other — charges the scene with dramatic tension.
collection-of-beauty-bruni-christ: The head of Christ crowned with thorns is presented within a circular format, the face bowed and eyes downcast in meditative sorrow, long hair and beard rendered with fine linear precision. The monochrome tonal modelling places the work in the Russian academic graphic tradition; it is catalogued in "Русская графика от А до Я" (Moscow, 2002). Fyodor Bruni was a leading figure at the Imperial Academy of Arts in St Petersburg, where he held the chair of historical painting.
collection-of-beauty-bruni-f-a-bogomater: The Virgin holds the Christ Child against a darkened ground, the academic Madonna type Bruni returned to across his career. He painted this oil in 1858, in the years when he directed the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery in St Petersburg.

The young Mary stands by a low stone wall, the Christ Child against her, roses banked behind them. Bruni painted this oil, 'Madonna with Child in Roses', in 1843; it measures roughly 64 by 40 cm and is held in the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-bruni-f-a-golova-ma: A close head study of the Virgin, her face inclined and eyes lowered, isolated against a plain ground. Bruni, who served as curator of the Imperial Hermitage picture gallery from 1849, worked the academic Madonna type throughout these decades; the study is dated to the second half of the 1830s into the 1840s and is held in the Hermitage, St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-buddiyskiy-khram-v-: A Buddhist temple at Darjeeling in the eastern Himalayas, its painted woodwork and prayer banners set against the mountains. Vereshchagin made the study during his Indian journey of 1874 to 1876, one of roughly 150 sketches from the trip, oil on canvas in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-bust-of-pseudo-sene: Rubens drew this gaunt, furrowed head from the famous Hellenistic bust then believed to portray the Stoic philosopher Seneca — an identification since abandoned, hence 'Pseudo-Seneca.' The sheet is worked in pen and brown ink over black chalk, heightened with white and gray wash, with the searching intensity Rubens reserved for his studies after antique sculpture. He owned a version of the bust himself and reused the head in paintings such as The Death of Seneca; the drawing is now in the Robert Lehman Collection at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-byam-shaw-omphale-1: The Lydian queen Omphale stands nearly nude, draped only in the lion skin of Hercules which she wears as a hood, holding his club and displaying the amber necklace and blue bracelet that mark her royal status. Behind her an ornate roundel of mythological figures provides a decorative backdrop in the manner of John Byam Liston Shaw's late Pre-Raphaelite idiom. Dated 1914, the vertical canvas treats the mythological role-reversal — Hercules served Omphale as penance for murder — with full-length figural command.
collection-of-beauty-ca-rezzonico-matrim: The Christ Child, seated on the Virgin's lap, reaches toward Saint Catherine in the traditional gesture of the Mystic Marriage, while an elderly bearded male figure — likely Saint Joseph — attends on the right. The panel is attributed to the Bolognese painter Biagio Pupini, called Dalle Lame, and dated circa 1530–1540; it is held at the Ca' Rezzonico in Venice under inventory number 236. The Raphaelesque grace of the figures reflects the influence of the Roman manner on Bolognese painting of the period.
collection-of-beauty-caillebotte-gustave: A nude woman reclines at full length on a cushioned divan, one arm raised behind her head, her body rendered with candid, almost photographic directness against crumpled silken bedding. Caillebotte painted this canvas in 1873, and the work exemplifies the unsentimental scrutiny he brought to the female nude in contrast to the academic tradition of idealized form. The freely handled fabric and warm tonal palette place it securely within his early Impressionist manner.
collection-of-beauty-caillebotte-l-homme: A top-hatted figure stands on a wrought-iron balcony overlooking one of Haussmann's new Paris boulevards, his back to the viewer as he surveys the street below. Caillebotte painted the canvas in 1880, repeatedly using the high vantage point of the Parisian balcony to explore the detached gaze of the modern urban observer. The bold compositional cut, with the figure isolated against the receding avenue, is characteristic of his Impressionist manner.
collection-of-beauty-campo-de-trigo: A field of standing wheat under a broad sky, the grain laid in with quick yellow and green strokes and no incident to interrupt the view. Renoir painted the landscape in 1879, probably near Wargemont on the Bérard family estate in Normandy; it belongs to the Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection in Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-canestra-di-frutta-: A wicker basket of grapes, figs, peaches and a withered apple sits at eye level on a bare ledge, projecting slightly into the viewer's space. Often cited as the first autonomous still life in Italian painting, the work is unsparing about wormholes and decay; its plain ground is a later overpaint.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-i-musici: Four young musicians, one tuning a lute, prepare to perform in a tightly packed half-length composition. Commissioned by Cardinal Francesco Maria del Monte for his Roman household, the picture launched Caravaggio's career and introduced his trademark modelling of flesh against deep shadow.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-judith-b: The Hebrew widow grips the Assyrian general's hair and saws through his neck while her aged maid waits with a sack. Caravaggio renders the ugly mechanics of beheading with forensic clarity, the spurting blood lit as starkly as the white sheets.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-la-depos: Christ's lifeless body is lowered onto the anointing stone, his arm and shroud dropping toward the viewer. Painted for the Chiesa Nuova in Rome, the altarpiece compresses the mourners into a powerful diagonal lit by Caravaggio's signature raking shaft.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-medusa-g: The Gorgon's severed head shrieks the instant of decapitation, her snakes still writhing. Painted on a convex tournament shield as a gift from Cardinal del Monte to the Grand Duke of Tuscany, the work conflates mirror, weapon, and self-portrait.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-sette-op: All seven corporal acts of mercy, from burying the dead to Roman Charity, unfold in a single torch-lit Neapolitan alley. Painted for the Pio Monte della Misericordia, the altarpiece set the template for Neapolitan tenebrism that Ribera and the Caravaggisti would extend.
collection-of-beauty-cardinal-fernando-n: Cardinal Fernando Niño de Guevara sits in an ornate chair, his scarlet robes spread across the canvas against a gold-patterned tapestry backdrop, a pair of round spectacles resting on his nose. Painted around 1600 by El Greco, the portrait records the Grand Inquisitor of Spain and stands among the artist's most commanding ecclesiastical likenesses.
collection-of-beauty-carl-friedrich-seif: Sunlight refracted through the submerged entrance of Capri's Grotta Azzurra fills the cavern with the cobalt glow that made it a Grand Tour pilgrimage site. The picture is in fact by Berlin landscapist Carl Friedrich Seiffert, who specialised in luminous Italian veduta.
collection-of-beauty-carl-joseph-begas-f: A half-length portrait of Wilhelmine Begas, wife of the painter Carl Joseph Begas, dated 1828. The sitter gazes upward, her auburn hair braided and adorned with a blue ribbon, wearing a dark velvet gown with lace sleeves and a cross pendant; an open landscape with a river and red flowers provides the background. Reinhold Begas, the celebrated German sculptor, was among the couple's sons.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-013: Two figures lean over a window balcony on the upper storey of an old German townhouse, reading what appears to be an intercepted letter while figures in neighbouring windows look on. Spitzweg's handling of the ornate façade, animated characters, and warm light exemplifies his affectionate, narratively rich approach to Biedermeier genre painting.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-036: A bourgeois family in their Sunday best parades down a country path under a parasol, the children straggling behind. Spitzweg captures the small comedies of Biedermeier ritual with affectionate, miniaturist precision.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-das-a: A weathered statue of blindfolded Lady Justice stands with broken scales while a soldier loiters in shadow behind her, a wry Biedermeier comment on the gap between law and power. The panel was sold under Nazi duress by Jewish collector Leo Bendel and only restituted to his heirs in 2019.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-a: A penniless poet lies in his cramped garret bed beneath a propped umbrella, one hand raised in poetic inspiration while books and papers lie scattered at his feet. Spitzweg's most celebrated Biedermeier image, painted in 1839 and now in the Bavarian State Painting Collections, distils the era's affectionate caricature of the impoverished literary eccentric.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-b: A postman in a yellow coat stands in a narrow old-town street, looking up at the ornate storeys of a tall townhouse where inhabitants lean from windows and balconies. Painted around 1858 and held in the Museum für Kunst und Kulturgeschichte der Philipps-Universität Marburg, the composition is a characteristic Spitzweg vignette of small-town life observed with warm, understated humour.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-e: An aged hermit in a white habit dozes on a bench set against a rocky cliff face, his breviary fallen to the ground beside him, while a wide seascape opens out behind. Spitzweg used these solitary monastic figures as gentle emblems of retreat from the modern world, rendered here with the sunny, detail-laden touch characteristic of his Romantic panel paintings.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-m: A plein-air painter has stretched out on his back beneath a propped umbrella in a forest clearing, a folding stool and hat lying nearby. Painted around 1850 in oil on canvas (49.5 × 30.2 cm), the picture is a gentle self-mockery of the Romantic artist's communion with nature, entirely characteristic of Spitzweg's wry, intimate vision.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-s: A naturalist in a light coat pursues two vivid blue butterflies through a lush tropical forest, net raised and mouth agape with excitement. Towering palms and broad exotic foliage dwarf the eccentric collector — a figure type Spitzweg returned to repeatedly in his Biedermeier comedies of bourgeois obsession. The work is held at Museum Wiesbaden (1840).
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-im-da: Carl Spitzweg's oil painting shows an elderly man in cap and spectacles leaning from his garret window to water the flowers crowding his window box, birdcages hanging from the eaves above and church towers rising over the rooftops; far below, a child tends potted plants at another window. Painted around 1848-49, it is characteristic of Spitzweg's affectionate Biedermeier observations of modest life in old German towns. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-im-ha: A bearded man in a red fez and dark, fur-trimmed robes sits beside a hookah pipe while a woman leans against him in a dimly lit interior. Spitzweg's orientalist fantasy draws on European print culture rather than direct observation, rendering the harem through a Biedermeier lens of wry domesticity. The painting, dated after 1855, is held at Museum Georg Schäfer.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-in-th: A solitary figure stands at the base of a dramatic alpine gorge, dwarfed by sheer cliff faces that rise on either side into a storm-lit sky. The steep, narrow composition concentrates the sense of scale and isolation that marks Spitzweg's later landscapes. Painted circa 1871 and now in the Museum Kunstpalast, Düsseldorf.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-stand: A lone violinist perches on a rooftop wall, hat on head and back turned to the viewer, playing into the open air of a quiet town. Spitzweg's Ständchen subjects typically savour the absurdity of private Romantic impulse played out in a small-town public space. This vertical panel dates to 1854.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-the-b: Spitzweg's elderly bibliophile stands high on a library ladder, spectacles on his nose, a volume open in his hands and more books wedged under both arms and between his knees, oblivious to everything but the shelf marked 'Metaphysics'. Painted around 1850, the picture is a gentle Biedermeier satire of bookish absorption and one of Spitzweg's best-loved subjects.
collection-of-beauty-carlos-v-en-muhlber: Titian's monumental equestrian portrait shows Charles V in gilded armour, lance couched, astride a black charger caparisoned in crimson and gold — painted in Augsburg in 1548 to commemorate the Habsburg victory at the Battle of Mühlberg. The image defined the template of sovereign equestrian portraiture that Velázquez and Van Dyck would later inherit. The work has been in the Museo del Prado, Madrid, since the seventeenth century.
collection-of-beauty-carlyle-maclise-ori: Daniel Maclise's full-length pencil study shows Thomas Carlyle leaning against a pillar, right elbow crooked against it, hat held loosely in his left hand. The portrait belongs to the celebrated series of literary figures Maclise drew for Fraser's Magazine during the 1830s, capturing Carlyle's angular, informal presence with characteristic economy of line.
collection-of-beauty-carnegiemuseumofvin: Furrowed wheat fields on the plain of Auvers, the soil glistening after a storm, painted in the final weeks of Van Gogh's life. The high horizon, ribbon-like brushwork, and rain-washed greens belong to the productive Auvers months that ended in July 1890.
collection-of-beauty-carp-leaping-up-a-c: A koi battles upstream against a thundering waterfall, illustrating the Chinese legend that any carp scaling the falls of the Dragon Gate is transformed into a dragon. The motif, emblematic of perseverance and male coming-of-age, was a staple of East Asian ink painting and ukiyo-e print design.
collection-of-beauty-casincaillebotte: Four women — Caillebotte's mother, aunt, cousin, and a family friend — sit reading and sewing on the terrace and lawn of the family's Yerres estate, bathed in dappled afternoon light. Caillebotte organises the figures with his characteristic geometric clarity, each woman absorbed in her own activity while the lush garden stretches behind them. Painted in 1876, the canvas is a study in bourgeois leisure rendered with Impressionist directness.
collection-of-beauty-caspar-david-friedr: A procession of monks bears a coffin into the snow-rimed ruin of a Gothic abbey, the gnarled oaks around them silhouetted against a pale winter dusk. Friedrich exhibited the canvas in Berlin alongside Mönch am Meer as a Romantic meditation on death and resurrection.

A wayside crucifix stands atop a fir-clad alpine peak, gilded by rays of an unseen setting sun. Originally an altarpiece for the Tetschen chapel, the work provoked the so-called Ramdohr controversy by daring to treat pure landscape as a vehicle of religious revelation.

A weathered oak rises at the centre of a Bohemian valley at dawn, its dead crown set against luminous distant mountains. Friedrich uses the broken tree as a quiet emblem of endurance, paired with the morning panorama as one half of a meditation on the cycle of day and life.

A solitary figure stands on a pale dune before an immense, near-empty expanse of sea and sky. Friedrich strips the composition to horizontal bands, dwarfing the human silhouette to evoke spiritual confrontation with the infinite — a foundational image of German Romantic landscape.

Five figures on a Baltic shore correspond to five sailing vessels at varying distances — an allegory of the ages of human life rendered in Friedrich's late, hushed palette. The painting was made near the artist's birthplace of Greifswald and is now in Leipzig's Museum der bildenden Künste.

Two women and a man on a rocky shore watch sailing ships approach beneath a rising moon, the sky banded violet and gold. Friedrich repeated the moonlit-sea motif throughout his career as a Rückenfigur meditation on faith, return, and the threshold between visible and unseen.

Three figures peer over the dizzying white precipices of Rügen onto the Baltic far below, framed by an arch of beech branches. Painted shortly after Friedrich's honeymoon, the picture invests a real coastal panorama with Romantic allegories of marriage, faith, and mortality.

Seen from behind on a rocky outcrop, the wanderer surveys a swirling fog that swallows the peaks below. Friedrich's signature Rückenfigur device invites the viewer into the figure's vantage, making the landscape an interior as much as a topography of the Elbe Sandstone Mountains.
collection-of-beauty-cassatt-mary-lydia-: Lydia Cassatt, the artist's elder sister and frequent model, leans forward absorbed in her work at a tapestry loom, painted in soft indoor light. The picture belongs to Cassatt's series of women engaged in domestic occupations, executed around 1881 with the loose, colour-saturated brushwork she developed in the circle of Degas.
collection-of-beauty-cassatt-mary-matern: A mother, her shoulders draped in a rosy wrap, gazes down at the infant she holds against her in close, quiet intimacy. Cassatt returned repeatedly to the maternité theme after 1880, treating the secular subject with a formal tenderness recalling Renaissance Madonnas while maintaining a bright, contemporary palette.
collection-of-beauty-cats-suggested-as-t: Kuniyoshi, a noted cat lover, replaces every post town on the Tōkaidō highway with a cat whose pose or attribute puns on the station's name. The triptych is a tour de force of Edo wordplay (mitate) and ukiyo-e woodblock printing, made when actor prints had been restricted by Tenpō reform censorship.
collection-of-beauty-cawing-crow-by-ohar: A black crow perches on a snow-covered branch, beak open mid-call, while snow-laden willow fronds hang around it against a pale grey ground. Koson specialised in kachō-e (bird-and-flower) prints for the early-twentieth-century shin-hanga revival, producing naturalistic studies such as this one for Western collectors.
collection-of-beauty-cb9001fb: The basalt sea-stacks of Chongseokjeong rising from the East Sea coast, the fourth leaf of Kim Hong-do's album of the four districts of Geumgang. Ink and light colour on silk, roughly 30 by 44 cm, painted about 1788 after a tour the court painter made of Mount Geumgang and Gangwon Province under King Jeongjo. The clustered hexagonal columns are drawn in fine vertical strokes.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-ambroise-vo: The dealer Ambroise Vollard sits forward with hands clasped, his bald head catching the light against a brown studio wall. Cézanne painted the portrait in 1899; it is held by the Petit Palais in Paris. Vollard recalled posing more than a hundred times, after which the painter declared only the shirtfront finished.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-fwn-1974: A landscape study in pencil and watercolour, the forms of trees and rock laid in with translucent patches of blue and ochre over open paper. Catalogued as FWN 1974 in the online Cézanne catalogue raisonné among the works on paper. Cézanne built such sheets from overlapping washes, leaving the white of the paper to carry the light.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-le-printemp: A female personification of Spring stands with a garland of blossom, one of four season panels Cézanne signed 'Ingres'. He painted them about 1860 to 1861 for the salon alcove of the family estate, the Jas de Bouffan near Aix; the panels were later transferred to canvas and given to the Petit Palais, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-thyssen: A man in a wide-brimmed hat sits against a pale terrace balustrade, his features summarily indicated and patches of bare canvas left in reserve. Painted in 1905-06, oil on canvas, the sitter is Vallier, the gardener at Cézanne's studio at Les Lauves near Aix-en-Provence; the work has been in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, since 1993.
collection-of-beauty-charing-cross-bridg: Monet painted Charing Cross Bridge during winter stays in London, working on multiple canvases simultaneously as the light shifted. In this 1899 version, bridge, water, and sky dissolve into a haze of pale blue and diffuse yellow, characteristic of his atmospheric London series now held in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza.

One of nearly forty variants Monet made of Charing Cross Bridge, focused here on the trembling reflections beneath the iron span. The series, painted between 1899 and 1904, was the artist's sustained study of London fog as a coloured atmospheric medium rather than a mere obscurant.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-dae: Daedalus attaches wings to the seated young Icarus, who raises his arm as if readying himself for flight. Attributed to Charles Le Brun and dated between 1645 and 1646, the canvas was painted during the artist's Roman period when he was working in proximity to Poussin, whose classicising influence is evident in the monumental figure grouping.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-la-: Sheet from the Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions, showing the face of Anger with brows drawn together, nostrils flared and teeth bared. Le Brun's 1668 lecture at the Académie Royale built a Cartesian taxonomy of emotion for painters, and the engraved sheets circulated in artist pattern books well into the nineteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-les: The mother, wife and daughters of the defeated Darius prostrate themselves before Alexander and Hephaestion in the Persian camp after Issus. Painted between 1660 and 1661 and shown to Louis XIV at Fontainebleau, the canvas won Le Brun his role as premier peintre and ushered in his cycle of Alexander histories for the Crown.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-pri: A vast allegorical ceiling composition painted by Charles Le Brun between 1681 and 1684 to commemorate Louis XIV's capture of Ghent in 1678. Winged personifications of Fame and Victory surge through clouds above prostrate enemy figures and symbols of conquest, while allegorical figures of France and the defeated city occupy the lower register — part of Le Brun's pictorial programme glorifying the Crown.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-the: Studies of emotive heads, including wonder, despair and joy, from the series Le Brun developed to illustrate his 1668 lecture at the Académie Royale de Peinture et de Sculpture. Published posthumously as Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions, the drawings codified facial expression for two centuries of academic teaching, with the eyebrows treated as the primary diagnostic feature.

Polyxena is led to the altar to appease the ghost of Achilles while her mother Hecuba reaches to restrain her and the soldier Neoptolemus lifts his sword. Le Brun painted the subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses in 1647, before his career as premier peintre to Louis XIV.
collection-of-beauty-charles-w-bartlett-: Pilgrims and worshippers gather in a courtyard of the Golden Temple complex at Amritsar, their colourful robes set against the arched stone architecture. The colour woodblock print was published in Tokyo in 1916 by Watanabe Shōzaburō and is now in the Honolulu Academy of Arts.

Dark lava rocks along the Hana coast of Maui meet crashing surf, with tropical vegetation clinging to the headland at left and an open expanse of deep blue ocean beyond. Bartlett rendered the scene in watercolour and ink in 1920, part of the Hawaiian landscape work he produced after settling in Honolulu following his earlier Asian travels.

Bartlett depicts himself in watercolour, signed and dated September 1933. The English-born artist had settled in Hawaii by 1917 after extensive travels in Japan and India, where he became closely associated with the shin-hanga movement and collaborated with the Tokyo publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō. The work is held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-charlotte-dubourg-p: Charlotte Dubourg, Fantin-Latour's sister-in-law, sits in a pale blue dress on a red upholstered chair, holding a small fan or card, her gaze directed at the viewer. The portrait was painted in 1882 and is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, where it exemplifies the quiet psychological intensity that characterises Fantin-Latour's figure work.
collection-of-beauty-chase-mrs-meigs-pia: Mrs. Meigs is seen from behind at her organ in a simply furnished, light-filled interior, her white dress luminous against the pale walls. Chase painted several such domestic interiors in the early 1880s, applying the assured tonal handling he had developed through study of Old Masters and through his time in Munich.
collection-of-beauty-chase-william-merri: A woman in a grey dress and red hat stands beside a beached white rowboat on a sandy Shinnecock shore, while a small child in pink plays nearby and a dog investigates the water's edge. Chase painted this circa 1892 at his Long Island summer school, capturing the bright, breezy atmosphere of the bay with loose, confident brushwork characteristic of his plein-air practice.

Chase portrays Whistler full-length against a warm golden ground, the subject dressed head to toe in black and holding a slender cane — a dandyish self-presentation in keeping with Whistler's own aesthetic persona. Painted in 1885 and now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the canvas records Chase's admiration for his fellow artist while asserting his own formidable painterly confidence.

Dora Wheeler, a designer trained alongside Chase in Munich, sits in a blue gown amid the embroidered hangings of her mother Candace's Associated Artists studio. The portrait won a medal at the 1883 Paris Salon and helped establish Chase's reputation for atmospheric, aesthetic-movement interiors.

Chase shows himself at work in his studio, holding a loaded palette and brushes before a large blank canvas, his working jacket open over a dark waistcoat. Painted in 1915 in his Fourth Avenue studio and now in the Richmond Art Museum collection, the picture captures the theatrical self-assurance Chase brought to teaching and to his own public persona.

An early student work made during Chase's Indianapolis years, the cut watermelon is laid out with the dark ground and dramatic highlights of the Munich-school tradition he would soon study at first hand. The picture predates his shift toward looser, brighter American Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-chaumiere-italienne: This etching by Jean-Honoré Fragonard depicts a dilapidated Italian rural cottage sheltered by trees, with small figures visible nearby. The composition is characteristic of Fragonard's landscape prints made from sketches gathered during his Italian travels, and an impression is held at Ghent University Library.
collection-of-beauty-chen-rong-nine-drag: Nine dragons surge through clouds, mist, and crashing water across a long handscroll of ink and wash on paper. Chen Rong, a Southern Song scholar-official, painted the work in 1244; it is celebrated for its splashed-ink dragons and is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-chichester-canal-18: The still water of the Sussex canal mirrors a tall-masted ship and a sky drenched in late sun. Turner painted the scene for his patron the Earl of Egremont, one of a set of canvases made for the panelled dining room at Petworth House and now in the Tate.
collection-of-beauty-childe-harold: Inspired by Byron's Mediterranean poem, Turner builds a luminous Italian campagna of crumbling arches, distant hills, and a glowing sky. The picture is part of the artist's long late dialogue with Claude Lorrain, dissolving classical landscape architecture into atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-chinese-warship-tin: The German-built ironclad Tingyuan, then the largest warship in the Far East, lies at anchor in a Japanese port flying her flags. Kōitsu records the ship's Meiji-era courtesy visit in a colour woodblock print that combines ukiyo-e tradition with the new Western subject matter of steam and steel.
collection-of-beauty-christ-on-the-cross: Christ hangs alone on the cross against a darkened sky, his pale body lit sharply against the gloom and his head sunk toward his shoulder. Rubens painted this single-figure devotional crucifixion in oil on oak panel, stripping away mourners and thieves to concentrate everything on the modelling of the body. The painting belongs to the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich.
collection-of-beauty-christian-ix-of-den: Tuxen assembles Christian IX — the so-called father-in-law of Europe — with his children and royal grandchildren in the garden hall of Fredensborg Palace. Painted between 1883 and 1886, the large group portrait records the Danish dynastic ties that linked the courts of Britain, Russia, and Greece and is now at Christiansborg Palace.
collection-of-beauty-circle-of-pieter-br: Villagers skate and slide on a frozen river beside snow-covered houses, while at right a propped board baited with grain forms a trap for unwary birds. One of around a hundred surviving versions after Pieter Bruegel the Elder's composition, it pairs winter genre with a quiet emblem of human precariousness.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-021: Several figures sit and stand in small rowing boats on a calm stretch of the Seine at Poissy, their reflections diffused in the warm green water below. Monet settled briefly at Poissy in 1881–82 before moving to Giverny, and this canvas — now in the Belvedere, Vienna — is among the river scenes he produced there.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-022: Jeanne-Marguerite Lecadre, a relative, stands among flowering beds in the family garden at Sainte-Adresse near Le Havre. The picture's bright local colour and crisp shadows show Monet absorbing the lessons of Manet and Japanese prints.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-023: Suzanne Hoschedé strides up a grassy slope, parasol angled against the wind that flattens her white dress. The picture revisits the 1875 Argenteuil composition of Camille, now reworked as a near-anonymous figure study with the face deliberately blurred.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-029: A modest fisherman's cottage perched above the Norman coast, painted during Monet's productive campaigns at Pourville and Varengeville. Broken brushwork dissolves cliff, sea, and sky into a single weathered atmosphere, the cottage anchoring the composition against the windblown grass.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-044: One of the large-scale Giverny pond pictures painted after 1916, the canvas shows lily pads adrift on a surface of shimmering gold and mauve, with willowy reflections along the right edge dissolving sky and vegetation into the water. Abandoning any fixed horizon, Monet treated surface and depth as a single chromatic field; the work is now in the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-051: A large bouquet of white chrysanthemums fills a decorative red-trimmed vase in this 1878 still life, now in the Musée d'Orsay. Painted around the time Monet settled at Vétheuil, the canvas applies loose, energetic strokes to the overlapping petals, treating the indoor subject with the same atmospheric directness he brought to his landscape work.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-052: A dense bouquet of sunflowers arranged in a glazed vase, painted in Vétheuil years before Van Gogh took up the same motif in Arles. Monet builds the heavy heads from short, comma-like strokes of chrome yellow and ochre, contrasting their warmth against a cool blue-grey ground.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1840-1: Two figures walk through a frost-covered landscape near Giverny in this 1885 canvas, now in Museum Barberini, Potsdam. Frost-laden branches fill the upper half of the composition, and Monet renders the chill morning light in pale violet, rose, and white, the delicate tones characteristic of his winter subjects painted after he settled at Giverny in 1883.

From the late Nymphéas cycle, the canvas dissolves the lily pond into floating pads, drowned grasses, and reflected sky. Working at monumental scale in his Giverny studio, Monet abandoned the horizon altogether to let surface and depth fuse into a single chromatic field.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1867-r: Sailboats and onlookers crowd the beach at Sainte-Adresse, the Norman resort where Monet spent the summer with relatives. The crisp horizontals and bright local colour are still indebted to Boudin and Jongkind, but already announce the open-air manner that Impressionism would soon codify.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1870-l: Painted on the Norman coast during Monet's summer honeymoon with Camille, the breakwater at low tide is laid down in rapid, salt-scratched brushwork. Sand was famously found mixed into the paint of his Trouville canvases, a record of their plein-air making in the wind off the Channel.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1875-t: A steam locomotive pushes through a snow-covered road flanked by bare trees, figures and fencing just visible in the grey winter light. Painted in 1875 and now in the Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris, the canvas shows Monet treating engine smoke and winter atmosphere as allied phenomena, building the scene from short, vigorous strokes of grey, white, and black.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-a-corn: An interior view of the Monet family's Argenteuil home, with young Jean standing at the end of a darkened hallway between hanging plants and curtained light. The painting marks one of Monet's rare domestic interiors, balancing silhouetted shadow against a glowing window.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-a-seas: A nocturnal Channel scene with moonlight breaking through cloud over distant sailing vessels. Made during Monet's formative summers on the Normandy coast, the picture follows the marines of Boudin and Jongkind, with feathery brushwork capturing reflected silver on dark water.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-a-walk: A red poppy field stretches across the foreground, with a woman and child near the lower centre and two more figures ascending the slope toward a pair of poplars in the middle distance. Painted in 1873 during Monet's Argenteuil years, the canvas combines vivid dots of scarlet with a broad, cloudy sky and is held by the Rhode Island School of Design Museum.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-adolph: The painter's father sits in a straw hat among flowering plants in the family's seaside garden at Sainte-Adresse. Painted during the same productive Norman summer as the Regatta, the picture combines a tender domestic portrait with Monet's emerging interest in dappled outdoor light.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-alice-: Alice Hoschedé sits among flowering plants and foliage in a garden, her light-coloured dress treated as one luminous accent within the surrounding greenery. Dahlias and other blooms are visible against a balustrade in the background. Monet painted this intimate garden figure at Vétheuil in 1881, during the period when Alice was living with his household.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-antibe: A view across the Mediterranean toward the snow-capped Alps, made during Monet's four-month campaign on the Côte d'Azur in early 1888. The pink and turquoise palette he developed here pushed his colour further than ever, anticipating the serial canvases of the 1890s.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-argent: Sailboats rest on the still surface of the Seine at Argenteuil, the suburban boating town where Monet settled after the Franco-Prussian War. Reflections on calm water became a central subject during his years there. Painted in 1872, the canvas is now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-arriva: Steam billows beneath the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare as a locomotive pulls in from the Normandy line. One of twelve canvases Monet made of the station in 1877, the series treated industrial vapour as a modern equivalent of mist on the Seine.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-automn: Riverside trees in russet and gold are doubled in the still surface of the Seine. Painted from the bank at Argenteuil, the picture exploits Monet's preferred device of mirrored reflection, the upper and lower halves of the canvas answering one another in horizontal bands.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-camill: An intimate domestic scene of Monet's first wife, Camille Doncieux, seated at an embroidery frame in their Argenteuil home. The painter treats the patterned tapestry, dress, and wall hangings as a single woven field of colour, dissolving figure and interior into a continuous surface of touches.

Monet painted his first wife within hours of her death from uterine cancer at age thirty-two, the brushwork dissolving her features into a veil of violet, grey and white. He later confessed unease at finding himself analysing her colour rather than mourning her.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-champ-: A summer wheatfield treated as an almost abstract field of warm strokes under a high sky. The subject anticipates the haystacks Monet would begin painting in series a decade later, where the same agrarian motif became a vehicle for studying changing light.

Several figures move through a dense field of red poppies, with the town of Vétheuil and its church tower visible across the river in the middle distance. Monet painted this scene near Vétheuil in 1879, combining the poppy motif with human figures as he had done earlier at Argenteuil. The canvas is in the Foundation E.G. Bührle Collection.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-cliff-: Two women stand on a cliff top above the English Channel at Pourville, one holding a red parasol, with sailing boats visible on the sea below. Painted during Monet's working stay on the Normandy coast in 1882, the canvas uses the figures as a compositional anchor against the broad open sky. It is now in the Art Institute of Chicago.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-der-ko: A bearded man in a white chef's jacket and tall toque looks outward in this unusual portrait by Monet, painted during his Normandy campaign of 1882. The loose, confident brushwork captures the sitter's weathered features and strong profile against a plain ground. Known as Père Paul, the subject was a local cook; the work is now in the Belvedere, Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-die-we: A willow standing on the bank of the Epte near Giverny, caught in the pale, cool light of a spring morning. The pastel palette and feathery brushwork are typical of Monet's mid-1880s riverside studies, in which he began to anchor compositions around a single tree as a recurring motif.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-eglise: The small church of Varengeville perches dramatically atop sheer chalk cliffs above the sea, painted in clear morning light. Monet returned to this cliff-top motif repeatedly during his 1882 stay on the Normandy coast, treating the chapel's silhouette as a study in shifting maritime light at different hours. The work is dated 1882.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-entree: Boats crowd the harbour mouth of the Norman resort of Trouville, where Monet honeymooned with Camille in the summer of 1870. The pictures from that holiday — sand still embedded in some of the canvases — were the last he made before fleeing the war to London.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-etreta: Beached fishing caïques dominate the foreground as the chalk Falaise d'Amont curves out into a green sea. Monet returned to Étretat repeatedly in the 1880s, drawn by the sculpted cliffs Courbet had also painted a generation earlier.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-fishin: Sail-rigged fishing boats slip out of Le Havre on an overcast day, the harbour walls and shipping dissolved into muted silhouettes. Monet painted the port repeatedly in the early-to-mid 1870s, and this canvas of 1874 belongs to the same serial engagement with the Norman coast that began with Impression, Sunrise two years earlier.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-flower: A bank of the Seine near Argenteuil glows with large-headed dahlias and chrysanthemums against the warm light of a late-summer evening. Industrial smokestacks and a church tower are visible across the river, grounding this 1877 canvas in the working landscape Monet inhabited during his Argenteuil years. The work is held by the Pola Museum of Art.

Plum trees in full white blossom fill the foreground, with the rooftops and church of a village and a green hillside rising clearly behind — a composition that combines spring abundance with the settled Norman landscape. Painted in 1879, during Monet's years at Vétheuil, the canvas is held by the Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-french: An early still life arranging garden blooms alongside ripe pears and grapes on a draped surface. Painted before Monet committed fully to plein-air landscape, the canvas shows him testing dense impasto and saturated colour against the conventions of Salon still-life painting.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-grayst: A single grainstack rises against a warm, luminous sky in a field near Giverny — one of the celebrated series of some twenty-five canvases Monet made between 1890 and 1891, tracking the same motif through different times of day and seasons. The work exemplifies his serial method at its most concentrated and is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-hotel-: Holiday-makers promenade before the grand facade of the Hôtel des Roches Noires at Trouville, flags snapping in the sea breeze above. Painted in the summer of 1870, shortly before the outbreak of the Franco-Prussian War, the canvas is a rapid plein-air study; traces of actual sand have been found embedded in the paint surface. It is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-houses: The Palace of Westminster looms through Thames fog at a moment of breaking sun. Monet painted some nineteen Parliament views from a balcony at St Thomas's Hospital between 1900 and 1904, returning to his hotel each evening to refine the series from memory and notes.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-in-the: Two of Alice Hoschedé's daughters work and read in the dappled woods near Giverny, where Monet had moved in 1883. Blanche, herself a painter, would later marry Monet's son Jean and become his nurse and companion in his final years.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-interi: A lamp-lit domestic interior from Monet's youth, with figures gathered after a meal. Indoor subjects are unusual in his work; here the warm artificial light and dark-keyed palette betray a debt to the realism of Manet and Bazille more than to his later high-colour outdoor practice.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-jardin: On a sunny terrace at Sainte-Adresse, two elegantly dressed figures stroll among vivid flower beds while two others sit in the foreground; two flags — one French tricolour — fly above a sea busy with sailing vessels and steamships. Painted in 1866–67 and now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, this is one of Monet's most composed and boldly coloured early canvases, its high viewpoint and flat decorative fields reflecting an awareness of Japanese prints.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-jean-p: Two young figures stand on the bank of the Epte beside tall bare-trunked trees, their reflections caught in the still water below. The muted, hazy palette — pale pinks, blues, and ochres — places the scene in late autumn or winter. Painted between about 1887 and 1890, the work is held at the National Gallery of Canada, Ottawa.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-l-ete-: A bank of red poppies climbs a sunlit slope above figures lost in the grass. The canvas is one of several Monet devoted to the motif of wildflower meadows, the bright dabs of red functioning as both botanical record and pure chromatic accent.

A woman sits in a broad, open meadow near Argenteuil, a parasol and light wrap beside her, while a second figure in pale dress stands in the distance. The vast sky and flat field fill the canvas with summer light and air. Painted in 1874 and now in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin, the work belongs to a group of figure-in-landscape compositions from Monet's Argenteuil period.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-cor: A coastal path winds through dense Mediterranean scrub and flowering plants below a steep rocky headland, with the sea glinting to the left. Monet made this and related Riviera views during his 1884 trip to the coast between Bordighera and Monaco, pushing his palette into the hot, saturated hues of the southern sun. The canvas is held at the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-man: The vast natural arch of the Manneporte rises from the surf at Étretat, one of three rock formations Monet painted obsessively during his Normandy campaigns of the early 1880s. The view from below dramatises the cliff's mass against breaking sea.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-poi: Wagons and figures cross the wet sand below the headland of La Hève near Le Havre, Monet's home town. Shown at the Salon of 1865 — his official debut — the canvas owes much to the marine realism of Boudin and Courbet.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-sei: A bend of the Seine at Vétheuil, the village where Monet lived through the bleakest years of his middle career. The river, opposite bank and sky are resolved into three horizontal bands of broken colour, a structural simplicity that points toward his coming serial work.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-bat: Monet's floating studio moored on a calm waterway, its cabin and hull reflected in still water below. A figure is visible aboard the boat, surrounded by the leafy bank beyond. The work is held by the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia, and dates from 1876, when Monet used the vessel at Argenteuil to paint the Seine from the water's surface.

The floating studio Monet had built at Argenteuil, a small cabined skiff that let him paint directly on the Seine. Reflections double the boat in rippling vertical strokes, an image of the artist's working method as much as a landscape.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-gra: Looking down the Grand Canal toward Santa Maria della Salute, Monet renders Venice as drifting reflections of pink and turquoise on water. The view comes from his only visit to the city, in autumn 1908, which yielded a late series exhibited at Bernheim-Jeune in 1912.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-pal: The Doge's Palace rises from the Venetian lagoon in dissolving pinks and aquamarines, painted during Monet's two-month stay in the city. The facade is treated less as architecture than as a screen for refracted light, with broken brushwork knitting stone, water and sky into a single luminous fabric.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-par: One of nineteen views of the Houses of Parliament that Monet worked on from a balcony at St Thomas' Hospital across the Thames. Westminster's Gothic silhouette is silhouetted against a sun-soaked fog, the river burning with reflected colour as atmospheric haze flattens detail into pure tonal envelope.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-pon: The iron railway bridge at Argenteuil cuts across the Seine in flat planes of pale stone, a steam train trailing white smoke above. Monet treats modern infrastructure as a legitimate motif of plein-air painting, balancing its industrial geometry against the soft river bank.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-les-ca: Sailboats and rowers drift on the Seine at Argenteuil, the Parisian suburb where Monet lived through the early 1870s and turned regatta-day leisure into a recurring subject. Quick comma-strokes describe water and rigging with equal economy.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-les-py: The jagged sea stacks off Belle-Île-en-Mer, painted during Monet's bracing autumn campaign on the Breton coast. Granite is built up in dense, crusted strokes against a churning Atlantic, a darker and rougher palette than his Norman seascapes.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-neige-: A muffled village street under fresh snow, part of Monet's sustained study of Argenteuil winters. The white ground is laid in with cool blues and lilacs rather than pure white, a decisive Impressionist break from academic monochrome.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-nymphe: An early canvas in the great water-lily cycle Monet pursued at his Giverny pond for the last three decades of his life. The horizon has already vanished; only floating pads, reflected sky and submerged depth remain, organised purely by colour.

A large-scale water-lily canvas of 1915, painted in the studio Monet built at Giverny to accommodate his ever-bigger formats. The pond has lost its banks entirely; tangled reflections of weeping willow descend through deep blues and violets while pads float as flat islands of green.

From the Giverny series, the Japanese-style pond seen close-up with no shore in sight. Lily pads punctuate broad zones of mauve and green reflection, the painted surface oscillating between water-skin and pure abstraction.

Held by the Musée Marmottan Monet, which inherited the artist's studio holdings, this Nymphéas frames the pond as an unbroken field of reflected light. Pads cluster as horizontal accents across deep blues and rose, the composition organised by colour weight rather than perspective.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-on-the: Two young women in white summer dresses and straw hats sit in a small rowing boat, their figures reflected in the shimmering water beneath. Painted in 1887 and held by the National Museum of Western Art, Tokyo, the canvas presents its subjects from an elevated vantage point that flattens the scene into broad planes of colour, a compositional strategy Monet shared with contemporaries drawn to Japanese prints.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-pond-w: A vertical Giverny canvas in which the lily pond is rotated almost into pure surface pattern. Pinks and violets float over deep greens, the brushwork loose enough that the pads sometimes read as drifting clouds of pigment.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-poplar: From the Poplars series, painted from a flat-bottomed boat moored in the river Epte near Giverny. The slender trunks form a rhythmic vertical lattice, doubled by reflection, that anticipates the decorative serial logic of the later Rouen Cathedrals.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-poppy-: Camille and the young Jean Monet wade through high summer grass at Argenteuil, scarlet poppies dotted across the field in dabs of vermilion. A second figure-pair higher on the slope mirrors the first, knitting two moments into one composition.

A sunlit meadow of red poppies, painted in 1881 and now in Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam. A single tall tree punctuates the flat plain, and a broad sky of pale grey-white occupies much of the canvas above a low horizon. The open, airy composition and loose broken touch are characteristic of Monet's rural landscapes of the early 1880s.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-red-an: Two opium poppies — one deep crimson, one pink — and a closed bud rise on long stems from a slim glass vase, their silvery scalloped leaves brushed loosely against a pale ground. The canvas is signed at upper left and painted in an unusually tall, narrow upright format. Monet's flower still lifes belong chiefly to the early 1880s, when work indoors filled the gaps between landscape campaigns.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-reflec: A late, large-scale Giverny panel related to the Grandes Décorations Monet was preparing for the Orangerie. Clouds are present only as inverted reflections, the painting collapsing sky, water and lily into one immersive plane.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-regatt: Sails crowd the Seine basin at Argenteuil, doubled in vivid downward strokes that read almost as flames on the water. The painting's loose vertical reflections were among the works that helped define the Impressionist handling of moving light on water.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-regnv-: Rain over Étretat: the Norman cliffs and arched rock recede behind a grey curtain of weather, the Channel rendered in broken slate strokes. Monet often returned to Étretat through the 1880s, attracted by its dramatic chalk geology under shifting marine light.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-road-a: A sunken Norman lane cuts down toward the sea at Pourville, where Monet spent productive months in 1882. Banks of grass and gorse frame a small triangle of bright Channel water, a composition organised by the steep diagonal of the path.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-rocks-: Jagged dark rocks at Port-Domois on Belle-Île rise dramatically against a warm sunset sky of pink and gold, the sea below rendered in deep blue-violet. Monet made an extended campaign on the storm-battered Breton coast in autumn 1886, producing a sequence of canvases focused on the island's rugged granite formations under shifting Atlantic light.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-spring: A young woman, almost certainly Camille, sits reading in dappled shade beneath flowering trees. Pink-white blossoms and green foliage are dissolved into a single shimmering screen of broken touch, an early statement of Monet's plein-air figure painting.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-still-: Two pheasants and several smaller game birds are arranged on a white cloth, painted in 1879 and now in the Minneapolis Institute of Art. The still life dates from a period of personal hardship for Monet following his wife Camille's death that year. The muted, earthy handling is markedly more sober than his contemporary plein-air landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-street: An early view of the seaside resort north of Le Havre, where Monet stayed with his aunt during a formative summer. Architecture is still drawn with relatively firm contour, but the bright Norman light and high-keyed palette already point toward Impressionist practice.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-temps-: A view along the Normandy coast from the clifftops near Pourville, painted in 1881 and now in the Staechelin collection at Kunstmuseum Basel. The reddish-brown cliffs fall away to the left while the Channel stretches to the horizon under a pale, overcast sky. The quiet stillness implied by the French title 'Temps calme' (calm weather) is captured in the subdued, close-valued palette of greens, blues and greys.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ar: The road bridge at Argenteuil, rebuilt after the Franco-Prussian War, frames moored sailboats on the Seine. Monet used the same bridge in several canvases of 1874, varying the viewpoint and weather to test how a single motif behaves under changing light.

Rows of irises beneath espaliered fruit trees in the artist's own garden at Giverny, which he designed and tended as obsessively as he painted it. The diagonal furrows of mauve and violet flowers organise the canvas as a near-abstract chromatic grid.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-cl: The famous Falaise d'Aval at Étretat, with its natural arch piercing the chalk cliff. Monet, who painted this Norman site repeatedly, here works with broken touches of cream, lilac and pale green to render limestone under shifting Channel light.

A view of the chalk cliffs and natural arches at Étretat on the Normandy coast, a motif Monet returned to repeatedly in the mid-1880s. He works the chalk face in pinks and creams against the green-blue Channel, alert to how the light shifts across the porous stone.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-du: Geese make their way along a sunlit stream past a farmhouse half-hidden by trees, painted in 1874 during Monet's Argenteuil years. The shimmering surface of the water and the dappled foliage are rendered in quick, broken touches of gold and green. Now held at the Clark Art Institute, the picture belongs to a group of rural farmyard subjects Monet pursued alongside his better-known river scenes of the mid-1870s.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-fo: The old fortifications of Antibes seen across the bay, from Monet's 1888 Riviera campaign. The southern light pushed his palette toward saturated pinks, turquoises and ochres, the Mediterranean treated as a high-keyed counterpart to his northern coasts.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ga: A locomotive pulls under the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare, steam rolling up to merge with the smoke-stained light. Part of a twelve-canvas series for which Monet secured permission to set up his easel inside the working terminus.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-hi: The highway bridge at Argenteuil is shown mid-repair, its timber scaffolding framing a view down the Seine toward a distant townscape, painted in 1872. Pedestrians and a horse-drawn cart cross the upper roadway while the river below carries sailing vessels through the construction. Monet treats the industrial scaffolding with the same attentiveness he brought to more conventional landscape motifs of the period.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ho: The Gothic silhouette of Westminster dissolves into a haze of violet and orange across the Thames. Painted from a terrace at St Thomas's Hospital, the canvas belongs to Monet's London series, in which he tracked the same motif under shifting fog, smoke and sun.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ma: A single magpie perches on a wooden fence gate at the left of a snowbound Norman landscape, its dark form casting a faint blue shadow on the drift below. Monet explored the chromatic subtlety of coloured shadow across white snow in this large canvas of 1868–69, which was rejected by the 1869 Salon. The work is now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ra: A railway bridge strides across the Seine on pale stone piers, a steam train trailing billowing smoke above the water, while a sailboat glides below on the left. Monet painted this junction of industry and leisure on the Seine at Argenteuil in 1873, making the bridge and its reflections a recurring subject of his years there. The canvas is held at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ro: A pale road curves along an open hillside toward the village of Vétheuil, visible in the middle distance beneath a high ridge, painted in 1879. The brushwork is dry and broken, warm ochres and mauves marking the early leafless trees on the left and the village beyond. Now in The Phillips Collection, Washington, the picture was made shortly after Monet settled at Vétheuil during a period of personal and financial difficulty.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-va: The wide valley of the Nervia opens beneath massive snow-capped peaks, a scatter of buildings nestled among low trees at the valley floor, painted during Monet's January 1884 journey along the Italian Riviera. The palette of pale mauves, greys and warm ochres reflects his sustained fascination with Mediterranean light and its effect on landscape form. The canvas is held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-wa: Pale lilies float on a luminous pond crossed by the trailing reflections of weeping willows. The panel forms part of the Grandes Décorations cycle Monet painted at Giverny for the oval rooms of the Musée de l'Orangerie in Paris, where pond, sky and bank dissolve into a continuous surface.

Lily pads and blossoms drift across a deep green-shadowed pond surface, the reflections of foliage dissolving the boundary between water and sky. This large panel, titled Reflets verts, is one of the Grandes Décorations that Monet created between 1914 and 1926 and which are permanently installed at the Musée de l'Orangerie, Paris. The compressed, all-over surface leaves no horizon, immersing the viewer in the unbroken world of the pond.

Pale dawn light catches the lily pads on the Giverny pond, the water dissolving into broad horizontal sweeps of mauve and cream. The work belongs to the great cycle Monet developed in his late, near-blind years for the Orangerie ovals.

Reflected clouds spread luminously across the pond surface, lily pads riding the image in loose clusters with no sky or bank to orient the eye. This mural-scale panel, titled Les Nuages, is part of the Grandes Décorations that Monet created between 1914 and 1926 and donated to the French state during his lifetime for the dedicated rooms of the Musée de l'Orangerie, Paris. The work dates from his final years, painted as he struggled with cataracts.

Two weeping willows anchor the left and right edges of this panoramic composition, their dark hanging branches framing the expanse of the Giverny pond below. Lily pads drift across a surface rendered in shifting tones of blue, grey, and muted lavender. The canvas belongs to Monet's monumental Nymphéas decorations, created between 1914 and 1926 for the Musée de l'Orangerie, Paris.
Inverted trees and clouds shimmer in the pond, lily pads punctuating the surface as the only signal of where water meets reflection. The picture pushes Monet's late style toward near-abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-wi: A tall Amsterdam windmill dominates the composition, flanked by Dutch canal-side buildings whose rooflines and reflections fill the water below. Monet painted this view on the Onbekende Gracht during his 1874 visit to Holland, one of several Dutch trips he made during his Impressionist years. The canvas is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-tulip-: Sweeping bands of red and violet tulips fill the foreground, with a windmill and farm buildings rising against a brisk cloudy sky. Monet visited the Dutch bulb fields in 1886 to paint these intensely saturated expanses of colour. The canvas, dated 1886, is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-vase-o: Red-and-yellow and white tulips splay from a slender dark vase against a pale ground, the leaves swept in as long strokes of blue-green and the blooms built up in thick wet-in-wet colour; the canvas is signed at lower right. Monet painted flower still lifes chiefly in the early 1880s, between landscape campaigns, and this bouquet belongs to that vein of his work.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-vetheu: A field of red poppies and summer grasses occupies the foreground, with tall poplars and cypresses framing the distant village of Vétheuil on the hillside. The Seine is glimpsed at the far right edge. Monet painted this sunlit meadow view in 1880, during his years living at Vétheuil; the canvas is in the Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow.

Snow blankets the village of Vétheuil and its church on the hillside above the Seine, while figures in a small boat navigate the icy, partly frozen river below. The chalky palette of blue-grey and white conveys the severity of the winter season. Monet painted this view around 1878–1879; the canvas is in the Frick Collection, New York.

The village of Vétheuil rises in tiers from the Seine to its tall Gothic church tower, which stands prominent against a pink-and-blue summer sky. The water below dissolves the buildings into shimmering reflections of golden and blue-grey. Monet painted numerous variants of this view during his years at Vétheuil; this 1879 canvas is held at the National Gallery of Victoria, Melbourne.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-view-o: A path bordered by red poppies and wildflowers leads through a summer meadow, with tall poplars rising to the right and the church and rooftops of Vétheuil visible in the middle distance. Monet painted this open-air view in 1880 during his years living at Vétheuil; the canvas is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-villas: A terracotta-coloured villa with arched loggia fills the left foreground, flanked by tall palms and lush flowering shrubs, with the sun-baked town of Bordighera rising on the hillside beyond. Monet spent several months on the Italian Riviera in early 1884, producing numerous canvases devoted to its luxuriant vegetation and brilliant light. This work is in the collection of Museum Barberini, Potsdam.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-voir-l: A snow-covered street or road at Argenteuil stretches toward buildings and hills in the background, with several dark-clad figures making their way through the winter landscape. Monet rendered the scene in a muted palette of white, blue-grey, and warm rooftop ochres. Painted in 1875, the work is in the collection of the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-water-: Lily pads float in even rhythms across green-blue water, with a pale band of sky-reflection running along the upper edge. The picture comes from the first mature group of Nymphéas exhibited by Durand-Ruel in 1909.

A canvas from the second great wave of Nymphéas pictures, painted as Monet exhibited forty-eight pond views at Durand-Ruel's Paris gallery. Pads drift across reflections of cloud and sky, the water surface flattened into a pure field of colour with no horizon to orient the viewer.

The pond surface fills the canvas edge to edge, lilies massing in clusters of rose and ivory among dark vegetal reflections. Painted as Monet's eyesight deteriorated, the picture's looser, more saturated handling anticipates mid-century abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-waterl: A horizontal screen of lily pads hovers over reflected sky on the Giverny pond. By 1906 Monet had abolished the bank entirely, treating the water as a self-contained world the eye could enter at any point.

Lily pads and blossoms drift across a pond suffused with warm yellow-green light and cloud reflections, the surface rendered in loose, luminous strokes. Monet painted this canvas in 1907, among the most chromatically adventurous of the Nymphéas series before his later cataract years. The work is in the Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art, Japan.

Pink water-lily blossoms float among green pads on a softly luminous pond rendered in pale blue, grey, and green. No bank or horizon orients the viewer; the water surface becomes the entire world of the canvas. Dated 1908, the painting was offered at Sotheby's London in June 2019.

The bridge's arches dissolve into Thames fog while the smoke-stained palette of the south bank glows behind. Monet worked on the Waterloo and Charing Cross views from a balcony at the Savoy Hotel, juggling many canvases as the light shifted.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-windmi: A girl walks the dyke path between Oostzaan and Zaandam, windmill sails turning over flat polder land. Painted during Monet's 1871 Dutch sojourn after his English exile, the picture's narrow tonal range catches a typical overcast Holland sky.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-woman-: Camille turns under a green parasol while young Jean stands among grasses on a windy bluff, painted from below so the figures rise into a billowing sky. The picture, now in Washington's National Gallery, is Monet's bid to handle the figure outdoors with full plein-air conviction.
collection-of-beauty-claudemonetbanksoft: The Seine winds past the village of Lavacourt across from Vétheuil, where Monet lived from 1878. The riverbank views he painted there mark the brightening palette and broken brushwork of his fully mature Impressionism, made under the strain of his wife Camille's final illness.
collection-of-beauty-clearing-sky-after-: A plate from Hasui's Twenty Views of Tokyo, depicting the Sensō-ji temple complex at Asakusa under fresh snow. A leading figure of the shin-hanga revival, Hasui rebuilt the older ukiyo-e collaboration of designer, carver, and printer to record a modernising city in soft, atmospheric colour woodblock.
collection-of-beauty-cleopatra-and-caesa: Cleopatra steps from the unrolled carpet to confront Caesar at his writing table, the ancient anecdote staged with the polished historicism Gérôme made his trademark. Smooth porcelain finish, archaeologically researched props, and a controlled tonal palette anchor the picture in academic theatre.
collection-of-beauty-clevelandart-1962-3: Cupid, depicted as an ungainly youth with wings and curly hair, sits beside the sleeping Psyche and turns to smirk at the viewer, his bow resting against the gilded couch below. David inverts the convention of the idealised adolescent god, rendering him as a self-satisfied teenager. Painted in Brussels during the artist's exile and dated 1817, the canvas is now at the Cleveland Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-cliffs-at-pourville: Two women sit at the edge of a grassy clifftop at Pourville, looking out over the Channel where numerous sailing vessels are scattered across a pale, mist-softened sea. Monet painted this view during his 1882 stay along the Norman coast between Dieppe and Varengeville, capturing the broad expanse of water under a clouded sky with the cliff and turf in rapid strokes of green and ochre. The canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
