collection-of-beauty-climbing-on-mt-fuji: A group of pilgrims ascends the steep, reddish volcanic slopes of Mount Fuji in single file, their straw hats and blue garments contrasting with the warm brown and orange of the mountain face. This print is plate 34 of Hokusai's celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, first published around 1830, and shows the climbers on the upper reaches of the sacred peak rather than its distant silhouette.
collection-of-beauty-col-tempo-by-giorgi: An elderly woman behind a parapet turns toward the viewer with her mouth half open, holding a small slip inscribed 'Col tempo,' so it goes with time. Painted on canvas around 1506, the work is one of the earliest unflinching portrayals of old age in Italian painting; it hangs in its original frame at the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-der-pok: A colossal goblet, its rim overgrown with vegetation and tiny structures, rises from a mountainous landscape as waterfalls cascade from its moss-covered rim into the valley below; tiny boats sail on the water filling its bowl. Thomas Cole painted this fantastical image in 1833, and it has been interpreted variously as an allegory of civilisation and the natural world. The canvas is in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-expulsi: Adam and Eve flee through a rocky defile as a blazing shaft of light marks the sealed gate of Eden behind them; to the right, the lush, sunlit interior of paradise recedes while storm, volcanic eruption, and a darkened wilderness surround them on the left. Thomas Cole painted this work in 1828 as a pendant to his Garden of Eden, deploying dramatic contrasts of dark and light to underscore the theological gravity of the fall. The canvas is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-the-con: The third canvas in The Course of Empire shows a fictive classical city at its zenith, with porticoes, rotundas, statuary and a triumphal procession crossing a marble bridge above the harbour. Cole painted the five-part allegory for his patron Luman Reed's Greenwich Street picture gallery between 1833 and 1836; Reed died in June 1836 without seeing the series completed.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-the-oxb: Storm clouds and a gnarled dead tree dominate the left half of the canvas while the right opens onto the sunlit Connecticut River looping in a wide oxbow around the cultivated meadows below Mount Holyoke, with Cole's own figure visible sketching among the rocks in the foreground. Painted in 1836 and exhibited that year at the National Academy of Design, the picture is one of the defining statements of the Hudson River School's dual vision of wild nature and settled landscape. It is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-the-tem: The unfinished Doric temple at Segesta in western Sicily stands in a broad valley landscape with mountains and a distant lake behind it, while at lower right a seated figure — Cole himself — sketches the ruins, accompanied by a companion and a donkey. Cole worked up the canvas from drawings made during his European travels, and the composition blends precise archaeological observation with the warm Sicilian light of late afternoon. The painting is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-colonel-john-bulloc: Thomas Gainsborough portrays Colonel John Bullock (1731–1809) full-length in scarlet uniform with green facings, holding his tricorn hat and leaning against a stone plinth, with a black-and-white spaniel seated at his feet. A wooded landscape and a decorative urn occupy the background in the relaxed outdoor manner Gainsborough favoured for his military sitters during the early 1770s.
collection-of-beauty-columbus-and-his-so: Eugène Delacroix depicts Columbus arriving at the Franciscan monastery of La Rábida with his young son Diego, the exhausted boy slumped asleep in a chair while friars in white-and-black habits address the explorer in an arched corridor. Painted in 1838 and held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the canvas presents a scene of weary petition set within the quiet architecture of the Spanish monastery.
collection-of-beauty-confusion-of-tongue: An illustration to Genesis 11 from Doré's English Bible, depicting the workers scattering as the Tower of Babel founders mid-construction. Doré stages the scene with vertiginous architecture and a gulf of stormy sky, exploiting the dense black hatching of wood-engraving to dramatise divine judgement.
collection-of-beauty-constable-osmington: Osmington Bay on the Dorset coast spreads under a sky of broken cumulus, the cliffs running off toward Weymouth. Constable painted the small oil on his 1816 honeymoon at the village of Osmington, where the rector John Fisher had married him to Maria Bicknell that October.
collection-of-beauty-constable-salisbury: A late, emotionally charged view of Salisbury Cathedral seen across the water meadows under a rainbow, painted in the wake of Constable's wife's death. Flickering white highlights, the celebrated Constable snow, animate trees and sky in a picture that fused topographic affection with personal grief.
collection-of-beauty-constable-seascape-: Constable records a squall over a flat shore in rapid, loaded brushwork, the composition almost entirely given over to sky and driving rain with the horizon reduced to a thin dark band. The small oil sketch, executed between 1824 and 1828, exemplifies the empirical attention to weather that Constable called the chiaroscuro of nature.
collection-of-beauty-constable-the-cornf: A boy drinking from a stream beside a flock of sheep on the sunken Fen Lane between East Bergholt and Dedham, a cornfield opening to a church tower in the middle distance. Painted in Constable's London studio in early 1826 and shown at the Royal Academy that summer, the picture was bought by subscription after his death and presented to the National Gallery in 1837.
collection-of-beauty-constable-the-wheat: Reapers and gleaners work a Suffolk wheat field under a high summer sky, painted on Constable's home ground near East Bergholt in 1816. The canvas, now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington with accession 2007.8.27, dates from the months around his marriage and prefigures the six-foot landscapes he began the following year.
collection-of-beauty-constable-view-on-t: Barges and bargemen on the Stour at Dedham, with Dedham church tower distant under broken cloud. The third of Constable's six-foot Stour canvases, exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1822 and now at the Huntington in San Marino.
collection-of-beauty-constantinople-la-m: Aivazovsky envelops a great two-minareted mosque on the Tophane waterfront of Constantinople in luminous morning mist, the domed structure rising into a blue-violet haze while a small boat carries passengers across the calm water below. Painted in 1884, the canvas is held at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Brest.
collection-of-beauty-copley-col-fitch-si: John Singleton Copley depicts Colonel William Fitch in scarlet army uniform beside his rearing chestnut charger, flanked by his two sisters — one in neoclassical white with a veil, the other in dark mourning dress. Painted between 1800 and 1801 in London, the group portrait is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-cornard-wood: An early woodland scene from Gainsborough's Suffolk years, made before he turned full-time to portrait commissions in Bath and London. Drawing on Dutch landscape models, particularly Ruisdael, he threads a sandy track through scrubby oaks under a broken English sky.
collection-of-beauty-cornelia-vetterlein: Joseph Karl Stieler portrays Cornelia Vetterlein as a three-quarter bust, the young woman in a deep-red velvet dress holding a small bunch of blue flowers, with a pearl headband, drop earrings, and a multi-strand necklace. An open landscape with a river valley and a ruined castle forms the background, characteristic of Stieler's romantic portrait manner; the picture is dated 1828.
collection-of-beauty-cornelis-cornelisz-: A monk and a beguine paired in earthy proximity, a stock anticlerical jab popular in late-sixteenth-century Dutch genre. Cornelis softens his Mannerist drawing for the satirical mode, fixing the figures in close focus against a plain dark ground.

Cornelis van Haarlem shows Ixion in extreme foreshortening, his muscular nude body tumbling headlong through flames into Tartarus, limbs splayed against a nearly black ground. The single-figure close-up, painted around 1588 and now at the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam, demonstrates the Haarlem Mannerists' virtuoso command of contorted anatomy and dramatic chiaroscuro.

The defeated Titans tumble headlong from heaven, their nude bodies twisting around each other in a virtuoso lattice of foreshortening. Cornelis treats the mythological subject as an excuse for anatomical display, central to the late-sixteenth-century Haarlem Mannerism he developed with Goltzius and Van Mander.
collection-of-beauty-cornelis-de-vos-el-: A Flemish baroque procession of Bacchus and Ariadne, with putti, satyrs, and tipsy revellers wreathed in vine. De Vos, best known for his crisp portraits of Antwerp burghers, here works closer to Rubens's mythological idiom, ordering the throng with broad, ruddy modelling.
collection-of-beauty-cornelis-springer-a: The Jodenbreestraat in Amsterdam, with the house once occupied by Rembrandt at number 4-6 reimagined in its supposed seventeenth-century guise, the Sint-Antoniesluis at right and the tower of the Zuiderkerk rising behind. Springer, a Romantic topographical painter, treated the city as a chain of historicising stage sets rather than the contemporary streetscape.
collection-of-beauty-corner-in-voyer-d-a: A spring corner of an Asnières park from Van Gogh's Paris years, when he absorbed Impressionism and Neo-Impressionism in the company of Bernard and Signac. Short divided strokes of green, blue, and rose lighten his palette decisively before he carried it south to Arles. The work, dated Spring 1887, is held at the Yale University Art Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-correggio-leda-and-: An erotic mythology painted for Federico II Gonzaga of Mantua as part of a series of Loves of Jupiter intended as a gift to Charles V. Correggio orchestrates Leda's encounter in soft chiaroscuro and a continuous lateral rhythm of figures, the smoky modelling that would inspire Parmigianino and the Carracci.
collection-of-beauty-correggio-ritratto-: A three-quarter-length portrait of a seated woman in a dark overmantle and white chemise, holding a small dish, set before an open landscape. The work is signed with the Latinised "Anton(ius) Laet(us)" and has traditionally been identified as either Veronica Gambara or Ginevra Rangoni. Painted between 1517 and 1518, it is held at the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg and represents Correggio's early mature manner.
collection-of-beauty-countess-siemontkow: A society portrait from Vigée Le Brun's years of exile from revolutionary France, painted in Vienna in 1793 when she received numerous commissions from Polish and Austrian aristocrats. The Countess is shown in a crimson antique-style drapery, wearing a floral wreath over a transparent veil and holding an ornate golden cup. The warm palette and classicising costume carry forward the idiom that had made Vigée Le Brun the pre-eminent portraitist of the Ancien Régime.
collection-of-beauty-courbet-autoportrai: An early self-portrait from Courbet's Romantic-tinged youth, the painter shown smoking a long pipe with hooded eyes and a tilted head. Strong dark-on-dark modelling and a deliberately bohemian air announce the self-mythologising persona he would build through the 1850s.
collection-of-beauty-courbet-l-hallali-d: A vast hunting picture, over five metres wide, in which hounds bring down a stag in deep snow under the eye of a mounted huntsman. Courbet draws on his Franche-Comté upbringing and the Flemish hunt tradition, scaling a popular subject up to the format of history painting in keeping with his Realist programme.
collection-of-beauty-courbet-the-sailboa: Two fishing boats heel through heavy chop, their tan sails straining against a pale sky while the foreground dissolves into churned green water laid on with the palette knife. The canvas dates from around 1869, when Courbet was painting the Channel coast at Étretat and produced some of the most physical seascapes of the nineteenth century. It is in the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute, Williamstown, Massachusetts.
collection-of-beauty-courtyard-with-luna: A small tin-plate painting from Goya's recovery after the illness that left him deaf, drawing on a violent scene he claimed to have witnessed in Zaragoza. Naked inmates wrestle under a barred opening while a warden flogs them, the cell's harsh chiaroscuro foreshadowing the Black Paintings.
collection-of-beauty-coypel-democritus: The laughing philosopher Democritus is shown in close-up, a broad grin revealing his teeth, clad in a reddish-purple robe and holding a small object in his raised hand. Coypel renders the Abderan sage as a lively bust-length figure against a dark ground, using warm chiaroscuro to convey the philosopher's characteristic amusement at human folly. Painted in 1692, the work exemplifies the late-seventeenth-century French taste for half-length figures of antique sages treated in a Flemish-influenced painterly manner.
collection-of-beauty-cranach-madonna-und: The Virgin cradles the Christ Child against a landscape backdrop dominated by a dark fir tree, a German woodland motif that replaces Italian landscape conventions with Saxon scenery. Cranach's panel, dated 1510, balances tender intimacy against the spiky verticals of conifer needles, a hallmark of his court style at Wittenberg. A castle and mountain range recede into the distance behind the figures, giving the devotional image a characteristically Northern Renaissance sense of place.
collection-of-beauty-cristo-en-casa-de-m: A bodegón that folds a domestic kitchen scene around a small framed vignette of Christ admonishing Martha. The young Velázquez sets garlic, eggs and a glistening fish in tight tenebrist focus, signalling the Sevillian taste for moral allegory dressed as still life.
collection-of-beauty-crossing-the-river-: Charon ferries a soul across the underworld river, with paradise and a fiery hell flanking the panel in classic Netherlandish duality. Patinir, credited as the first dedicated landscape painter, expands the mythological subject into a panoramic geography of cliffs, water and atmospheric distance.
collection-of-beauty-crow-and-blossom-by: A solitary crow perches on a flowering branch, the bird's blue-black plumage set against pale petals. Koson's shin-hanga woodblock print refines Edo-period kachō-e bird-and-flower conventions for early-twentieth-century export collectors, prizing economical line and atmospheric ground.
collection-of-beauty-crucifixion-andrea-: The central panel of Mantegna's San Zeno altarpiece predella, showing Christ crucified between the thieves on a rocky knoll. Mantegna deploys archaeological architectural detail and sharp foreshortening, treating the figures with the chiselled severity of Roman relief sculpture.
collection-of-beauty-cult-of-beauty-001: Joanna Hiffernan, Whistler's model and companion, stands at a fireplace mantelpiece in a white muslin dress, her reflection visible in the mirror behind her. She holds a Japanese fan and rests one arm along the mantel shelf, where a blue-and-white vase and pink azalea blossoms are arranged. Conceived as a study in tonal harmony, the picture was exhibited in 1865 and became a touchstone for the Aesthetic movement's pursuit of art for art's sake.
collection-of-beauty-dance-at-bougival: A young couple turns together at an outdoor dance hall near Paris, the woman's red-flowered hat vivid against the dappled crowd. Renoir worked from sittings with Suzanne Valadon and Paul Lhote to anchor Impressionist light within a tightly composed figural scene, painted in 1883 and now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-danceringreen: A ballet dancer in a green tutu tilts and sways mid-performance, her arms lifted and her figure caught from a steep overhead angle characteristic of Degas. Pastel hatching layers powdery greens and warm orange accents, with additional dancers visible in the background, in a composition from Degas's long series devoted to the Paris Opéra.
collection-of-beauty-dancers-1900-degas: Two ballet dancers rest or adjust their costumes, their figures rendered in warm rust and blue-green pastel with Degas's characteristically loose, layered hatching. Worked around 1900 as the artist's eyesight declined, the pastel is notable for its intensified, close-keyed colour and the compressed, cropped framing typical of his late dancer series.
collection-of-beauty-daniel-crommelin-ve: Nine-year-old Daniel Crommelin Verplanck sits against a classical column in a red coat, a squirrel on a chain in his lap, with a landscape background traditionally identified as the Verplanck country house at Fishkill-on-Hudson. John Singleton Copley painted the portrait in 1771, and the work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-daniel-in-the-lion-: Daniel sits among nine lions in a rocky den, hands clasped and gaze lifted upward in prayer as the beasts prowl, yawn, and doze around him. Painted circa 1614–1616 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the canvas demonstrates Rubens's close study of live lions and his ability to combine vigorous animal observation with Counter-Reformation religious conviction.
collection-of-beauty-dans-la-foret-de-fo: Massive oak trunks rise through a sun-dappled interior of the Forest of Fontainebleau, the ground covered in grass and low undergrowth. Renoir painted this woodland study in 1866, early in his career, working in an earthy tonal range indebted to the Barbizon painters who had long used the forest south of Paris as an open-air studio.
collection-of-beauty-dans-la-prairie-by-: Camille Monet reads in a meadow thick with wildflowers, a green parasol raised above her and the blooms dissolving around her in broken, high-keyed brushwork. Monet painted this in 1876, during his Argenteuil years, and first exhibited it in Paris in 1877 — an early demonstration of his method of integrating the figure into the vibrating colour of an outdoor scene.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-bbalrae-teo: Women beating laundry at a stream while a passing scholar peers over a rock, from Kim Hong-do's Danwon pungsokdo cheop. The sheet, ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, is held by the National Museum of Korea and belongs to the album of genre scenes that established his reputation as the great chronicler of everyday Joseon life.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-mudong: Dancing boy with musicians playing flute, drum, and zither, a scene from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do worked in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, with the album of genre studies now held by the National Museum of Korea and considered a benchmark of late 18th-century Joseon painting.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-nongali: Farmers driving an ox-drawn plough through a paddy field, from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do painted the leaf in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, part of the album of agricultural and artisanal scenes held by the National Museum of Korea as a record of common life under King Jeongjo.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-ssireum: Two wrestlers locked in a ssireum hold while spectators ring the contest, divided into upper and lower groups around the action. From the Danwon pungsokdo cheop in the National Museum of Korea, the sheet is ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm and counts as the most reproduced image of Joseon genre painting.
collection-of-beauty-darmstadtmadonna: The Virgin stands on a shell-headed niche above the kneeling family of Burgomaster Jakob Meyer zum Hasen, the Christ Child raising a small hand in blessing. Commissioned in 1526 from Holbein the Younger during his first Basel residency, the panel is now in the Johanniterkirche in Schwäbisch Hall after a long sojourn at Schloss Darmstadt.
collection-of-beauty-david-brutus: The Roman consul Brutus sits in shadow as lictors return the bodies of his sons, executed for treason on his order. David exhibited the picture at the Salon weeks after the storming of the Bastille, and Revolutionary audiences read its civic stoicism as immediate political instruction.
collection-of-beauty-david-dessinant-mar: Jacques-Louis David sketches Marie Antoinette in the tumbril as she is led to the guillotine, the queen seated upright with her hands bound behind her. Painted in 1900 by the Belgian artist Joseph-Emmanuel van den Büssche, the canvas dramatises the famous October 1793 sketch David made from a window on the rue Saint-Honoré.
collection-of-beauty-david-etienne-mauri: General Étienne Maurice Gérard stands in full military dress uniform, medals and decorations prominent on his chest, holding papers in one hand. David painted the portrait in Brussels in 1816, sharing exile with his sitter in the aftermath of the Hundred Days. The canvas, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, shows Gérard against a red drapery with a landscape beyond.
collection-of-beauty-david-napoleon-cros: Bonaparte, wrapped in a billowing orange cloak, reins in a rearing piebald horse on the slopes of the Great St Bernard Pass, the names of Hannibal and Karolus Magnus carved into the rock at his feet. David painted this Neoclassical equestrian portrait in 1800, one of five autograph versions produced over the following decade. The Malmaison version is among the best-known, and records the idealized image of command Napoleon wished to project after his Marengo campaign.
collection-of-beauty-david-portrait-of-m: The chemist Antoine Lavoisier looks up from a manuscript while his wife Marie-Anne stands at his side, her arm resting on the back of his chair; their pneumatic apparatus and glassware are arrayed on a red-draped table. David completed this double portrait in 1788, the year before Lavoisier published the Traité élémentaire de chimie. It entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1977 as accession 1977.10.
collection-of-beauty-david-s-leonidas-an: Jean-Nicolas Laugier's calcographic engraving after David's vast Louvre canvas shows the Spartan king standing bare-chested at the centre, helmeted and holding shield and sword, as warriors around him prepare to defend the pass against Xerxes. David worked on the original painting from 1799 to 1814, and this engraving was published in 1826 by the National Gallery of Art. The dedication below the image reads 'Dédié aux Hellènes.'
collection-of-beauty-david-self-portrait: David portrays himself in three-quarter bust, holding a palette and brushes, wearing a white cravat beneath a reddish-brown coat. The self-portrait, executed in 1794 while he was imprisoned in the Luxembourg Palace after the fall of Robespierre, shows an intent, slightly dishevelled sitter against a plain warm ground. The canvas is now in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-david-the-death-of-: Socrates sits upright on his prison bed, one hand reaching for the cup of hemlock, the other raised in mid-discourse as his grieving disciples surround him. David painted the canvas in 1787 for Charles-Michel Trudaine de la Sabliere, exhibiting it at the Salon as a Neoclassical exemplum of stoic civic virtue; it now hangs at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-david-vilain: The Comtesse Vilain XIIII, identified by the source as Sophie-Louise-Zoé de Feltz (1780–1853), sits in a deep navy velvet dress with white lace frills and a bold orange shawl, her young daughter Marie-Louise standing before her. David painted the double portrait in 1816 during his Belgian exile, one of the most intimate of his late commissions. The neutral interior background is characteristic of his Brussels portrait style.
collection-of-beauty-david-wilkie-chelse: Veterans cluster outside a Chelsea pub as a despatch announcing the victory at Waterloo is read aloud. Commissioned by the Duke of Wellington, Wilkie filled the genre tableau with regimental specificity, prompting crowd-control rails when it was shown at the Royal Academy in 1822.
collection-of-beauty-david-with-the-head: The young David holds out the severed head of Goliath, in which Caravaggio is widely thought to have painted his own features. Made in his fugitive late period and probably sent to Cardinal Scipione Borghese as a plea for pardon, the canvas distils tenebrist drama into a single beam of light.
collection-of-beauty-david98: Anne-Marie-Louise Thélusson, Comtesse de Sorcy, sits in a white gown with a cream embroidered shawl, her powdered hair piled high, against a plain grey wall. David painted the portrait in 1790, the austere setting and clear contour typifying his late pre-Revolutionary female portraits. The picture is now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.
collection-of-beauty-de-gion-brug-te-hon: A woman carrying vegetables pauses on the riverbank beneath the arching wooden piers of the Gion bridge at Hondo in Amakusa, as ducks rest in the shallow water beside her. Kawase Hasui designed this woodblock print in 1924 for Watanabe Shōzaburō's publisher, as part of the series Selected Views of Japan. The composition uses cool blues and the textured structure of the bridge to frame the quiet, low-tide scene.
collection-of-beauty-de-grote-lantaarn-v: Pilgrims climb the steps beneath the giant red lantern that marks the entrance to the Kannon temple at Asakusa. Kasamatsu Shirō issued the design through the Watanabe publishing house at the height of the Shin-hanga revival of traditional ukiyo-e subjects.
collection-of-beauty-de-humani-corporis-: A muscleman écorché stands in a Paduan landscape, layers of musculature peeled back to reveal underlying anatomy. The plate, cut for Vesalius' 1543 treatise, was carved in the Titian workshop circle and revolutionised medical illustration by binding observation to a humanist visual language.

Another of the Fabrica's flayed figures, posed against a continuous Veneto skyline that links the seven plates into a single panorama when arranged in sequence. Vesalius insisted on direct dissection, and the woodcut renders the layered musculature with unprecedented anatomical accuracy.

A deeper écorché stage from the Fabrica, with skin and superficial muscle stripped away to expose the trunk and limbs. Printed in Basel by Oporinus, the plates set a new standard for the integration of artistic skill and dissection-based medical knowledge.

An écorché muscle man from Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, standing upright with the superficial musculature of the trunk and limbs laid bare. Published in Basel in 1543 by Johannes Oporinus, the woodcut plates of the Fabrica set a new standard for anatomical illustration by uniting empirical dissection with the figure conventions of Renaissance art. This plate is held in the Bijzondere Collectie of the Universiteit van Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-de-pruimenboomgaard: A celebrated plum tree in the Kameido garden east of Edo, its blossoming branch thrust across the foreground while visitors stroll behind in a red-suffused dusk. Hiroshige's print from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo was later copied in oil by Van Gogh.
collection-of-beauty-de-rand-van-de-shin: Lanterns burn in the haze of a foggy evening at Ueno Park, with figures passing beside the still water of Shinobazu Pond and a pagoda rising behind. Kasamatsu Shirō was a leading designer of the second Shin-hanga generation; this print was issued by Watanabe Shōzaburō in 1932.
collection-of-beauty-de-warme-bronnen-va: Lit hotels line the Katsura River at the hot-spring town of Shuzenji on the Izu peninsula, with cherry blossom in the foreground. Kasamatsu Shirō's 1937 design pairs the meticulous block-cutting of Shin-hanga with a romanticism inherited from late nineteenth-century landscape prints.
collection-of-beauty-death-of-camilla-by: Horatius stands over the body of his sister Camilla, whom he has just killed for mourning her Curiatii lover, drawn from Livy's account of the early Roman duel. Fyodor Bruni painted the canvas during his Italian pensioner years for the Imperial Academy; it now hangs in the Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-death-of-the-virgin: The Virgin lies dying on a great canopied bed surrounded by the twelve apostles: one reads the office of the dying, another places a taper in her hands, and a tall candlestick stands at the foot of the bed. Engraved around 1470-75, it is one of Schongauer's largest and most influential prints, copied across Europe and studied closely by the young Dürer. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-degas-a-woman-seate: Madame Valpinçon glances aside while a riotous bouquet dominates the canvas, the figure pushed to the edge in a deliberate inversion of conventional portrait hierarchy. Degas treats the flowers with thick impasto, the sitter with restrained drawing-led brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-degas-cafekonzert-s: A café-concert singer performs with mouth open, her black-gloved arm thrust upward in a dramatic gesture, lit from below against a striped backdrop. Degas captured the raw physicality of popular entertainment in this 1878 pastel on canvas, now held at the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg Museum), part of a sustained series exploring the electric artifice of gas-lit stages.
collection-of-beauty-degas-deux-danseuse: Two dancers in white tutus pause at the barre, both bent forward — one tending to her ankle, the other leaning along the rail. The ca. 1879 pastel and gouache on paper, measuring approximately 46 by 67 cm, belongs to the Shelburne Museum, Vermont, and exemplifies Degas's sustained attention to the unstaged moments between exercises.
collection-of-beauty-degas-frau-mit-stad: A woman in a long coat and dark hat is shown from a three-quarter rear angle, her face visible in profile against an open ground. Degas made this 1879 pastel study of a modern Parisienne in street dress, using spare contour lines and restrained colour to evoke the character of anonymous urban life rather than the formality of a commissioned portrait.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-barque-of: Dante and Virgil cross the Stygian marsh in Phlegyas's skiff as the damned claw at the gunwale, drawn from the eighth canto of the Inferno. Delacroix's Salon debut in 1822, the picture was bought by the state and now hangs in the Louvre; the dripping water beads on the nude bodies pay direct homage to Rubens.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-eugene-fe: A nude woman reclines on richly coloured draperies, with a small parrot nearby at the lower edge of the composition. Painted in 1827, the canvas is a small-scale cabinet work by Delacroix combining the Orientalist interest in luxurious interiors with the Romantic preoccupation with the erotic figure, produced in the same period as his large Salon submission The Death of Sardanapalus.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-louis-dor: Louis I, Duke of Orléans lifts the bedclothes to display the lower half of his sleeping mistress to her own husband, the chamberlain Albert Le Flamenc, who fails to recognise her in the half-shadow. Painted in 1825-26 and now in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, the small canvas draws on an anecdote from Brantôme's Vie des dames galantes.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-marc-aure: The dying emperor Marcus Aurelius commends his unworthy son Commodus to a grave circle of Stoic counsellors. Delacroix exhibited the picture at the 1845 Salon, where Baudelaire singled out its sombre violet and ochre palette as the chromatic distillation of Romantic history painting.
collection-of-beauty-delaunay-champdemar: The Eiffel Tower rises in fractured red and ochre planes above the Champ de Mars. Delaunay's Orphic Cubism dismantles the engineered iron icon into prismatic facets, part of his sustained series treating the tower as a modern motif of Parisian light and movement.
collection-of-beauty-delaunay-portuguese: A woman in embroidered folk dress stands amid a swirl of concentric chromatic discs, exotic plants, and stacked vessels, the figure and environment dissolving into interlocking arcs of colour. Robert Delaunay painted this large canvas in 1916, applying the Simultanism he had developed with Sonia Delaunay to a subject rooted in the couple's wartime stay in Portugal.
collection-of-beauty-delftsedonderslag: A wide panoramic record of the destruction wrought by the Delft gunpowder magazine explosion of 12 October 1654, showing collapsed buildings, scattered rubble and groups of survivors picking through the debris in the foreground against a broad, cloud-filled sky. Egbert van der Poel painted the aftermath of the disaster, and returned repeatedly to the subject across several canvases. This example, dated 1654, is held at the National Gallery, London (NG1061).
collection-of-beauty-descent-from-the-cr: Christ's slack body is lowered from the cross onto a white shroud while torchlight picks out Joseph of Arimathea, the weeping Virgin and a clamouring crowd below. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas in the State Hermitage, Saint Petersburg, is the second of Rembrandt's full-scale Passion pictures commissioned by Stadholder Frederick Henry of Orange.
collection-of-beauty-descente-de-croix-r: A workshop variant of Rubens' Antwerp Cathedral altarpiece, with the pale body of Christ lowered diagonally onto a white shroud held by mourners. The composition's coiling diagonals and contrasted flesh tones became a Counter-Reformation template repeated across Catholic Europe.
collection-of-beauty-destruction-of-levi: God smites the sea-monster Leviathan with a sword, the beast writhing in the deep amid lightning-lit clouds. Doré's wood-engraved illustration appeared in his folio English Bible, blending Romantic sublimity with the dense cross-hatching that defined his commercial print style.
collection-of-beauty-die-kreuzabnahme-ru: A Descent from the Cross after Rubens, transposing the master's Antwerp altarpiece composition into reproductive form. The diagonal sweep of Christ's pallid body lowered onto a white winding-sheet preserves the Baroque dramaturgy of the original.
collection-of-beauty-die-landschaft-mit-: Three trees crown a low rise above a flat Dutch polder, with a thunderstorm rolling in from the left and tiny figures fishing and sketching at the margins. Rembrandt's largest landscape etching combines drypoint and engraving to model an unusually dramatic sky.
collection-of-beauty-dolley-madison: Dolley Madison faces the viewer in a low-cut white Empire-waisted gown with a gold chain at her throat and dark hair dressed close to the head. Gilbert Stuart painted this portrait in 1804, when Madison was wife of the Secretary of State, four years before James Madison became president. The work is associated with the White House Historical Association.
collection-of-beauty-domenikos-theotokop: The Virgin, dressed in rose and blue, kneels at a lectern as the Angel Gabriel approaches from the right in a luminous yellow robe, his hand extended in address. Above, a heavenly gathering of figures and cherubim surrounds a radiant burst of light, with the Holy Spirit implied by the golden glow descending between the two figures. El Greco painted this Annunciation in 1614, in the elongated, flickering style characteristic of his final years.
collection-of-beauty-don-juan-by-eugene-: Survivors of a foundered ship draw lots for cannibalism in an open boat, an episode adapted from Byron's poem. Delacroix turns the literary Romantic subject into a study of taut, sea-tossed bodies and overcast Channel light in the wake of Géricault's Raft of the Medusa.
collection-of-beauty-don-quijote-illustr: A lone armoured knight on horseback makes his way through a dense forest, a stream in the foreground and a turreted castle visible through the trees in the distance. The wood-engraved plate, from Gustave Doré's celebrated 1863 illustrated edition of Cervantes' Don Quixote, exemplifies Doré's mastery of atmospheric forest light and fine parallel hatching.

A turbaned figure seated in an ornate stone archway reads or writes, surrounded by scattered books and papers, with the domes and minarets of an Eastern city visible beyond. Signed by Gustave Doré, this wood-engraved plate depicts an Oriental subject and does not belong to the Don Quixote cycle despite the catalogue title.
collection-of-beauty-dong-yuan-mountain-: Attributed to the tenth-century master Dong Yuan, this hanging scroll in ink and light colour on silk imagines a paradise hall of the Immortals deep in the mountains, its pavilions nested among mist-wrapped peaks. The towering vertical composition, over 1.8 metres tall, is held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei.
collection-of-beauty-dong-yuan-rivers-de: A detail from a long handscroll associated with the Southern Tang master, depicting the misted reaches of the Xiao and Xiang rivers in Hunan. Dong Yuan's soft hemp-fibre brushstrokes and graded ink washes established the canonical southern landscape mode followed for centuries.
collection-of-beauty-dore-gustave-la-sai: A Counter-Reformation altar composition showing the Trinity enthroned amid swirling clouds and angels. Rubens deploys his characteristic ruddy flesh tones, golden draperies and dynamic Baroque diagonals to lift the eye toward the heavenly group.
collection-of-beauty-dore-i-had-done-a-h: A wood-engraving from Doré's late illustrated edition of Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, showing the sailor clinging to the rigging after slaying the albatross. Dense parallel hatching builds the storm-charged sea and the cramped vertigo of the crow's nest.
collection-of-beauty-dortordordrecht: A luminous view of the Dutch port of Dordrecht with the packet-boat becalmed at sunrise, openly indebted to Cuyp. Turner dissolves shipping, water and sky into a single golden haze that anticipates his later atmospheric experiments.
collection-of-beauty-dr-deijman-s-anatom: A foreshortened cadaver lies on the dissection table while Dr Joan Deijman, his hands shown above, performs an autopsy on the brain. Painted in 1656 for the Amsterdam Surgeons' Guild as a sequel to the Tulp anatomy of 1632, most of the canvas was destroyed by fire in 1723; only the central fragment survives in the Amsterdam Museum.
collection-of-beauty-dr-richard-price-dd: The dissenting minister and moral philosopher Richard Price sits in his study in clerical black, a letter dated 1784 from Benjamin Franklin open before him. Benjamin West painted the portrait in 1784, the year Price recorded the sittings in his shorthand journal, now held at the National Library of Wales (NLW MS 20721A). This original oil painting remains in the National Library of Wales collection; a later copy is at the National Museum of Wales.
collection-of-beauty-dragomirov-by-repin: A bust-length state portrait of the Russian general and military theorist, hero of the crossing of the Danube in 1877. Repin works in his vigorous realist manner, building the weathered face and braided uniform from loaded, broken strokes.
collection-of-beauty-drawing-of-mules-by: Three mules stand in various poses across the sheet — one shown full length in profile with pack saddle on the left, the others more lightly indicated to the right. A brush drawing in brown wash over graphite, 143 by 257 mm, held at the British Museum, London, it is among the livestock studies Claude Lorrain made from observation, later informing the staffage of his pastoral and harbour compositions.
collection-of-beauty-duchess-of-polignac: Yolande de Polastron, Duchess of Polignac and intimate of Marie Antoinette, is shown half-length in a straw hat adorned with flowers and black feathers, a white gauze dress, and a dark shawl. Her hands rest lightly on a ledge. Vigée Le Brun signed and dated the canvas 1782; the portrait epitomises her characteristically luminous flesh tones and the informal elegance fashionable at the late ancien régime court.
collection-of-beauty-durer-academie-de-f: A pen study of a standing female nude seen from behind, holding a staff from which a veil falls. Made during Dürer's first Italian journey, the sheet shows him grappling with classical proportion and the contrapposto idealised by his Venetian contemporaries.
collection-of-beauty-durer-agnes-durer-m: A rapid pen sketch of Agnes Dürer, the artist's wife, shown in profile with head bowed, wearing the voluminous sleeved dress and headdress typical of Nuremberg burgher fashion. An inscription at the lower edge reads 'mein Agnes' with Dürer's monogram. The sheet is preserved at the Albertina, Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-durer-ecureuil: A watercolour and gouache study of two red squirrels rendered with near-zoological precision, each tuft of fur picked out in fine brush. The sheet belongs to Dürer's lifelong investigation of nature, alongside his hare and great piece of turf.
collection-of-beauty-durer-hieronymus-ho: Hieronymus Holzschuher, Nuremberg patrician and city councillor, is rendered in near-forensic detail: flowing white curling hair, a full beard, and a fur-trimmed cloak. Painted in 1526 and now in the Gemäldegalerie Berlin (inv. 557E), the portrait stands as one of Dürer's most penetrating late character studies, fixing the sitter's frank gaze with an intensity the artist had refined over three decades of observing individual faces.
collection-of-beauty-duse-by-repin: A charcoal portrait of the Italian tragedienne Eleonora Duse, capturing the famously expressive actress in a moment of inward concentration. Repin exploits the chalky drag of charcoal on canvas to model her face while leaving the gown in summary, atmospheric strokes.
collection-of-beauty-e-v-pavlov-by-repin: A documentary group composition showing the surgeon Evgeny Pavlov operating in a St Petersburg theatre, witnessed by gowned colleagues. Repin treats the modern clinic as a secular history piece, marshalling sharp tonal contrasts and a tightly bracketed perspective around the patient.
collection-of-beauty-e1924-3-16-pma2018: A meander of the Epte near Giverny, the small river that fed Monet's water-garden. The canvas is built from short, broken touches that knit foliage, bank and reflection into a single shimmering surface, characteristic of his late 1880s plein-air practice.
collection-of-beauty-eakins-ashbury-w-le: The elderly Philadelphian Ashbury Wright Lee is shown three-quarter length in a dark coat, the loose handling of the face typical of Eakins's late portraiture. Painted around 1905, the canvas belongs to the unsparing commissioned likenesses Eakins produced for friends and acquaintances in his final productive decade.
collection-of-beauty-eakins-selfportrait: Eakins faces the viewer in a dark suit and waistcoat, his grey-streaked hair swept back and a trimmed beard and goatee framing a direct, unsparing gaze. Painted in 1902 as his diploma piece upon election to the National Academy of Design, the canvas is among the rare self-portraits the Philadelphia realist produced in his maturity.
collection-of-beauty-eakins-thomas-wrest: Two male wrestlers grapple on the floor of an athletic gymnasium, their intertwined bodies studied with the anatomical rigour Eakins brought to all his sporting subjects. Secondary figures — a rower in the background and clothed observers at right — extend the spatial depth. The canvas, dated 1899 and now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, reflects Eakins's sustained investigation of the male figure through both observation and photographic study.
collection-of-beauty-east-cowes-castle-t: Racing yachts heel into the wind as they beat to windward through a choppy Solent, with the wooded shoreline of East Cowes Castle beyond. Turner painted this oil on canvas and a companion view for the architect John Nash after staying at the castle, Nash's residence on the Isle of Wight, during the Cowes regatta of 1827, and exhibited both at the Royal Academy in 1828. This canvas is in the Indianapolis Museum of Art; its pendant, showing the regatta boats starting for their moorings, is in the Victoria and Albert Museum.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-1834-19: A nude woman leans forward over a shallow tub, one arm reaching up her back in the act of scrubbing, her face hidden and her weight supported by the rim. The pastel of around 1887, now at the Honolulu Museum of Art, belongs to the bather series Degas pursued through the late 1880s, presenting the toilette as an unselfconscious physical act with no acknowledged observer.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-achille: The artist's younger brother Achille stands in the dark uniform of a French naval cadet, a gold aiguillette at his shoulder and one hand resting on a stone ledge. Painted around 1856-57 while Degas was beginning his Italian study years, the canvas is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-after-t: A nude woman seen from behind and in partial profile raises one arm above her head, drawing a large dark towel across her shoulders as she dries herself. Degas crops the composition tightly around the torso, dissolving the background into warm ochre and blue pastel strokes. The work dates to 1884–1886 and belongs to the sustained series of intimate bather studies Degas produced in that decade.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-at-the-: An open carriage at a country racecourse, with a woman holding an infant under a parasol and a man in a top hat seated behind, while two horses are cropped abruptly at the right edge. Degas places the viewer alongside the Valpinçon family as racehorses and riders move across the wide green field behind them. The painting, dated 1869, is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-ballet-: Dancers in tutus drift through a stage rehearsal, one yawning behind a flat, the ballet master and observers grouped in shadow at the wings. The Metropolitan's version, in oil thinned to a near grisaille, is one of three closely related compositions Degas worked on around 1874, the largest of which appeared in the first Impressionist exhibition that April.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-before-: Several jockeys on thoroughbreds mill in loose formation across open ground, their mounts shown in varying gaits. Degas painted the small panel between 1882 and 1884, a period in which he drew on recently published stop-action photographs to sharpen his understanding of the horse in motion. The work is held by the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-chasse-: Young ballerinas gather in a high-windowed rehearsal room of the Paris Opera, one working at the barre while the others wait their turn or adjust their dress. This small oil, roughly 19 by 27 centimetres and painted around 1870-1872, stands at the very beginning of Degas's ballet series, in which the company's working spaces served as a laboratory for studies of light and arrested movement. It came to the Metropolitan Museum of Art with the H. O. Havemeyer bequest in 1929.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-dancers: Two dancers in blue tutus stretch along a barre, one reaching forward and one turned away, against a warm orange ground that fills the composition. Degas worked the canvas around 1900, the broadly handled contours and saturated colour characteristic of his late style. The painting hangs in the Phillips Collection, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-in-a-ca: The actress Ellen Andrée and the engraver Marcellin Desboutin sit side by side at a marble café table, the woman staring blankly past a tall glass of cloudy absinthe. Originally exhibited under the title Dans un café and reset as L'Absinthe at its London showing of 1893, the picture was painted at the Nouvelle-Athènes in Pigalle and is now in the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-place-d: Ludovic-Napoléon Lepic, cigar in hand and umbrella tucked under his arm, strides across the windswept square with his two daughters and a borzoi, a solitary man cropped at the left edge. Painted in 1875 and now at the Hermitage by way of the Gerstenberg collection and Soviet trophy art transfers, the picture places Lepic's silhouette over the statue of Strasbourg, then a recent emblem of loss to Prussia.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-portrai: Hortense, the young daughter of Degas's childhood friend Paul Valpinçon, stands at a richly embroidered table and holds a small object in her hands, returning the viewer's gaze with quiet composure. Painted in 1871, the portrait is celebrated for the vivid textile in the foreground set against the plain floral wallpaper behind the girl. It is now at the Minneapolis Institute of Art.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-bal: In a rehearsal room of the old opera house on the rue Le Peletier, dancers in white tutus practise at the barre and rest along the back wall while the ballet master Jules Perrot leans on his long staff at the centre. Degas worked on the oil on canvas between 1871 and 1874, repeatedly revising the poses. One of the founding pictures of his ballet series, it now hangs in the Musee d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-bel: Degas's aunt Laura Bellelli stands in mourning black with her two daughters in their apartment, her husband Gennaro seated and turned away at right, a framed chalk portrait of her recently deceased father hanging on the wall behind her. Begun during the artist's 1858–59 stay with the family and completed in Paris, the large canvas is now the centrepiece of the early Degas rooms at the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-mil: Three women crowd together around a hat being trimmed and adjusted, their figures loosely rendered against a warm, brushy background. Degas returned repeatedly to the millinery subject through the 1890s, and the 1898 canvas shows the late thickening of paint into broad, almost tapestry-like surfaces. It entered the Saint Louis Art Museum in 2007.

A woman in a green dress leans over a counter to inspect a wide-brimmed hat perched on its stand, while other trimmed hats crowd the foreground on their stands. Degas reworked the canvas between 1879 and 1886, leaving the figure's status — customer or shopworker — deliberately ambiguous. The painting entered the Art Institute of Chicago in 1933.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-orc: Degas looks into the orchestra pit of the Paris Opera, where the bassoonist Desire Dihau, a friend of the painter, dominates the foreground among portrait heads of fellow musicians, while the stage above is reduced to a frieze of cropped dancers' legs and glowing tutus. Painted around 1870, the oil on canvas now hangs in the Musee d'Orsay. Its abrupt cropping and off-axis viewpoint anticipate the compositional devices of the ballet pictures Degas pursued over the following two decades.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-tub: A nude woman stands in a shallow metal tub, bending forward as she sponges the bath, her body modelled in chalky strokes against a blue-grey ground. Degas exhibited the 1886 pastel with the rest of his bather suite at the Eighth and final Impressionist Exhibition that year, drawing critics' attacks on the bluntness of the poses.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-ukraini: Three dancers in embroidered Ukrainian folk costume — white blouses, coloured skirts, and flowered headdresses — turn and lean together in a close formation caught mid-step. Degas worked the pastel around 1899, the loose, vigorous strokes and pastel palette typical of his late works on paper. The sheet is held by the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-waiting: On a bench at the Paris Opera, a young dancer in a tutu bends to clasp her ankle beside a woman in black street clothes with a furled umbrella, presumably her mother or chaperone, who stares at the floor. Degas drew the pastel around 1882, setting the silent pair against steeply raked floorboards seen from above. Since 1983 the sheet has been owned jointly by the Norton Simon Art Foundation in Pasadena and the J. Paul Getty Museum.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-germain-hilai: Dancers in white tutus rehearse in a large, light-filled studio, a seated violinist accompanying them at the left while tall windows open onto a view of rooftops and trees. Degas captures the informal rhythm of preparation, the figures scattered across the room in varied poses. The 1873 painting, titled Ballettprobe, is held by the Fogg Museum, Harvard.

Dancers in white tutus rehearse on a sparsely set stage while the ballet master gestures from the right and men in dark coats - the subscribers admitted backstage - watch from chairs at the wings. Executed around 1874 in pastel over a brush-and-ink drawing on paper, the sheet exploits the steep downward view from a stage box, pushing the floor up against the picture plane in a manner Degas absorbed in part from Japanese prints. One of three closely related versions of the composition, it belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

A nude woman sits on a yellow armchair, her head tilted back as a maid standing behind her draws a comb through her loose reddish-brown hair. Degas treated this gesture of intimate grooming in pastel and oil through the mid-1880s, an extension of his series of women at their toilette. The work dates to around 1885.

A nude woman seen from behind raises both arms to brush her auburn hair, a white cloth gathered beside her. Degas worked the composition in pastel on cardboard around 1885, the warm orange ground and tightly cropped viewpoint concentrating attention on the body's movement. The work belongs to his sustained series of women at their toilette.

A nude crouches in a shallow zinc tub sponging her neck, beside a marble-topped washstand whose pitcher and brushes are seen from a sharply tilted angle. Degas drew the pastel on heavy wove paper in 1886 and showed it at the Eighth Impressionist Exhibition that May; the sheet entered the Musee d'Orsay as one of his most accomplished bather compositions.

A café-concert singer leans forward at the footlights, her gloved hands shaped like a dog's paws as she performs the popular novelty song known as the Chanson du chien. Worked up between 1875 and 1877 in gouache and pastel over a monotype base, the sheet belongs to a group of small night-life scenes Degas made of the open-air café-concerts along the Champs-Élysées.

A seated nude faces the viewer, wrapping herself in a white cloth against a floral-patterned background, her loose reddish hair falling around her shoulders. Degas rendered the figure in pastel with the soft, chalky hatching characteristic of his bathing series, dating the sheet 1884.

The mixed-race acrobat Anna Olga Albertina Brown, billed as Miss La La, hangs by her teeth from a rope below the Cirque Fernando's painted dome. Degas attended several performances in January 1879 and produced sketches and an oil study before this canvas, his only circus subject, went on view at the Fourth Impressionist Exhibition.

A nude woman seen from behind kneels and reaches up to dry her neck with a white cloth, set against a colourful backdrop of textiles and furnishings. Degas worked the composition in pastel, building layered hatchings characteristic of his late bathing series; the work is dated 1898.

A ballerina holds a low curtsy at the front of the stage, bouquet in hand, the corps blurred behind her in the footlight haze. Degas returned obsessively to such after-performance moments around 1878, drawn to the gap between drilled spectacle and momentary stillness.

Four ballerinas in vivid blue tutus stand in a group, adjusting their shoulders and costumes, their faces largely averted from the viewer. Degas worked this pastel from the 1870s onward; the work, titled Tänzerinnen in Blau, hangs in the Pushkin Museum in Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-edge-of-the-forest-: Tall dark tree trunks rise through a shadowed forest interior, with a small lone figure visible among them and glimpses of white buildings through the haze beyond. Painted in 1891 and held at the Yale University Art Gallery, the canvas is characteristic of Inness's late tonalist landscapes, in which light and atmosphere dissolve solid forms into muted, unified fields of colour.
collection-of-beauty-edinburgh-ngs-singe: Gertrude, Lady Agnew of Lochnaw lounges in a bergère, her white satin gown and lilac sash dashed in with bravura wet-into-wet brushwork. The portrait's frank gaze and easy elegance made Sargent's reputation when shown at the Royal Academy in 1893.
collection-of-beauty-edmund-blair-leight: The philosopher Abelard instructs his young pupil Heloise in an open medieval colonnade, both figures absorbed in the illuminated book resting on her lap. Edmund Blair Leighton painted this chivalric-romantic subject in 1882, rendering the costumes and stone architecture with the fastidious detail that characterised his Academy submissions.

A family taking refuge in a fortified chamber as conflict rages outside, painted in Blair Leighton's polished late-Victorian historical idiom. Stained-glass light, careful armour detail and a contained narrative tension are the artist's stock in trade.

A young woman in 18th-century dress pauses on the steps of a Georgian doorway while a man above her leans in to speak, the encounter framed by classical columns. Edmund Blair Leighton painted this period genre scene in 1894, capturing a moment of polite social exchange with his characteristic precision of costume and architectural detail.

Three women in 18th-century dress gathered at a doorway examine goods offered by a male pedlar bearing a basket, the scene animated by the exchange of ribbons or lace. Edmund Blair Leighton painted the work in 1902 under the full title Ribbons and Laces for Very Pretty Faces, rendering costume and setting with his characteristic attention to period detail.

A Crusader knight in chainmail lays his sword upon an altar as a woman in a green gown and white veil kneels beside him in prayer within a stone chapel. The work was known only through a 1908 black-and-white photogravure for over seventy-five years before the original canvas was rediscovered; it was sold at Christie's, London, in December 2013.

A young man in a rowboat reaches up toward a woman standing beside an iron garden gate on a brick wall, the two figures caught in a moment of clandestine exchange beside a still waterway. Edmund Blair Leighton painted the scene in 1893 with his customary period accuracy of dress and setting.

A lutenist seated at a courtly lady's feet as the last chord fades, an invented scene that nods to Tristan and Iseult and Paolo and Francesca without illustrating either. Blair Leighton uses the lull after music to suggest dangerous feeling held in check.

A young woman in a rust-red gown leans against the stone parapet of a coastal castle, gazing out over the sea, while three attendant figures — a seated woman with a book and a standing companion — remain behind her on the sun-lit rampart. The work, signed and dated 1912, depicts a subject that sources link to the legend of Tristram and Isolde, and the painting was subsequently sold at auction by Sotheby's.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-031: On the terrace of a fashionable suburban restaurant, the proprietor's son leans intimately toward a lady lunching alone. Painted en plein air during Manet's late embrace of Impressionist technique, the canvas glows with dappled sunlight and feathery, summery greens.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-at-th: Café patrons gather around a table in a Parisian brasserie, observed with the cool detachment Manet brought to modern social life. A man in a top hat and a woman drinking from a glass are among the loosely rendered figures, their faces emerging from sketchy, broadly brushed handling. The high horizon and cropped edges signal Manet's increasingly Impressionist-inflected approach, painted around 1879.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-boati: A man in a straw hat and white clothes handles the tiller of a small sailboat while a woman in a blue dress reclines at the stern, her back turned to the viewer. The saturated blue of the water fills the entire background, creating the flat, cropped composition that reveals Manet's debt to Japanese prints. Painted at Argenteuil in 1874, the work is now in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-by-he: Fantin-Latour's 1867 portrait presents Édouard Manet three-quarter length in a dark coat and top hat, gloves and cane in hand, against an austere neutral ground. The characterisation — assured, dandified, self-possessed — accords with the Manet Fantin-Latour would place at the centre of his 1870 group canvas Un atelier aux Batignolles. The portrait is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-der-f: A bouquet of white lilacs leans from a clear glass vase against a darkened ground, the flowers worked in loaded, gestural strokes. The picture belongs to the small floral still lifes Manet painted at the very end of his life, when illness had reduced his ambitions to flowers brought by visitors.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-kears: Two warships engage in the English Channel off Cherbourg: the burning Confederate raider Alabama, struck by Union fire, lists amid billows of smoke as the Kearsarge stands off to the right. French spectator boats occupy the foreground, including a sailing vessel whose scale underscores the distance of the action. Manet painted the scene in 1864, immediately after the battle, in a broadly brushed marine style that belongs to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-le-ch: A young woman — identified as Victorine Meurent — sits before iron railings above the cutting of the Gare Saint-Lazare, a puppy cradled in her arms and a closed book in her lap, her gaze meeting the viewer's directly. Beside her, a small girl in white leans against the railings to watch a passing train, visible only as a cloud of steam below. The painting was exhibited at the Salon of 1874 and is now held at the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

Two angels support the slumped body of the dead Christ, his pallid torso lit against shadow. Manet borrows a traditional Lamentation type but flattens modeling and exposes brushwork in a way that scandalized the 1864 Salon, where critics also faulted the placement of the side wound on the wrong flank.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-olymp: A reclining nude courtesan meets the viewer's gaze with cool defiance, attended by a Black maid bearing flowers from a client. Manet flattens form with stark lighting and sharp tonal contrasts, scandalising the 1865 Salon by transposing Titian's Venus into contemporary Parisian demi-monde.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-the-p: A young woman sits alone at a café table, her chin resting on her hand and a brandy-soaked plum in a small glass before her, her gaze directed away. Manet renders her absorbed, suspended stillness in loose brushwork, her pink blouse and feathered black hat set against a red banquette and warm wood panelling. Painted around 1877, the work is held at the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-ans: Gaertner's 1855 painting records the rear façades of the middle-class houses lining the Schloßfreiheit along the Spree, with the dome of the palace rising behind and strollers along the opposite bank. The source description notes gold and silver shops and warehouses fronting the row, overshadowed by Schinkel's Building Academy to the right. The entire street was demolished in 1896 to make way for the Wilhelmine Monument to Emperor Wilhelm I.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-ber: The Brüderstraße on the Spreeinsel in Berlin-Mitte recedes between rows of plastered townhouses toward the tower of the Petrikirche. Gaertner painted the view in 1863, still working in the precise Berlin Biedermeier vedute mode he had practised since the 1820s.

Gaertner's 1830 view of the Klosterstraße shows the wide Berlin street under a dramatic cloudy sky, with classical and older buildings lining both sides and a church tower rising in the distance. Small figures — pedestrians and a mounted rider — animate the foreground. The composition exemplifies the precise vedute style Gaertner had developed since the 1820s for documenting Berlin's urban fabric.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-die: Gaertner's 1831 painting records a narrow Berlin street lined with colourful tenements and workshops, its cobbles busy with tradespeople, pedestrians and dogs. A church spire rises at the far end, framing the receding perspective. The work demonstrates Gaertner's characteristic method of combining precise architectural observation with vivid street-level genre incident.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-unt: Berlin's grand boulevard stretches past the equestrian statue of Frederick the Great, with the Königliche Oper on the right and the dome of the Stadtschloss closing the vista. Gaertner, the city's pre-eminent vedutista, charts the Prussian capital with architect's precision under a clear summer light.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gartner-002: One panel of Gaertner's six-part 1834 Panorama von Berlin, painted from the roof of the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche, surveys the city's rooftops looking westward toward the Lustgarten and the dome of the Berliner Dom, with the colonnade of the Altes Museum visible to the left. The Gothic parapet of the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche occupies the immediate foreground, grounding the viewer's elevated vantage point. The panorama is one of the most complete topographical records of Berlin in the Biedermeier era.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-1893-t: A skeletal figure clutches its head beneath a blood-red sky on a fjord-side bridge, mouth agape in soundless anguish. Munch combined oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard to externalise an attack of existential dread, anchoring the visual vocabulary of European Expressionism.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-1922-s: Painted from the terrace of Munch's Ekely estate outside Oslo, this nocturne reduces landscape to broad zones of indigo, snow-white and shadow. A revisitation of his 1893 motif, it trades earlier symbolism for a quieter, late-career meditation on solitude under the winter sky.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-bathin: Multiple nude men stand and move near the water's edge in this large canvas painted at the Baltic coastal resort of Warnemünde between 1907 and 1908. Munch celebrated sun, sea and male vitality through vigorous, gestural brushwork and a warm, luminous palette. The work is part of his series on the ages of man and is held at the Ateneum in Helsinki as part of the Finnish National Gallery collection.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-jealou: A bearded man stares from the foreground in sickly pallor while behind him a nude central figure and a clothed woman are visible in the background. Munch returned to the jealousy motif repeatedly across his career, treating the triangular composition as an emblem of erotic anxiety. This version, dated 1913–15, is held at the Munch Museum, Oslo.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-the-br: The English violinist Eva Mudocci, with whom Munch had a brief affair, gazes from a cloud of dark hair in this lithograph. Drawn directly onto stone in Berlin and printed in soft black, it is among Munch's most tender portraits, sometimes called his Mona Lisa.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-train-: Tall pine trees frame a sweeping fjord landscape at dusk, while a plume of white locomotive steam billows through the foliage in the middle ground. Sailing boats dot the calm water and islands lie in the distance beneath a pink-violet sky. Painted in 1900 and now in the Munch Museum, Oslo, the work turns industrial incursion into an organic element within a richly coloured natural scene.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-two-hu: A woman in a long white dress and a man in a dark suit stand with their backs to the viewer on a vividly coloured rocky shore, both gazing out to sea. The couple are painted close together yet communicating nothing, Munch's enduring image of emotional isolation. This version, dated 1906–08, is held at the Busch-Reisinger Museum, Harvard Art Museums.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-vampir: A red-haired woman bends over a man, her lips at his neck while her hair cascades like flowing blood. Originally titled Love and Pain, the picture was rechristened by Munch's Symbolist circle and became a key motif of his Frieze of Life.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-weepin: A nude woman lies face-down on a red-orange surface, her dark hair obscuring her face entirely and her limbs spread across the couch in an attitude of complete abandonment or grief. Munch renders the figure raw and unidealised, channelling emotional collapse through agitated brushwork and a heated palette of reds and oranges. The canvas, dated 1913–14, is held at the Munch Museum, Oslo.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-americ: Pairs of animals — lions, horses, zebras, goats and many others — are gathered on the hillside around the great wooden ark beneath a stormy, darkening sky. Edward Hicks, the Quaker minister and sign painter from Bucks County, Pennsylvania, based this 1846 canvas on the Genesis flood narrative, rendering the scene with the flat, vivid colours characteristic of his folk-art manner.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-painti: Thomas Hicks portrays his older cousin Edward Hicks seated in three-quarter pose, palette and brushes in hand, with a canvas showing animals and children from the Peaceable Kingdom visible on the easel beside him. Thomas Hicks painted the homage in 1839, when Edward was in his fifty-ninth year. The work commemorates the elder Hicks's lifelong devotion to his signature subject, drawn from Isaiah's prophecy of natural harmony.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-peacea: A lion lies beside a lamb, a leopard with a kid, and a child rests his hand on the leopard's neck, while in the left background William Penn signs his 1681 treaty with the Lenape on the Delaware. Hicks, a Quaker minister and sign painter, made roughly a hundred versions of the Isaiah 11 prophecy as an emblem of Pennsylvania's promise.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-the-co: Cattle, horses and other livestock are paraded in the foreground of a broad pastoral landscape, with white fences, bare-branched trees and farm buildings stretching towards rolling hills behind them. Edward Hicks painted this farmstead view in 1848 in the same folk-art manner he brought to his Peaceable Kingdom series — carefully observed animals set within an ordered, sunlit countryside.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hopper-night: An anonymous pedestrian crosses an empty street under a sharply raking street lamp, watched from a high, vertiginous viewpoint. The etching, published in Shadowland magazine, sets out the lonely urban geometry Hopper would later expand into his great oil paintings.
collection-of-beauty-edward-savage-georg: Edward Savage depicts Washington in a close three-quarter bust portrait, the sitter wearing a dark coat with lace cravat against a warm neutral ground. Painted around 1796, this intimate format draws on Savage's earlier life studies of the president and presents Washington in civilian dress rather than military uniform. The portrait is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-edward-savage-the-w: George Washington, dressed in military uniform and seated at a table, examines a large map alongside Martha Washington and her two grandchildren in an interior setting hung with red drapery, with an enslaved attendant visible in the background. A globe stands to the left, reinforcing the statesmanlike theme. Savage worked on the canvas from 1789 to 1796 and subsequently engraved a widely circulated print after it; the painting is now at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-el-beso-pinacoteca-: A young couple embrace on a stone staircase, the woman's blue gown and the man's red tights forming the colours of the French and Italian flags. Hayez's most popular canvas became a coded emblem of the Risorgimento and the alliance behind Italian unification.
collection-of-beauty-el-caballero-de-la-: A bearded Castilian gentleman in black lays his right hand flat against his chest in a deliberate gesture, the gold hilt of his sword visible below. Painted around 1580 and now in the Prado, the portrait is often read as an oath of loyalty and is among the most reproduced images of the Spanish Golden Age.
collection-of-beauty-el-coloso: A naked giant rises behind a mountain ridge as a panicked crowd and herds flee across the plain below. Long attributed to Goya and tied to the Peninsular War, the picture stages collective terror with the bituminous darkness of his late, troubled imagination.
collection-of-beauty-el-dos-de-mayo-de-1: Madrileños with knives drag Mamluk cavalrymen of the imperial guard from their rearing horses in the Puerta del Sol. Companion to The Third of May, Goya's painting reconstructs the chaos of the popular uprising against Napoleon's occupation in tumbling diagonals.
collection-of-beauty-el-expolio-por-el-g: Christ in a vivid red robe stands hemmed in by jeering soldiers as a workman bores holes for the nails in the cross at his feet. Painted between 1577 and 1579 for the sacristy of Toledo Cathedral, El Greco's first major Spanish commission compresses the crowd into a vertical wall of heads behind the still, gazing figure.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-christ-as-: Christ raises his right hand in benediction and rests his left on a dark orb, his face framed by a luminous halo against a near-black ground. The panel is part of the Apostolado series painted by El Greco, preserved in the Museo del Greco in Toledo, where the Saviour heads a cycle of the twelve apostles.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-domenikos-: Christ swings his cord of whips through the money-changers in a vaulted Renaissance temple, figures recoiling around him in pinks, blues, and acid greens. Painted probably before 1570 during El Greco's Venetian apprenticeship and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the panel is the earliest of his several versions of the subject.

The Trinitarian preacher Hortensio Félix Paravicino sits upright in a carved chair in his black and white habit, a book open on his lap. Painted in 1609 and now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the portrait depicts the court preacher to Philip III, who celebrated El Greco in verse.

An elderly man in a dark robe trimmed with fur sits before an open book spread on a table, his hands resting on its pages. Painted between circa 1610 and 1614 in El Greco's late manner, the portrait is identified as the Toledan canon and historian Dr. Francisco de Pisa.

Jerome appears as a bare-chested penitent in half-length, holding a crucifix in his right hand and a stone in his left, a skull and hourglass placed before him and a red cardinal hat visible to his side. Dated to around 1610 and held at the Hispanic Society of America in New York, the painting belongs to El Greco's late series of the penitent saint in contemplation.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-portrait-o: A bald, white-bearded man in a white ruff collar and dark robe trimmed with fur turns toward the viewer, the lined face rendered with El Greco's characteristic psychological directness. Painted between 1595 and 1600, the portrait has traditionally been described as a presumed self-portrait, though the identification of the sitter remains uncertain.

A young man in a starched white ruff and dark doublet holds the brushes and palette of a painter, his gaze level and composed. Painted between 1600 and 1605, the portrait shows Jorge Manuel Theotocópuli, El Greco's son and workshop heir, who would later complete several of the master's late altarpieces in Toledo.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-the-burial: Saints Stephen and Augustine lower the armoured body of Don Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo into his tomb while a celestial throng receives his soul above. Painted between 1586 and 1588 for the parish church of Santo Tomé in Toledo, where it still hangs over the count's actual grave, the canvas splits earthly funeral and heavenly vision across a single vertical axis.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-the-vision: Saint John, robed in blue, raises his arms toward a turbulent sky as nude figures surge upward grasping a billowing green cloth at the opening of the fifth seal. Painted between 1608 and 1614 and now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, the unfinished canvas is cited as an acknowledged source for Picasso's Demoiselles d'Avignon.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-view-of-to: A spectral storm rolls over the Spanish hill city, with the Alcázar and cathedral picked out against acid-green hills and ink-black clouds. One of the earliest pure landscapes in Western art, El Greco rearranged Toledo's topography for symbolic, almost visionary effect.
collection-of-beauty-el-jaleo-singer: A near life-size scene of a flamenco dancer mid-stride before a row of seated musicians, lit by raking footlights that cast huge shadows on the back wall. Sargent worked the picture up from sketches made in Spain, marrying Velázquez's tonal economy to a thoroughly modern sense of theatrical staging.
collection-of-beauty-el-jardin-de-las-de: Bosch's triptych unfolds from the Garden of Eden through a teeming central panel of nude pleasure-seekers to a hellscape of musical instruments turned instruments of torture. Painted for a Habsburg patron, its inventory of fantastical hybrids has resisted definitive iconographic decoding for five centuries.
collection-of-beauty-el-jardin-del-amor-: Elegant couples flirt and recline in a balustraded garden while putti scatter roses overhead. Painted soon after Rubens's marriage to Helena Fourment, the scene celebrates conjugal pleasure in his late, pearly Flemish manner and now hangs in the Prado.
collection-of-beauty-el-tres-de-mayo-by-: A Spanish patriot in a luminous white shirt flings out his arms before the firing squad of Napoleonic troops on Príncipe Pío hill. Commissioned after the French withdrawal, Goya treats martyrdom with the brutal lighting and crude paint of modern history painting.
collection-of-beauty-elisabeth-louise-vi: Painted during Vigée Le Brun's émigré years in Saint Petersburg, the Russian countess wears a soft white gown and a velvet wrap. The artist's Russian sitters helped sustain her career through the Revolution and account for many of her finest late portraits.

Hubert Robert, the celebrated painter of ruins, is shown half-length in a dark coat with a red-lapelled collar and a loose white cravat, holding a palette and brushes. His grey curly hair and alert, upward gaze animate this intimate portrait of a fellow artist. Vigée Le Brun painted this in 1788, shortly before the Revolution disrupted the social world both painters shared.

A half-length portrait of the marine painter Joseph Vernet, palette and brushes in hand, in a powdered wig and dark coat against a neutral ground. Vigée Le Brun renders the older painter with the soft modeling and warm flesh tones that defined her late-Ancien Régime studio practice, treating him as a colleague rather than a patron.
