A mustachioed musician in a feathered hat holds a viola da gamba and bow, glancing sideways with a hint of a smile against a dark background. The half-length musician type, here clothed in blue satin, continues the format Honthorst popularised after returning from Rome in 1620. The work is dated 1631 and hangs in the Lviv National Art Gallery.

Margaretha Maria de Roodere sits before an easel, palette in hand, pointing to the portrait she has painted while a figure in black stands behind her to the right. Honthorst signed and dated the picture in 1652, presenting his sitter as a practising painter — one of the few documented women artists working in Utrecht in the mid-seventeenth century.

A laughing young woman in a feathered cap leans toward a richly dressed gallant while an older bawd counts coins behind them. Signed and dated 1625, the panel is in the Centraal Museum, Utrecht, and ranks among the earliest Northern transpositions of Caravaggio's candlelit bordello scenes into the Dutch market.

A young blonde woman in a white chemise with blue and yellow drapery plays a guitar, looking sideways with parted lips. Painted around 1624, the canvas is one of Honthorst's Utrecht single-figure musicians in which the open neckline and direct presentation pitch the work between portrait and genre piece for the cabinet market.
collection-of-beauty-gerechtigkeit-1537: Justice personified as a nude woman holding sword and scales, a humanist subject Cranach's Wittenberg workshop produced in many versions for Saxon patrons. The sinuous body type and dark ground are signatures of his late mythological and allegorical nudes.
collection-of-beauty-gerhard-von-kugelge: A bust-length portrait of the Romantic landscapist Caspar David Friedrich, showing him with reddish-blonde curly hair, a short beard, and an open coat with a green cravat against a loosely sketched landscape ground. Painted in 1808 by his contemporary Gerhard von Kügelgen, the work is housed in the Hamburger Kunsthalle and represents the canonical early image of Friedrich at the outset of his mature career.
collection-of-beauty-gericaulthorseman: A mounted officer of Napoleon's Imperial Guard wheels his rearing grey horse against a smoke-streaked battlefield sky, sabre drawn and leopard-skin saddle cloth billowing. Géricault's Salon debut of 1812, made when the artist was twenty-one, announced a new Romantic energy in French painting through Rubensian colour and a kinetic diagonal that broke decisively from Davidian decorum.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-an-idyll-185: An early pastoral by Gérôme in the vein of his Néo-Grec circle, reaching back to Anacreontic and Pompeian models. Slender nudes, shallow stage-like space and porcelain-cool color place the picture closer to his Greek Interior than to his later Orientalist scenes.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-cave-canem: A near-nude crouching male figure huddles in a doorway beneath a stone tablet inscribed CAVE CANEM, a chain lying on the ground beside him. Gérôme sets the scene in a sun-drenched Roman streetscape with tightly rendered architectural detail. Completed in 1881, the work is held in the musée Jean-Léon Gérôme in Vesoul.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-eminence-gri: Capuchin friar François Leclerc du Tremblay descends a staircase at the Palais-Cardinal, courtiers bowing to the grey habit while ignoring the man inside it. Gérôme stages the scene as silent political theatre, contrasting the friar's coarse wool against polished marble and gilded livery.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-execution-of: A cold December morning at the Luxembourg gardens: Napoleon's marshal lies face down in the mud as the firing squad turns away, posters of his condemnation peeling on the wall behind. Gérôme uses an austere, almost reportorial composition to deliver a quiet indictment of Bourbon vengeance.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-femme-circas: A bust-length study of a Circassian woman whose features are partially obscured by a dark veil, her eyes meeting the viewer directly as she holds a long staff. She wears a richly embroidered blue robe with gold decoration. Signed by Gérôme and dated 1876, the work — oil on canvas, 40.7 × 32.6 cm — is now in the Lusail Museum's collection.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-horse: A single chestnut Arabian horse is led at a spirited trot through a narrow North African street by a handler in white, while three robed figures watch from the left and a veiled woman looks down from an upper window. Gérôme's characteristic ethnographic precision is on full display in the ornate carved woodwork of the mashrabiyya balcony and the sun-bleached plasterwork. The picture, dated 1867, belongs to the Haggin Museum in Stockton, California.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-saddl: A white Arab horse fitted with an ornate embroidered saddle stands in a Cairo courtyard while a buyer in colourful Eastern dress haggles with an elderly merchant at a saddler's stall. Gérôme renders the horse and its richly decorated tack with meticulous academic precision, set against the shaded stone arcades he observed on his Egyptian travels. The work, dated 1883, is held at the Haggin Museum, Stockton, California.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-the-a: An elderly sculptor — likely Gérôme himself — leans intently over a white marble seated figure, comparing it with a live nude model posed beside it on a low platform. The studio is filled with props and sculptural studies, articulating Gérôme's lifelong interest in the relationship between sculpture and the living body. Painted in 1895, the work is in the Haggin Museum, Stockton, California.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-unfol: A solitary, face-veiled standard-bearer in a white robe stands before an ornate mosque entrance holding an enormous green and red ceremonial banner aloft on its staff. Gérôme, working from his Egyptian observations, renders the carved stone portal and embroidered textile with characteristic precision. Titled also The Standard Bearer, the painting dates to 1876 and belongs to the Haggin Museum, Stockton, California.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-l-entree-du-: Christ rides a donkey toward the walls of Jerusalem under a cloudy sky, while a large crowd gathers to receive him, some holding palm fronds. Gérôme's panoramic composition, painted in 1897, sets the Gospel narrative in a topographically plausible Levantine landscape drawn from his Holy Land travels. The painting is housed in the Musée Jean-Léon Gérôme in Vesoul, France.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-painting-bre: An ancient Greek artisan paints a terracotta Tanagra figurine, the Latin title declaring that 'painting breathes life into sculpture'. The picture is Gérôme's manifesto for polychromy, arguing that the white marbles museums revered were originally as colored as this little figure.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-summer-after: A shaded lakeside glade in late summer light, with anglers at the water's edge and a small boat visible on the still surface beyond. Gérôme renders the wooded atmosphere with careful tonal control, producing a quiet landscape far removed from his orientalist subjects. The painting dates to circa 1895.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-the-two-maje: A male lion sits upright on a rocky desert outcrop, gazing toward a vast setting sun that floods the horizon with warm colour. Gérôme reduces the composition to two confronting presences — king of the beasts and king of the sky — stripped of any human element. Painted in 1883, the work is in the collection of the Milwaukee Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-venus: Venus emerges from the sea trailing the morning star, her body lit with the pale, enamel finish Gérôme cultivated late in life. The composition revisits the Anadyomene tradition while flirting with the polychrome sculpture project that preoccupied his final decades.
collection-of-beauty-gerrit-van-honthors: A candle-lit brothel scene in which an old procuress brokers a young woman to a leering client. Honthorst, nicknamed Gherardo delle Notti in Rome, transplanted Caravaggio's tenebrism north; here a hidden flame carves the faces from the dark in glowing reds and ochres.

A bearded fiddler in a plumed hat raises a wine glass with one hand and holds his violin aloft with the other, leaning out through a window hung with an ornate carpet. Gerard van Honthorst painted this merry half-length figure in 1623; it belongs to the Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, and is among his best-known tavern genre works.

A group of musicians and singers lean over a painted balustrade, looking down at the viewer in a bold di-sotto-in-su perspective — a composition Honthorst would have absorbed during his years in Italy. Instruments include a lute and a long wind instrument, with a red macaw visible among the figures. Signed and dated 1622, the painting demonstrates Honthorst's mastery of illusionistic ceiling decoration.

A grinning young man in a feathered hat raises a wine glass while cradling a violin against his body, his expression caught in a moment of convivial pleasure. Painted circa 1624, this half-length belongs to the series of merry musicians that Honthorst's Utrecht workshop produced for the bourgeois market, each varied by costume and instrument.
collection-of-beauty-gherardo-delle-nott: The infant Christ lies on manger straw and radiates his own light, illuminating the faces of the Virgin and gathered figures who lean in from surrounding darkness. Honthorst's hidden-light technique — the source of his Italian nickname Gherardo delle Notti — reaches its clearest expression here. The painting is oil on canvas, dated circa 1619–1620, and is held in the Uffizi, Florence (Inv. 1890 no. 739).

A large company gathers around a candlelit table — a lutenist plays at centre while the other revellers drink, laugh, and converse in the warm glow of a hidden candle. Gerrit van Honthorst, known in Italy as Gherardo delle Notti for scenes like this one, deploys Caravaggesque nocturnal lighting to animate an expansive genre subject. The work's current location is unrecorded in the catalogue sources.
collection-of-beauty-giaele-e-sisara-ca-: Jael drives a tent peg through the temple of the sleeping Canaanite general Sisera, a biblical assassination Artemisia returned to repeatedly. Caravaggesque chiaroscuro isolates the act against deep shadow, with the heroine's calm, deliberate grip typical of Gentileschi's strong-willed women.
collection-of-beauty-giambattista-pitton: This engraved bust portrait of Giambattista Pittoni was made by Bartolomeo Nazari and reproduced in Laura Coggiola Pittoni's 1907 monograph Dei Pittoni, Artisti Veneti, published in Bergamo. The original painting is held by the Museo Correr, Venice. Pittoni, the leading Rococo history painter of Venice, is shown in a large powdered wig, the inscription below identifying him as 'Johanni Bapt. Pittoni Pictori Venet.'

The Carthaginian noblewoman receives the cup of poison sent by Masinissa, surrounded by attendants as she chooses suicide over Scipio's Roman triumph. Pittoni, a founding member of the Venetian Academy in 1750, treats the Livy episode with the pale flesh and silver-grey palette typical of his late Rococo manner.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-1755: John Philip Kemble appears in a deep blue coat with a frilled white cravat, painted by Gilbert Stuart in 1785, two years after Kemble's celebrated London debut as Hamlet at Drury Lane. The canvas, NPG 49 in the National Portrait Gallery, London, captures the actor in three-quarter bust-length pose against a warm brown ground.

Sarah Siddons, the leading tragedienne of the London stage, is shown here in a white dress and a large white turban, her gaze turned towards the viewer, holding a fan. Gilbert Stuart painted the portrait in 1787 during his London years; it is NPG 50 in the National Portrait Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-bish: Jean-Louis Lefebvre de Cheverus, French émigré priest and first Catholic bishop of Boston, is depicted in black episcopal robes with a large gold pectoral cross suspended on a chain. Stuart painted the portrait in 1823, shortly before Cheverus returned to France; the canvas belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, accession 21.9.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-cath: Catherine Brass Yates is shown at her needlework, holding thread between her fingers, in a silvery-grey dress and a pale blue and white cap with ribbon trim. Stuart painted the New York merchant's wife in 1793 just after his return from Dublin; the canvas is now in the Andrew W. Mellon Collection at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-geor: Washington stands full-length in a black velvet suit, his right hand extended over a table covered with bound volumes and a quill, an upholstered chair and crimson drapery behind. Stuart painted the Lansdowne portrait in April 1796 for William Petty, Marquess of Lansdowne, the British statesman who had supported American independence.

The unfinished bust of Washington against a brown ground shows the sixty-four-year-old president from the chest up, his hair powdered and his mouth set over the new wooden dentures. Stuart began the Athenaeum portrait on 12 April 1796 and kept the original at his easel as the master from which he produced more than seventy replicas.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-jame: James Madison in old age, in dark coat against neutral ground, painted years after his presidency ended. Stuart had first taken Madison's likeness in 1804; this late repetition, now at the National Gallery of Art, descends from that earlier sitting.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-majo: Henry Dearborn, the Jefferson-era Secretary of War newly returned to active command at the outbreak of the War of 1812, sits in dark blue uniform with gold epaulets. Stuart painted him in 1812; the canvas entered the Art Institute of Chicago as accession 1913.793.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-mart: Martha Washington, in old age, is shown in a dark bonnet and white collar, the bust barely emerging from the unpainted canvas in the unfinished manner Stuart retained for his template portraits. Painted by Gilbert Stuart in 1796 as a pendant to his Athenaeum portrait of the president, this canvas is jointly owned by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (accession 1980.2), and the National Portrait Gallery, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-mrs-: Sally Foster Otis, wife of the Federalist senator and mayor of Boston, sits in a white empire-line gown with a red shawl draped at her elbow. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1809, the canvas now held by the Reynolda House Museum of American Art in Winston-Salem.

Hepzibah Clarke Swan, wife of the speculator James Swan, sits in a high-waisted dress with a sheer wrap around her shoulders. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1808; the portrait, accession 27.539 at the Museum of Fine Arts, joined the museum from the sitter's descendants over a century later.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-sir-: Sir Joshua Reynolds, first president of the Royal Academy, sits in a dark coat with his wig powdered, his gaze turned away in three-quarter profile. Stuart painted the portrait in 1784 during the years he spent in Reynolds's London circle; the canvas is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-thom: Thomas Jefferson in old age, painted by Stuart from earlier sittings taken in 1805 during Jefferson's second presidency. Stuart kept the original Edgehill portrait in his Boston studio for years, working up replicas like this one for collectors and family members.
collection-of-beauty-ginger-pot-with-pom: A glazed ginger jar bound with cord stands among pears and a split pomegranate on a rumpled white cloth. Oil on canvas of 1893, held by The Phillips Collection in Washington. Cézanne tipped the tabletop forward so the fruit reads against the dark ground rather than receding into it.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-029b: Three robed men stand at the entrance of a rocky outcrop, the youngest seated with a compass and tablet, the older two conferring behind, a sunlit valley falling away to the right. The Three Philosophers, painted around 1508 for the Venetian collector Taddeo Contarini, hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-adoration: Two shepherds kneel before the Christ Child at the mouth of a dark cave, Mary and Joseph adoring beside them, a pastoral landscape opening to the left. The Allendale Nativity, painted around 1505 to 1510 and now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, is among the most secure attributions to Giorgione.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-bildnisgi: The young Giovanni Borgherini faces the viewer from the left, holding a book or tablet, while the older Trifone Gabriele, draped in a fur-lined blue and red mantle, turns to address the space behind him. The double portrait on canvas, dated 1509 to 1510, is held by the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich and is traditionally attributed to Giorgione, though an attribution to the young Titian has also been advanced.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-judith: Judith stands in a pink and red dress beside a balustrade, a long sword in her right hand, her bare left foot resting on the severed head of Holofernes below her. Painted around 1504 and now in the State Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg, the work was originally on panel and later transferred to canvas; it is one of the most securely attributed works in Giorgione's small surviving oeuvre.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-pala-di-c: A sacra conversazione altarpiece commissioned for the chapel of Tuzio Costanzo in Castelfranco Veneto, with the enthroned Virgin lifted high above SS. Francis and Nicasius. Giorgione's softly fused light and twilight landscape behind the parapet anticipate the lyrical mood of Venetian painting to come.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-sleeping-: A nude Venus reclines along a hillside, eyes closed, her body echoing the gentle curves of the landscape. Begun by Giorgione and finished after his death by Titian, who is thought to have added the drapery and setting, the picture launched the long line of reclining Venuses culminating in the Urbino Venus.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-the-tempe: A nursing woman sits on the right bank of a stream while a young man with a staff watches from the left, a thunderstorm breaking over the small walled city behind them. Painted in oil on canvas around 1505 and listed in Marcantonio Michiel's notes of 1530, the picture entered the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice in 1932.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-young-wom: A young woman in a fur-trimmed red mantle turns to the viewer with one breast bared against a sprig of laurel, the leaves giving the panel its traditional title. Inscribed on the reverse with the date 1 June 1506, the picture is the earliest dated work by Giorgione and hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-an: Olympian gods picnic in a wooded clearing while Priapus reaches under the sleeping nymph Lotis at right, a satyr filling cups from a wine bowl. Signed by Giovanni Bellini in 1514 for Alfonso d'Este's camerino in Ferrara, the landscape background was overpainted by Titian around 1529 and the picture is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-ch: Christ is shown half-length, raising his right hand in blessing and holding a long staff in the other, a landscape with buildings and a cloudy sky opening behind him. The oil-on-panel painting, dated around 1500, is in the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth and exemplifies Bellini's late preference for isolated devotional figures set against an evocative outdoor background.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-cr: Christ is shown crucified against a detailed Italian cityscape of towers, domes, and fortified walls, with a tree and bare branches framing the composition. Known as the Niccolini da Camugliano Crucifixion and dated around 1480 to 1485, the panel is attributed to Giovanni Bellini and takes its name from the private collection in which it was long preserved.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-fe: A clean-shaven man in a dark cap and tunic faces slightly left against a pale ground, depicted in the bust-length format Bellini favoured for Venetian portrait subjects. The painting, dated between 1490 and 1495, bears the inscription 'IOANNES BELLINUS' on the lower frame and is sometimes identified as a self-portrait by Giovanni Bellini.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-ho: A tiled marble terrace beside a lake gathers the Virgin enthroned, saints, and the infant Christ playing with cherubs beneath an apple tree, while pilgrims and a centaur wander a rocky shore. Long known as the Sacred Allegory, the small panel of around 1490 is one of Bellini's most enigmatic compositions and entered the Uffizi from the Habsburg collection in 1793.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-sa: Jerome reads at the mouth of a rocky grotto with the lion crouched beside him, a fortified town and distant horsemen visible beyond. The oil-on-wood panel, 151 by 113 cm, hangs in the Uffizi and shows Bellini integrating northern landscape detail into a Venetian devotional altarpiece.

Saint Jerome sits at the entrance of a rocky red-brown outcrop, a book open on his lap and his hand raised, while a lion faces him from the foreground and a horse grazes in the arid landscape beyond. The panel, signed 'IOANNES BELLINVS' and dated around 1455 to 1460, is among the artist's earliest treatments of the hermit-saint subject he would revisit throughout his career.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-st: Francis stands barefoot outside his rocky cell, arms slightly spread, lit by a raking light that ignites a slender laurel and bends the surrounding plants toward him. Oil on poplar, around 1480, the panel is at the Frick Collection in New York and is among the earliest devotional pictures to place an outdoor landscape on equal footing with the saint.
collection-of-beauty-girl-carrying-a-bas: A young woman trudges along a windswept English coast with her basket, painted during Homer's stay at the fishing village of Cullercoats. The Northumbrian sojourn shifted his palette toward greyed blues and ochres and gave his figures the weathered seriousness that marks his late marines.
collection-of-beauty-girl-in-the-sunligh: Maria Simonovich, Serov's cousin, sits leaning against a large tree at Domotkanovo, dappled summer light falling across her white blouse and dark skirt. Painted in 1888 and acquired by the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow, the portrait is paired with Girl with Peaches as the second of the two early canvases that established Serov's reputation as a colourist.
collection-of-beauty-girl-in-white-by-vi: A young woman in a white dress and broad yellow hat stands before a green wheatfield scattered with orange-red poppies, her hands empty at her sides. Painted at Auvers-sur-Oise in 1890 in the last weeks of Van Gogh's life, the figure is built up in ribbed parallel touches of green, gold, and white; the work is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-girl-with-a-hoop: Marie Goujon, aged nine, in a blue dress and sash holding a hoop against a screen of foliage. Oil on canvas painted in 1885 and commissioned by her father, the physician Étienne Goujon, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, from the Chester Dale Collection.
collection-of-beauty-giuseppe-arcimboldi: Emperor Maximilian II stands with his consort Maria of Austria and their children Anna, Rudolf, and the infant Ernst in a cradle, dressed in mid-century Spanish court fashion. Painted around 1563 after a model from 1553-54, the dynastic group is preserved in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-giuseppe-arcimboldo: Part of the Four Elements cycle painted for Maximilian II in Vienna, Fire builds a head from candles, oil lamps, flintlocks and burning kindling. Arcimboldo's witty composite portraits flatter the Habsburgs as masters of the elements while showcasing his Mannerist appetite for paradox.

A grizzled head turned in profile, with a wrinkled tree-bark cheek, a cluster of cherries and grapes for the brow, withered leaves for the hair and a stump for the throat. Painted in his final Milanese years around 1590, Arcimboldo collapses the earlier Four Seasons cycle into a single allegorical face about aging and the passage of time.

A profile bust composed entirely of spring blossoms, with a face of pink and white rose petals, a collar of small white flowers, and a torso of green leaves and flowering branches. Painted in 1573 as part of the Four Seasons series presented to Emperor Maximilian II, the panel exemplifies Arcimboldo's Mannerist conceit of building a human likeness entirely from natural produce.

The painter looks out frontally in a black cap and dark doublet, presenting himself in straightforward likeness rather than as a composite. Drawn in the 1570s while in service to the Habsburg court in Prague, the sheet stands apart from his fruit-and-fish portraits as a record of how Arcimboldo wished to be remembered by his employers.

A profile head built from peaches, cherries, plums, ears of wheat, a cucumber nose, and an artichoke breastplate, the collar inscribed with the artist's name and the date. Painted in 1563 as part of the first Four Seasons cycle for Maximilian II, the panel is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

A figure assembled entirely from cellar vessels: stacked wooden barrels form the torso, while earthenware jugs, cups, and smaller drinking vessels compose the head and face beneath a red beret-like hat. Painted in 1574, the image extends Arcimboldo's composite-portrait method from natural produce to the tools of the wine cellar.
collection-of-beauty-giuseppe-bartolomeo: The chaste Susanna twists away from two leering elders who corner her at her bath, the apocryphal subject a favorite vehicle for the female nude. Chiari, a pupil of Carlo Maratta, paints in a late-Roman Baroque idiom of cool flesh tones and theatrical gesture.
collection-of-beauty-glazunov-by-repin: A three-quarter-length portrait of the young composer Alexander Glazunov, who meets the viewer with a level, brooding gaze, one hand tucked into his dark coat against a deep red ground. Repin works with the loose, painterly attack of his portrait practice in the late 1880s, when he documented much of the Russian musical and literary intelligentsia.
collection-of-beauty-goethe-kugelgen: A three-quarter portrait of Goethe, painted by Gerhard von Kügelgen in 1808–1809, showing the poet in a dark coat with a crimson sash and an order on his chest against a grey-blue atmospheric ground. The smooth, restrained handling is characteristic of Kügelgen's Neoclassical manner, and this is among the best-known likenesses of the poet from his later years.
collection-of-beauty-golden-autumn-zolot: A sunlit forest interior with large broadleaf trees bearing golden-yellow autumn foliage, their trunks casting deep shadows across a carpet of fallen leaves. Isaac Levitan's 1895 canvas, signed at the lower right and exhibited at the Munich Secession in 1896, captures the mood of a Russian autumn woodland in a 58 × 68 cm oil on canvas.
collection-of-beauty-goltzius-s-right-ha: A virtuoso pen-and-ink study of the artist's own drawing hand, deformed since childhood by a burn. Goltzius turns the disability into a manifesto of skill, building the form from his signature swelling-and-tapering parallel hatchings copied across Europe.
collection-of-beauty-gowy-atalanta-prado: Hippomenes sprints ahead as Atalanta stoops to retrieve one of the golden apples, the mythological wager from Ovid's Metamorphoses that costs her the race. The painting, attributed to Jacob Peter Gowy after a design by Rubens and dated between 1635 and 1637, is held at the Museo del Prado. Spectators crowd the background while the two protagonists surge diagonally across the foreground, their fluttering drapery and animated bodies typical of Flemish Baroque treatment of Ovidian subjects.
collection-of-beauty-goya-maja-naga2: A reclining nude meets the viewer's gaze without mythological alibi, the first life-size unidealized female nude in Spanish painting. Commissioned by prime minister Manuel Godoy for a private cabinet, the picture later drew the Inquisition's attention to Goya himself.
collection-of-beauty-goya-the-garroted-m: An etching of a condemned prisoner slumped in the iron collar of the garrote, crucifix in hand. Goya pares the scene to a single lit body against deep aquatint shadow, prefiguring the political grimness of the Disasters of War.
collection-of-beauty-goyo-hashiguchi-191: A nude woman sits cross-legged after bathing, bent forward to tend to her foot, a red basin placed before her. The colour woodcut print, titled Yokugo no onna (Woman after a Bath), was made by Hashiguchi Goyō in 1915 and is held in the Library of Congress. Goyō's close observation of the figure and his mastery of flat, subtly gradated colour place the work within the emerging shin-hanga tradition that sought to revive the intimacy of classical bijin-ga.
collection-of-beauty-grant-wood-american: A stern Iowa farmer and his daughter stand before a white frame house with a Carpenter Gothic window, the pitchfork echoing the seams of his overalls. Wood used his sister Nan and his dentist as models, fashioning a dry, hard-edged image that became shorthand for rural America.
collection-of-beauty-grecian-interior-le: A scene in the women's quarters of a Greek house, with nudes lounging amid braziers, drapery and patterned tile. The picture is one of Gérôme's Néo-Grec confections, dressing up an academic studio nude in archaeological props derived from Pompeian wall painting.
collection-of-beauty-griffin-met-dp82001: A griffin — eagle's head, beak and wings joined to the body of a lion — stands in profile, its tail curling over its back and its front talons gripping the ground. The small engraving, one of Schongauer's rare secular subjects, bears his monogram below the creature. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, acquired through the Harris Brisbane Dick Fund.
collection-of-beauty-group-portrait-of-t: An assembly of the World of Art group, with Bakst, Benois, Roerich, Somov, Dobuzhinsky, and other members gathered around a table. Painted in 1920 as a study for an unrealised composition, the canvas portrays the Saint Petersburg circle that had shaped Russian fine printing and Diaghilev's early ballet productions before the Revolution dispersed it.
collection-of-beauty-gsskater: William Grant of Congalton glides on the frozen Serpentine in a black coat and hat, arms folded, with skating figures and Westminster trees behind. Stuart's 1782 portrait, exhibited at the Royal Academy, established his London reputation and is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-guercino-martirio-d: A pen and brown ink with wash drawing shows an executioner raising a sword over a kneeling martyr while a second figure lies fallen to the right. The study, made by Guercino between 1630 and 1632, depicts the martyrdom of Saints John and Paul and is held at the Courtauld Institute of Art. The loose, energetic draughtsmanship and dramatic lighting typical of Guercino's preparatory works are evident in the quick contour lines and brown wash modelling.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-aged-phoenix-i: A grotesque bird-like figure stands on thin legs, one arm raised to grasp the branch of a spindly plant, feathers hanging limply from its body. Paul Klee made this etching, titled Aged Phoenix and bearing the designation Invention 9, in 1905; it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The wiry precision of the line and the absurdist subject reflect Klee's early engagement with satirical printmaking before his later move towards colour and abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-dancers: Three female dancers are shown in vigorous motion, their high-kicking legs and ruffled skirts rendered in bold black ink with rapid, gestural strokes. The work, made by Ernst Ludwig Kirchner in 1906 and held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, captures the energy of contemporary cabaret or folk dance in a medium that appears to be ink on paper rather than a print. It dates from the same year Kirchner co-founded Die Brücke in Dresden.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-eiffel-tower: A graphite drawing depicts the Eiffel Tower from close below, the lattice ironwork and arched base filling the composition in a steep upward-looking perspective. Robert Delaunay made this study between 1926 and 1928, and it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The monochromatic pencil work records the tower's structural geometry with an emphasis on the play of angled members that also informs his painted versions of the subject.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-hilterfingen: A pencil sketch records the village of Hilterfingen, with a church tower rising above houses and trees, inscribed and dated 19 July 1895. Paul Klee made the drawing at age fifteen, and it is now held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The assured observation of the townscape suggests Klee's early facility with landscape draughtsmanship before his later stylistic experiments.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-nudes: Two figures face each other in close proximity, rendered in loose charcoal strokes on brown paper, their heads and bare shoulders filling the sheet. Ernst Ludwig Kirchner made this drawing around 1908, and it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The sketch economy of line and absence of setting are consistent with the rapid figure studies Kirchner produced during the Brücke years.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-old-woman-and-: Two angular figures are seated at a table, a bowl of food between them, rendered in stark black and white in a bold woodcut print. Ernst Ludwig Kirchner made this work in 1921, and it is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The angular distortion of the faces and the high-contrast graphic language link it to Kirchner's continued development of Expressionist printmaking during his Swiss years.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-saint-severin-: The ribbed vaults and ambulatory columns of Saint-Séverin in the Latin Quarter buckle and twist inward in Delaunay's bold reinterpretation of the Gothic interior, suffused with deep blue-green light. This oil on canvas, dated 1909–10, belongs to Delaunay's celebrated series of the Paris church that marked his move toward proto-Cubist spatial distortion. It is held by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.
collection-of-beauty-gunseondo: Gunseondo depicts a procession of Daoist immortals rendered in Kim Hong-do's fluid ink line across multiple screen panels, with figures shown in animated groupings alongside animals and attendants. Painted in 1776 for the court of King Jeongjo, it stands as one of the Korean master's most ambitious figure compositions and a landmark work of the Joseon dynasty's classical painting tradition.
collection-of-beauty-guo-zhongshu-travel: Cargo ships with stern-mounted rudders glide through a snow-stilled river, accompanied by a smaller craft. Painted in fine ink on silk, the work exemplifies early Song dynasty jiehua, the precise ruled-line technique used to render boats and architecture with engineering accuracy.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-her: Herman Petersen is shown in a reddish-brown coat with elaborate braid closures and a lace cravat, the pastel medium giving his face a characteristic softness. Gustaf Lundberg, who spent two decades in Paris absorbing the French pastel tradition before returning to Stockholm as court portraitist, brought the same refined technique to commissions for Swedish merchants and aristocrats throughout the eighteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-lou: Louis XV is shown in armour beneath the blue sash of the Order of the Holy Spirit, his wig tightly curled in the high court fashion of the late 1730s. Lundberg drew the king in pastel around 1740, the portrait once attributed to Louis-Michel van Loo before research reassigned it to the Swedish pastellist working in Paris.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-mar: A young woman, identified as Marie Anne de Bourbon-Condé, is shown in a pink silk dress adorned with floral garlands, seated in a landscape setting and holding a flower wreath. This pastel copy, executed in 1720 by Gustaf Lundberg after a painted prototype by Jean-Baptiste Santerre, is an early example of the Swedish pastellist's work adapting the Parisian court portrait formula.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-por: Pastel portrait of the Swedish industrialist and entomologist Friherre Charles de Geer, shown in coat and powdered wig against a neutral ground. Lundberg, court painter in Stockholm after a long apprenticeship in Paris under Boucher and La Tour, built his reputation on exactly these intimate pastel likenesses of Sweden's eighteenth-century aristocracy.

Juliana Dorotea Henck is shown in a broad-brimmed straw hat trimmed with flowers, her light curled hair framing her face, wearing a pink-toned dress with lace at the collar. The pastel, dated circa 1750, exemplifies Gustaf Lundberg's skill in combining the fashionable informality of French Rococo portraiture with the intimate likeness that made him the foremost pastellist at the Swedish court.
collection-of-beauty-gustav-bauernfeind-: A bustling Damascus thoroughfare rendered with the German Orientalist's exacting eye for tilework, lattice and crowd. Bauernfeind, trained as an architect, treated the city's facades almost archaeologically, balancing photographic detail with the strong overhead light of the Levant.

Pilgrims and worshippers gather between the Mamluk-era Sabil of Qaytbay and the gleaming Dome of the Rock on the Haram al-Sharif. Bauernfeind, who eventually settled in Jerusalem, painted the site repeatedly, prizing the geometry of its mosaic and stone over picturesque incident.

The walled Old City catches first light from the Mount of Olives, the Dome of the Rock luminous above the Kidron Valley. One of Bauernfeind's last major canvases, painted after he made Jerusalem his home, it trades street bustle for an almost devotional topographic stillness.

Viewed through the massive carved doorway of the Great Umayyad Mosque, the sunlit courtyard beyond is occupied by a handful of figures while others rest in the doorway's shade, shoes arranged on the cobbled threshold. Bauernfeind's architectural training is evident in the meticulous rendering of polychrome marble inlay, inscribed frieze, and ornamental stonework that frame the scene, painted in Damascus around 1890.

An elderly bearded warden sits at the arched entrance of the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus, his blue robes and red boots set against the elaborately carved and inlaid stonework of the doorway, with shoes scattered on the cobbled threshold and the sunlit courtyard visible beyond. Bauernfeind painted this intimate figure study in 1891, combining precise architectural detail with quiet observation of daily religious life in the Syrian capital.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-caillebotte: Several oarsmen paddle narrow canoes along the Yerres river in bright afternoon light, the green riverbank reflected in the still water. Caillebotte painted this scene near his family estate at Yerres in 1877, now held at the Milwaukee Art Museum; the cropped horizontal composition and clean observation of leisure activity are characteristic of his approach to depicting bourgeois recreation outdoors.

A wet-cobbled Place de Dublin in Haussmann's rebuilt Paris, viewed from Rue de Moscou. Caillebotte, the Impressionists' patron and engineer, here departs from their feathery touch for a cool, photographic precision, deploying steep perspective and a near-life-size foreground couple.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-029: Painted during Courbet’s 1865 stay at Trouville, this canvas shows a young woman in profile with freshly caught seagulls slung over her shoulder, their wings spilling across the picture plane. The subject came from the fishing life of the Normandy coast, handled with the dense, kneaded paint of Courbet’s Realist maturity.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-038: A young spinner has fallen asleep at her wheel, distaff drooping in her lap. Courbet treats the rural genre subject with monumental gravity, applying paint thickly with knife and brush so that the homely interior carries the weight of a Salon picture.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-jo-: A portrait of Joanna Hiffernan, model and lover of Whistler, gazing into a hand mirror as she draws her copper-red hair through her fingers. Courbet painted at least four versions, the dense impasto and earth-toned palette characteristic of his Realist studio practice.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-la-: A large breaking wave surges beneath a brooding overcast sky, the foaming crest laid on with Courbet's characteristic palette-knife impasto. Painted between 1869 and 1870 on the Normandy coast, the canvas treats seascape as an encounter with raw matter rather than picturesque incident. The work is held at the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-le-: A wide-eyed self-portrait, the young Courbet gripping his hair with both hands and staring directly out at the viewer with an expression of extreme agitation. Executed between 1843 and 1845, when the artist was in his mid-twenties, it announces the confrontational self-fashioning that would define his career and the Realist project. The canvas is now in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-la-sie: A large group of men, women, and children huddles in the shadowed recess of an archway or doorway in a Spanish town, their varied costumes and postures evoking poverty and rest. Painted circa 1868 and now in the National Museum of Western Art, Tokyo, the work draws on Doré's Spanish travels and applies the strong chiaroscuro of his illustrative work to an ambitious oil composition.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-la-val: A vast multitude of suffering humanity fills a rocky valley, prostrate or reaching toward a luminous, haloed figure at the left who radiates divine light. Painted in 1883 and now held at the Petit Palais, Paris, the canvas — over six metres wide — extends Doré's biblical illustration practice into monumental oil, retaining the steep tonal contrasts of his engraved work.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-landsc: A Highland glen opens between steep, bare mountains toward a distant loch under a turbulent sky, with weathered trees, scattered boulders, and a stag visible in the middle distance. Painted in 1878 and held at the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore, the canvas applies the dramatic atmospheric effects associated with an earlier Romantic generation to a Scottish subject.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-mont-s: A panoramic view in the Vosges of the wooded heights of Mont Sainte-Odile, ringed by the prehistoric drystone enclosure known as the Pagan Wall. Better remembered for his book illustrations, Doré here works at large scale in oil, treating his native Alsace with a dark Romantic grandeur.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-roland: A wood engraving from Quatrelles' Légende de Croquemitaine, depicting the Carolingian hero Roland in full armour. Doré's chivalric illustration trades on the same dense crosshatching and theatrical lighting that made his Don Quixote and Bible plates ubiquitous in nineteenth-century print culture.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-st-joh: Death rides forth as the pale horseman of Revelation, illustrating Saint John's vision in the Apocalypse. The print belongs to Doré's widely circulated Bible illustrations, where dense wood-engraved hatching and theatrical lighting gave Victorian readers their dominant visual image of scripture.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-the-ho: The frontispiece to Doré's 1866 illustrated Bible: humans and a tigress alike struggle to save their young as the floodwaters rise. Engraved in dense black-and-white from Doré's design, the plate established the visual template for the Deluge in popular imagination for generations.
collection-of-beauty-guy-johnson-by-benj: Colonel Guy Johnson, British superintendent of Indian affairs for the northern colonies, stands in a red military coat beside the Mohawk diplomat Karonghyontye, with a waterfall visible in the distance. West painted the double portrait between 1775 and 1776, and the canvas is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-hampstead-heath-by-: View looking across the undulating ground of Hampstead Heath, where Constable lived for stretches of his later life. The British Museum sheet, watercolour at 124 by 206 mm, belongs to the artist's sustained engagement with the Heath as a working subject for cloud and weather studies.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-d-a-00: Katharina Schwarz of Augsburg stands holding the attributes of her name-saint Catherine of Alexandria, the broken wheel and the sword at her side. Painted around 1509 to 1510 as a donor portrait, the panel is among the late works of Hans Holbein the Elder before his move to Issenheim and Lucerne.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-d-a-po: A clean-shaven man in a black cap and dark cloak fills a narrow panel, the modelling concentrated in the smooth planes of cheek and brow. Painted between 1518 and 1520, the portrait is held by the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid and shows the Augsburg branch of the Holbein workshop in its last years.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-d-j-he: A young woman's head and bust, her hair worn loose in braided plaits and falling to her shoulders, is depicted with fine chalk on paper. Dated 1522, the drawing is an early study from Holbein the Younger's Basel years, before his departure for England and the Tudor court portraits that would define his later practice.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-da-und: A seated woman is shown from behind, her head wrapped in a cloth and her body enveloped in heavy drapery that pools at the base of the chair. The drawing, produced circa 1500 in the workshop of Hans Holbein the Elder, is a preparatory study for the figure of Saint Thecla in the Basilica panel for San Paolo fuori le Mura, now in the Staatliche Kunstsammlungen, Augsburg.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-der-ju: The Hanseatic merchant Georg Gisze stands in his London counting-house among a glass vase of carnations, scales, a table clock, a quill, signet rings, and letters precisely arranged on the carpet-covered table. Painted in 1532 for the German Steelyard community on the Thames, the panel is now in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-the-el: Hans Holbein the Elder draws his own face in middle age, a long flowing beard framing his features, his gaze directed upward and to the side. Inscribed and dated 1516, this silverpoint sheet is among the last self-portraits by the Augsburg master before his final years in Isenheim and Lucerne.

The Virgin lies on her deathbed surrounded by the apostles, one holding a taper, another reading aloud from a book, Christ receiving her soul above. The panel of 1491 to 1492 is part of a Marian altarpiece from the Augsburg workshop of the elder Holbein, father of the better-known portraitist.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-the-yo: Charles de Solier, Sieur de Morette, French ambassador to the English court, stands three-quarter length in a dark fur-trimmed coat, his hand resting on a sword hilt. Holbein painted the panel around 1534 during the sitter's Tudor mission; it entered the Saxon collections in the seventeenth century and now hangs in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

The infant Edward Tudor, future Edward VI, stands frontally in red and gold brocade with his right hand raised in blessing and a golden rattle held like a sceptre in his left. Likely presented to Henry VIII as a New Year's gift in 1539, the panel carries a Latin inscription by Richard Morrison and now belongs to the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

Holbein portrays Edward Tudor, the future Edward VI, as an infant in a red velvet cap and gold-embroidered dress, his right hand raised in a gesture borrowed from adult royal portraiture. A Latin inscription below urges the boy to equal and surpass his father Henry VIII. The panel was likely presented to the king as a New Year's gift in 1539 and now hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

The painter shows himself in three-quarter view against a gold ground, bearded and cap-clad, his eyes shadowed. Drawn in coloured chalks around 1542, the sheet in the Uffizi was later enlarged and reworked, but enough of the original survives to confirm Holbein's hand in the last year of his life before his death from plague in London.

Sir Thomas More sits in a black gown with brown fur trim and crimson velvet undersleeves, the Collar of Esses hanging at his chest and a paper held in one hand. Painted in 1527 during Holbein's first London stay, the portrait is now in the Frick Collection, New York.

Jean de Dinteville, French ambassador to Henry VIII, stands beside Georges de Selve, Bishop of Lavaur, with a globe, lute, Lutheran hymnal, and astronomical instruments on a shelf strewn between them. Across the foreground lies a famous anamorphic skull, decipherable only from an oblique angle, painted in 1533 and now in the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-harlech-castle-from: An early oil painting by J. M. W. Turner of Harlech Castle on its crag above the Welsh coast, seen across the estuary from Tygwyn Ferry in the fading light of a summer evening. Turner exhibited the picture at the Royal Academy in 1799, the year he was elected an Associate of the Academy, translating his watercolour studies of Welsh castles into the atmospheric oil manner of his early maturity. The painting is in the Yale Center for British Art.
collection-of-beauty-harmensz-van-rijn-r: Saskia van Uylenburgh in the guise of the goddess Flora, a garland of roses and mixed blooms crowning her head and a flowering staff in her hand. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas at the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg was painted in the year of Rembrandt's marriage, recasting his young wife in Venetian pastoral dress.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-2-pers: A pair of figures in the slender, doll-like proportions Harunobu favoured, set within a softly muted interior. He was the pioneer of full-colour nishiki-e printing in 1760s Edo, shifting ukiyo-e away from hand-tinted limited palettes toward layered woodblock impressions.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-bijin-sur-: An oversized nishiki-e showing a woman on a veranda outside a chamber where a party is underway, parodying the Muken-no-Kane scene from the play Hiragana Seisuiki. Harunobu's mitate updates classical drama into the language of the Edo pleasure quarters, with his characteristically delicate, almost weightless figures.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-jouvenceau: An unsigned chuban egoyomi, or pictorial calendar print, in which the days of the long and short months are concealed within the design. Harunobu produced these privately commissioned prints for poetry circles in the mid-1760s, and their experiments drove the development of full-colour brocade printing.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-kanzan-et-: A mitate of the Chinese Chan eccentrics Hanshan and Shide, here reimagined as two Edo youths sharing a scroll, rendered in Harunobu's characteristic nishiki-e palette against a swirling ground. The woodblock print, dated between 1765 and 1770, exemplifies the classical-vernacular layering that defines Harunobu's refined output.
collection-of-beauty-harvard-theatre-col: Watercolour set design for Act I of Daphnis and Chloe, with a wooded grove and rocky outcrop sketched in pale washes. Bakst made the drawing in 1912 for the Ballets Russes production choreographed by Fokine to Ravel's score; the sheet survives in the Harvard Theatre Collection at Houghton Library.
collection-of-beauty-harvesting-at-winds: Workers cut and gather sheaves in the fields below Windsor Castle, whose outline rises on the distant ridge. Benjamin West painted this harvest scene in 1795; it is now in the Berger Collection, Denver, Colorado.
collection-of-beauty-hasegawa-tohaku-pin: The right wing of the celebrated Pine Trees screens, designated a National Treasure of Japan. Tōhaku, founder of the Hasegawa school, paints the pines with rapid sumi ink in pale wash and dry brush, leaving vast areas of unpainted paper to suggest swirling mist — a high point of Momoyama monochrome ink.
collection-of-beauty-hashiguchi-goyo-wom: A woman in a blue floral kimono draws her fingers through her long, loosened black hair, her gaze downcast in quiet concentration. Published in 1920 as a colour woodblock print of the Taishō era, the work revives the bijin tradition in the refined shin-hanga style associated with Hashiguchi Goyō; it is now at the Walters Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-hasui-kawase-evenin: A shin-hanga woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from 1940. Mount Fuji rises with rose-colored evening light on its snows, framed between the dark trunks and boughs of pines, while a farmer leads a loaded horse cart across the fields of Tagonoura below, a stretch of coast whose views of Fuji have been celebrated since classical poetry. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-hasui-kawase-shinag: Rain slants across a canal in Shinagawa's old fishing quarter at dusk: roofed boats lie moored along the bank, a figure under a blue umbrella hurries past the weathered houses, and a single lit window warms the gray-blue scene. The 1931 color woodblock print is characteristic of Hasui's shin-hanga landscapes, which revived the ukiyo-e tradition with Western atmosphere and a fascination for rain, snow, and nightfall. Shinagawa was the first post station of the old Tokaido road out of Edo.
collection-of-beauty-hatred-or-jealousy-: A grimacing head with knotted brow and bared teeth illustrates Hatred or Jealousy, plate from Heads Representing the Various Passions of the Soul published by Robert Sayer in 1765. The series engraves Le Brun's 1668 Paris lecture diagrams, turning the French academy's physiognomic codes into a drawing manual for English students.
collection-of-beauty-hatsuhana-doing-pen: From the series Lives of Wise Women and Virtuous Wives, Hatsuhana of the joruri play Hakone Reigen prays under the icy Tonosawa falls to obtain her crippled husband's revenge. Kuniyoshi treats the ascetic subject with characteristic dynamism, the cascading water rendered in steep blue parallel lines.
collection-of-beauty-havremonet: A canvas of Le Havre's commercial basin, the harbour from which Monet had launched Impression, Sunrise two years earlier. Painted with rapid broken touches, the work continues his investigation of Channel-port atmospheres, where masts, smoke and reflected light become almost interchangeable.
collection-of-beauty-hawaiian-fisherman-: A Hawaiian fisherman stands at the water's edge, holding a cast-net as he faces the open sea under a luminous sunset sky. Bartlett produced this shin-hanga woodblock print in 1916, combining the Western artist's compositional sense with the Japanese publisher's flat planes of colour and serene atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-francesco-acc: A Venetian noblewoman pauses by the bocca di leone, the lion's-mouth letterbox into which secret denunciations were dropped under the Republic. Hayez, leader of Italian Romantic painting, often coded contemporary Risorgimento politics into such historical scenes, here rendered with his porcelain-smooth flesh and rich brocades.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-lot-con-le-fi: Lot's daughters offer their father wine in a cave above the destroyed city of Sodom, Francesco Hayez's treatment of the episode from Genesis 19. Painted in 1833, the canvas stages the scene in a sharply lit grotto, combining Romantic theatricality with the polished figure modelling Hayez retained from his early years in Canova's circle in Rome. The work is recorded in both major catalogues raisonnes of the artist.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-selbstportrat: A late self-portrait at age seventy-eight, the Milanese master appraising himself with calm, unflattering directness. The restrained palette and tightly painted head reflect the academic rigour Hayez upheld at the Brera even as Romanticism gave way to verismo.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-tamar-di-giud: Tamar, daughter-in-law of Judah, is shown as a near-full-length figure pulling open her ochre mantle to reveal her breast, a shepherd's staff in one hand and a gold collar at her throat. Hayez, the leading painter of Italian Romanticism, treats this Old Testament heroine with characteristic sensuality, combining theatrical pose and warm Mediterranean light. The painting, dated 1847, is held at Masnago Castle.
collection-of-beauty-head-of-a-monk-1625: A monk's head is shown in three-quarter view with downcast, closed eyes, the cowl framing a heavy, meditative face. The drawing, 277 by 196 mm, is held by the British Museum and dated between 1625 and 1664; it belongs to the body of figure studies Zurbarán made in connection with his austere Seville altarpieces depicting Carthusian and Mercedarian friars.
collection-of-beauty-head-of-cyrus-broug: Herodotus' Massagetae queen receives the severed head of the Persian king Cyrus, whom she will plunge into a vessel of blood. Rubens stages the Antwerp workshop's signature pile-up of muscular soldiery and silken courtiers, the carmine drapery and pearled flesh tones unmistakably his.
collection-of-beauty-heirin-ji-nobidome-: A late woodblock print by Kawase Hasui, published in 1952, of Heirin-ji, a Rinzai Zen temple at Nobidome in Saitama prefecture. The temple's dark timber gate stands in deep shadow while sunlight breaks through the foliage in bright patches across the flagstone path, autumn maples burning orange in the middle distance. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-goltzius-d: The Terentian motto — without Ceres and Bacchus, Venus grows cold — is set as a chiaroscuro nocturne, the goddess illuminated by a torch held by a satyr. Goltzius, the virtuoso Haarlem engraver, here works with brush on prepared ground in his late painterly mode.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-goltzius-f: The colossal Farnese Hercules, leaning on his club with the apples of the Hesperides behind his back, observed from below by two awed connoisseurs. Goltzius' celebrated engraving exaggerates the antique's swelling musculature with his trademark swelling-and-tapering burin lines.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-goltzius-p: Jan Govertsz. van der Aer, a Haarlem shell collector, is depicted seated and holding a large conch aloft, with further exotic shells arranged on the table beside him. Goltzius records both the penetrating directness of the sitter's gaze and the varied surfaces of his collection with equal precision in this 1603 painting, now in the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-martensz-s: A young man plays the lute beside an open window in a Dutch interior, while a woman seated at the laden table listens with her chin resting on her hand. A dog lies on the tiled floor and a canal view opens beyond the red curtain. Sorgh's The Lute Player (1661) exemplifies the warm-toned, anecdotal domestic genre he practised in Rotterdam.
collection-of-beauty-hendrik-avercamp-wi: Skaters, kolf players and bundled townsfolk fan out across a frozen canal under a low pearly sky. The deaf-mute Avercamp made the panoramic winter landscape his exclusive subject, populating each ice with hundreds of carefully observed figures in a high horizon line inherited from Bruegel.
collection-of-beauty-henri-fantin-latour: A group portrait of the avant-garde gathered around Manet at his easel, with Renoir, Bazille, Monet and Zola among the standing figures. Fantin-Latour records the Batignolles circle as a sober Salon homage, painted in the muted blacks and greys he preferred to his friends' brighter palette.

A glass vase of mixed flowers — hydrangeas, peonies, ranunculus, and white blossoms — stands beside a plate of strawberries, a whole orange, and segments of tangerine, with a small white lidded pot, all arranged on a dark cloth. This 1866 still life, held at the Toledo Museum of Art, shows Fantin-Latour's characteristic precision of observation and his quiet refinement of the Dutch still-life tradition.

Edwin Edwards and his wife Ruth are portrayed together, he seated among papers and prints, she standing beside him, both in Fantin-Latour's habitual sober blacks. The Edwardses were the artist's closest English patrons, channelling his still lifes into the London market; this 1875 double portrait, held at Tate, London, is among the most intimate records of that long friendship.

A glass carafe, scattered fruit and a small bouquet are composed on a dark cloth in disciplined Salon order. Among Fantin-Latour's earliest mature still lifes, it shows the precise tonal modelling that drew Whistler's circle to his work.

A loose spring bouquet — striped and red tulips, yellow wallflowers, clusters of small daisy-like blooms and a sprig of lilac — fills a round glass vase, with a white porcelain coffee cup, saucer and silver spoon set before it on the polished tabletop. The canvas is signed and dated at lower right. Fantin-Latour built much of his reputation on quiet flower pieces of exactly this kind, which found an especially eager market among English collectors.
collection-of-beauty-henri-julien-felix-: Two carnival figures in white costume stand at the forest edge beneath a full moon, bare winter trees silhouetted against a blue-grey sky. A small kiosk stands at the lower left, and soft clouds drift above the treeline. Painted in 1886 and now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, this early canvas already displays the flattened silhouettes and dreamlike stillness central to Rousseau's vision.
collection-of-beauty-henri-matisse-1902-: Notre-Dame's twin towers rise as muted mauve-brown forms above the Seine, viewed from an elevated vantage point over the river and a bridge, with tiny figures on the quay below. Matisse painted this oil on paper in 1902, using structural colour blocks of blue and green to simplify the Parisian cityscape. The work is held at the Albright-Knox Art Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-henri-matisse-1920-: A reclining model in a red garment rests on a striped sofa, her dark hair falling across her face, in the loose, sensuous manner of Matisse's Nice-period figuration. Painted in 1920–21 and held at the Stedelijk Museum, this odalisque belongs to the series of decorative studio interiors in which Matisse returned to warm colour and relaxed figuration after the austerity of the war years.
collection-of-beauty-henri-meunier04: A poster, L'Heure du Silence, by the Belgian Art Nouveau designer Henri Meunier, lithographed in the flat planes and sinuous contour the Brussels school adopted from Japanese prints. Meunier worked extensively in advertising, treating commercial commissions with the same graphic refinement as his fine-art prints.
collection-of-beauty-henri-rousseau-la-e: A dark silhouetted figure pipes serpents from a moonlit jungle on a riverbank, commissioned by the mother of Robert Delaunay. Rousseau, a self-taught customs officer, never left France; his jungles were composed from the Jardin des Plantes, picture books and dream, layered in his deliberate, flattened naïve manner.
collection-of-beauty-henri-rousseau-the-: In a dense jungle at sunset, a lion sinks its teeth into the neck of a collapsing antelope while other creatures — an owl among the branches, a dark feline half-hidden in the foliage — look on. Rousseau exhibited the huge canvas at the 1905 Salon d'Automne with a long narrative caption, in the same room as Matisse and his circle, whose paintings prompted the label 'fauves.' It is now in the Fondation Beyeler near Basel.
collection-of-beauty-henry-fuseli-titani: The fairy queen, drugged by Oberon's love-juice, fawns over the ass-headed weaver from A Midsummer Night's Dream. Fuseli, a key contributor to Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, exaggerates limbs and eyes into a mannerist dream-language drawn from Michelangelo and his own night terrors.
collection-of-beauty-henry-laurens-1782-: Henry Laurens sits in a rich burgundy velvet suit, resting one arm on a table strewn with documents and a quill, in this formal portrait by John Singleton Copley dated 1782. Copley painted Laurens in London shortly after his release from the Tower of London, where he had been held as a captured American envoy, and the composition conveys the statesman's recovered dignity.
collection-of-beauty-henry-rice-met-dp20: A young man in a dark coat and full white cravat is depicted in three-quarter bust against a plain dark ground, his ruddy complexion and brown hair rendered with the fluid brushwork characteristic of Gilbert Stuart. Painted around 1815 and attributed to Stuart, the portrait reflects his command of the New England mercantile sitter type in his later career.
collection-of-beauty-henry-viii-of-engla: Henry VIII is shown in three-quarter view, wearing an embroidered doublet with jewelled gold chains and a black cap trimmed with white feathers, his broad shoulders and steady gaze projecting regal authority. Painted around 1537 in a type derived from Holbein the Younger's lost Whitehall mural, workshop versions such as this one disseminated the canonical royal image across Europe.
collection-of-beauty-hercules-lucha-con-: Hercules grapples with the many-headed Hydra of Lerna, his muscular body twisting against the dark serpentine coils. The canvas belongs to a series of ten Labours of Hercules painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro Palace, where Zurbarán's stark tenebrism set the hero against an almost theatrical void.
collection-of-beauty-het-drijvende-pavil: Ukimidō, the floating pavilion of Katada, stands in the dark waters of Lake Biwa during a night snowfall, its lantern light reflected in the still surface below, while a snow-laden pine frames the scene from the near shore. This colour woodblock print, published by Watanabe Shōzaburō in March 1934, exemplifies Tsuchiya Kōitsu's mastery of nocturnal atmosphere within the Shin-hanga tradition.
collection-of-beauty-het-suwa-meer-in-de: Hokusai's view across Lake Suwa, with Mount Fuji on the far horizon and a shrine and two windswept pines on a rocky outcrop in the foreground. The sheet belongs to the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, printed by Nishimura Yohachi in shades of blue using imported Prussian pigment.
collection-of-beauty-het-zojo-heiligdom-: The Zōjō-ji temple at Shiba, captured by Kawase Hasui for Twenty Views of Tokyo. Hasui became the most prolific landscape designer of the Shin-hanga revival, working closely with the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō from the early 1920s.
collection-of-beauty-hieronymus-bosch-th: When closed, the triptych shows the world on the third day of Creation in grisaille: a translucent globe enclosing a dark, watery earth, with God depicted small in the upper left. The muted tonality contrasts sharply with the saturated colour of the interior panels, framing the work as an unfolding cosmological drama.

A pen drawing illustrating the Flemish proverb that walls and woods betray secrets, with eyes scattered through the meadow and ears sprouting on tree trunks. The sheet, in the Berlin Kupferstichkabinett, is among the few autograph drawings linking Bosch's moralising imagination to his painted demonology.
collection-of-beauty-hieronymus-bosch-tr: The desert hermit Anthony is besieged by a phantasmagoria of hybrid demons, burning villages and blasphemous rites across three panels now in Lisbon. Bosch's most influential triptych, it codified the visual vocabulary of grotesque temptation that fed Bruegel and the later Surrealists alike.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshi-yoshida-hik: Two sailing boats rest on the glistening water of the Inland Sea, their reflections shimmering on an almost glassy surface. From Yoshida's 1926 series Setonaikai shū (A Series of Ocean Views at Seto), the print demonstrates his mastery of tonal gradation and the subtle play of light on water.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshi-yoshida-kum: Two figures stand beneath a weeping cherry tree at night, its blossoming branches silhouetted against a deep teal sky and a luminous full moon. The woodblock print, dated 1926 and held at the Toledo Museum of Art, exemplifies Yoshida's ability to capture atmospheric nocturnal effects through delicate gradations of colour.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshi-yoshida-yom: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida of the Yomeimon, the lavishly carved and gilded gate of the Tosho-gu shrine at Nikko, with small figures on the steps below and towering cedars closing in behind. Yoshida renders the gate's dense ornament in a subdued harmony of golds and greys, capturing the gleam of gilding in deep forest shade. The print was made in 1937.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-1838-two-: A pair of mandarin ducks is shown near flowering plants, one swimming in the water while the other descends with wings spread. The print, dated 1838, belongs to Hiroshige's kachō-e (bird-and-flower) work, in which paired oshidori served as a traditional symbol of conjugal devotion.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-53-statio: A daimyō procession sets out across Edo's Nihonbashi bridge at dawn, opening Hiroshige's Tokaido Road series for the publisher Hōeidō. The print establishes the journey's ceremonial scale before the road's weather and incident take over.

Two travellers make their way across the open plain at Hara station as Mount Fuji dominates the background beneath a pink-tinged morning sky, with birds in flight along the mountain's flank. From Hiroshige's Hōeidō Tōkaidō series (c. 1833–35), this impression is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Three muffled figures trudge through deep night snow at Kanbara, the white sky bokashi-graded into a heavy grey. Long counted among Hiroshige's finest landscape prints, the design treats silence and stillness as subject in their own right.

Travellers approach a thatched teahouse on the windswept Sarugababa heath outside Futagawa station. Hiroshige builds the scene from broad fields of muted ochre and pine green typical of the Hōeidō Tōkaidō's middle stretch.

Workmen scaffold the Toyokawa River bridge at Yoshida station while Yoshida castle rises beyond. Hiroshige uses the diagonal of the bridgework as a vehicle for his characteristic recession into atmospheric distance.

Serving women aggressively haul reluctant travellers into an inn at Goyu, a stock comic episode of the Tōkaidō. The print is one of several in the series in which Hiroshige slips genre observation into what is nominally a landscape.

The Akasaka inn is shown in a tilted cross-section view: on one side, a traveller is attended to while a companion waits; on the other, maids prepare for guests, the two halves separated by a palm in the courtyard. Hiroshige's elevated vantage and interior detail make this one of the most architecturally observed scenes in the Hōeidō Tōkaidō (c. 1833–35).

Station Chiryū from the Tōkaidō series, depicting the early-summer horse fair on a grassy plain where merchants and tethered animals scatter under wide skies. Hiroshige uses subtle bokashi gradations along the horizon to evoke seasonal atmosphere; the Hoeidō publisher seal marks this as part of his career-making 1833 edition.

At Yokkaichi, a traveller rides in a low cart pulled by a bearer along the Mie River's bank, reeds and a lone tree bent hard by the wind against a pale sky with boats beyond. The print, from Hiroshige's Hōeidō Tōkaidō (c. 1833–35), is one of several in the series that makes wind and weather its principal subject.

The penultimate station of the Tōkaidō, Kusatsu was famed for its meibutsu tateba teahouse where porters rested with fast palanquins. Hiroshige captures the bustle of arriving travelers under banners, his linework crisp and his palette anchored by the deep indigo blues of the early Hoeidō printing.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-a-large-w: The Yōrō Falls of Mino Province are shown as a single broad ribbon of bright blue water descending between steep, densely wooded cliffs under an autumnal sky. From Hiroshige's late series Famous Views of the Sixty-odd Provinces (c. 1856), the tall vertical format emphasises the sheer drop of the cataract.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-a-shrine-: A wooded shrine complex stands on a low promontory or islet amid a flat coastal marsh, its grove of dark pines reflected in the surrounding water. Sailing boats move across the broad inlet beyond, and a flock of birds crosses the pale sky. Utagawa Hiroshige depicts the site with the same reverent quietude he brought to rural sacred places throughout his landscape work.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-atake-sou: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, figures hurry across the Shin-Ōhashi bridge as a sudden summer downpour falls in fine engraved lines over the Sumida. The compressed perspective and slanting rain made the print a touchstone for European Japonisme; Van Gogh later copied it in oil.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-full-moon: The Autumn Moon at Ishiyama Temple, from Eight Views of Ōmi, shows the bright disc rising over Lake Biwa behind the temple's wooded bluff. Hiroshige draws on the classical meisho tradition, pairing a literary scenic theme with his characteristic graded blue skies.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-heavy-rai: Night Rain at Karasaki, the second view in Hiroshige's Eight Views of Ōmi (c. 1834), isolates the celebrated pine of Karasaki shrine as a dark, cloud-like mass beneath a steady downpour rendered in dense vertical lines. Blue water glimmers below the canopy, and small structures are just visible through the rain. The near-monochrome palette and relentless verticals give the print the hushed atmosphere of a classical meisho theme translated into the late ukiyo-e idiom.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-traveller: Several travelers hunch forward against a sudden downpour on an open road or hillside, their yellow rain-capes bent nearly horizontal as they press on through the squall. Hiroshige renders the storm with sweeping diagonal lines that emphasize the force of the weather against the small, determined figures. The woodblock print belongs to his Tōkaidō series and exemplifies his skill at capturing the hardships and drama of travel.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-view-of-a: Evening Glow at Seta, from Eight Views of Ōmi, depicts the Karahashi bridge stretching across the southern reaches of Lake Biwa under a flushed sky. Hiroshige uses bokashi gradations to model dusk, a printing technique that gives the series its meditative tonal character.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige11-hakone: Hakone Station: View of the Lake (1833/34), from Hiroshige's Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, depicts the steep, faceted peaks above Lake Ashi in vivid planes of yellow ochre, green, and blue. The dramatic verticality of the mountains — the most challenging terrain on the entire road — dominates the composition, conveying the scale of the obstacle that travellers faced at this pass.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige19-ejiri: Ejiri, set on Suruga Bay near the Miho pine grove, looks across a calm inlet dotted with sailing boats. Hiroshige flattens the distance into bands of graded color, a hallmark of his ukiyo-e landscape mode that influenced later Western printmakers.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige20-fuchu: Travelers ford the Abe River at Fuchu, carried piggyback or on platforms by the station's licensed porters. The rhythmic figures across the shallow water exemplify Hiroshige's interest in the practical theater of travel along the Tōkaidō road.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige22-okabe: The Okabe station turns inland through the gorge of Utsu Pass, where a stony stream cuts between steep wooded slopes. Hiroshige's compressed verticals and overlapping rocks give the print a closed, intimate atmosphere unusual for the series.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige25-kanaya: Kanaya sits on the western bank of the Ōi River, reached only by porters who carried travelers across its broad flats. Hiroshige looks down on the receding scene from a high vantage, ordering the mountains and water into clean horizontal registers.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige28-fukuroi: At Fukuroi, travelers rest at a tea stand pitched beneath a leafy tree, a kettle steaming on the open fire. The genre vignette is set against a low, level landscape, demonstrating Hiroshige's gift for everyday observation within the Tōkaidō format.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige30-hamamat: Hamamatsu features a great solitary pine on a windswept field, with figures gathered around a small fire at its base. The motif distills Hiroshige's recurring concern with weather and season, the bare branches and grey sky reading as winter on the road.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige38-fujikaw: Fujikawa Station: Scene at Post Outskirts (1833/34), from the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, shows travelers and station hands gathered at the edge of the post town, with a tall lantern post marking the road and trees framing the scene. Hiroshige presents a quiet moment of arrival and rest rather than a grand ceremonial event, capturing the everyday texture of life along the road.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige39-okazaki: The Yahagi Bridge at Okazaki, said to be the longest on the Tōkaidō, stretches across the river in a single shallow arc. Hiroshige aligns the procession crossing it with the distant castle, framing infrastructure and authority in one elegant span.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige45-ishiyak: Ishiyakushi takes its name from the Buddhist temple visible among trees behind the village fields. Hiroshige's quiet rural composition, with farmers at work and a stand of pines, exemplifies the lyrical pastoral mode he interleaved with the busier station scenes.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige47-kameyam: Kameyama Castle rises above a snow-blanketed slope as a daimyō procession climbs toward the gate. The print is among the most admired snowscapes of the Hoeidō Tōkaidō, its diagonal trail and white expanse drawn with Hiroshige's restrained graphic economy.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige49-sakanos: Sakanoshita lies at the foot of the steep Suzuka pass, here dominated by the cliff known as Fudesute-yama, the 'brush-throwing mountain'. Travelers pause at a teahouse to contemplate the rock face, a scene that joins landscape and legend in Hiroshige's understated manner.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige50-tsuchiy: Tsuchiyama is shown in heavy spring rain, a daimyō procession crossing a swollen stream beneath dripping trees. The slanting rain lines and saturated greens make this one of the most atmospheric prints in the Tōkaidō series.
collection-of-beauty-hodakayama-from-the: From Yoshida's Twelve Scenes in the Japan Alps, this view of Hotaka-dake records the artist's own mountaineering observations of the Northern Alps. Yoshida combined ukiyo-e block techniques with Western tonal modeling, often printing the same blocks in different palettes to capture changing light.
collection-of-beauty-hokusai-1760-1849-o: Chōshi in Shimōsa Province, from Hokusai's Oceans of Wisdom series (c. 1833), places two fishing boats amid churning open seas, their crews bracing against the swell as a rocky headland rises in the background.
