collection-of-beauty-kitagawa-utamaro-ha: A hairdresser (kamiyui) carefully arranges a seated woman's coiffure in this print from Utamaro's series Twelve Types of Women's Handicraft (Fujin tewaza juniko), dating to around 1797–98. Both figures wear patterned grey kimono, and Utamaro's precise linework isolates the subtle gestures of the task against a plain ground. The work is held in the Art Gallery of South Australia (inv. 838G66).
collection-of-beauty-kitagawa-utamaro-ta: Ohisa, a celebrated Edo teahouse beauty, inspects the back of her coiffure with paired mirrors during the Asakusa autumn festival. Utamaro's precise hairlines and luminous mica-dusted ground typify his bust-portrait okubi-e of fashionable contemporary women.
collection-of-beauty-kitayskaya-palatka: A Chinese tent standing in a Central Asian landscape, recorded as Kitayskaya palatka. The study comes from Vereshchagin's Turkestan travels of 1869 to 1870 across the Russian Empire's newly conquered frontier in Central Asia.
collection-of-beauty-kiyonaga-bathhouse-: Half of a celebrated diptych depicting women in a public bathhouse, an unusually informal subject from the Tenmei era. Kiyonaga, head of the Torii school, sets his tall, calm figures in the careful spatial recession that reformed bijinga for the next generation.
collection-of-beauty-kiyonobu-yamanaka-i: Two kabuki actors square off in a confrontational pose typical of aragoto bravura roles. Kiyonobu, founder of the Torii line of theatre artists, defined the early ukiyo-e print with bold contour lines and the hand-applied tan-e orange-red pigment characteristic of pre-polychrome woodblock work.
collection-of-beauty-konrad-witz-004: Saint Christopher wades through dark water bearing the Christ Child, his giant frame sharply lit against a wooded shore. Witz, working in Basel, was an early Northern realist whose granular textures and naturalistic landscape settings broke with International Gothic abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-korinsscreen: A six-panel folding screen depicting the rocky, pine-clad islets of Matsushima Bay, with stylised waves rendered in gold leaf and green pigment. Ogata Kōrin, leading master of the Rinpa school, treats the celebrated scenic site as flat decorative pattern rather than topographic record, in a work of c. 1700 held at the Smithsonian's Freer Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-kuniyoshi-utagawa-a: A waterside Edo scene along the Sumida, the river that defined the city's ferry traffic, festivals and pleasure boating. Kuniyoshi, an Utagawa-school designer best known for warrior prints, here turns to a quieter genre subject in the bold linework typical of late ukiyo-e.
collection-of-beauty-kuniyoshi-utagawa-p: Men bathe and swim in the pool beneath the Great Falls of Sekison at Ōyama in this woodblock print of c. 1840. Kuniyoshi exploits the vertical ōban format to dramatise the columnar fall of water, setting the bathers in scale against the sheer dark cliffs — a theatrical staging characteristic of his Utagawa-school training.
collection-of-beauty-kuniyoshi-utagawa-t: A hanging scroll depicting the arhat Handaka Sonja, shaven-headed and wearing large earrings, summoning a small dragon from his begging bowl amid a coiling rain cloud. Executed in ink and slight colour on paper, signed and sealed, and dated c. 1848–1854, the work demonstrates the muscular brushwork Kuniyoshi refined in his celebrated warrior compositions.
collection-of-beauty-kuroda-seiki-kohan0: A woman in a striped kimono sits by a calm lake, a round paper fan held loosely in her hands, with wooded hills visible across the water. Painted in 1897, Lakeside is among Kuroda Seiki's best-known canvases; trained in Paris under Raphaël Collin, he brought plein-air colour and a high-key palette to Meiji Japan. The work is held at the Tokyo National Museum.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-goluboydo: A blue-roofed provincial house fills the canvas, its balcony occupied by figures taking tea at a samovar while a child releases kites from the rooftop and neighbours gather in the sunlit garden below. Boris Kustodiev returned obsessively to small Russian towns and merchant life, painting them in saturated colour — an idealised vision of provincial domesticity drawn from memory.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-merchants: A merchant's wife sits before a samovar, holding a tea cup, with a cut watermelon, cakes, fruit, and grapes on the table before her; her cat perches at her side. Painted in 1918 and one of Kustodiev's most reproduced canvases, the picture is an elegy for pre-revolutionary provincial bourgeois life composed while a spinal tumour had confined the artist to a wheelchair.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-promenade: Townsfolk in summer hats and dresses stroll along the Volga embankment at Tutaev, with birch trees, market stalls, and onion-domed churches visible across the wide river. Painted in 1909, Promenade Along the Volga marks Kustodiev's sustained engagement with provincial merchant life as a subject, rendered in his characteristically bright, saturated palette.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-renee-not: Renée Ivanovna Notgaft is shown in three-quarter length, seated in a green armchair in a black dress with a white neckline, a large bouquet of pink hydrangeas filling the background behind her. Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1914, in a mood of quiet elegance that contrasts with the vivid provincial festival scenes he would concentrate on in later years.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-russian-v: A full-length nude woman stands in a wooden bathhouse, smiling as she combs her long auburn hair, a birch besom held in her other hand, with steam and bath implements around her. Painted c. 1925–26, Russian Venus was Kustodiev's last major work, completed from his wheelchair; it now hangs in the Nizhny Novgorod State Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-self-port: Kustodiev depicts himself in a heavy fur coat and fur hat, arms folded, against a snowy Russian townscape of onion-domed churches and market activity. The canvas is dated 1919 in the artist's own hand; it places him squarely within the Russian merchant world that had become his chief subject.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-the-bolsh: A giant Bolshevik in winter coat strides over the snow-covered rooftops of a Russian city, carrying an enormous red banner while crowds fill the streets below. Painted in 1920 and held at the Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas draws on the monumental scale rhetoric of icon and lubok traditions, treating a contemporary revolutionary figure with the visual language of folk heroic art.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-trinity-d: Villagers in bright Sunday clothes gather under birches for the Orthodox feast of the Trinity, with onion-domed churches behind them. Painted in 1920, the canvas belongs to Kustodiev's cycle of provincial holiday scenes composed from memory during his confinement to a wheelchair, an idealised reconstruction of pre-revolutionary peasant ritual.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-voloshin: Portrait of the Symbolist poet and critic Maximilian Voloshin, painted in 1924. By that date Kustodiev had been confined to a wheelchair for eight years after spinal surgery, working almost entirely from photographs and sittings arranged at his Petrograd apartment.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiev-winter-sh: Sledges glide through a snowbound Russian provincial town during the carnival week before Lent, with onion-domed churches and crowds of fairgoers under a pink winter sky. Painted in 1919 at the height of the Civil War, Kustodiev's nostalgic merrymaking belongs to a cycle of Maslenitsa scenes that imagined the lost merchant culture as folk pageantry.
collection-of-beauty-kustodievb-provinc: Townsfolk in mid-nineteenth-century dress stroll through a tree-lined provincial Russian square, with onion-domed church towers rising behind a bakery shopfront. The scene belongs to Kustodiev's cycle of idealised merchant-town views, capturing the rhythms of everyday provincial life.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiyev-fair: A provincial Russian fair crowds the foreground beneath vivid church towers, vendors and buyers in folk dress pressing among textiles and goods. Painted in 1910 in tempera on cardboard, the work is held by the A. N. Radishchev Museum of Arts in Saratov, and reflects Kustodiev's abiding fascination with market days as popular spectacle.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiyev-mate: Vasily Mathé (1856–1917) stands at a table spread with large prints, a magnifying glass in hand, his gaze directed at the viewer. Painted by Kustodiev in 1902, the portrait honours the printmaker during the period when Kustodiev was still close to his Repin training at the Academy.
collection-of-beauty-kustodiyevsemenov-k: Pyotr Kapitsa and Nikolai Semyonov are shown in a close half-length portrait, one holding a pipe beside a gleaming samovar-like vessel. Painted by Kustodiev in 1921, the double portrait captures two physicists at the outset of careers that would both be recognised with Nobel Prizes.
collection-of-beauty-l-embarquement-pour: Lovers prepare to leave the island of Venus in golden afternoon light, a melancholic departure rather than the arrival the title might suggest. Watteau's reception piece for the Académie royale invented the genre of the fête galante, with feathery brushwork drawn from his study of Rubens.
collection-of-beauty-l-enlevement-des-sa: Roman soldiers seize the Sabine women at Romulus's signal in a frieze of taut, sculptural figures arrayed before classical architecture. Poussin choreographs the violence with archaeological detail and disciplined gesture, exemplifying the rational French classicism he forged in Rome.
collection-of-beauty-l-enlevement-par-pa: An early figural composition treating the rape of Persephone by Pluto in dark, churning paint and a fevered ochre-and-black palette. Cézanne dedicated the canvas to his friend Émile Zola; it dates from the violent, romantic phase that preceded his Impressionist conversion at Pontoise.
collection-of-beauty-l-ermitage-par-paul: A poster lithograph for the Symbolist literary review L'Ermitage, showing a woman with flowing auburn hair bent over a spray of lilies, rendered in warm golden and amber tones. Paul Berthon, a pupil of Eugène Grasset, designed the piece in 1897, applying an Art Nouveau linearity that gives his work a distinctive decorative flatness.
collection-of-beauty-l-homme-au-bonnet-d: A seated man in a white cotton cap, his face built up in thick ridges of paint. Oil on canvas, painted in 1866 and held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. The sitter is the artist's uncle Dominique Aubert, whom Cézanne painted in a series of portraits laid in heavily with the palette knife, a phase he later called couillarde.
collection-of-beauty-l-l-boilly-une-loge: Spectators crowd a theatre box on a free-admission performance day, a working-class audience pressed shoulder to shoulder. Boilly titled the panel 'Une loge, un jour de spectacle gratuit'; the small oil measures 32.5 by 41.7 cm and hangs in the Musée Lambinet at Versailles.
collection-of-beauty-l-ultimo-bacio-di-g: Romeo and Juliet embrace in a farewell kiss within a vaulted church interior, stained glass and a crucifix visible in the background. Hayez painted this large canvas in 1823 — now held by Villa Carlotta in Tremezzo — charging the Shakespearean subject with the emotional intensity that defines his Italian Romantic manner.
collection-of-beauty-la-batalla-de-casci: Florentine soldiers scramble naked from the Arno after a false Pisan alarm, twisting their bodies as they grab for arms on the bank. The composition survives only through Bastiano da Sangallo's 1542 grisaille copy at Holkham Hall, the lost cartoon Michelangelo prepared in 1504 for the Palazzo Vecchio having served as a school of anatomy for a generation of Florentine artists.
collection-of-beauty-la-bohemienne-endor: A lion stands over a sleeping figure in a striped robe on a moonlit desert plain, a mandolin and earthenware jar lying nearby. Rousseau painted this dream-image in 1897; now in the Museum of Modern Art, it exemplifies the self-taught artist's flattened forms and eerie calm.
collection-of-beauty-la-continence-de-sc: The Roman general Scipio refuses the captive Iberian princess offered as spoils of war, gesturing for her return to her betrothed Allucius. Pittoni painted the moral exemplum in 1733, one of many Venetian treatments of the Livy episode in the pale, sweetened palette he favoured.
collection-of-beauty-la-debacle-monet-w5: The breakup of ice on the Seine after a hard winter near Vétheuil, with floes drifting past bare riverbanks. Monet returned to this motif repeatedly in 1880, using broken brushwork to register the shifting interplay of water, ice and reflected sky.
collection-of-beauty-la-famille-lafitte-: A group portrait of the Laffite family by the leading court painter of Louis XIV. Rigaud's studio specialised in elaborate full-length likenesses of French nobility, with rich drapery, polished flesh tones and carefully posed sitters that established the visual vocabulary of Bourbon state portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-la-foire-chinoise: Figures in fanciful Eastern dress mingle at a lively outdoor market beneath parasols and canopied stalls, with an elevated pavilion at centre right. Boucher designed the canvas around 1742 as part of his chinoiserie cycle for the Beauvais tapestry manufactory, supplying cartoons for a suite of woven panels.
collection-of-beauty-la-fornarina-by-raf: Long identified as the baker's daughter Margherita Luti, Raphael's lover, the sitter wears an oriental turban and a slim arm-band inscribed with the painter's name. The picture, completed near the end of Raphael's life, has the tactile sfumato modelling and direct erotic charge of his late Roman period.
collection-of-beauty-la-grande-piscine-d: Gérôme depicts the great communal bath at Bursa in Ottoman Anatolia, its vaulted stone arches admitting shafts of light above a crowded pool of nude bathers attended by robed servants. Painted by 1885, the canvas exemplifies the academic precision and ethnographic ambition of his Eastern subjects, rendering human figures and architectural atmosphere with the hard-edged finish characteristic of his Orientalist work.
collection-of-beauty-la-inmaculada-conce: The Virgin rises on a billowing cloud attended by four full-sized angels against a dramatic sky, her hands clasped at her breast, with lilies and symbolic objects below her. Begun by El Greco between 1608 and 1614 and completed by his son Jorge Manuel Theotokópoulos, the painting presents the Immaculate Conception in the elongated, intensely spiritual manner of El Greco's late Toledan period, and now hangs in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-la-liberte-guidant-: An allegorical Liberty, bare-breasted and clutching the tricolore, leads insurgents over a barricade strewn with the dead during the July Revolution of 1830. Delacroix, the standard-bearer of French Romanticism, fuses contemporary reportage with classical personification in vivid, brushy oil.
collection-of-beauty-la-peche-chinoise: Groups of figures in oriental costume populate a fanciful waterside setting, with a pagoda pavilion at centre-left and boatmen fishing from a vessel at right. Painted around 1742, the work belongs to François Boucher's chinoiserie series and evokes an imagined China assembled from imported porcelains and travel prints rather than direct observation.
collection-of-beauty-la-pisanella-by-l-b: Set design for the Port of Famagusta, the Cypriot harbour from Gabriele d'Annunzio's play La Pisanelle ou la Mort parfumée. Bakst made the watercolour in 1913 for Ida Rubinstein's production at the Théâtre du Châtelet, staged by Vsevolod Meyerhold with music by Ildebrando Pizzetti.
collection-of-beauty-la-ronda-de-noche-p: Captain Frans Banning Cocq in black with red sash steps forward giving the order to march, Lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch in pale yellow strides beside him, and the company tumbles into motion behind. Signed and dated 1642, the canvas of 363 by 437 cm in the Rijksmuseum is the largest of the Amsterdam civic-guard group portraits.
collection-of-beauty-la-route-de-vetheui: A snow-effect view of the road leading into Vétheuil, the Seine-side village where Monet lived from 1878. The picture belongs to his series of winter landscapes painted en plein air, the broken brushwork registering the muted blues and lilacs of low northern light on settled snow.
collection-of-beauty-la-seine-a-lavacour: A broad, sunlit view of the Seine at Lavacourt, the village directly opposite Vétheuil where Monet lived from 1878 following his wife Camille's death. Painted in 1879, the canvas balances Impressionist broken brushwork with a spacious, horizontal calm, the sparkling river surface and cumulus sky rendered in vivid blues and greens.
collection-of-beauty-la-seine-a-vetheuil: The Seine at Vétheuil, the riverside village where Monet settled in 1878 after leaving Argenteuil. Soft poplars and reflections built up in short, drily loaded strokes typify the more sober palette of his late-1870s landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-la-table-de-cuisine: A kitchen table crowded with a fruit basket, pots and a folded cloth, the tabletop tipped sharply toward the viewer. Oil on canvas worked between 1888 and 1890, now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Cézanne tilts the planes and crops the cloth at the lower edge to make geometric form, not accurate space, the subject.
collection-of-beauty-la-vision-apres-le-: Breton women in white coiffes lean forward in prayer, their vision of Jacob wrestling the angel materialising across a vermilion field divided by an apple tree. Painted at Pont-Aven in 1888 and now in the National Galleries of Scotland, the canvas is the breakthrough work in which Gauguin abandoned naturalistic colour for symbolic, cloisonné planes outlined in dark blue.
collection-of-beauty-la-vision-de-san-hu: A collaborative panel: Rubens painted the kneeling huntsman Saint Hubert encountering the cross-bearing stag, while Jan Brueghel the Elder provided the meticulous forest setting. Such division of labour between figure-painter and landscape specialist was a hallmark of Antwerp's Baroque studio system.
collection-of-beauty-la-yole-the-skiff-r: Two young women row a vivid orange skiff on the Seine at Chatou, the river populated by sailboats and a distant railway bridge. Renoir's complementary contrast of cobalt water and chrome-orange hull, applied in feathered touches, captures the leisurely Impressionist suburb of the 1870s.
collection-of-beauty-lac-d-annecy-par-pa: Painted during a summer stay at Talloires, the canvas reduces the Savoyard lake and the Château de Duingt to interlocking planes of blue, green and ochre. Cézanne's structural brushwork and tilted perspective treat water and stone as equivalent geometric facets, prefiguring Cubist analysis of form.
collection-of-beauty-lady-with-the-rose-: Charlotte Louise Burckhardt stands full-length in a black dress against a neutral grey ground, holding a single white rose. Sargent painted this portrait in 1882, drawing on the tonal restraint of Velázquez — as urged by his teacher Carolus-Duran — to achieve a commanding silhouette and psychological directness; the work was shown at the Salon of 1882 and is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-lake-nemi-by-george: Lake Nemi, the ancient crater lake in the Alban Hills south of Rome, is seen under clear summer light from the wooded shore, a small town perched on the far ridge. Two women rest in the foreground while a figure swims in the calm water below. Inness painted the scene during his Italian sojourn, dated 1857, and the canvas is now in the Yale University Art Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-landscape-with-a-gn: A twisted, half-bare tree dominates this quick pen-and-brown-ink study of a farmstead, its trunk drawn with the same nervous, broken line as the low buildings behind. Landscape drawings like this are rare survivals from Van Dyck, who made them for his own use rather than as preparation for paintings — private observations from a career otherwise devoted to portraiture. The sheet is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, acquired in 1997.
collection-of-beauty-landscape-with-pan-: A collaborative mythological landscape in which Rubens painted the figures of Pan pursuing the nymph Syrinx while Jan Brueghel the Younger supplied the dense reed bed and wooded river setting. Such partnerships between Antwerp masters were a hallmark of Flemish Baroque cabinet painting.
collection-of-beauty-landscape-with-the-: An imaginary landscape staging Christ's parable beneath a turbulent, storm-bruised sky. Rembrandt dwarfs the small figures of the Samaritan and the wounded traveller at lower right within a vast expanse of rocky terrain, tossed trees, and brooding tonal contrasts that recall the influence of Hercules Seghers. Dated 1638, the work exemplifies Rembrandt's brief engagement with the heroic landscape tradition.
collection-of-beauty-landschaft-mit-kuhe: A wooded pastoral landscape in which a large herd of cattle fills the foreground, with dairymaids milking and carrying filled copper jugs, while a figure at right appears to be a hunter near the water. Painted by Rubens between 1635 and 1638, the work belongs to a group of expansive Flemish landscapes notable for their loose, atmospheric handling, and is held by the Gemäldegalerie Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-landschaft-mit-turm: A small panel showing a fortified tower set on a wooded rise, approached by a slender bridge under the warm light of a lowering sun. The intimate scale and rapid, fluid brushwork are characteristic of the late landscape sketches Rubens made around his estate at Elewijt.
collection-of-beauty-las-meninas-by-dieg: The Spanish court group portrait centred on the Infanta Margarita, her maids and dwarves, with Velázquez himself at the easel and the king and queen reflected in a distant mirror. The picture is a sustained meditation on vision, painted for Philip IV and now the cornerstone of the Prado.
collection-of-beauty-last-judgement-by-m: Christ presides at the centre of a roiling vortex of saints, the resurrected, and the damned dragged toward Charon's boat, the entire altar wall of the Sistine Chapel given to a single muscular composition. Commissioned by Pope Paul III and painted in fresco between 1536 and 1541, the work was later partly draped by Daniele da Volterra under the censorship of the Council of Trent.
collection-of-beauty-laurits-tuxen-the-n: A view of the North Sea at Højen on the northern tip of Jutland, painted near Tuxen's home at Skagen. Associated with the Skagen painters, Tuxen here forsakes the colony's clear summer light for a churning storm twilight, with thick impasto registering wind-driven spray.
collection-of-beauty-le-bain-turc-by-jea: A circular tondo crowded with bathing women, drawn together from poses Ingres had refined across half a century of nudes. Painted in his eighties for Prince Napoléon, the work distils his lifelong fascination with sinuous contour and the Orientalist harem trope into a single hothouse composition.
collection-of-beauty-le-bassin-aux-nymph: From the late Giverny series, the canvas crops the lily pond into a near-abstract field of floating pads and reflected sky. By 1919 Monet's failing eyesight pushed him toward broader, more saturated touches that would culminate in the wraparound Grandes Décorations of the Orangerie.
collection-of-beauty-le-bassin-du-jas-de: The pond in the grounds of the Jas de Bouffan, the Cézanne family estate near Aix-en-Provence, ringed by trees with a sculpted lion spout at the water's edge. Cézanne painted the bastide and its garden in some thirty-six oils across forty years; this view, dated about 1876, is in the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-le-brun-alexander-a: The wounded Indian king Porus is brought before Alexander the Great after the Battle of the Hydaspes, his tall figure refusing prostration. Le Brun painted the scene in 1673 as part of his cycle on the conquests of Alexander, commissioned by Louis XIV to flatter the Sun King by historical parallel.
collection-of-beauty-le-chancelier-segui: Chancellor Pierre Séguier rides on horseback beneath a large parasol, clad in magnificent golden ceremonial robes, accompanied by six young pages on foot. Painted between 1660 and 1661 and now in the Louvre, the picture was Le Brun's tribute to the patron who had supported his Italian studies and secured his career at the French court.
collection-of-beauty-le-chapeau-de-paill: A portrait long mistitled 'The Straw Hat' — the hat is in fact black felt — depicting Susanna Lunden, sister of Rubens's second wife Helena Fourment. The sitter wears a black bodice with vivid red sleeves, and the picture is celebrated for its luminous flesh painting and the deft rendering of cool daylight on her tilted hat brim. Now in the National Gallery, London, it dates from between 1622 and 1625.
collection-of-beauty-le-concert-champetr: A Venetian poesia of two clothed gentlemen and two nude female figures, attended by music, in a pastoral landscape. Begun by Giorgione and likely completed by the young Titian, the picture established the lyrical pastoral genre that would echo through Manet's Déjeuner sur l'herbe.
collection-of-beauty-le-corps-d-hector-h: Académie of a recumbent male nude, posed as the dead Hector with one arm hanging limp. David painted the study in 1778 during his Prix de Rome years at the French Academy in Rome, and it never left his studio, eventually entering the Musée Fabre in Montpellier where it remains.
collection-of-beauty-le-debarquement-de-: From the Marie de' Medici cycle commissioned for the Luxembourg Palace, the canvas shows the queen's arrival at Marseilles in 1600, greeted by an allegorical France while Tritons and Nereids churn the water below. Painted between 1622 and 1625, Rubens fuses official Bourbon state imagery with Baroque mythological invention in this monumental work now in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-le-dieu-bleu-nijins: Bakst's 1911 costume design for Vaslav Nijinsky in the title role of Le Dieu bleu shows a cross-legged figure with green-painted skin, an elaborate feathered headdress, and richly patterned yellow and jewelled garments. The design drew on South and Southeast Asian court dress that Bakst had studied, for the Cocteau-Hahn-Fokine ballet premiered by Diaghilev's Ballets Russes in 1912.
collection-of-beauty-le-fils-de-l-artist: The artist's son Paul shown from the waist up in a blue jacket and a small black bowler hat, glancing sideways. Oil on canvas worked between 1885 and 1890, the face shaded in visible strokes of slate blue, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. Paul was Cézanne's most frequent sitter.
collection-of-beauty-le-havre-muma-monet: A coastal view of Fécamp on the Normandy chalk cliffs, painted during a productive Channel-side campaign in the early 1880s. Monet works the cliff face and sea in parallel ribbons of pigment, registering the cool grey-green light of the Pays de Caux.
collection-of-beauty-le-jardinier-vallie: Vallier, the gardener and odd-job man at Cézanne's house near Aix, sits with hands resting in his lap, the figure built from dark greens and blues. One of six portraits of the sitter, painted in the summer and autumn of 1906, the last months of Cézanne's life. The painter worked on the Vallier series within days of his death that October.
collection-of-beauty-le-pain-et-les-ufs-: A baguette, eggs, red onions, a pewter tankard, a knife and a wine glass arranged on a cloth-draped table. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Cincinnati Art Museum, one of Cézanne's earliest dated still lifes. X-ray scanning in 2022 revealed an earlier portrait beneath the surface.
collection-of-beauty-le-pere-du-peintre-: The painter's father, the banker Louis-Auguste Cézanne, seated frontally in a large armchair and reading the newspaper L'Événement. Oil on canvas, 198.5 by 119.3 cm, painted in 1866 and held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington. It is the second of three portraits Cézanne made of his father.
collection-of-beauty-le-pont-d-argenteui: Monet's 1875 view of the road bridge at Argenteuil looks across dense riverside vegetation toward the rebuilt multi-arched span, with the town of Argenteuil visible beyond. The composition is unusual in privileging the lush foreground growth over the river itself, rendered with the quick, broken brushwork that defines his Impressionist period at this Seine town. The work is held in the National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina.
collection-of-beauty-le-port-de-zaandam: Monet painted this view of Zaandam harbour in 1871 during a stay in the Netherlands, showing moored sailing barges and Dutch townhouses beneath a warm, golden evening sky reflected in the still water. The canvas belongs to a series of Zaandam works in which Monet explored reflected light and the picturesque character of the Dutch waterways.
collection-of-beauty-le-reniement-de-sai: Around a candlelit table, a servant girl holds a flame and points an accusing finger at Peter while other figures look on and play cards at the right. Honthorst, who trained in Rome and absorbed Caravaggio's tenebrism, uses the hidden candle to bathe the apostle's denial in warm planes of orange light, a technique that earned him the Italian nickname Gherardo delle Notti. The work dates between 1612 and 1620.
collection-of-beauty-le-serment-des-hora: Three brothers extend their arms to swear an oath on the swords their father holds aloft, while their womenfolk collapse in grief at the right. David painted the canvas in Rome in 1784 to 1785 for Louis XVI, and its severe Doric setting and frieze-like composition became the manifesto of Neoclassical history painting; it hangs in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-le-serment-du-jeu-d: Deputies of the Third Estate raise their right hands and swear not to disperse until France has a constitution, packed into the Versailles tennis court on 20 June 1789. David began this monumental project in 1791, working from sketches and portrait studies; the large unfinished drawing is now preserved at the Château de Versailles.
collection-of-beauty-lebrun-self-portrai: Painted in Florence for the Uffizi's gallery of artists' self-portraits during her revolutionary exile, Vigée Le Brun shows herself at the easel sketching Marie Antoinette. The picture asserts both her professional standing as portraitist to the queen and her loyalty in the face of political upheaval.
collection-of-beauty-leda-and-the-swan-b: Gérôme treats the classical myth in his characteristic polished academic manner, placing the pale nude figure of Leda in a sunlit green landscape where a swan glides toward her on the water, accompanied by a flock of putti. Trained as both painter and sculptor, he returned repeatedly to mythological subjects that displayed his mastery of smooth, near-tactile flesh, as in this 1895 canvas.

An early treatment of the myth from Rubens's Italian years, when his study of Michelangelo and Venetian colour was reshaping his approach to the sensual nude. The composition shows Leda reclining against a dark landscape as the swan presses close, its large dark wings contrasting with warm flesh tones in the kind of erotically charged mythology Rubens would refine for decades. The work, dated 1601, is now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.
collection-of-beauty-leda-et-le-cygne-pa: Veronese's late rendering of Jupiter's seduction of Leda shows the reclining nude against a richly draped background of deep crimson velvet, the white swan pressing close as she reclines on a cushioned couch. The work demonstrates the master's assured handling of the female figure and luxuriant textiles, characteristic of his mature Venetian style around 1585.
collection-of-beauty-leighton-alain-char: Edmund Blair Leighton's 1903 painting depicts the moment Margaret of Scotland is said to have kissed the lips of the sleeping French poet Alain Chartier in tribute to his eloquence, surrounded by attendant ladies on a garden stair. The subject suits Leighton's characteristic medievalising genre, here enriched with elaborately rendered gold brocade and lace costumes within a Gothic architectural setting.
collection-of-beauty-leighton-captive-an: A long procession of women in flowing drapery filing toward a well, the widowed Andromache in black at the centre near a family group. Oil on canvas of about 1886 to 1888, the subject taken from a passage in Homer's Iliad. Manchester City Council bought the picture from Leighton for £4,000 in 1889; it hangs in Manchester Art Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-leighton-god-speed: Edmund Blair Leighton's farewell scene shows a red-haired woman in cream and gold dress leaning from a castle parapet to fasten a red token to the armour of a departing knight below. The composition is typical of his medievalising Academicism, combining careful costume detail with warm, clear lighting and a narrative of chivalric devotion.
collection-of-beauty-leighton-stitching-: Edmund Blair Leighton's 1911 canvas shows a young woman seated on a castle battlement, sewing a yellow-and-black heraldic standard against an open landscape. The medieval-revival subject is characteristic of Leighton's Academicist work, combining careful attention to period costume and stone setting with a quietly focused feminine figure.
collection-of-beauty-leighton-the-king-a: King Cophetua kneels before the barefoot beggar maid, who stands beneath a gilded baldachin clutching her shawl, as he offers his crown. Edmund Blair Leighton painted the subject in 1898, drawing on the Tennyson ballad, with richly modelled brocade and warm Orientalising architecture characteristic of his academic narrative style.
collection-of-beauty-leighton-the-painte: A man guides a woman's hand at a drawing as she leans against his shoulder, her golden gown set off by darker surroundings. Oil on canvas, 83.8 by 76.8 cm, painted around 1864 and acquired by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, in 1912. A genre subject unusual for Leighton, who more often worked in classical and mythological themes.
collection-of-beauty-leo-tolstoy02: Tolstoy sits writing at a cluttered desk in the vaulted room at Yasnaya Polyana, dressed in the plain peasant blouse he adopted in his later years. Ilya Repin, the leading Peredvizhniki realist, captured this scene of the writer at work in 1891, the composition inscribed with the location and date in the lower left.
collection-of-beauty-leon-bakst-001: A costume design for the Firebird, showing the dancer in a swirling confection of orange, red, and gold with feather-like flame motifs, arms outstretched mid-movement. Léon Bakst created designs for Stravinsky and Fokine's Firebird, premiered by Diaghilev's Ballets Russes at the Paris Opéra on 25 June 1910, with sets principally by Alexander Golovin.
collection-of-beauty-leon-bakst-carnival: A large crowd fills a Paris square at dusk, with French and Russian tricolour flags, flares, and the silhouette of a monumental statue against a fiery sunset sky. Léon Bakst painted this record of the festivities held in 1893 to celebrate the French Republic's reception of the Russian Imperial Navy, the diplomatic occasion that sealed the Franco-Russian Alliance.
collection-of-beauty-leon-bakst-lyubov-g: Lyubov Gritsenko, daughter of the collector Pavel Tretyakov and Bakst's future wife, stands on an outdoor terrace wearing a white dress and a wide-brimmed hat, with a wooded lakeside landscape behind her. Léon Bakst painted this portrait in 1903; it entered the Tretyakov Gallery (inventory no. 22001) and is now recorded in the Goskatalog of the Russian Museum Fund.
collection-of-beauty-leon-bakst-peasant-: A peasant woman seen from behind, wearing a white blouse with green and red banding, a boldly patterned skirt with floral embroidery in red, yellow, and blue stripes, and a flower-decorated kokoshnik. Léon Bakst designed this costume in 1922 for the vaudeville Old Moscow, drawing on Russian folk dress to evoke the repertoire of his early career.
collection-of-beauty-leon-bakst-portrait: Alexandre Benois reclines in a leather armchair reading papers, set against a warm interior with a framed portrait visible on the wall behind him. Léon Bakst painted this portrait of his friend and Mir iskusstva co-founder in 1898, the year the journal was launched in St Petersburg, where the two artists shaped a programme of Russian art nouveau and stage design.
collection-of-beauty-leon-bakst-the-prin: Within an ornate arched alcove hung with violet and gold drapery, the prince kneels before the princess, who sits up in her canopied bed as she wakes. Léon Bakst painted this panel between 1913 and 1922 as part of a Sleeping Beauty decorative cycle commissioned for Waddesdon Manor, now held by the National Trust.

The prince and his hunting party pause in a vivid twilight landscape, a winged figure visible in the upper sky as they survey the enchanted terrain before them. Léon Bakst painted this panel between 1913 and 1922 as part of a Sleeping Beauty decorative cycle commissioned for Waddesdon Manor, now in the care of the National Trust.

Figures from the royal court lie fallen in sleep across the courtyard and steps of an ivy-covered castle, while a crowned figure in gold still stands at the entrance as the enchantment takes hold. Léon Bakst painted this panel between 1913 and 1922 for a Sleeping Beauty cycle at Waddesdon Manor, now held by the National Trust.

The princess recoils at the moment the spindle pierces her finger, the old crone leaning over the wheel in a shadowed tower chamber. Bakst painted the panel between 1913 and 1922 for James de Rothschild's Sleeping Beauty cycle at Waddesdon Manor, where the National Trust still keeps the series.
collection-of-beauty-leonardo-da-vinci-g: Ginevra de' Benci, daughter of a Florentine banker, is portrayed before a juniper bush whose Italian name, ginepro, puns on her own. Painted in oil on poplar between circa 1474 and 1478, the panel is the only Leonardo in the Americas and hangs at the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-leonardo-da-vinci-v: Saint Anne supports the Virgin on her lap as Mary reaches for the Christ child, who plays with a lamb foreshadowing the Passion. Left unfinished at the artist's death and now in the Louvre, the panel is celebrated for its pyramidal grouping, soft sfumato modelling and atmospheric mountainous landscape.
collection-of-beauty-leopold-boilly-les-: Young conscripts of the 1807 class marching past the Porte Saint-Denis as families crowd to bid them farewell. Oil on canvas, 84.5 by 138 cm, in the Musée Carnavalet, Paris, since 1888 and first shown at the Salon of 1808. The triumphal arch anchors the deep boulevard view behind the column of recruits.
collection-of-beauty-les-amours-de-paris: Paris, partially draped and holding a golden lyre, sits turned toward Helen, who stands close beside him in a richly coloured interior with heavy blue and red fabric. Commissioned by the comte d'Artois in 1788, David's canvas is now in the Louvre and reflects the archaeological exactness he developed from his Roman studies.
collection-of-beauty-les-grands-boulevar: A Paris boulevard busy with strollers and carriages beneath thin spring trees, the rebuilt Haussmann city stretching back along the pavement. Renoir painted it in 1875, oil on canvas measuring about 52 by 64 cm, now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-les-oceanides-les-n: Nude sea nymphs recline and swim among storm-tossed rocks in a turbulent ocean under an overcast twilight sky, with spectral figures dissolving into cloud on the right. Gustave Doré painted this large oil canvas of the Oceanids (Naïads of the Sea) between circa 1860 and 1869, demonstrating his ambitions as a painter beyond his celebrated illustration work.
collection-of-beauty-les-papillons: A young woman reaches after butterflies in a small boudoir scene, the figure finished with the close, enamel-smooth handling Boilly favoured. The Lille-born painter built his reputation on such intimate genre pictures in Paris from the late 1780s. Oil on canvas.
collection-of-beauty-les-soleils-jardin-: A dense bed of sunflowers fills the canvas, painted in the artist's own garden at Petit Gennevilliers on the banks of the Seine. The loose handling and saturated yellows reflect a late shift toward Impressionist plein-air practice, after he had largely turned from urban subjects to horticulture.
collection-of-beauty-leve-de-lune-sur-le: From the series One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, the print shows the warlord Cao Cao gazing at the moon rising over Mount Nanping on the eve of the Battle of Red Cliffs. Yoshitoshi distils the Chinese narrative into a spare vertical composition, a hallmark of his late ukiyo-e woodblock work.
collection-of-beauty-levitan-nad-vech-po: A small wooden chapel and graveyard sit on a windswept bluff above a vast inland lake, dark storm-clouds piled over the horizon. Levitan painted Above the Eternal Tranquility at Lake Udomlya in 1894, calling it the work in which he had put most of himself; it entered the Tretyakov Gallery the same year.
collection-of-beauty-levitan-ozero28: A broad inland lake spreads beneath a high blue sky scattered with cumulus clouds, reeds and a low village visible along the far shore. Levitan began the large canvas in 1899 and was still working on it at the time of his death in 1900; it is regarded as the culminating statement of his lyrical landscape practice.
collection-of-beauty-levitan-sokolniki-a: A woman in black walks a damp avenue through Moscow's Sokolniki park as wet yellow leaves and bare birches close in on either side. Levitan was nineteen and living in Saltykovka, having been expelled from Moscow in an anti-Jewish edict, when Pavel Tretyakov bought the canvas, the first Levitan to enter the Tretyakov collection.
collection-of-beauty-levitan-solnechnyde: A sunlit Russian farmyard in spring: a weathered wooden cottage stands amid birch trees in fresh leaf, chickens scratch in the foreground, and warm light falls across the scene. Levitan painted this small oil in 1876 as a student at the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture, and the title Sunny Day. Spring accords with the verdant, tranquil mood on display.
collection-of-beauty-levitan-vesna-bolsh: Slender birches and mixed trees stand half-submerged in the floodwaters of a Russian spring, their pale trunks reflected in the still surface, while a wooden boat rests on the muddy bank in the foreground. Levitan painted Spring. High Water in 1897, capturing the annual inundation of low-lying woodland that became one of the touchstones of the Russian mood landscape.
collection-of-beauty-levitan-vesnavitali: Blossoming trees in shades of pink line a winding road through a mountain valley, snow-capped peaks rising beyond forested slopes under a blue sky. Levitan painted Spring in Italy during his foreign travels, capturing a luminous southern landscape sharply different from the melancholy Russian scenes for which he is best known.
collection-of-beauty-levitan-zolotaya-os: A birch grove turns yellow above a slow blue river in the Russian countryside, a sliver of field and far village closing the view. Levitan painted this smaller variant of Golden Autumn at Slobodka in 1895; the larger canvas of the same year belongs to the Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-levitani-lilii-ast: Water lily pads — green and reddish — drift across a dark, still pond, their white flowers opening above the surface while aquatic vegetation fills the shallower water throughout. Levitan painted Water Lilies in 1895, approaching the subject with the same close attention to natural light and reflected colour that characterises his finest mood landscapes; the canvas is held by the Astrakhan State Picture Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-levitanii-osennpzh1: A hunter and his dog move along a path through bare late-autumn woodland, the pale sky pressing low over the tangle of brown branches. Levitan painted this Autumn Landscape in 1880, early in his career, already loading the season with the quiet atmospheric weight that would define his later work.
collection-of-beauty-liefdespaar-rp-p-ob: A pair of lovers sits in a wooded grove, the nude man turning toward the woman beside him. The plate is one of the engravings published after Parmigianino's drawings, the Mannerist designs that carried his eccentric grace north into the print culture of sixteenth-century Europe.
collection-of-beauty-lilium-superbum-lit: A Turk's cap lily (Lilium superbum) with downward-facing orange flowers spotted maroon, the petals sharply reflexed and curving back toward the stem. Plate from Redouté's Les Liliacées, published in Paris by Didot Jeune between 1802 and 1816. The print is a colour stipple engraving after Redouté, finished by hand.
collection-of-beauty-lille-pba-boilly-ro: A presumed portrait of Maximilien de Robespierre in a high cravat, set against a dark ground. Oil on canvas, about 41 by 32 cm, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille and usually dated around 1791. The attribution and date remain contested, with some scholars placing the canvas before 1789.
collection-of-beauty-lille-pba-boilly-tr: A crowd carries the deputy Jean-Paul Marat aloft after his acquittal before the Revolutionary Tribunal in April 1793, banners and pikes raised above the throng. Oil on canvas, dated 1794, in the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille. Boilly turned to the multi-figure street scene that would occupy much of his later career.
collection-of-beauty-lille-pdba-delacroi: Medea clutches her two sons to her chest in a rocky grotto, the dagger raised as she prepares to kill them in revenge against Jason. Painted between 1836 and 1838 and shown at the Salon, the canvas was bought by the State and sent to the Palais des Beaux-Arts in Lille, where it has hung since 1839.
collection-of-beauty-lille-pdba-monet-la: Painted after the spectacular Seine ice break-up of January 1880, the canvas shows broken floes drifting past the bare poplars at Vétheuil. The subject — provoked by a thaw following one of the century's harshest winters — gave Monet a chance to study fragmented reflections and pearl-grey winter light.
collection-of-beauty-lille-pdba-rubens-m: The Magdalene lies swooning on rocky ground, supported by two angels, as a shaft of heavenly light breaks through the dark canopy above. Painted between 1619 and 1620 and held at the Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille, the large canvas deploys the dramatic chiaroscuro and dynamic figural grouping characteristic of Rubens's mature Baroque manner.
collection-of-beauty-lion-tentant-de-sai: A lion lies recumbent in a rocky, cave-like interior, its jaws open wide toward a tiny butterfly hovering before it. Gérôme renders the animal with the precise anatomical finish of his academic training, turning the predator's power into a moment of comic disproportion; the canvas is held at the Carnegie Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-little-red-riding-h: From Doré's celebrated illustrations to Perrault's Contes, the wood engraving stages the child's fateful meeting with the wolf among forest shadows. Doré pioneered cinematic tonal staging in printed fairy tales, and these designs shaped the visual imagination of the genre across Europe.
collection-of-beauty-london-national-gal: Turner depicts the moonlit parting of Hero and Leander on a turbulent sea, figures clustered on a terrace as the waters churn under a cloud-veiled moon. The canvas, exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1837, is now in the National Gallery, London, and exemplifies Turner's late mythological seascapes in which architecture, water, and atmosphere dissolve into one another.
collection-of-beauty-london-the-houses-o: Part of Monet's Houses of Parliament series painted from his window at St Thomas's Hospital, the canvas dissolves the Gothic Revival silhouette into mauve and orange vapour. The campaigns of 1899–1904 used the Thames fog as a coloured veil through which Monet tracked the changing hours.
collection-of-beauty-londres-tate-modern: Yellow-orange bodies wade and sprawl beside cobalt water at the Moritzburg lakes outside Dresden, where Kirchner and the Brücke painters spent summer weeks bathing naked from 1909 onward. Begun in 1909, the canvas was repainted in 1926 in lighter, more even tones. It is now in Tate Modern, London.
collection-of-beauty-lord-frederic-leigh: Iphigenia asleep on the ground at evening, the herdsman Cymon halted at the right as he comes upon her. The subject is from a tale in Boccaccio's Decameron; Leighton exhibited the oil at the Royal Academy in 1884. The painting is now in the Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney, which acquired it in 1976.

Two fair-haired women wind a skein of wool on the flat roof of a whitewashed house, a bay and distant hills behind them. Leighton drew on sketches made at Lindos on Rhodes in 1867 and first exhibited the canvas in 1878; it is now in the Art Gallery of New South Wales, Sydney.
collection-of-beauty-lord-frederick-leig: Daedalus fastening the wax-and-feather wings onto his son Icarus before flight, a subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses. Leighton painted the oil around 1869; it measures roughly 138 by 106 cm and belongs to the Faringdon Collection at Buscot Park, Oxfordshire.
collection-of-beauty-los-horrores-de-la-: An allegory painted for the Medici and addressed to the disasters of the Thirty Years' War. Mars, dragged forward by a Fury, tramples the arts and a despairing Europe, while Venus tries vainly to restrain him — Rubens's late, politically engaged history painting at its most charged.
collection-of-beauty-los-nenufares-monet: A study of water lilies drifting on the surface of the Giverny pond, where reflected sky and submerged stems dissolve any fixed horizon. Monet returned to this motif obsessively in his final decades, building dense, broken touches of pigment into a shimmering field of colour.
collection-of-beauty-lot-and-his-daughte: The episode from Genesis 19, in which Lot's daughters ply their father with wine to secure descendants after the destruction of Sodom. Rubens treats the subject with characteristically warm flesh tones and muscular, twisting figures, the canvas later extended at top and bottom in the early eighteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-lot-en-zijn-dochter: Beneath a tree the daughters press wine on their father while Sodom burns in the distance, a small dog and a still life of bread and cheese anchoring the foreground. Goltzius, the great Haarlem engraver turned painter, sets the nudes in cool, sculptural light typical of his late Mannerist style.
collection-of-beauty-louis-francois-bert: The newspaper editor of the Journal des Débats sits forward, hands planted on his thighs, in a pose that became a touchstone for nineteenth-century bourgeois portraiture. Ingres's polished surface and tightly drawn contours register every wrinkle of Bertin's waistcoat without disturbing the granite stillness of the sitter.
collection-of-beauty-louis-leopold-boill: A billiard room crowded with players and spectators, a woman taking her shot at the centre of the table. Oil on canvas, 56 by 81 cm, in the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg, dated 1807. The presence of women at the game reflects the looser social manners of the First Empire.

A portrait of Jan Anthony d'Averhoult, the Dutch Patriot of Huguenot descent who chaired parliament in 1792, the year of this likeness and of his death. Oil on canvas by Boilly, the sitter shown bust-length against a plain ground. The portrait dates from the height of the Revolutionary period.

Figures gathered around a tonneau game of skill, tossing discs toward the scoring holes of the cabinet. Oil on canvas, 37.8 by 46.8 cm, dated about 1828, in the Ramsbury Manor Foundation. Boilly drew the players in the tight finish he used for his late genre scenes of Parisian amusement.

The paymaster Monsieur Gaudry instructing his daughter at a globe and map, the cartouche of which carries a sphinx and pyramid recalling Napoleon's Egyptian campaign. Oil on canvas, 73.6 by 59 cm, in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth, shown at the Salons of 1812 and 1814. The fine interior detail draws on the seventeenth-century Dutch genre pictures Boilly collected.

A family hauling its furniture through a Parisian street near the Port-au-Blé, the household goods piled on a handcart. Oil on canvas, 73 by 92 cm, signed and dated 1822, in the Art Institute of Chicago. Boilly exhibited the canvas at the Salon of 1822 in the hope, unrealised, that the state would buy it.

A dense crowd of visitors examining Jacques-Louis David's vast 'Coronation of Napoleon' on the wall of the Louvre, a guidebook in the hands of a soldier at left. Oil on canvas, 61.6 by 82.6 cm, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. David's painting was shown at the Louvre between 1808 and 1810, the occasion Boilly records here.

A family gathered around a printed Napoleonic bulletin, tracing the army's progress on a map. Oil on canvas, 44 by 59 cm, in the Saint Louis Art Museum, shown at the Salon of 1808. The scene follows the campaign of the War of the Fourth Coalition against Prussia.

A young woman seated at a pedal harp, her gaze turned toward the viewer. Oil on canvas catalogued 1977.152 at the Yale University Art Gallery and dated about 1804 to 1806. The harp signals the musical accomplishment expected of women in this period.

A woman presents an oval portrait of herself to a small company while a gentleman peers at her through a magnifying glass. She appears twice, as both the living sitter and her painted likeness. Painted about 1790, oil on canvas, roughly 46 by 56 cm, in the Dallas Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-louis-xiv-equestria: Louis XIV reins in a rearing mount in a gold-brocade costume with red ribbons and a red-plumed hat, a blue sash at his waist, while troops mass on the plain beyond. The canvas is attributed jointly to Charles Le Brun and the Flemish battle painter Adam Frans van der Meulen and hangs in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Tournai.
collection-of-beauty-louis-xiv-of-france: The Sun King at sixty-three, draped in ermine and blue velvet fleurs-de-lis, his bewigged head turned over a leg cocked in a courtly dance pose. Rigaud's state portrait set the template for European royal imagery, multiplied across embassies and palaces in countless studio replicas.
collection-of-beauty-louise-jane-jopling: Louise Jopling, painter and society figure, stands three-quarter length in a dark dress richly decorated with floral embroidery and red trim at collar and cuffs, her dark hair close-cropped. By 1879 Millais had moved beyond his Pre-Raphaelite beginnings into a fluent portrait manner, and the work is now in the National Portrait Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-love-and-life: A winged male figure of Love guiding the slight nude figure of Life up a steep rocky path, violets springing where they tread. Watts called the picture a painted parable and first showed it at the Grosvenor Gallery in 1885. He gave a version to the United States; the work seen here is the one in the Tate (N01641).
collection-of-beauty-low-tide-at-pourvil: Exposed sand flats stretch beneath the chalk cliffs of the Normandy fishing village, painted on one of Monet's productive 1882 campaigns along the coast. Quick, broken brushwork captures the shifting light and damp air, and X-rays reveal an earlier composition lying beneath the beach.
collection-of-beauty-lowenjagd-peter-pau: Mounted hunters and lions tangle in violent diagonal motion, men and beasts pulled into a single churning mass. This small oil sketch, held by the Alte Pinakothek in Munich, is a preparatory modello for one of Rubens's larger hunt scenes, with the brushwork left openly visible.
collection-of-beauty-luca-signorelli-por: A bust-length study of a weathered older man, painted with the linear precision and severe modelling for which the Cortona master was celebrated. Signorelli's interest in anatomical truth, sharpened by his fresco cycles at Orvieto, surfaces in every furrow of the sitter's face.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-0: Johann Friedrich, the Lutheran champion who would lose his electorate after the battle of Mühlberg, shown here in jewelled chain and flat black cap. Cranach was court painter at Wittenberg for half a century and produced numerous variants of this loyal Reformation portrait.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-a: The first parents stand on either side of the apple tree, slim and pale against a forest dense with deer, lions and stags. Cranach made the Fall a workshop staple, prized by Lutheran patrons as a meditation on sin made flesh.

A naked Venus wears only a wide-brimmed hat and gold chain while a small Cupid, stung by bees, complains of the honey he has stolen. Cranach often paired the subject with a Latin epigram warning that pleasure is mixed with pain.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-c: The personification of Christian charity sits nude, nursing one infant at her breast while holding a second child against her shoulder and a third rests at her feet — the traditional three-child emblem of the virtue. Cranach reduced the iconography to slender contours and a verdant garden setting, producing the composition in several small-scale variants between circa 1537 and 1540; this panel is held at the Royal Museum of Fine Arts, Antwerp.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-d: Naked figures dance in a ring beneath fruit trees in the mythical age of innocence described by Hesiod and Ovid. Cranach turns the classical theme into a playful, decorative idyll suited to the humanist tastes of the Saxon court.

Saint Barbara kneels as her own father raises the sword, the executioner's act that, according to legend, struck him down with lightning. The early panel shows Cranach still close to the dramatic, expressive line of the Danube School.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-h: In this pen-and-wash drawing of 1530, Hercules bears the great celestial globe aloft while the freed Atlas stands to one side in a broadly sketched landscape — the eleventh labour rendered in Cranach's assured draughtsmanship. The sheet, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, illustrates the Renaissance enthusiasm for Antique mythology and offers a rare glimpse of Cranach's working method outside the painted panel.

The Saxon court drives stags into the Elbe before the towers of Schloss Hartenfels, with the Elector and his guests stationed at crossbows along the bank. Cranach made several versions of this hunt, half topographical record and half dynastic propaganda.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-j: The Hebrew widow displays the severed head of the Assyrian general she has just decapitated to save her city, set against Cranach's signature inky black ground. Pearled jewels and a slashed velvet bodice betray the panel's origin as a courtly Saxon trophy rather than a devotional image.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-k: The Virgin and Saint John mourn beneath the crucified Christ in a windswept landscape that owes much to the young Cranach's time in Vienna. The agitated drapery and emotional pitch place the panel at the heart of the early Danube School.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-p: A young Saxon prince is shown half-length against a flat black ground, his golden hair crowned with a delicate jewelled garland and his pale features set above a richly jewelled collar and brown fur-trimmed cloak over red brocade sleeves. The portrait, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, exemplifies the dynastic likenesses Cranach produced for the Saxon court around 1517.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-s: The Hebrew judge Samson straddles the lion and pries its jaws apart in the act recounted in Judges 14. Cranach treats the subject with the heraldic clarity and brilliant local colour favoured by his patron, the Elector of Saxony.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-d-a-w: Moses leads the Israelites through the wilderness beneath the divine pillar of cloud described in Exodus 13. A workshop production from the busy Cranach studio, the panel keeps the master's compact figure types and bright, decorative landscape.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-der-j: Aged women are carried into a stone basin on the left and emerge as nubile young brides on the right, an allegory of rejuvenation popular at the Saxon court. Cranach unfolds the fantasy across a panoramic landscape with the crisp outlines and porcelain flesh tones of his Wittenberg workshop.
collection-of-beauty-lucas-cranach-the-e: Adam reaches for the apple Eve has plucked while the serpent watches from the branches above, the trees of paradise teeming with creatures. The panel is among Cranach's most fully developed treatments of the subject, painted for the Lutheran market that prized its theological clarity.
collection-of-beauty-ludwig-deutsch-the-: A solitary figure in white robes stands in an ornately appointed interior, examining a small object — a pen or similar instrument — amid an array of brass vessels, inlaid boxes, and richly embroidered hangings. Painted in 1883, the small panel exemplifies Ludwig Deutsch's meticulous Orientalist technique, in which every textile and metalwork surface is rendered with near-photographic precision.

A palace guard stands sentinel before a carved geometric screen, dressed in a voluminous yellow cloak and blue garment, carrying a long spear and a round shield surmounted by a coiled serpent and falcon finial. Deutsch returned repeatedly to this figure type, polishing each gilded boss and inlaid tile to an almost photographic enamel finish that made his Orientalist set-pieces sought after across European salons.

A street vendor of sahleb, the hot orchid-root drink popular in Ottoman Cairo, pours a cup before a tiled wall. Deutsch worked from sketches and props gathered on visits to Egypt, finishing each picture in his Paris studio with jewel-like precision.

A robed man sits on a carved wooden bench, a long-stemmed pipe at his feet, in a richly appointed interior whose walls are faced with elaborate geometric tilework. Costume, carpet, and inlaid surfaces are rendered with Deutsch's characteristic precision. Painted in 1903, the work belongs to the series of Orientalist interiors the Austrian-born artist produced in his Paris studio, drawing on studies and props gathered during his Egyptian travels.
collection-of-beauty-luisa-maria-amelia-: Maria Luisa di Borbone, princess of the Two Sicilies, shown in a green silk gown and white cap, holding a pen over a large sheet of blue paper at a draped table. The portrait was painted in 1790 by Élisabeth Louise Vigée Le Brun during her Italian years following her departure from France, and is now held at the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples.
collection-of-beauty-ma-yuan-dancing-and: A hanging scroll in ink and light colour depicting misty mountains, gnarled trees, and a small figure resting near a rocky outcrop, with calligraphic inscriptions at the upper left. Ma Yuan, a leading court painter of the Southern Song dynasty working around 1200, was celebrated for compositions that concentrate pictorial weight to one side and leave open space to suggest an infinite, fog-shrouded distance.
collection-of-beauty-macke-august-promen: Strolling figures, including a man in a straw hat and a woman with a white parasol, move through a sun-dappled avenue of large green trees, their forms built from broad planes of saturated colour. August Macke, associated with the Der Blaue Reiter group, painted this promenade scene in 1913, translating everyday leisure into the luminous colour harmonies he had developed in dialogue with Robert Delaunay's Orphism.
collection-of-beauty-macke-seiltanzerin-: A tightrope walker poised above a fairground crowd, the scene built from interlocking translucent diamonds of colour. Painted in the artist's most prolific year, the composition shows Macke fusing his Blaue Reiter sensibility with the prismatic geometry he had absorbed from Robert Delaunay in Paris.
collection-of-beauty-madame-monet-au-can: Camille Doncieux, the painter's first wife, reclining on a sofa in quiet thought. The intimate domestic subject and muted tonal range belong to Monet's early-1870s figure painting, before his work shifted decisively outdoors toward pure landscape and atmospheric study.
collection-of-beauty-madame-recamier-by-: Juliette Récamier reclines barefoot on a Directoire-style chaise longue in a white chemise dress, her dark curls lightly bound, a tall floor candelabrum standing at the head of the couch. David left the canvas unfinished in 1800 following a dispute with the sitter, and the unpainted ground together with the severe antique furniture have come to embody the austerity of the emerging Empire taste.
collection-of-beauty-madame-x-madame-pie: Virginie Gautreau stands in profile in a black satin gown, her lavender-powdered skin set against a brown ground in a near-monochrome scheme. Sargent's salon submission caused such scandal in Paris over its eroticised pose and originally fallen strap that the painter eventually decamped to London.
collection-of-beauty-madeleine-undressin: Inspired by Keats's poem, Madeline stands in a grand, candlelit interior bathed in warm amber and gold, her pale gown luminous against the richly panelled walls as moonlight falls across the floor in greenish patches. Millais painted the scene in 1863, and the work, now in the Royal Collection, exemplifies the atmospheric, freely handled manner of his later career rather than the tight early Pre-Raphaelite finish.
collection-of-beauty-mademoiselle-guimar: The Paris Opera dancer Marie-Madeleine Guimard appears as Terpsichore, the muse of dance, in classical drapery with a lyre at her side. Jacques-Louis David painted the canvas around 1773-1775 in connection with the decoration of Guimard's hotel particulier on the Chaussee d'Antin, a scheme the young painter is traditionally said to have taken over after the dancer's quarrel with Fragonard. The picture was left unfinished and offers an early glimpse of the classicizing manner David would soon bring to maturity.
collection-of-beauty-madonna-and-child-g: The Virgin, in a pink robe and blue mantle with a halo suggested by warm light, holds the Christ Child on her lap as he reaches up toward her, a tall candle visible in the upper left. Painted between 1613 and 1614 and now in the Galleria Spada, Rome, the work demonstrates Artemisia Gentileschi's adaptation of Caravaggesque modelling — strong directional light giving the figures a sculptural solidity — to an intimate devotional subject.
collection-of-beauty-male-nude-edgar-deg: An academic study in oil on canvas of a reclining male nude, painted by Edgar Degas around 1856 during his years as a young art student in Paris. The canvas was reused, and traces of an earlier figure study, including toes and a bearded face, remain visible beneath the present nude. The painting is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, a gift of Philip and Catherine Korsant in 2007.
collection-of-beauty-man-in-a-black-cap-: An unknown sitter in a flat black cap and fur-collared dark coat, turned three-quarters to the viewer, inscribed with his age and the date 1545. The panel — signed on the reverse 'faict par Johan Bettes Anglois' — is the only securely attributed work by Bettes, whose technique shows the influence of Hans Holbein the Younger; the background, originally painted in blue smalt, has since degraded to brown. The portrait is now in Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-manet-edouard-portr: Ernest Hoschedé and his young daughter Marthe seated together on a garden bench, the girl holding a flower, the paint laid down in broad open strokes. Manet began the plein-air portrait at the Hoschedé estate at Montgeron in 1876; it is now in the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Buenos Aires.
collection-of-beauty-manet-musica-en-las: A fashionable crowd in top hats and crinolines listens to a band in the Tuileries gardens, the canvas crowded with portraits of Manet's circle, including Baudelaire, Gautier and Fantin-Latour. The flat patches of black coats and abrupt cropping mark Manet's first decisive turn toward painting modern Parisian life.
collection-of-beauty-mann-mit-dem-goldhe: A bearded soldier in shadow tilts his head down, the entire light of the picture pooled on the embossed gold helmet that gives the work its name. Long catalogued as a Rembrandt at the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin, the painting was reattributed in 1986 to a member of his close circle, though the impasto handling of the gilt remains exceptional.
collection-of-beauty-marc-franz-the-tige: A crouching tiger built from interlocking facets of yellow, green, red, and blue, its alert gaze directed outward while its body merges with the angular planes of the surrounding landscape. Franz Marc, co-founder of Der Blaue Reiter, painted this work in 1912, treating the animal as an emblem of primal vitality and borrowing Cubist faceting to fuse predator and habitat into a single dynamic composition.
collection-of-beauty-margaret-kemble-gag: Margaret Kemble Gage, wife of British General Thomas Gage, is shown seated in a rose-coloured gown with a decorative blue and gold sash and a turban-style headdress trimmed with gold, her elbow resting on the arm of a dark upholstered sofa. Copley painted the portrait in 1771, adopting the fashionable Turkish-costume convention for informal female portraiture. The work hangs at the Timken Museum of Art in San Diego.
collection-of-beauty-margaret-lady-elyot: Margaret à Barow, wife of the humanist Sir Thomas Elyot, faces right in a gabled hood, drawn in coloured chalks strongly reinforced with Indian ink around the head and headgear. Holbein made the study around 1532 alongside one of her husband, as preparation for matching painted portraits now lost, both sheets preserved in the Royal Collection at Windsor. The drawings are unusually well preserved, retaining white chalk heightening on the nose and forehead.
collection-of-beauty-maria-cristina-by-e: Princess Maria Christina of the Two Sicilies (1779–1849) is shown as a young girl in a white dress with a red sash, picking roses from a garden bush with a wicker basket of blooms at her side. Vigée Le Brun painted the portrait in 1790, during her period of exile from Revolutionary France. The work is held at the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples.
collection-of-beauty-maria-de-tassis-by-: Maria de Tassis is shown in a three-quarter-length portrait, wearing a starched lace ruff collar and a dark gown with gold-striped bodice, holding an ostrich-feather fan. Van Dyck painted the work circa 1629–30, bringing the silvery elegance of his Genoese manner to this Flemish aristocratic commission. The canvas is in the Liechtenstein princely collection at Vaduz.
collection-of-beauty-maria-omringd-door-: Painted as the altarpiece for Rubens's own funerary chapel in St Jacob's Church, Antwerp, the panel surrounds the Virgin and Child with saints in whose features the artist included self-portrait and family likenesses. It is among his last works, executed in the warm, fluid manner of his final Antwerp years.
collection-of-beauty-marie-buloz-pailler: Marie Buloz Pailleron stands outdoors in a black lace-trimmed dress, her red hair and pale complexion contrasting against a lush green garden background. Sargent painted the full-length portrait in 1879 at the family estate, adopting a plein-air setting unusual for a society commission. The canvas is in the collection of the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-market-scene-on-a-q: A teeming Antwerp quayside laden with game, fish, fruit and live animals, painted on a near three-metre canvas typical of Snyders's grand market series. The Flemish Baroque specialist often collaborated with Rubens on such still-life pageants, and his workshop reproduced the format for aristocratic dining halls.
collection-of-beauty-marktjaffagustavbau: A bustling market square in Ottoman Jaffa rendered with Bauernfeind's near-photographic precision, every robe, awning and stone of the citadel sharply observed. A trained architect turned Orientalist painter, he based such scenes on extensive study trips and on-site sketches in the Levant.
collection-of-beauty-mars-venus-and-vulc: Vulcan looms at the forge while Venus reclines with Mars and two cupids gather around a heap of armour, after Ovid's tale of the lovers exposed in the smith god's net. Signed and dated 1754, the canvas is among the earliest surviving paintings by Copley, then about sixteen and working out a European mythological vocabulary from prints in colonial Boston.
collection-of-beauty-mart-levitan: Sunlit snow lies thick around a yellow porch and stable, a single saddled horse waiting in the yard while bare aspens cast long blue shadows. Levitan painted March in 1895 at the Gorka estate, the canvas now in the Tretyakov Gallery and credited with bringing plein-air winter painting into Russian landscape.
collection-of-beauty-martelaarschap-van-: The martyrdom of Saint Apollonia, whose teeth are being torn out while her pyre is prepared in the foreground. The print follows a composition by Jacob Jordaens and was engraved by the Antwerp printmaker Marinus Robyn van der Goes for the seventeenth-century devotional market.
collection-of-beauty-martin-schongauer-c: An engraving of the procession to Calvary thronged with mounted soldiers, jeering onlookers and dogs winding across a vast horizon. Schongauer, the leading German printmaker before Dürer, brought a refined, silvery line and unprecedented compositional ambition to copperplate engraving.
collection-of-beauty-martin-schongauer-n: An Adoration of the Shepherds set in a ruined Romanesque shed, the rough stonework and spiky straw rendered in the crisp, hatched line for which Schongauer was renowned. His Late Gothic prints circulated widely and were copied closely by the young Albrecht Dürer.
collection-of-beauty-martin-schongauer-t: The Virgin in a red gown holds the Christ Child while Joseph, holding a bundle of straw, stands behind her alongside an ox and donkey in a stable interior. This painting, attributed to Martin Schongauer or his circle, is in the collection of the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna. A wicker basket sits in the foreground of the intimate, devotional scene.
collection-of-beauty-mary-cassatt-the-ch: Seen from a steep, raised viewpoint, a woman in a boldly striped dress bathes a small child in a plain basin, their bodies pressed together in tender absorption. Cassatt borrows the high vantage and patterned surfaces from Japanese woodblock prints, which she had studied closely in the Paris exhibition of 1890.
collection-of-beauty-mary-cassatt-the-te: Two women take afternoon tea, the visitor at right lifting her cup to her face while the hostess at left sits composed before a gleaming silver tea service. Cassatt painted the work in 1880, treating a bourgeois social ritual with an Impressionist looseness of touch and close attention to the decorative still-life passages in the foreground. The canvas is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-mary-stevenson-cass: A young woman in a pale pink evening dress occupies a theatre loge, a pearl necklace at her throat and a fan in her gloved hands. The warm interior of the opera house stretches behind her, with other boxes and their occupants visible in the distance. Painted in 1879, the work is held by the Philadelphia Museum of Art and belongs to Cassatt's series depicting fashionable Parisian leisure.

Cassatt depicts herself in a large hat and dark dress, her gaze directed downward as she works at a canvas just visible at the right edge. The loosely worked gouache and watercolour over graphite, made around 1880, is a rapid, intimate record of the artist at work rather than a formal posed likeness. The self-portrait belongs to the National Portrait Gallery in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-masked-ball-at-the-: Top-hatted men press around costumed women in dominoes beneath the colonnaded foyer of the old Paris Opéra on rue Le Peletier, painted only months before the building burnt down. Manet compresses the crowd into a frieze of black coats, reading the bourgeois carnival as a study in modern social ritual.
collection-of-beauty-maslenitsa-kustodie: Townspeople and sleigh teams cross a snowy public square ringed by onion-domed churches and merchant houses during the Eastern Orthodox Maslenitsa festival. Kustodiev returned to the Shrovetide subject several times in 1916, painting these celebrations of Russian provincial life from his wheelchair while bedridden Russia was fighting the Great War.
collection-of-beauty-massysm-quentin-the: A money changer weighs gold coins on a precision balance while his wife, distracted from a book of hours, turns to watch. Signed and dated 1514, the Louvre panel adapts Jan van Eyck's convex mirror motif on the table edge, reflecting a window and a small figure reading outside.
collection-of-beauty-mathis-gothart-grun: Christ hangs on a T-shaped cross against a deep teal sky, his contorted figure framed by the grieving Virgin and a kneeling Magdalene on his left, and the upright John the Evangelist on his right. Painted on panel between about 1511 and 1520, the Small Crucifixion is among Grünewald's most concentrated expressions of sacred suffering and is now held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

Christ hangs on a T-shaped cross against a near-black ground, flanked by the Virgin on the left and John the Evangelist on the right in attitudes of grief and supplication. Painted between 1523 and 1524 for the parish church of Tauberbischofsheim, the panel is one of Grünewald's last known works and is now in the Staatliche Kunsthalle, Karlsruhe.

A crowd of figures mock and beat a bound Christ, pressing around him in a compact, turbulent mass rendered in a shallow pictorial space. The Mocking of Christ was painted between 1503 and 1505 and is one of Grünewald's earliest surviving works, prefiguring the expressive violence of the Isenheim Altarpiece.
collection-of-beauty-matisse-open-window: The view from Matisse's hotel window at Collioure looks out through pots of climbing flowers to a harbour of sailboats under pink and green water. Painted in 1905 and shown at the Salon d'Automne that autumn, the canvas was bequeathed in 1998 to the National Gallery of Art, Washington from the estate of Mrs John Hay Whitney.
collection-of-beauty-matsue-izumo-576590: A crescent moon hangs in the twilight sky above a quiet canal at Matsue in Izumo Province, a lone boatman poling through still water that mirrors the warm glow of lamplight from the low buildings lining the bank. The woodblock print of 1924, titled 'Matsue (Crescent Moon), Izumo,' belongs to Hasui's 'Souvenirs of Travel, Third Series,' published by Watanabe Shōzaburō as part of the shin-hanga revival.
collection-of-beauty-matteo-ripa001-morn: A copperplate view of the Kangxi Emperor's summer retreat at Chengde, with mist breaking over the western ridge in fine engraved hatching. Ripa, a Neapolitan missionary at the Qing court, produced the imperial album that introduced Western intaglio printing techniques to China.
collection-of-beauty-matthias-grunewald-: Christ rises from the tomb in a halo of gold and crimson light, his shroud trailing as the helmeted Roman guards collapse blinded beneath him.
