collection-of-beauty-rubens-apostel-simo: Simon the Zealot appears in profile, absorbed in a worn book, the long saw of his legendary martyrdom resting half-visible at the lower left against a dark ground. The panel belongs to the Twelve Apostles series Rubens painted around 1610-12 for the Duke of Lerma, preserved intact at the Museo del Prado.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-de-verenigin: An allegorical pairing of Earth and Water in which a muscular Neptune-like figure crowns a reclining female personification, while putti frolic below and a cornucopia of fruit overflows at left. Painted in 1618 and now in the Hermitage Museum, the picture has been read as a plea for Antwerp's access to the sea. The warm flesh tones and surging figures are characteristic of Rubens's mature Baroque manner.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-feast-of-sim: Christ sits at the Pharisee's table while a kneeling woman — traditionally identified as Mary Magdalene — bows over his feet, scandalising the assembled guests. Rubens orchestrates the Gospel scene as Baroque theatre, with richly contrasted light, elaborate tableware, and vivid emotional reaction rippling through the crowd. The painting, dated between 1618 and 1620, is in the Hermitage Museum.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-landscape-wi: A panoramic Flemish countryside after a storm, peasants and cattle moving among glistening fields beneath a translucent rainbow. Painted on his country estate at Het Steen, it shows Rubens turning to landscape in his late years with broad atmospheric breadth.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-mars-et-rhea: The war god looms over the Vestal Rhea Silvia, the union that will produce Romulus and Remus and so found Rome. Rubens stages the encounter with cascading drapery, fluttering putti and the warm flesh-tones that mark his mythological inventions.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-medusa: The severed head of the Gorgon lies on a stony ledge, eyes still rolling and snakes writhing into a teeming brood of vipers, scorpions and lizards. Rubens collaborated with the animal specialist Frans Snyders on the reptilian still life, fusing Baroque horror with naturalist precision.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-painting-ada: Adam and Eve stand in a verdant Paradise in a dialogue that alludes to the Fall — Adam gestures toward Eve beside the Tree of Knowledge, an apple visible among the branches above. Painted between 1597 and 1600 and now in the Rubenshuis, Antwerp, this is among Rubens's earliest surviving figure compositions, reflecting the influence of his Flemish training before his Italian sojourn.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-peace-war: Painted in London for Charles I as a diplomatic gift, the allegory shows Minerva pushing back the war-god Mars while Pax nurses Plutus and children gather around the fruits of peace. The picture distilled Rubens's hopes for an Anglo-Spanish accord into a sumptuous tableau of bodies and abundance.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-peter-paul-m: A violent biblical tableau of soldiers wrenching infants from their mothers in a tangle of straining muscle and contorted limbs. Rubens compresses the figures into a writhing pyramid, drawing on his Italian study of Michelangelo, Caravaggio and antique sculpture.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-peter-paul-t: The three mythological Graces stand intertwined in an open garden setting, a garland of flowers suspended above and a fountain at right, their forms set against a luminous landscape sky. Rubens is said to have modelled the figures on his second wife Helena Fourment, celebrating a sensuous, unidealised standard of beauty. The painting, from around 1630–35, is held at the Museo del Prado.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-pieter-paul-: Part of the twenty-four-canvas Marie de' Medici cycle commissioned for the Luxembourg Palace, this scene stages the queen's 1610 coronation at Saint-Denis. Rubens orchestrates a vast crowd of dignitaries in a sweeping diagonal, mythologizing the event the day before Henri IV's assassination.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-portrait-of-: A bust-length portrait of a young fair-haired woman, her blond curls gathered into braids above a plain dark dress with a simple white décolletage. The luminous skin and lively gaze are typical of Rubens's smaller-scale portraits, now in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-rkdimages-27: A close study of a bearded man's head thrown violently upward in an expression of anguish or extremity, the loose, energetic brushwork typical of Rubens's preparatory studies. The work, titled 'Christ between the two malefactors,' is held at the Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh, and dates to the early seventeenth century.

A close study of a young man's head in strict profile, turned to the left, with wavy blond hair rendered in vigorous chiaroscuro. Dating to 1612 and held at the Norton Simon Museum, the panel demonstrates Rubens's habit of accumulating head studies as reference material for larger narrative compositions.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-saturn: The aged god Saturn devours one of his infant sons, biting into the flesh as the child writhes in his grip beneath the cold light of his eponymous planet. Painted for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada, Rubens fuses Ovidian myth with unflinching late-Baroque violence.
collection-of-beauty-rudolf-ernst-after-: Two men leave prayers through a magnificent horseshoe-arched doorway framed by carved stucco and blue-green tilework: an elderly worshipper in white robes and turban leans on his cane, steadied by a companion in an embroidered violet kaftan and red fez. The oil on panel, signed 'R. Ernst,' is typical of the Vienna-born Orientalist's polished studio compositions, which assembled Moorish architectural detail — much of it derived from the Alhambra — around quiet moments of daily ritual. Ernst spent most of his career in Paris painting such scenes for the Salon market.
collection-of-beauty-rue-neuve-notre-dam: A view down the Rue Neuve Notre-Dame on the Île de la Cité, the stone façades of tall urban buildings flanking the street as the towers of Notre-Dame loom at the far end. Eduard Gaertner painted this precisely observed cityscape in 1826, capturing pedestrians, riders, and the everyday activity of a Parisian street before the area was substantially altered in later decades.
collection-of-beauty-russian-victory-vyb: Russian galleys and ships of the line break through the Swedish fleet trapped in Vyborg Bay in June 1790, smoke from broadside fire rolling across the Baltic. Aivazovsky painted the engagement in 1846 as part of a Naval Ministry commission documenting Russian victories at sea.
collection-of-beauty-russians-at-navarin: Warships flying Russian and Ottoman flags exchange fire in Navarino Bay on 20 October 1827, masts toppling and flames rising as gunsmoke rolls across the open water. Painted in 1846, Aivazovsky's canvas records the allied action that effectively secured Greek independence, with survivors visible in small boats in the foreground.
collection-of-beauty-sa-8422-de-klovenie: View of the Kloveniersdoelen on the Amstel, with the militia guildhall and the Swijgh Utrecht tower rising at the corner of the Kloveniersburgwal. Painted in 1775, the cityscape records a stretch of Amsterdam that the Dutch capital would substantially rebuild in the nineteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-after: From the Inland Sea series of woodblock prints, this view shows fishing junks under afternoon light. Yoshida printed the same key block in successive variants from morning to night, a shin-hanga experiment in atmosphere achieved by altering only the inking and color blocks.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-eveni: Junks ride a glassy sea under a low evening sun in this version of Yoshida's six-state Sailing Boats suite. The warm orange ground and silhouetted sails show how shin-hanga printers could transform a single composition through color alone.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-mist-: Sailing junks drift in a pale, fog-bound sea, their masts dissolving into the haze. One of six time-of-day variants printed from a single key block, this state demonstrates Yoshida's command of bokashi gradations and his shin-hanga sensitivity to weather and air.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-morni: Sailing junks rest on a glassy sea suffused with warm rose and orange tones in this morning state of Yoshida's Sailing Boats suite, part of his Inland Sea series of 1926. One of six time-of-day variants printed from a single key block, the work exemplifies shin-hanga's command of atmospheric colour.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-night: In the night state of Yoshida's Sailing Boats suite, the junks' sails appear luminous against a deep indigo sea, their reflections shimmering below while distant shore lights glow on the horizon. Printed in 1926 as part of the Inland Sea series, the sheet demonstrates shin-hanga craftsmen's ability to evoke nocturnal light through carefully graded colour blocks.
collection-of-beauty-saint-christopher-f: A small copper engraving by Albrecht Dürer showing Saint Christopher wading through the river with the Christ Child on his shoulders, bracing himself on his staff as he strides to the left. Dürer engraved two versions of the subject in 1521, distinguished by the direction the saint faces. This impression, measuring only about twelve by seven centimeters, is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, which received it in the bequest of Julie Parsons Redmond.
collection-of-beauty-saint-francis-of-as: The saint swoons in the arms of an angel after receiving the stigmata, his companions sleeping in the moonlit landscape behind. One of Caravaggio's earliest religious nocturnes, the picture introduces the raking light and tender naturalism that would shape his mature style.
collection-of-beauty-saint-jerome-writin: The aged Church Father bends over an open volume, his bald skull echoing the memento mori at his elbow. Painted in Rome for Cardinal Scipione Borghese, Caravaggio strips the scholar's cell to a few essentials so that flesh, parchment and shadow can do all the speaking.
collection-of-beauty-saint-john-on-patmo: Saint John the Evangelist sits on the rocky shore of Patmos with a book open on his lap, looking up at a radiant vision of the Virgin and Child in the sky; his eagle perches at his side and a small sailing boat crosses the sea behind him. Schongauer's engraving joins the saint's exile on the island to the apocalyptic vision he recorded there, and carries his monogram below. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-saint-sebastian-ten: After the Roman martyr's ordeal at the column, two angels withdraw the arrows and bind his wounds. Rubens treats Sebastian's nude body in the heroic manner of antique sculpture and Italian masters, softening the violence into a Baroque tableau of muscular grace.
collection-of-beauty-samovar-malevich-19: A Russian samovar dissected into cylindrical and conical facets of grey, ochre, and tin. Painted in 1913 and now at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, the still life sits between Malevich's Cubo-Futurist machine subjects and the radical abstraction he would unveil as Suprematism two years later.
collection-of-beauty-san-jeronimo-leyend: The Church Father is depicted half-length in a rocky grotto, bare-chested and absorbed in his book, a crucifix steadying his left hand. Murillo treats the penitent scholar with restrained naturalism, the warm Sevillian light modelling weathered skin and beard against a deep brown ground.
collection-of-beauty-san-romano-battle-p: From the three-panel cycle painted for the Bartolini Salimbeni and later Lorenzo de' Medici, this London panel shows Niccolo da Tolentino leading the Florentines against Siena. Uccello's foreshortened lances, fallen soldier and patterned ground are a famous early experiment in linear perspective.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-0: A late Lamentation showing the dead Christ across the Virgin's knees, ringed by mourners in a steeply compressed group. Botticelli's tightly knotted figures and stark grief reflect the religious severity that gripped Florence in the Savonarola years.

Saint Augustine sits in his study, deep in thought before book, inkwell and astronomical instruments. Botticelli's fresco for the Florentine church of Ognissanti casts the Church Father as a Renaissance scholar, painted as a pendant to Ghirlandaio's Saint Jerome.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-a: The Virgin stands before a landscape background, her blue mantle wrapping around the Christ Child, who reaches upward and meets her gaze. The panel, dated 1490, is in the collection of the Fogg Museum at Harvard Art Museums. Botticelli's characteristic linear contours and pale tonality place the work within the Florentine devotional tradition of the late Quattrocento.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-i: A profile bust of a young woman with elaborately plaited hair, long identified, however speculatively, with the Florentine beauty Simonetta Vespucci. Botticelli converts a Quattrocento portrait formula into a half-mythological nymph, the linear refinement balanced by jewels and serpentine ornament.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-l: Botticelli reconstructs a lost painting by the Greek master Apelles as described by Lucian: King Midas with ass's ears is approached by Slander, dragged forward by a sinister train of Envy, Deceit and Conspiracy, while naked Truth points to the heavens. The panel is a humanist defense of innocence against false accusation.

The newborn goddess arrives at Cyprus on a scallop shell, blown ashore by Zephyr while a Hora prepares to robe her. Painted on canvas for a Medici villa and indebted to the antique Venus Pudica, the image fuses Neoplatonic philosophy with Botticelli's hallmark linear grace.

The dead Christ is supported across the Virgin's lap as Mary Magdalene clasps his feet and saints crowd the dark mouth of the tomb. Botticelli's late Lamentations, painted in the wake of Savonarola's preaching, abandon courtly sweetness for compressed, anguished figures.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-m: The enthroned Virgin prepares to nurse the Christ Child, flanked by Saint John the Baptist at left and Saint John the Evangelist at right, set against a lush garden bower dense with lilies and palms. Known as the Madonna Bardi, the panel was painted by Botticelli between 1484 and 1485 and is held in the Gemäldegalerie, Berlin. The figures' linear refinement and the symbol-laden botanical setting are hallmarks of Botticelli's mature altarpiece manner.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-r: Judith strides forward carrying an olive branch and sword, while her maidservant lifts the shrouded head of Holofernes behind her. The small Uffizi panel, dated 1470, pairs Old Testament tyrannicide with Botticelli's lyrical, wind-swept drapery. It is held in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.
collection-of-beauty-sans-culotte: A standing sans-culotte in the striped trousers, short carmagnole jacket and red cap of the Revolutionary Parisian, a pike at his side. Boilly recorded such figures and the street life of Paris through the 1790s. Oil on canvas, in the small finished format characteristic of the artist.
collection-of-beauty-sanson-matando-al-l: Samson grapples a roaring lion to the ground and tears its jaws apart, the biblical strongman rendered with anatomical force and twisting torso. Rubens reworked the subject several times, transposing the heroic male nude of antique sculpture into a violent Old Testament exemplum.
collection-of-beauty-sarah-goodridge-bea: A self-portrait restricted to the artist's bared breasts amid loose white linen, painted at miniature scale on a 6.6 by 8 centimetre ivory. Goodridge sent the case to the newly widowed senator Daniel Webster in 1828; he kept it among his papers until his death, and the Met acquired it in 2006.
collection-of-beauty-sarah-goodridge-eli: Elizabeth Greenleaf Parsons in lace cap and dark dress, painted in watercolor on ivory. Goodridge was the leading miniaturist of Federal-era Boston, trained partly by Gilbert Stuart; the portrait belongs to the Harvard Art Museums.
collection-of-beauty-sarah-goodridge-gil: A miniature portrait of the elderly portraitist Gilbert Stuart, his white hair and white cravat set against a deep green ground. Painted in watercolour on ivory circa 1825 by his pupil Sarah Goodridge, it is among the most intimate likenesses of the celebrated American painter.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-group-with-: Four figures recline on a grassy slope beneath parasols, their forms half-dissolved in dappled shade. Sargent treats the bourgeois leisure scene with rapid, broken brushwork, prizing the play of filtered light over portrait specificity.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-life-study-: A standing nude rendered with academic precision during Sargent's travels in North Africa, the body modeled in warm earth tones against a neutral ground. The study reflects his sustained interest in the figure outside commissioned portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-madame-ramo: Amalia Subercaseaux, wife of the Chilean diplomat Ramón Subercaseaux, is shown seated at a piano in a light interior, wearing a black-and-white dress with red floral accents. The composition belongs to Sargent's early Parisian period and was shown at the 1881 Salon, demonstrating his bravura handling of costume and interior atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-monetpainti: Sargent depicts his friend Monet at work outdoors at Giverny, easel propped beside a thicket as a young woman reads nearby. The picture is a personal homage from one painter to another, executed with the very plein-air looseness it documents.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-robert-loui: Robert Louis Stevenson strides across a dark red interior, his figure caught mid-step while his wife Fanny is glimpsed seated at the far right beneath a pale shawl. Painted by Sargent in 1885, the unconventional composition places the two figures in oblique relationship, the writer commanding the room while his wife recedes into the shadowed corner.
collection-of-beauty-sarto-andrea-del-se: The Florentine painter regards the viewer with a sober, narrow-eyed gaze, his beard close-trimmed and his black cap drawn low. Painted in 1528 and now in the Uffizi, the panel belongs to the final years of Sarto's career, two years before his death from plague during the siege of Florence.
collection-of-beauty-scene-des-massacres: Greek civilians huddle in the foreground as Ottoman cavalry round up survivors after the 1822 massacre on the island of Chios, in which tens of thousands were killed or enslaved. Delacroix exhibited the canvas at the 1824 Salon alongside Constable's Hay Wain; the picture entered the Louvre directly from the state purchase.
collection-of-beauty-scene-from-the-last: Thomas Cole depicts the scene from Cooper's novel in which Cora Munro kneels before the Delaware chief Tamenund on a rocky outcrop, a crowd of warriors encircling them against a sweeping mountain landscape. Painted in 1827, shortly after the novel's publication, the picture subordinates the narrative figures to a grand Hudson River School wilderness, the human drama rendered small beneath the soaring peaks.
collection-of-beauty-scheherazade-rimsky: A stage design for the Ballets Russes production of Scheherazade, set to Rimsky-Korsakov's symphonic suite, with billowing curtains and oriental cushions in saturated greens and oranges. Bakst's 1910 décor for Diaghilev established the scenographic vocabulary of jewel-toned exoticism that defined the company's early Paris seasons.
collection-of-beauty-schinkel1: A bust-length portrait of the Prussian architect Karl Friedrich Schinkel, painted by Carl Joseph Begas in 1826, showing the sitter with curling hair and a white cravat against a dark ground. Schinkel was at this date the leading architect of Berlin, responsible for the Altes Museum and the Schauspielhaus.
collection-of-beauty-schinkel2: Schinkel's elevation of the terrace at Orianda, a country retreat for Tsarina Alexandra Feodorovna planned on a cliff above the Black Sea in the Crimea. The architect's 1838 design fused a caryatid portico with hanging gardens and museum rooms; the cost was prohibitive and the palace was never built, surviving only in lithographs.
collection-of-beauty-schinkel3: An imagined interior of the reception hall in Schinkel's projected royal palace for King Otto on the Athenian Acropolis, with polychrome red-panelled walls, Corinthian columns, and a richly gilded beamed ceiling. Caryatid figures occupy the middle register, and bright light streams through the distant colonnade. Schinkel submitted his drawings in 1834 and the scheme was never built; the design was published in his Werke der höheren Baukunst (Berlin, 1840).
collection-of-beauty-schongauer-anthony: An engraving in which the hermit saint is hoisted into the air and tormented by a swarm of bristling, scaled, and beaked demons. Schongauer's burin work, with its dense parallel hatching and inventive monstrous anatomy, exerted a famous influence on the young Dürer.
collection-of-beauty-scops-owl-cherry-bl: A scops owl swoops in flight through a spray of cherry blossoms against a pale full moon, in the kachō-e bird-and-flower tradition. Ohara Koson's woodblock print, held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, combines soft tonal printing with the quiet naturalism characteristic of his Shin-hanga work aimed at early-twentieth-century export markets.
collection-of-beauty-scorn-from-le-brun-: Head turned aside with brow raised and lip curled to illustrate the passion of scorn, drawn from Charles Le Brun's lecture on expression. Issued by Bowles around 1785 in red-brown ink as part of his English Passions of the Soul, the print belongs to the long afterlife of Le Brun's 1668 lecture to the French Academy.
collection-of-beauty-sebastiano-ricci-it: The huntress goddess sits at rest, largely unclothed with white drapery beside her, a large white hound pressed at her side and hunting equipment at her feet. Painted by Sebastiano Ricci between circa 1700 and 1705, the work demonstrates the rich chiaroscuro of late Venetian Baroque while treating the mythological subject with sensuous ease.
collection-of-beauty-sebastiano-ricci-ve: A reclining nude Venus, a single sleeping infant putto at her legs, is approached by a leering elderly satyr in a warm palette of reds and pale flesh tones. Painted by Sebastiano Ricci between 1716 and 1720, the work is held at the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest, and reflects his debt to the Venetian mythological tradition of Veronese translated into a more intimate register.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-1628-: The young Rembrandt presents himself in a close-cropped bust, face half-lost in raking shadow beneath a tangle of frizzy hair, set against a plain grey ground. Painted between 1628 and 1629 during his Leiden years, the picture is among the earliest in his long series of self-portraits and already shows the experimental chiaroscuro that would define his mature work.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-1769-: Copley presents himself in a powdered wig and richly embroidered teal coat, his gaze directed steadily at the viewer. Painted in 1769, the portrait exemplifies the meticulous attention to surface and texture that distinguished his pre-European Boston work and is now held at The Athenaeum.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-1908-: Malevich confronts the viewer in a dark green coat against a swirling red-orange background of abstracted figures, rendered in bold, flat colour that prefigures his primitivist turn. The gouache, dated 1910–1911, marks a decisive shift from descriptive form toward the declarative palette of his early avant-garde work.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-as-th: Gentileschi merges self-portrait and emblem, depicting herself as the personification of Painting from Ripa's Iconologia: brush raised, gold chain bearing a mask, sleeves pushed back over a working arm. The conceit could only be staged by a woman, since the allegory was female.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-ed: The young Degas, around twenty-nine, looks out from a dark ground in a black coat and high collar, his expression guarded and slightly aslant. Painted around 1863, the picture entered the collection of Calouste Gulbenkian and now hangs at the Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-ge: A half-length self-portrait in which Watts wears a dark slouch hat and black velvet coat against a plain ground. Oil on canvas, 64.8 by 52.1 cm, painted in 1864 and held by Tate Britain. Watts painted it during his years at Little Holland House in Kensington, drawing on Old Master portraiture such as Raphael's Castiglione.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-gi: A young man in armour, long dark hair framing a pensive face turned slightly aside, emerges from a deep shadow in this work attributed to Giorgione and titled Self-portrait as David. The panel, dated circa 1508–1510, is held at the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum in Braunschweig and has long been identified through Vasari's account of the painter's self-portraits.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-pa: Gauguin shows himself half-length at a table with palette and brushes, the slope of an attic beam behind him, painted in the loosely broken brushwork he was developing in 1885. Painted the year he committed fully to painting, the picture is held at the Kimbell Art Museum and is one of several self-portraits from his early Post-Impressionist period.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-sa: Lepsius portrays herself three-quarter length holding palette and brushes, her gaze angled slightly downward against a warm golden ground. Dated 1885 and now in the Alte Nationalgalerie, Berlin, the picture displays the confident naturalism she developed through her training in Berlin and Paris.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-in-a-: The artist holds palette and brushes beneath a wide plumed straw hat, smiling outward in a pose adapted from Rubens's Chapeau de Paille. Vigée Le Brun cast herself as both fashionable subject and confident professional, a self-promotional image she repeated.

The artist holds palette and brushes beneath a wide plumed straw hat, smiling outward in a pose adapted from Rubens's Chapeau de Paille. Vigée Le Brun cast herself as both fashionable subject and confident professional, a self-promotional image she repeated.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-leani: Rembrandt leans his folded arm on a stone ledge, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer and wearing a beret and furred cloak — a composition that self-consciously echoes the poses of Titian and Raphael portraits then in Dutch collections. Signed and dated 1639, this is among the most ambitious of Rembrandt's self-portrait etchings, the work now held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-with-: Vigée Le Brun embraces her young daughter Julie, the painter in a white dress with red sash and headband, the child in blue. The intimate staging — figures locked in mutual embrace against a plain ground — was devised to project natural maternal feeling for a Salon audience in 1789. The painting is held in the Louvre, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-selfportrait-rembra: A tiny self-image of the painter in dark cloak and beret, head turned three-quarters into a pool of light. Measuring just 15.5 by 12.2 cm on copper and held by the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm, the panel is among Rembrandt's smallest self-portraits, made for the same collectors' cabinets that prized his etched heads of the same year.
collection-of-beauty-seriziat: Pierre Sériziat, the painter's brother-in-law, sits casually in riding dress — black tailcoat, buff breeches, and a tall black hat — a riding crop in one hand. David painted the portrait in 1795 after his release from prison following the fall of Robespierre, combining relaxed informality with Neoclassical clarity of contour.
collection-of-beauty-serov-devochka-s-pe: Vera Mamontova sits at a sunlit dining table in a pink blouse, peaches and autumn leaves scattered on the white cloth before her. Serov painted the work over several weeks at Abramtsevo in 1887, the canvas now in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-serovelizabethdepar: Peter II and Princess Elizabeth Petrovna ride out to hound — the young emperor on a grey horse, Elizabeth alongside him — borzoi streaming across the foreground beneath a cloudy sky. Serov painted the work in tempera on cardboard in 1900; it is held in the Russian Museum, St. Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-sesshushuutoutou: A winter landscape in ink on paper, with sheer rock formations rising over snow-laden ground, bare trees, and a small dwelling nestled in the valley below. Attributed to the Muromachi-period Zen monk-painter Sesshū Tōyō and dated to around 1470, the work is held in the Tokyo National Museum.
collection-of-beauty-seven-sacraments-ro: A triptych setting the seven sacraments inside a vast Gothic church, with the Crucifixion at the center of the nave and the rites unfolding in the aisles. Van der Weyden orchestrates devotional precision, contemporary Netherlandish architecture, and an extraordinary system of inscribed banderoles.
collection-of-beauty-shah-alam-conveying: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II hands a scroll to Robert Clive on a raised platform, transferring the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the East India Company. West reconstructed the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad fifty years after the event, recasting a profit-making contract as a regal ceremonial scene for the Company's London directors.
collection-of-beauty-sharaku-1794-ebisu: The lucky deity Ebisu is shown clutching a large red sea bream and laughing, a basket of fish at his feet — a subject associated with good fortune and abundance. Issued in 1794 by Tōshūsai Sharaku, the print is part of the artist's brief but prolific output during a single ten-month period of activity.
collection-of-beauty-shipwreck-turner: A naval transport founders amid towering green-grey waves, lifeboats overloaded with survivors swept up the swells. Turner makes the wreck of HMS Minotaur an early demonstration of his lifelong subject of nature's indifferent force at sea.
collection-of-beauty-shironeko-by-takaha: A white cat with orange patches and a decorative red collar rests compactly against a dark green ground, gazing directly at the viewer. Published in 1924, this shin-hanga woodblock print by Takahashi Shōtei is held in the National Diet Library and exemplifies the movement's close observation of animals within a traditional Japanese printing format.
collection-of-beauty-show-booths-kustodi: A colourful theatre booth dominates a winter fair, crowds in bright coats gathered around it beneath frost-white trees hung with pennants. Boris Kustodiev's painting of the Shrovetide balagany captures the festive character of provincial Russian folk celebration, a subject the artist returned to repeatedly around 1916–1920.
collection-of-beauty-shurygin-levitan-18: A bust-length portrait of the landscape painter Isaac Levitan, shown with dark curly hair and a beard, wearing a blue painter's blouse with a white ruffled collar. Painted by Alexander Shurygin in 1889, the work dates to the years when Levitan was consolidating his reputation in Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-siberische-blauwe-n: A small green Siberian blue robin perches on a snow-dusted reed shelter above a single pink peony, the composition set against a deep black ground. Ohara Koson worked closely with the Watanabe house to produce a long sequence of bird-and-flower designs for export.
collection-of-beauty-siernetel-in-bloemp: A potted coleus painted in Paris during Van Gogh's transition from the dark Dutch palette toward brighter, more broken color. The everyday flowerpot becomes an exercise in observing complementary reds and greens at close range.
collection-of-beauty-silk-merchants-indi: Turbaned figures rest and trade beneath spreading trees along a lakeside promenade in an Indian setting. Charles W. Bartlett's 1919 woodblock print, held at the Honolulu Museum of Art, belongs to his shin-hanga series in which Asian travel subjects are rendered through the Japanese colour-woodblock medium. The composition balances the blue water and dappled shade with the white-clad figures grouped across a broad stone terrace.
collection-of-beauty-simple-bodily-pain-: Head contracted around tightened brow and grimacing mouth to illustrate simple bodily pain, after Charles Le Brun. The red-brown stipple engraving was issued by Bowles around 1785 in his English Passions of the Soul, one of many reprints that carried Le Brun's expression studies into eighteenth-century drawing manuals.
collection-of-beauty-sinite-parvulos-a-g: Christ stands and places a hand on the head of a small child while a second child leans close, rendered in a spare, close-cropped composition against a landscape background. Artemisia Gentileschi painted this interpretation of the gospel injunction 'Suffer the little children to come unto me' between 1624 and 1625, applying the direct naturalism and strong colour contrasts associated with the Caravaggesque Baroque. The reduced cast of figures concentrates attention on the gesture of blessing rather than on narrative spectacle.
collection-of-beauty-sir-anthony-van-dyc: Van Dyck painted Charles I simultaneously from three angles — left profile, full face, and three-quarter right — providing the sculptor Gian Lorenzo Bernini with the reference views needed to carve a marble bust without the king travelling to Rome. Executed between 1635 and 1636 and now in the Royal Collection (RCIN 404420), the work is one of the most innovative portraits of the Stuart court, combining technical virtuosity with a dynastic purpose beyond the conventions of single-sitter portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-sir-david-wilkie-17: Wilkie commemorates the heroine Agustina de Aragón seizing a linstock to fire a cannon during the 1808 siege of Zaragoza, painted after his Spanish travels of 1827–28. The composition — with its windswept figure, fallen defenders, and ruined church towers — reaches beyond Wilkie's usual domestic genre toward the broader Romantic history mode. The work is held in the Royal Collection at Windsor Castle (RCIN 405091).

A crowded Scottish wedding feast unfolds in a low-beamed interior, fiddler at the front and dancers, drinkers, and gossips crammed across the canvas. Wilkie's careful Dutch-inspired genre painting helped popularize sentimental rural Scottishness for a Regency audience.
collection-of-beauty-sir-henry-raeburn-c: The Highland chieftain stands in full tartan dress against a plain interior wall hung with a circular targe and crossed weapons, every element of clan regalia on calculated display. Raeburn's 1812 full-length portrait, now at the National Galleries Scotland (NG 420), uses broad, direct brushwork to render Macdonell's self-presentation as a living embodiment of traditional Highland identity — a persona he cultivated with considerable deliberateness.
collection-of-beauty-sir-peter-paul-rube: Milkmaids tend cattle amid baskets of fruit and vegetables in a fertile Brabant landscape, a cornucopia of rural abundance. Rubens fuses pastoral genre and landscape with sweeping diagonal composition and an almost mythological sense of fertility.

Peasants, cattle, horses, and farm tools fill an open barn structure whose rear doorway reveals a snowy yard beyond. Rubens painted this interior scene circa 1618–19 — one of several works from this period treating the working Flemish countryside with the same vigorous handling he applied to mythological subjects. The painting is held in the Royal Collection at Buckingham Palace (RCIN 401417).
collection-of-beauty-sisley-bridge-at-vi: The cast-iron suspension bridge of 1844 across the Seine, looking toward Villeneuve-la-Garenne, with boats and figures along the bank. Oil on canvas, about 50 by 65 cm, painted in 1872 and acquired from the artist by Durand-Ruel that August; now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (object 437680).
collection-of-beauty-slave-ship: A slaver flings the dead and dying from its hold as a typhoon rises over a blood-orange sea, painted in response to the Zong massacre and abolitionist debate. Turner dissolves moral horror into dazzling atmosphere, the figures and chains barely surfacing through churning paint.
collection-of-beauty-sleeping-beauty-by-: Bakst's 1921 design for Scene 4 (The Awakening) of Tchaikovsky's Sleeping Beauty shows crimson curtains framing a canopied bed, with a dark winged form presiding over the sleeping figure. Executed in pencil and watercolour (48 × 66.8 cm) and held in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection in Lugano, the sheet was made for Diaghilev's 1921 London production at the Alhambra Theatre — the last major Ballets Russes collaboration before Bakst's death in 1924.
collection-of-beauty-slovane-v-pravlasti: The opening canvas of Mucha's Slav Epic shows a huddled couple on dark rocks beneath a starry sky while a towering spectral figure looms over the scene and fires burn in the distance — representing the early sufferings of the Slavic peoples between the Turanian and Gothic threats. Mucha's tempera-and-oil technique on the vast 810 × 610 cm canvas lends the symbolist scene a pale, dreamlike pallor distinct from his Art Nouveau poster work. Painted in 1912, the work is now in the Prague City Gallery collection.
collection-of-beauty-smalllakewithboatmu: An early oil sketch on cardboard from Munch's teenage years, depicting a still pond with a moored rowboat. The plein-air naturalism, painted before his Symbolist breakthrough, shows him absorbing Norwegian landscape conventions in compact, atmospheric form.
collection-of-beauty-smiling-girl-holdin: A young woman grins broadly at the viewer while holding up a small framed picture of a couple in flagrante. Signed oil on canvas of 82 by 64 cm in the Saint Louis Art Museum, the painting belongs to the genre of Utrecht Caravaggesque half-figures in which Honthorst turned tavern wit into salon entertainment.
collection-of-beauty-snow-over-zojoji-te: Kawase Hasui's woodblock print of 1953 shows the great red gate of Zojo-ji temple in the Shiba district of Tokyo under heavily falling snow, kimono-clad figures sheltering beneath umbrellas at its base against a darkened sky. The print was commissioned by the Japanese cultural authorities to document the craft of polychrome woodblock printing, subsequently designated an intangible cultural property. It was published by Watanabe Shozaburo in the large oban format, carved by Sato Jurokichi and printed by Ono Gintaro.
collection-of-beauty-snowscape: A winter landscape of snow-laden peaks and bare trees rising above a misty valley, the foreground pushed to one corner in the asymmetric manner that earned Ma Yuan the nickname 'one-corner Ma'. Attributed to the Southern Song court painter and held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei. Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk.
collection-of-beauty-sokokura-by-hiroshi: A woodblock view of Sokokura, one of the seven hot springs of Hakone, with travelers moving along a path through a steep wooded mountain gorge beside a rushing stream. The print belongs to Hiroshige's series Hakone shichiyu zue, devoted to the spa villages prized by Edo-period travellers along the Tōkaidō, and dates to 1852.
collection-of-beauty-song-of-the-lark-wi: A young farmhand pauses in a sunlit field, scythe and hat in hand, head tilted skyward toward the call of an unseen bird. Homer's 1876 canvas, now at the Chrysler Museum of Art, captures a suspended moment of rural American labour against an open summer landscape of green grasses and tall trees.
collection-of-beauty-songhamaenghodo: A tiger strides forward beneath a gnarled pine, rendered in colour on silk in the Korean Joseon tradition of auspicious beast painting. The work, attributed to Kim Hong-do (1745–1806?), pairs the apotropaic tiger with the longevity symbol of the pine and is held at the Ho-Am Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-sophia-alekseyevna-: Repin depicts the deposed regent Sofia Alekseyevna confined at Novodevichy Convent in 1698, her glare turned outward as a hanged Streltsy is glimpsed through the barred window. The picture compresses defeat, fury, and political claustrophobia into a single suffocating cell.
collection-of-beauty-sotatsu-dragons-and: Two dragons coil out of swirling ink clouds across a pair of folding screens by Tawaraya Sōtatsu, the early seventeenth-century founder of the Rinpa school. Working in ink alone, Sōtatsu pooled and blotted washes to make the beasts surface and dissolve in the mist. The screens are held by the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, D.C.
collection-of-beauty-spring-blossoms-mon: Flowering trees in full white and pink blossom spread across a green meadow beneath a luminous pale-blue sky, with a house glimpsed in the middle distance and a solitary figure standing among the trees. Painted around 1891 by George Inness near Montclair, New Jersey, the canvas exemplifies his late tonalist approach of softened forms and unified atmospheric light.
collection-of-beauty-spring-flowers-by-c: Peonies, hydrangeas, and lilacs spill from basket and pot against a darkened ground, painted with an almost botanical attentiveness. An early still life, it shows the young Monet weighing studio precision against the looser, light-driven handling that would soon define his work.
collection-of-beauty-spring-kustodiev: A spring thaw in a Russian provincial town, with flooded pathways, figures including children crossing planks over the melt-water, and birch trees coming into leaf before colourful houses and a distant church. Boris Kustodiev captures the festive mood of the Russian season in a bright, high-keyed palette typical of his townscape paintings.
collection-of-beauty-st-martin-met-dp820: Saint Martin stands wrapped in a deep fur-lined cloak, drawing his sword to cut away a portion of it for the half-naked beggar kneeling at his feet. Schongauer presents the saint's famous act of charity as a standing figure rather than the more familiar scene on horseback, signing the plate below with his monogram. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-st-michael-met-dp82: The archangel Michael, wings spread and robes swirling, drives a long-shafted lance into the dragon sprawled beneath his feet, its clawed wings and barbed tail thrashing across the lower margin. Schongauer's engraving renders feathers, drapery, and scaled hide with the disciplined burin work that made him the most influential Northern printmaker before Dürer. The plate carries his M†S monogram and dates from his Colmar workshop, around 1470-91.
collection-of-beauty-stadtschloss-schlue: The Schlüterhof, the baroque inner courtyard of the Berlin Palace redesigned by Andreas Schlüter, seen around 1830 with carriages, elegantly dressed figures, and onlookers gathered beneath a cloud-filled sky. Eduard Gaertner's topographically precise canvas records the courtyard's monumental Baroque façades before the palace's later demolition.
collection-of-beauty-starry-night-over-t: Gaslamps along the Arles quay double in the dark water of the Rhône while the Great Bear hangs overhead. A small couple strolls in the foreground, anchoring Van Gogh's nocturne to the human scale of the river town.
collection-of-beauty-stenka-razin-by-vas: The Cossack chieftain Stepan Razin sits brooding at the centre of a sailed river vessel, surrounded by his crew as the boat crosses a wide expanse of water. Vasily Surikov completed the large canvas in 1906; it is held in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-alexandra-p: A Schönheitengalerie portrait of Princess Alexandra of Bavaria, daughter of Ludwig I, rendered in Stieler's characteristic porcelain finish. The sitter is shown with the soft idealization the Munich court demanded of its gallery of beauties.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-auguste-str: A half-length portrait of Auguste Strobl (later Auguste Hilber), shown turning over her shoulder in a white off-shoulder dress with red ribbons in her dark curly hair and a pearl necklace. Painted by Joseph Karl Stieler in 1827 for King Ludwig I of Bavaria's Gallery of Beauties at Nymphenburg Palace, it exemplifies his characteristic smooth Romantic technique.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-jane-digby: Painted for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie, the portrait shows the English aristocrat at twenty-four, before the marriages and travels that would carry her from Munich to a Bedouin tent near Damascus. Stieler's smooth, neoclassical finish lends the sitter the air of court decorum she would soon scandalously discard.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-lola-montez: The Irish-born dancer who styled herself a Spanish noblewoman, painted at the height of her hold over Ludwig I of Bavaria. Her place in the Schönheitengalerie was itself a small political event, the affair contributing to the king's abdication the following year.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-marianna-ma: The Italian noblewoman, translator and longtime confidante of Ludwig I of Bavaria, shown with the soft idealisation reserved for the king's Gallery of Beauties in Munich. Stieler emphasises her dark eyes and intellectual composure, signalling her standing as a scholar rather than mere society sitter.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-portrait-of: Countess Caroline von Holnstein is shown half-length against a dark background, her braided hair dressed high, wearing a white silk dress with pink sleeves beneath a dark fur-trimmed wrap. The smooth flesh modelling and level gaze are characteristic of Stieler's portraits for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie, painted in 1834.

Friederike Freiin von Gumppenberg is depicted half-length against a luminous outdoor landscape of sky, hills, and water, wearing a deep crimson velvet wrap over a white dress with dark curling hair loose at her shoulders. The open background distinguishes this circa-1845 entry in Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie, now held at Nymphenburg Palace, from the darker grounds of Stieler's earlier portraits in the cycle.
collection-of-beauty-still-life-with-fru: The Antwerp specialist piles a Baroque larder with grapes, peaches, dead hare and game birds, animated by a thieving monkey, a wary cat and a darting squirrel. Snyders, Rubens's regular still-life collaborator, treats abundance as theatre, a moralising display of plenty under threat.
collection-of-beauty-stormy-sea-at-night: A three-masted ship rolls in heavy seas under a broken moon, its sails reefed against the swell, foam glowing pale where the waves crest. Aivazovsky painted dozens of nocturnal storm scenes throughout the 1840s, perfecting the thinly glazed translucent water that became his signature.
collection-of-beauty-stra-e-mit-kirche-i: August Macke's 1911 canvas shows a narrow street in Kandern winding toward a village church tower, the facades and road resolved into bold flat patches of violet, blue, purple, red, and ochre. The work, held at the Augustiner Museum in Freiburg, reflects Macke's assimilation of Cézanne's constructive approach and the Blaue Reiter colour sensibility he was developing at this time.
collection-of-beauty-stuart-george-washi: Gilbert Stuart's 1797 portrait of George Washington shows the president seated nearly full-length, dressed in black, with a red curtain to the left, a stone column and naval battle scene to the right, and the American eagle on the chair back — characteristics of the presidential portrait type rather than Stuart's unfinished Athenaeum bust. The work was painted for William Constable of New York and is dated 1797.
collection-of-beauty-stuck-franz-von-sal: Franz von Stuck's 1906 Salome depicts the dancer nearly nude, her torso bare above a fringed skirt, turning ecstatically against a dark star-scattered ground, adorned with a jewelled headdress and collar necklace. At the lower right, the Baptist's severed head rests on a dish that emits a blue glow, while a shadowed face looms behind it — a characteristic piece of Munich Secessionist Symbolism centred on the femme fatale.
collection-of-beauty-stuckelberg-sappho-: The Swiss painter imagines the Greek poet on a Lesbos cliff, lyre in hand, gazing seaward in the conventional pose of impending suicide. Stückelberg works in the late academic idiom, smoothing antique legend into a moralized salon image.
collection-of-beauty-sumida-river-the-wo: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, the print frames the Sumida River through the trees of the Suijin shrine grove at Masaki. Hiroshige uses the steep foreground branches and high horizon characteristic of the late series to fold the viewer into the riverside scene.
collection-of-beauty-sumo-wrestling-toad: Ohara Koson's colour woodblock print shows a group of toads in various animated poses — two grappling upright, others leaping or watching — on a grassy ground with a single autumn leaf in the air. Working in the shin-hanga idiom, Koson brings naturalist observation to a comic subject with long roots in Japanese caricature, here dating to around 1930.
collection-of-beauty-sunset-across-the-r: Plate twelve of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows boatmen and stevedores along the Sumida embankment, the long span of Ryōgoku Bridge cutting the composition while Fuji rises faintly in the dusk. Hokusai keeps the celebrated peak modest in scale, ceding the foreground to working Edo.
collection-of-beauty-sunset-at-montmajou: Painted on the rocky outcrop near Arles, the work surveys the plain of La Crau through a foreground of scrub oak and limestone, the abbey ruins behind. Long doubted as authentic, it was reattributed in 2013 on the basis of letters, pigments, and the painter's own catalogue.
collection-of-beauty-suprematist-composi: Geometric rectangles and bars in green, blue, yellow, orange-red, black, and pink float against a white field in dynamic, tilted arrangement. Painted in 1916 and held at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, the canvas is a key example of Malevich's Suprematist project to express pure feeling through non-objective form.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-by-repin: Vasily Surikov, the future painter of the Boyarynya Morozova and the Streltsy, sits in dark coat and full beard against a neutral wash, painted by his older Itinerant colleague Ilya Repin. The portrait is a record of friendship between two of the central figures of the Peredvizhniki, made at the start of Surikov's career as a history painter.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-horseman2: An alternate version of the Bronze Horseman composition, with Falconet's equestrian Peter the Great rearing on the Senate Square pedestal beside the Neva. Surikov produced the study in 1870 during his Academy years in St Petersburg, before the Moscow history paintings that would make his reputation.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-pokoreniye-: Cossack atamans under Yermak Timofeyevich fire muskets from low boats at Khan Kuchum's mounted Tatar host on the Irtysh River in 1582. Surikov worked on Yermak's Conquest of Siberia for four years, exhibiting the canvas in 1895; Nicholas II bought it for the Russian Museum the same year.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-streltsi: Condemned streltsy in white death shirts hold lit candles in carts before the Kremlin wall, watched by their wailing families and by Peter the Great mounted at the right, as the gallows wait at Lobnoye Mesto. Surikov set his 1881 canvas on Red Square in the autumn of 1698, after the second streltsy revolt; Tretyakov bought it from the ninth Peredvizhniki exhibition almost as soon as it opened.
collection-of-beauty-surikovmenshikovber: The disgraced Prince Alexander Menshikov sits hunched in a low wooden izba with his three children in Siberian exile, the ceiling pressing down on his bulk. Surikov finished the canvas in 1883, not 1888, and Pavel Tretyakov bought it from the eleventh Peredvizhniki exhibition for the gallery in Moscow, where the brooding interior still hangs.
collection-of-beauty-surikovsnowfortress: Cossack riders charge a snow fortress while villagers in sheepskin coats throw snowballs and brandish brooms, the assault staged as part of the last day of Maslenitsa. Surikov painted the Shrovetide game from memory of his Siberian childhood, exhibiting the canvas at the 1891 Peredvizhniki show before it entered the Russian Museum.
collection-of-beauty-surprised-rousseau: A tiger crouches through whipping grasses as rain slashes a tropical thicket lit by lightning. Rousseau's first jungle picture, it stitched together motifs from botanical gardens and prints into the imagined wilderness that would occupy him for the rest of his life.
collection-of-beauty-susana-acusada-de-a: Susannah stands draped before the council of Israel while the two elders point in false accusation, the young Daniel rising to interrogate them. Coypel painted the Book of Daniel episode between 1695 and 1696, the smooth modelling and theatrical gesture already pointing toward the early Rococo.
collection-of-beauty-susanna-and-the-eld: A late treatment of the Book of Daniel episode, with the bathing Susanna recoiling from the two judges who threaten to denounce her. Gentileschi returned to the subject across her career, here in a more restrained, tenebrist key than her early Pommersfelden version.

Painted when the artist was seventeen, the canvas turns the usual erotic pretext on its head: Susanna twists from the leering elders in unmistakable distress. The closed marble parapet and tightly wound figures give the scene a claustrophobia rare in the subject's long history.
collection-of-beauty-susanna-i-badet-187: Laurits Tuxen's 1879 canvas takes up the biblical subject in a polished academic idiom. The nude Susanna crouches beside a serving woman while a single elder, glimpsed at the upper left, reaches for the drapery — the intrusion caught at the moment of discovery. The work is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-suzanna-en-de-ouder: A Neoclassical treatment of the biblical episode in which the chaste Susanna, bathing in her garden, is spied upon by two elders concealed in foliage. The smooth handling of the nude and theatrical contrast of light and shadow reflect the Flemish painter's training in the academic tradition of David.
collection-of-beauty-suzanna-rembrandt-v: Rembrandt's small panel catches Susanna at the moment she steps from her robe, glancing back with sudden alarm as the elders emerge from the dark garden. The pearly nude and deep umber surroundings show the painter testing a Lastman-derived biblical mode in the year of Danaë.
collection-of-beauty-suzanne-et-les-viei: Susanna recoils in her bath as two white-bearded elders crowd in from the shadows, one gripping her arm as the other pulls back the drapery. Giambattista Pittoni painted the Old Testament subject in the 1720s in his Venetian Rococo manner, treating the apocryphal Book of Daniel episode with the pale flesh tones and sweeping silks typical of the city's settecento.
collection-of-beauty-suzuki-harunobu-c-1: From Harunobu's Eight Views of Ōmi, the print transposes the Chinese landscape topos onto Lake Biwa, here the returning sails at Yabase. Slender figures in a domestic interior stand in for the classical scenery, a witty mitate typical of his refined nishiki-e.
collection-of-beauty-suzuki-harunobu-wom: A young woman in a kimono holds a paper lantern aloft on a veranda at night, gazing up at a flowering plum branch above her. Suzuki Harunobu was among the first ukiyo-e artists to master the full polychrome nishiki-e technique, and this quiet nocturne, preserved in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, shows the delicate colour harmonies of dark ground, pale blossoms, and warm candlelight that define his work.
collection-of-beauty-svetlana-at-fortune: A young woman sits with her back to the viewer, gazing into a candlelit mirror in a darkened interior, performing a traditional Epiphany fortune-telling rite. Bryullov based the 1836 canvas on Vasily Zhukovsky's popular 1812 ballad 'Svetlana,' and the Russian Museum source identifies it as the only work by the artist on a national everyday theme; it is held by the Nizhny Novgorod State Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-swimming-hole: Six male figures occupy a stone masonry pier and the water around it in the afternoon sun, while a dog leans from the edge and a swimmer — identified in scholarship as Eakins himself — moves toward it in the lower right. Completed in 1885 and painted partly from photographic studies of Eakins's students, the canvas has been in the collection of the Amon Carter Museum of American Art in Fort Worth since the twentieth century.
collection-of-beauty-tab-v-fetus-with-um: An engraving from Tabulae VII uteri mulieris gravidae (Seven Tables of the Pregnant Uterus, 1748-51), the obstetric atlas of the Leiden anatomist Bernhard Siegfried Albinus. The fifth table shows a full-term fetus curled with its limbs drawn up, the umbilical cord running to the opened placenta, whose branching vessels are spread for display; an engraved Latin key fills the lower part of the plate. This impression is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
collection-of-beauty-tabi-miyage-dai-iss: A solitary worker bends over mats of drying red peppers on the shore, flanked by tall thatched stacks and bare wooden drying frames, with breaking sea-waves and a blue autumn sky beyond. The woodblock print is from the first volume of Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel series (Tabi miyage dai isshū), published in 1920, and captures a working coastal landscape in the Koshiji region.

Iwai Beach on the Bōshū coast, fishing boats drawn up under a high cloud bank. Hasui's first travel album returns again and again to such quiet shorelines, the bokashi gradients standing in for shifting maritime weather.

A sailboat rests at a rocky outcrop along the Bōshū (Awa Province) coast at dusk, its masts and banner reflected in calm water as a single figure stands on deck. The pale pink sky and still sea give the composition a contemplative stillness characteristic of Hasui's shin-hanga prints. The sheet belongs to Souvenirs of Travel I (1920), the series that established his collaboration with publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō.

A long wooden bridge spans the Asano River at Kanazawa, its dark piers mirrored in the shallow water below, while a grove of silhouetted pines rises against a muted evening sky. White egrets rest on the sandy bank beneath the bridge. The horizontal print belongs to Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel I (1920), rendered in the cool blue-green palette he favoured for twilight river scenes.

At night, the rooflines and lanterns of the Nagare pleasure quarter in Kanazawa are reflected in the dark water of a canal, a crescent moon rising above the pine trees beyond the compound wall. Hasui's deep blues and the still mirror of the water give the licensed district an atmosphere of hushed elegance. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel I series (1920).

A large orange moon hangs over a cluster of rustic wooden buildings on the Mishima River in Mutsu Province, its glow reflected in the water below as small figures go about evening tasks. The nocturnal scene — warm light against the deep blue of the night sky — exemplifies Hasui's mastery of atmospheric colour in the shin-hanga idiom. Published in 1919 (Taishō 8), the print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel I series.

A small boat with a lone figure drifts on the still waters of Tsuta Marsh in Mutsu Province, framed by overhanging green pines and overlooked by a rounded forested mountain catching the last light of day. Hasui's cool blues and greens render the lake surface with characteristic atmospheric depth. The print is part of the Souvenirs of Travel I series, published in 1919 (Taishō 8), and is held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

A mountain temple outside Sendai is glimpsed through a screen of trees, the architecture half-absorbed into the hillside. Hasui's compact composition and softly graded skies belong to the shin-hanga revival, which reworked classical ukiyo-e idioms with modern atmospheric effects.

A lone figure walks down the main street of the hot-spring village of Arayu in Shiobara, flanked by the dark wooden façades of inns and bathhouses, as a single autumn tree glows orange-gold at the far end of the lane and blue mountains rise behind it. The sharp contrast between the dark eaves and the luminous sky gives the composition its characteristic shin-hanga drama. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel I series, published in 1920 (Taishō 9).

Yuhi Falls drops between mossy cliffs at Shiobara, rendered with the layered greens and quietly observed water Hasui made his signature. Carved and printed in collaboration with publisher Watanabe Shozaburo, it is part of the first Souvenirs of Travel cycle.

The cliff face of Senjomaku rises from the still surface of Lake Towada, its scale exaggerated by Hasui's high horizon. Carved from successive woodblocks, the print exploits the bokashi gradient technique to soften water into mist.

Pine-fringed Kude Beach in Wakasa Province curves along the Sea of Japan, the foreground trees framing a low strip of water and sky. Hasui's clean geometry and reduced palette draw on Hiroshige's coastal landscapes while pushing toward modern simplification.

Lake Kugushi lies under a still, overcast sky, its shore traced by reeds and a scatter of fishing boats. The composition is typical of Hasui's first travel series, which favored the unspectacular waterways and country roads of provincial Japan.
collection-of-beauty-tabi-miyage-dai-nis: Rain falls in long diagonal strokes across the wooden stage of Kiyomizu-dera in Kyoto, its temple roofs darkened against a washed grey sky. Hasui treats the famed pilgrimage site not as a monument but as an atmospheric encounter with weather.

Two boats push through choppy seas close to the base of steep, densely forested cliffs at Urahama in Echigo Province, waves breaking white around them as diagonal rain marks the stormy sky. The close viewpoint and the turbulent water convey the physical effort of coastal labour in rough weather. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel II series (1921) and is held in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

At dusk, a solitary figure walks along a narrow lane beside the high stone walls and overhanging rooflines of Kōshō Temple in Himi, Etchū Province, a large tree silhouetted against the pale evening sky above. The close, vertical composition directs attention down the darkening passage to the fading light beyond the compound wall. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel II series, published in 1921 (Taishō 10).

Tall pines with rust-red trunks line the foreground of this view of the Ōi River at Arashiyama, their green canopy framing a covered pleasure boat moving across the water against a warm golden sky. The composition looks through the vertical trunks to a middle distance of rocky shore and distant hills, a device Hasui used throughout the Souvenirs of Travel II series (1921).

Moonlight silvers the surface of Lake Kamo on Sado Island, the far shore reduced to a dark silhouette. The night scene relies on the bokashi technique, gradient printing across a single block to model the broad sky.

A rough beach hut at Himi sits low against the Etchu shoreline, its dark timbers contrasted with pale sand and water. Hasui's interest is in working coastal architecture rather than scenic landmarks, a recurring trait of the second Souvenirs cycle.

A street view in the Shimohonda neighborhood of Kanazawa shows a low row of merchant houses under a wide, flat sky. The print's restrained palette and elongated horizontal proportion are characteristic of Hasui's urban observation prints.

The Yanagawa district in Kai Province appears as a cluster of farmhouses and rice paddies set against distant mountains. Hasui sketched directly from life on his journeys, then reworked the studies for the carvers and printers of Watanabe's workshop.

Wooden irrigation troughs lift water across a Sado hillside, a practical landscape of rural infrastructure. The print's quiet subject reflects Hasui's commitment to ordinary working scenes over the picturesque set pieces of older ukiyo-e.

Two deer stand before the vermilion facade of the Kasuga Shrine in Nara, their presence evoking the sacred deer that have roamed the precinct for centuries as divine messengers. Stone lanterns are ranged along the building's front, and a large tree rises behind the roofline into a partly cloudy sky. The print belongs to the Souvenirs of Travel II series (1921), from Hasui's Shin-hanga series.

Nigatsu-do, the hall on the eastern slope of Todai-ji where the Omizutori water-drawing rite is held each spring, is shown perched above its veranda balustrade. Hasui's diagonal viewpoint compresses the wooden gallery into a strong horizontal band.

A woodblock print from the Souvenirs of Travel II series depicts the Asahi Bridge spanning the river at Ojiya. Hasui's shin-hanga style fuses Western perspective with traditional Japanese block-printing, building atmosphere through layered bokashi gradations.

Morning along Osaka's Dotonbori canal finds the famed entertainment district at its quietest, the theater district's lanterns unlit and its banks emptied of crowds. The composition trades nightlife spectacle for a city caught off-stage.

A waterfront street in Aikawa on Sado Island at dusk, with rough wooden boat sheds lining a rocky shore and an adult and child picking their way along a fence. The sourceDescription notes this is a dusk scene from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, published 1921. Hasui renders the coarse timber structures and pebbled beach with the atmospheric economy characteristic of his shin-hanga work.

Two figures — an adult and a child — pause on a path that descends toward the bay at Kamo-mura on Sado Island, with scattered buildings to either side and a mountainous ridge rising beyond the water. The wide middle ground of blue water and cloud-reflected sky does most of the visual work. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, published 1921.

Mano Bay opens across the full width of the composition, a long low coastline of green hills and what appear to be stone piers stretching along the horizon. Above it, a sky full of billowing pink and white clouds dominates the upper two-thirds of the print, their warm tones reflected in the water below. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, published 1921.

A snowy winter coastal scene at Nishimikawa-zaka on Sado Island, with a curving bay of deep blue water sheltered by snow-laden slopes and foreground pines. Small figures are visible on the path near the shore. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II, published 1920, exemplifying the shin-hanga interest in seasonal atmosphere.

A full moon rises over a calm bay at Ogi on Sado Island, casting its reflection on the dark water while a lone figure crouches at the base of a large rock formation in the foreground. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II series, the composition contrasts the luminous moon and its reflection against the dark mass of rock and densely wooded islets beyond.

Takamatsu Castle in Sanuki Province, one of the few sea-fed castles in Japan, is glimpsed across its tide-fed moat. Hasui's view registers the rebuilt keep and surrounding stone embankments under a softly graded shin-hanga sky.

A snow-covered corridor and gallery of the Itsukushima Shrine at Miyajima extends over the sea, its vermilion pillars contrasting with the white snow on every horizontal surface and the blue-grey water below. Snow falls steadily against a clouded sky. A woodblock print from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel II (1921), published as part of his extended series of atmospheric Japanese landscapes.

The fishing town of Miyazu in Tango Province, near the spit of Amanohashidate, opens onto a calm bay edged by mountains. Hasui's restrained palette of slate blues and greens is tuned to the overcast light of the Sea of Japan coast.

Night rain falls heavily on the port of Teradomari, lantern light scattering across wet ground. Hasui was a master of nocturnes, and the sheet uses successive overprintings to build a saturated, almost lacquered darkness.

A partial view of the Phoenix Hall at Byodo-in in Uji, rendered as a shin-hanga woodblock print. Hasui isolates a fragment of the eleventh-century temple's tiled roofline, using flat colour fields and quiet tonal washes characteristic of the Souvenirs of Travel II series.

Dawn snow lies thick over the harbor at Ogi on Sado, with moored boats reduced to silhouettes against pale water. The print pairs a graded pink horizon with cold blue shadows, a daybreak chord Hasui returned to throughout his career.

Snow blankets the pine spit of Amanohashidate, the narrow sandbar in Tango Bay long counted among the Three Views of Japan. Hasui strips its familiar profile back to a quiet white horizontal between sea and sky.
collection-of-beauty-tabi-miyage-dai-san: A torii gate stands on a rocky shore at Futomi in Awa Province, flanked by a pair of stone lanterns and backed by crashing waves and distant green islands. A small figure shelters beneath the gate, and a wooden boat rests to one side. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1925), the composition centres on the coastal shrine's gateway as a framing device for sea and sky.

Asahi Peak fills the composition as seen from Mount Hakuba, its steep rocky faces streaked with snow and flanked by dark green forest slopes under a vivid blue sky. A single bank of cloud breaks around the upper ridge. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1924), the print's bold close-up perspective and saturated colour are characteristic of Hasui's mountain subjects within the shin-hanga tradition.

A traveller's view along the Nakayama-Shichiri road threading through the mountains of Hida Province. The print belongs to Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III, in which woodblock bokashi gradations evoke the changing light of remote inland routes.

The narrow lanes of the Arifuku hot-spring quarter in Iwami Province glow with the warm amber light of inn windows at night, red-tiled rooftops clustered beneath a dark hillside of pines. A few figures move along the alley. A woodblock print from Kawase Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III (1924), the composition conveys the intimate warmth of a provincial onsen town through its contrast of lit interiors against the dark forest above.

A coastal view of Hinomisaki on the Izumo peninsula, where pine-clad cliffs meet the Sea of Japan. Hasui's woodblock translates wind, wave and weather into a few decisive colour blocks, a characteristic of his Souvenirs of Travel III landscapes.

A hazy moon hangs over the canals of Matsue in Izumo Province, the city's wooden buildings dissolving into a violet dusk. Hasui's bokashi shading delivers the title's oborozuki — the misted moon of classical Japanese poetry.

Fishing boats and tile-roofed houses cluster along the harbour at Mihogaseki on the Shimane peninsula. The shin-hanga print balances closely observed coastal architecture against the broad calm of the bay.

An autumn rainbow arcs above rice fields at Hatta in Kaga Province. Hasui uses overlapping bokashi gradations to render the prismatic band — a meteorological subject that had become a quiet specialty of his shin-hanga landscapes.

The five timber arches of the Kintai Bridge in Suo Province span the Nishiki River, a famed seventeenth-century engineering feat. Hasui presents the structure in shin-hanga woodblock, foregrounding its rhythmic silhouette against riverbank pines.

A woodblock print from Hasui Kawase's Souvenirs of Travel III series (1926), depicting the torii gate of Gozanoishi Shrine standing in the waters of Lake Tazawa. The large, dark-timbered gate occupies the foreground, its reflection shimmering in the calm lake, with green hills rising beyond under a cloud-dappled summer sky. The composition exemplifies the shin-hanga movement's combination of traditional Japanese subject matter with precise, luminous colour printing.
collection-of-beauty-taj-mahal-by-charle: A 1916 woodblock print by Charles W. Bartlett depicting the Taj Mahal viewed from across the Yamuna River, with a small boat and a seated figure in the foreground. The mausoleum and its flanking structures are rendered in pale, graded washes against a clear blue sky, their forms reflected in the still water. Made during Bartlett's Asian travels and printed in Tokyo, the work combines British watercolour sensibility with the flat, refined colour harmonies of the shin-hanga woodblock tradition.
collection-of-beauty-takiyasha-the-witch: A nishiki-e triptych staging the sorceress Takiyasha as she summons a colossal skeleton against the warrior Mitsukuni in the ruined Soma palace. Kuniyoshi compresses three full sheets into one continuous, theatrically lit scene drawn from the gothic literature of late Edo.
collection-of-beauty-tamakatzura-tamator: A woodblock print by Utagawa Kuniyoshi depicting Tamatori, sword raised, confronting a large octopus as she recovers the Dragon King's pearl from his underwater realm. The composition shows a sailing vessel in an upper vignette and the dramatic underwater struggle below, with waves and the octopus's coiling tentacles filling the lower sheet. The subject, drawn from the legend of Prince Fujiwara no Fusasaki's mother, was a recurring theme in Kuniyoshi's ukiyo-e narrative prints.
collection-of-beauty-tamatori-being-purs: A second telling of the Tamatori legend, with the diver fleeing the underwater palace as a dragon and its attendants give chase. Kuniyoshi exploits the woodblock medium's capacity for sweeping diagonals and undulating tendrils of marine life.
collection-of-beauty-tempelskatten-peter: Despite the catalogue title, the panel records a bustling Flemish ferry crossing to Antwerp, packed with passengers, cargo and livestock. Jordaens animates the scene with the boisterous, low-life realism that anchored his early Antwerp output.
collection-of-beauty-tentaciones-de-cris: A fresco from the south wall of the Sistine Chapel staging all three temptations of Christ around a centrally placed temple based on Rome's Hospital of Santo Spirito. Botticelli folds the gospel narrative into a contemporary Roman setting alive with allegorical figures and Medici allusions.
collection-of-beauty-terror-antiquus-by-: Lightning splits a darkening sky over the Aegean as an archaic kore smiles enigmatically in the foreground, the Acropolis and the citadels of Mycenae and Tiryns flickering below. Bakst built the 250 by 270 cm canvas after a 1907 trip to Greece with Serov, aiming at an apocalyptic fable of ancient cataclysm. It won a gold medal at the 1910 Brussels Exposition Universelle and entered the State Russian Museum.
collection-of-beauty-terrour-or-fright-f: A head with eyes flung wide and mouth open in a scream, codifying Terrour or Fright in the system of facial passions. Engraved for Robert Sayer's 1765 English edition after Charles Le Brun's Paris academy lectures, the plate is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-abduction-of-th: Roman men seize struggling Sabine women in a tangle of figures, a classical history subject. Millet worked the canvas around 1844 to 1847, in the period before he settled at Barbizon and turned to peasant labour; the scene follows the Livy episode long favoured by academic painters.
collection-of-beauty-the-antiques-seller: An Orientalist genre interior (1887, oil on panel) by Rudolf Weisse, depicting three figures — two seated or standing buyers in colourful robes and a merchant in a doorway — examining a large brass tray in a richly appointed bazaar setting. Carpets hang on the walls behind, while a rifle, brass lamps, and decorative vessels fill the foreground. The work is characteristic of the meticulous cabinet-picture precision applied to Near Eastern market subjects in late nineteenth-century European painting.
collection-of-beauty-the-artist-s-garden: Painted in 1873 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, this canvas by Claude Monet shows a corner of his Argenteuil garden in full summer bloom, dahlias massed in reds and whites before the painter's house. Broken, impasto-rich brushwork captures the shimmer of light on foliage and flowers, with a lone figure visible near the building in the background. The work is a confident example of Monet's Impressionist garden subjects from his years in Argenteuil.
collection-of-beauty-the-artist-s-wife: The painter's wife seated in his studio, surrounded by the props of his trade. Oil on canvas, 40.6 by 32.9 cm, at the Clark Art Institute and dated about 1795 to 1799. Boilly returned often to domestic interiors built around a single figure.
collection-of-beauty-the-arts-painting: Alphonse Mucha's 1898 lithograph Painting, from his four-panel allegorical suite The Arts, presents a young woman in three-quarter view holding a red carnation and a paintbrush against a softly tinted circular ground. Her auburn hair is adorned with a jewelled headpiece, and a ring of decorative medallions frames the composition within the arabesque border typical of Mucha's Paris-period Art Nouveau style. The work was published by F. Champenois, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-the-attack-by-veres: Painted between 1887 and 1895 and held at the Museum of Patriotic War 1812, Moscow, this canvas by Vasily Vereshchagin depicts Russian infantry charging through a snow-covered forest, bayonets fixed and a standard raised against bare and frost-laden pines. A mounted officer urges the advance at left while soldiers press forward through drifts and fallen timber, smoke drifting through the trees. The work belongs to Vereshchagin's series on Napoleon's 1812 Russian campaign, rendered with the unvarnished realism characteristic of his battle subjects.
collection-of-beauty-the-back-of-the-fuj: A woodblock view from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, taken from the rear face of the mountain along the Minobu River. Hokusai contrasts the sinuous river bend and rocky banks with the broad, simplified silhouette of the peak, animated by tiny travelling figures.
collection-of-beauty-the-barber-institut: Turner's marine pairs working fishermen and beached fish with a low sun burning through coastal mist. Held by the Barber Institute, the picture exemplifies his early atmospheric naturalism, in which form is dissolved by light and humidity rather than drawn line.
collection-of-beauty-the-bathing-posts-b: Two slender bathing markers rise from the surf off the Brittany coast, flanking a pale horizon where small sailboats pass under a broken, cloud-streaked sky. Whistler reduces the scene to horizontal bands of blue-grey and green, exercising the tonal restraint characteristic of his late Aestheticist practice. Painted in 1893 and now in the Hunterian Museum and Art Gallery, Glasgow, this small oil on wood measures only 16.6 by 24.3 centimetres.
collection-of-beauty-the-beach-at-etreta: Monet painted the famous arched chalk cliff at Étretat with the slender Aiguille needle beyond, seen from the water's edge where a fleet of small sailing boats crosses the luminous surf. Broken brushwork in pink, blue, and cream dissolves the forms in atmospheric haze. Painted in 1885–86, the canvas is held by the Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts, Moscow.
