collection-of-beauty-the-beach-at-trouvi: Monet depicts the busy wooden boardwalk at Trouville, where fashionably dressed visitors promenade with parasols against the backdrop of the town's grand seafront hotels and flags. The sea gleams in the distance under a cloudy sky, and the composition captures the resort's sociable, sunlit atmosphere through loose, confident brushwork. Painted in 1870, the work is now in the Wadsworth Atheneum Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-beautiful-serva: In this oval-format Rococo canvas, a young woman reclines on a canopied bed and turns to glance at a youthful male figure who reaches over her, the whole scene bathed in golden-yellow drapery. Fragonard's fluid, loaded brushwork animates the silks, linens, and curtains with characteristic speed and lightness. The painting is held by the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm.
collection-of-beauty-the-beheading-of-sa: Painted for the Oratory of San Giovanni in Valletta, where it remains the only canvas Caravaggio signed — in the spilled blood of the saint. The huge, half-lit composition stages the executioner mid-action with Caravaggio's signature tenebrist sobriety.
collection-of-beauty-the-blinding-of-sam: A violent rendering of Judges 16, with Philistine soldiers pinning Samson while a blade is driven into his eye and Delilah flees with the shorn hair. Rembrandt extracts maximal drama from a sudden shaft of daylight cutting into the cave-like darkness.
collection-of-beauty-the-blue-boy: A young man in a slashed blue satin suit of the Van Dyck period stands in a parkland landscape, plumed hat in hand. Painted around 1770 and shown at the Royal Academy in 1770, Gainsborough's portrait of the ironmonger's son Jonathan Buttall now hangs at the Huntington Library in San Marino.
collection-of-beauty-the-burning-of-the-: Aivazovsky depicts the Greek fireship attack led by Konstantinos Kanaris against an Ottoman flagship, its hull erupting in a column of fire and sparks while observers row clear in the foreground and steep cliffs rise in the background. The night sky and churning water reflect the blaze in the painter's characteristic dramatic marine style. Painted in 1881, the canvas is in the National Gallery of Athens.
collection-of-beauty-the-card-sharp-on-t: A card game at a makeshift table on a sunlit Parisian boulevard, a sharper at work among a mixed crowd of players and onlookers. Oil on panel, 24 by 33 cm, in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. Boilly showed it in 1808 with a pendant of young Savoyards displaying their marmot, among his first street scenes of everyday Paris.
collection-of-beauty-the-christian-marty: A Roman arena scene in which kneeling Christians pray as lions are released and crucified figures burn against the stadium walls. Gerome combines archaeological detail of the Circus Maximus with the polished academic finish typical of his Salon machines.
collection-of-beauty-the-coast-of-seven-: A print from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, in which a clearing of pruned, circular pines frames the distant volcano. The flattened decorative pattern of the foliage demonstrates the artist's command of Edo-period graphic abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-the-collector-of-pr: A bearded man in a dark coat and hat sits absorbed before a wall hung with botanical and decorative prints, a portfolio of images resting open on his knees. Degas renders the collector's interior with close-toned observation, placing the human subject within an environment defined by images rather than narrative action. Painted in 1866, the canvas is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-the-concert-a22894: A large company of musicians and revellers crowds around a draped table to sing, play lutes and violin, and drink by bright indoor light, with open music books spread before them. Gerard van Honthorst renders each face with animated expression, situating the scene within the Utrecht Caravaggist tradition of merry company paintings he developed after returning to his home city. Signed and dated 1623, the canvas is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.
collection-of-beauty-the-conspiracy-of-t: The surviving central fragment of Rembrandt's largest history painting, commissioned for Amsterdam's new Town Hall. Civilis raises a sword in a one-eyed oath-taking with his Batavian rebels — a coarsely lit, almost barbaric image that the city soon rejected.
collection-of-beauty-the-creation-of-ada: A fresco at the centre of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, in which God reaches across the void to a languid Adam. Michelangelo compresses the moment of ensoulment into the famously unmet gap between the two extended fingers.
collection-of-beauty-the-daughters-of-ed: Four sisters stand in the dim foyer of the Boit family's Paris apartment, the youngest seated on the rug, the eldest pair half-swallowed by shadow beside a pair of monumental Japanese vases. Sargent borrowed the deep recessive space and palette directly from Velazquez's Las Meninas, which he had copied in Madrid in 1879; the picture entered the MFA Boston in 1919.
collection-of-beauty-the-death-of-the-ea: William Pitt collapses among fifty-five identifiable peers beneath tapestries of the Spanish Armada's defeat, the moment of his fall in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778. Copley worked on the ten-foot canvas for two years and in 1781 installed it in a pavilion as a paying one-work show; it is now at Tate.
collection-of-beauty-the-descent-from-th: The body of Christ is lowered from the cross by several figures while the Virgin, clad in blue, has collapsed at the foot of the cross among the holy women. Painted by Charles Le Brun in the late 1640s during his first years back in Paris after studying with Poussin in Rome, the canvas was acquired by the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in 2004 with funds provided by the Joseph B. Gould Foundation, and Cary Grant and Fred Maxwell by exchange (M.2004.239).
collection-of-beauty-the-doorway-met-dp8: An ornate Renaissance doorway opens directly onto the water of a Venetian canal, its carved frame and latticed windows etched in dense detail that thins to almost nothing at the edges of the plate; a figure pauses on the shadowed steps within. The etching and drypoint belongs to the First Venice Set, the twelve plates the Fine Art Society commissioned from Whistler in 1879 after his bankruptcy. The doorway is that of Palazzo Gussoni on the Rio de la Fava; this impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-emperor-commodu: An engraving from Goltzius's Roman Heroes series, depicting the megalomaniac emperor in the lion-skin and club of Hercules. The muscular low-angle figure and virtuoso swelling burin lines exemplify the technical bravura of Northern Mannerist printmaking.
collection-of-beauty-the-end-of-the-pose: A studio interior in which a model steps down from the dais at the close of a session, while the artist's marble in progress stands beside her. Gerome, both painter and sculptor, treats the academic ritual with cool, polished precision and an eye for telling props.
collection-of-beauty-the-entombment-of-c: Nicodemus crouches under the weight of the dead Christ while the Virgin and the Marys raise their arms in grief above the cold stone slab. Painted between 1600 and 1603 for the Vittrice chapel in Santa Maria in Vallicella in Rome, Caravaggio anchors the descending diagonal of bodies on a corner of bare rock pushed out toward the viewer.
collection-of-beauty-the-fall-of-man-161: Adam and Eve recline together beneath the Tree of Knowledge, Eve offering the forbidden fruit while the serpent winds through the branches above. A cat rests at their feet and goats graze in the background landscape. Painted in 1616 by the Haarlem master Hendrick Goltzius and now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the picture exemplifies the smooth, naturalistic idealism of his mature style.
collection-of-beauty-the-famous-scenes-o: A vertical ōban from the Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces series, looking down on the swirling Naruto whirlpools that churn between Awa and Awaji. Hiroshige flattens the sea into concentric arcs of bokashi blue, framed by a steep cliff at left.
collection-of-beauty-the-farm-at-les-col: The farmhouse at Les Collettes seen through a screen of olive and orange trees, the foliage broken into flickering touches of green and rose. Renoir bought the estate at Cagnes near Nice in 1907 and moved there in 1908, painting the farm repeatedly between 1908 and 1914. Oil on canvas, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-the-feast-in-the-ho: A vast Venetian banquet is staged beneath a Palladian loggia of three grand arches, populated by guests of diverse social rank, servants, dwarves, dogs, and a falconer with a hawk at the right. Originally intended as a Last Supper for the refectory of Santi Giovanni e Paolo, the work was retitled after the Inquisition objected to its profane figures; it is now in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
collection-of-beauty-the-fighting-temera: The 98-gun veteran of Trafalgar is towed by a black steam tug along the Thames toward the breaker's yard, set against a smouldering sunset. Turner contrasts the pale, ghostly hulk with the squat industrial tug, mourning the passing of the age of sail.
collection-of-beauty-the-fountaine-famil: A conversation piece showing a man, woman, and two children with a spaniel in an elegant interior, painted by John Singleton Copley in 1776 at the outset of his English career. The warmly lit domestic setting and characterful poses reflect the English conversation-piece tradition, and the work is now at Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-the-fuji-from-kanay: An additional view from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, looking across the boulder-strewn Ōi River from the Kanaya post-station toward a snow-capped Fuji. Travellers and porters ford the shallows in the foreground, anchoring the landscape in everyday Tōkaidō life.
collection-of-beauty-the-gold-scab-erupt: Whistler's savage caricature of his former patron Frederick Leyland, painted in 1879 after the Peacock Room dispute and Whistler's bankruptcy, in which Leyland was a creditor. Leyland appears as a scaly, peacock-feathered demon seated on Whistler's White House while playing the piano — a jab at his amateur musicianship — with sacks of money at his feet. The painting is now in the de Young Museum, San Francisco.
collection-of-beauty-the-golden-age-oil-: A crowded paradisal scene drawn from Ovid's Metamorphoses, with figures feasting, dancing, and celebrating in a wooded landscape alongside cattle and other animals. Painted in oil on copper in 1605 and held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the small plate showcases Joachim Wtewael's Utrecht Mannerism at its most refined, the polished metal support intensifying the jewel-like colour of the intricate composition.
collection-of-beauty-the-golden-pavilion: Yoshida Hiroshi's colour woodblock print of Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion in Kyoto, from his 1933 Kansai District series. The gilded temple rises over its reflecting pond in the layered, atmospheric colour that defined Yoshida's shin-hanga landscapes. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-gorge-at-vareng: Monet depicts a rocky Normandy clifftop at Varengeville with a small stone cottage nestled among the scrubby vegetation, the open Channel stretching to the horizon beyond. Painted in 1882, the canvas translates the sunlit cliff vegetation into vibrating broken touches of green, lilac, and ochre, and is now on loan to the California Palace of the Legion of Honor in San Francisco.
collection-of-beauty-the-grand-canal-of-: Painted on a Venetian visit alongside Monet, the canvas captures the Grand Canal in shimmering broken touches of blue, white and ochre. Striped mooring posts cut vertical accents through the rippling water, marking Manet's most overtly Impressionist experiment.
collection-of-beauty-the-grand-quay-at-h: A working harbour view of Monet's home port, painted the year of the first Impressionist exhibition. Masts, smokestacks and reflections dissolve into rapid, comma-like strokes, the artist treating modern dockside bustle with the same atmospheric urgency he had just brought to Impression, Sunrise.
collection-of-beauty-the-holy-family-wit: An intimate devotional panel showing the Madonna and Child with St Elizabeth, the infant Baptist and a hovering dove of the Holy Spirit. The warm flesh tones and tender exchange of glances reflect Rubens's recent return from Italy.
collection-of-beauty-the-hookah-lighter: Nude women at leisure in a marble hammam interior, a hookah and brass vessels arranged in the foreground. Gérôme's polished academic technique renders the tiled architecture, carpets, and gleaming metalwork with characteristic precision. The painting dates to circa 1898.
collection-of-beauty-the-house-on-the-ri: Painted during Monet's Dutch sojourn after the Franco-Prussian War, the canvas shows a row of green-shuttered houses reflected in the Zaan. Long horizontal brushstrokes mirror the calm of the Holland waterways that fascinated him.
collection-of-beauty-the-ill-matched-pai: A satirical scene in which a young woman in an orange dress flatters an enamoured old man at a table set with gold coins, fruit, and bread, while a younger man smirks behind them and an old woman watches from a doorway. Jan Matsys treats an ill-matched-couple theme inherited from Flemish tradition with vigorous caricature and a warm, richly coloured palette. Dated 1566 and now held at the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
collection-of-beauty-the-incredulity-of-: Christ guides the apostle's finger into the wound in his side as two other disciples crane forward to watch. Caravaggio collapses the moment into a tight, half-length composition lit from the upper left, the brows knit in shared concentration.
collection-of-beauty-the-intervention-of: Hersilia throws herself between the Roman king Romulus and her Sabine father Tatius, infants crawling at her feet as the two armies pause on the field. David painted the canvas in 1799 during and after his post-Thermidor imprisonment, intending the subject of reconciliation as a plea for an end to French factional bloodshed.
collection-of-beauty-the-judgement-of-pa: Paris, seated in a red cap among a flock of animals, extends the golden apple towards Venus while the two other goddesses and Mercury look on, with Cupid hovering above and a peacock perched in the trees. Wtewael sets the Olympian contest in an elaborate wooded landscape peopled with gods, shepherds, and cattle. The work is dated 1615 and is held at the National Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-the-junction-of-the: An estuary scene with merchantmen and a small boat tossed in choppy water where the two rivers meet. Turner builds the squally light from layered glazes, showing his early debt to Dutch marine painters.
collection-of-beauty-the-kitchen-maid-re: A young girl in a red jacket rests her chin on her hand at a stone windowsill, her gaze directed slightly off to the side. Rembrandt renders her with warmth and individuality in the dark ochres and reds characteristic of his mid-career genre portraits; the Nationalmuseum's source notes she is probably someone from his household, though not Hendrickje. The painting is signed and dated 1651 and is held at the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
collection-of-beauty-the-knife-grinder-p: A knife grinder working at a grinding wheel is multiplied across the canvas in a sequence of overlapping Cubo-Futurist facets, his legs, hands, and the spinning disc fragmented to suggest continuous motion. Malevich gave the work the subtitle Principle of Glittering and exhibited it in 1913 alongside the Russian Cubo-Futurists. It is now in the collection of the Yale University Art Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-the-lake-of-hakone-: From Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, this print sets the still mirror of Lake Hakone in the foreground, with Fuji rising over wooded ridges beyond. Hokusai contrasts smooth bands of water with crisply outlined cedars and the modulated bokashi gradations of the sky.
collection-of-beauty-the-lawyer-possibly: A pile of legal books and document rolls draped in a fur-trimmed gown, the face assembled from plucked poultry and small fish, possibly satirising the humanist jurist Ulrich Zasius. Painted in 1566 and now in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm, the panel reads as a sly Habsburg court joke at the expense of paper-bound learning.
collection-of-beauty-the-lion-and-the-mo: A lion struggles and roars within a heavy rope net stretched across a stormy landscape, its powerful body pressing against the cords while birds circle in the darkening sky overhead. This large canvas, now at the Château de Canisy, is attributed to the collaboration of Frans Snyders and Peter Paul Rubens and illustrates the Aesopian fable of the lion caught in the hunter's net.
collection-of-beauty-the-luncheon-by-cla: An ambitious early figure painting by Monet showing a woman in black, a younger woman and a small child at a white-clothed luncheon table, and a servant standing in the background of a dark interior. The everyday domestic subject anticipates the themes that would define Impressionism; the canvas was submitted to and rejected by the Salon of 1870. Dated 1868, it is held at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt.
collection-of-beauty-the-lute-player: A turbaned musician sits against a stone wall playing a short-bodied lute, a hookah coiled at his feet. Gérôme uses the figure as a vehicle for meticulous study of costume, texture, and muted Near Eastern colour. The work is dated 1858.
collection-of-beauty-the-madonna-and-chi: The Virgin sits directly on the ground in the pose of the Madonna of Humility, her ample drapery pooling around her as she holds the Christ Child, whose head radiates spikes of light. Behind her a bare tree and the gate tower of a walled courtyard close off the scene — an enclosed garden alluding to Mary's purity. The engraving bears Schongauer's M†S monogram and was made in his Colmar workshop around 1470-91.
collection-of-beauty-the-mantree-bosch: A drawing of the hollow tree-bodied figure that recurs in the right wing of the Garden of Earthly Delights, his cracked eggshell torso supported on legs that end in tiny boats. Long attributed to Bosch's own hand, the sheet is among the few surviving drawings linked to him.
collection-of-beauty-the-massacre-of-the: Herod's soldiers, rendered as muscular nudes, seize infants from their screaming mothers in a paved square before a bridge, the violence choreographed across the sheet like a frieze. The engraving was cut by Marcantonio Raimondi around 1512-13 after a design Raphael made expressly for the print — the tablet at left reads 'RAPH URBI INVEN' — and their partnership became the chief channel through which Raphael's compositions spread across Europe. It ranks among the most celebrated engravings of the Italian Renaissance.

Herod's soldiers wrench infants from their mothers in a writhing knot of bodies before a palace portico, the women clawing and biting back at their attackers. This is Rubens's second, late treatment of the subject, painted around 1636-38 with the loose handling and theatrical energy of his final decade. The monumental canvas, over three metres wide, hangs in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich.
collection-of-beauty-the-milk-maid-by-wi: A young woman in a pink floral dress carries a wooden pail through a sunlit pasture, a cow grazing and roosters at her feet. Homer painted this watercolour in 1878 during his summers at Houghton Farm, where rural labour provided the subjects for a celebrated series of pastoral works now held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-the-mocking-of-chri: Soldiers crowd around the seated, crowned Christ by the light of a torch held openly at the centre of the composition, their mocking gestures emerging from dense shadow. Gerard van Honthorst painted this nocturnal devotional scene around 1617, applying the Caravaggesque tenebrism he developed in Rome; the work is now in the collection of the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-moreno-garden-a: Palms, agaves and dense subtropical foliage press forward in the foreground, with a tower and white buildings glimpsed through the canopy beyond. Monet painted this canvas during his 1884 stay at Bordighera on the Italian Riviera, recording the exotic garden of the Moreno estate with the richly varied greens and blues that mark his response to southern Mediterranean light. The work is held by the Norton Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-moscow-cathedra: A view across the thawing Moskva toward the bulbous domes of the Kremlin cathedrals. Vereshchagin, better known as a war painter, here records the Russian capital with the same documentary precision he brought to his battlefield reportage.
collection-of-beauty-the-muezzin-1865-je: A solitary cleric calls the faithful to prayer from a high minaret balcony, the city of Cairo spreading out far below. The vertiginous viewpoint and crisp morning light are typical of Gérôme's Egyptian travel subjects.
collection-of-beauty-the-muscles-of-the-: An anatomical engraving combining a flayed hand after Bernhard Siegfried Albinus with a foot after De Courcelles, the muscles, tendons and bones laid bare for study. Engraved by Robert Bénard for the late eighteenth-century editions of the Encyclopédie, the plate typifies the Enlightenment project of consolidating earlier anatomical illustration into a single compendium.
collection-of-beauty-the-old-adam-and-ev: Adam and Eve stand as unclothed figures on either side of a large serpent coiled around a tree, the scene rendered in dense black-and-white line. Edmund Joseph Sullivan made this illustration in 1898 for a published edition of Thomas Carlyle's Sartor Resartus, employing a bold graphic manner indebted to late-Victorian wood-engraving traditions.
collection-of-beauty-the-painter-s-daugh: Margaret and Mary Gainsborough, the painter's daughters, lean into one another while a cat curls into Margaret's arm, the picture left unfinished with the animal sketched only in outline. One of around a dozen portraits Gainsborough painted of the girls across their childhood, it now hangs in the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-the-petit-bras-of-t: A quiet backwater of the Seine fringed by bare poplars and reflected on a glassy surface. Painted in the first weeks of Monet's settlement at Argenteuil, the canvas balances delicate atmospheric grey-blues against incipient Impressionist touch.
collection-of-beauty-the-pond-at-benten-: Figures in kimono cross a low wooden bridge over a pond densely covered with lotus leaves and pink blooms, the overcast sky above suggesting a grey summer day. Kawase Hasui produced this shin-hanga woodblock print in 1929, using layered bokashi gradations and a precise keyblock to capture the Benten Shrine pond in Shiba, Tokyo.
collection-of-beauty-the-ragpicker-1869-: A life-size Spanish-inspired portrait of a Paris chiffonnier propped on his stick, set against a neutral grey ground. Manet borrows the format of Velázquez's philosopher portraits to dignify a marginal modern Parisian.
collection-of-beauty-the-rising-squall-h: An early oil view from the cliffs above the Avon Gorge as a sudden storm sweeps in over the Hot Wells spa. The seventeen-year-old Turner already orchestrates wind, rain and shifting light into a unified atmospheric event.
collection-of-beauty-the-river-le-fleuve: A male nude seated by water, the figure modelled in warm flesh tones against a loosely brushed bank. Dated 1885, the period when Renoir tightened his contours under the influence of Ingres and Raphael. The study is attributed to Renoir and reproduced from a monograph on the painter.
collection-of-beauty-the-school-of-athen: Ancient philosophers, mathematicians and scientists gather under coffered Roman barrel vaults, with Plato and Aristotle striding forward at the vanishing point. Painted between 1509 and 1511 for the Stanza della Segnatura in the Vatican, the fresco includes Raphael's own face beside Ptolemy in the lower right group.
collection-of-beauty-the-sea-at-le-havre: A dark sailboat rides rough, foam-flecked seas beneath a cloud-heavy sky, with the sandy shore and a harbour structure just visible at the left. Monet painted this Channel seascape at Le Havre in 1868, capturing the energetic movement of surf and sky in broad, vigorous strokes; the work is in the Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh.
collection-of-beauty-the-secret-message-: A young woman in a pink satin gown sits alone in a garden, leaning forward to read a letter while a white dove perches nearby and a basket of flowers rests at her feet. Signed and dated by François Boucher in 1767, the oil on canvas (60 × 50.5 cm) is in the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum, Braunschweig.
collection-of-beauty-the-seine-at-bougiv: Painted from the riverbank at the village that drew Monet, Renoir and Pissarro alike, the scene catches a row of moored boats and the mirror of the Seine. Quick, comma-shaped strokes record passing reflections rather than fixed contours.
collection-of-beauty-the-siege-and-relie: Spanish and French floating batteries burn at anchor under the guns of Gibraltar on the night of 13 September 1782, the rock looming behind the rescued sailors in the foreground. Copley spent eight years on the vast canvas, commissioned by the Corporation of the City of London, which still hangs in the Guildhall.
collection-of-beauty-the-sleepers-by-gus: Two nude women lie entwined in dishevelled bedding, jewellery and a broken pearl strand scattered on the sheet. Commissioned by the Turkish diplomat Khalil-Bey, the canvas treats lesbian love with a frank realism that scandalised the Second Empire.
collection-of-beauty-the-soldier-and-the: A smiling man and young woman bend close together over a smoldering torch in the darkness, their faces illuminated by its glow in a characteristic Honthorst candlelit half-length. The work, dated circa 1621 and held in the Herzog Anton Ulrich Museum, Brunswick, exemplifies Honthorst's Utrecht Caravaggism in its intimate nocturnal lighting and genre subject.
collection-of-beauty-the-sorrows-of-love: A woman supported by a companion grieves while a servant returns her portrait and an unopened letter, signalling the end of an affair. Oil on canvas, 45 by 55 cm, in the Wallace Collection, London. The picture belongs to a set of eleven works on the stages of love that Boilly painted for the Avignon collector Calvet de Lapalun.
collection-of-beauty-the-sower-jean-fran: A peasant striding across a furrowed field, his arm flung out in the act of casting seed. Pastel and Conté crayon on beige paper, about 47 by 37.5 cm, made around 1865 and held by the Clark Art Institute in Williamstown. Millet returned to the sower motif across his career in oil, pastel and print.
collection-of-beauty-the-steadfast-philo: A bearded scholar seated at a book-strewn table raises his hand in refusal as a laughing nude young woman in a feathered hat reaches toward him, staging the Stoic ideal of constantia. Signed and dated 1623, the candlelit half-length is held in the Hohenbuchau private collection at Schlangenbad and follows Honthorst's Utrecht practice of dramatising moral themes through strong chiaroscuro.
collection-of-beauty-the-taking-of-chris: Judas presses forward to deliver his kiss as an armoured soldier seizes Christ's neck and a fleeing apostle howls behind. A self-portrait of the painter raising a lantern at the right edge introduces the artist into the violent nocturne.
collection-of-beauty-the-tea-plantation-: A woodblock print from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, framing the sacred peak through workers tending neat rows of tea bushes in Suruga Province. Hokusai integrates rural labor with landscape, the foreground figures pressing leaves into bundles while Fuji rises in cool, flat planes behind.
collection-of-beauty-the-tea-service-oil: A red lacquered tray bearing blue-and-white porcelain cups, saucers, and a small teapot occupies the right half of a cloth-covered table, while a large potted plant fills the left in this 1872 still life by Monet. The spare arrangement and Japanese-style lacquer tray reflect the Japoniste taste of the period. The painting, titled Still Life, is held at the Dallas Museum of Art (inv. 2019.67.12.McD).
collection-of-beauty-the-third-wise-virg: A young woman with loose waist-length hair and a wreath of foliage holds a burning oil lamp upright on her open palm — the mark of the wise virgins in Christ's parable of the ten bridesmaids (Matthew 25), who kept their lamps filled for the bridegroom's arrival. The sheet belongs to Schongauer's engraved series of the Wise and Foolish Virgins, each figure isolated on a small mound of ground. His M†S monogram appears below.
collection-of-beauty-the-toilet-of-venus: Venus sits partially draped among silks, roses, and pearls while three putti attend to her hair and adornments in this 1751 canvas by François Boucher. The painting, a refined example of French Rococo mythological decoration, is held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (accession 20.155.9).
collection-of-beauty-the-tribute-money: Christ holds the coin retrieved from the fish's mouth before the Pharisees, instructing his followers to render unto Caesar. Copley painted the religious composition in 1782 for the Royal Academy, where he was working to extend his reputation beyond portraiture in the wake of his successful Watson and the Shark.
collection-of-beauty-the-tribute-money-j: John Singleton Copley's oil on canvas depicts the Gospel episode of the tribute money, in which Christ, asked whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, points heavenward as a grey-bearded questioner indicates the coin lying in his open palm. The half-length figures press close around Christ, their faces picked out against a dark ground in a deliberately old-masterly manner. Copley gave the painting to the Royal Academy of Arts in London in 1782 as his Diploma Work following his election as a Royal Academician.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-bacc: Bacchus, draped in a leopard skin and holding a thyrsus, raises a cup toward a putto who pours wine from above, while a female companion and a reclining satyr complete the intimate mythological group in a vine-hung landscape. Charles-Joseph Natoire painted this oil on canvas in 1736, demonstrating the light palette and fluid handling characteristic of French Rococo court decoration.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-chri: A vast allegorical canvas in which a cross-bearing Christ, ringed by sword-wielding angels, sweeps above the toppling deities of antiquity. Dore stages the contest as a vertiginous airborne procession, exploiting the canvas's monumental scale to push the pagan host into chaotic free-fall below.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-deat: Death triumphs over the world: a vast army of skeletons drives the living of every estate into a great coffin, the landscape behind reduced to ruin. Pieter Bruegel the Elder's panel of c. 1562 fuses the medieval danse macabre with the panoramic worldview that would carry into seventeenth-century Flemish painting.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-fred: An allegorical celebration of the Dutch stadtholder Frederick Henry, painted for the Oranjezaal at Huis ten Bosch. Jordaens orchestrates a swirling Baroque cavalcade of personifications, captives, and trophies in the Rubensian Antwerp manner, glorifying the prince's military and political triumphs.
collection-of-beauty-the-vision-of-the-v: An engraving from Dore's illustrated Bible, depicting Ezekiel's vision in which scattered bones reanimate as a vast army. The artist exploits dense crosshatching and dramatic chiaroscuro to give the desolate plain a haunted, otherworldly atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-the-wailing-wall-by: Worshippers in prayer shawls stand and kneel before the monumental ashlar courses of the Western Wall, Jerusalem, the wall's towering face dominating the composition. Gustav Bauernfeind painted this Orientalist scene in 1887, capturing the site with the meticulous attention to stonework and devotional atmosphere for which he was known.
collection-of-beauty-the-water-lily-pond: A view across the Japanese footbridge spanning the lily pond at Monet's Giverny garden, the green arch dissolving into shimmering reflections. The painting belongs to the celebrated bridge series in which Monet examined a single subject under shifting conditions of light.
collection-of-beauty-the-white-horse-by-: The first of Constable's six-foot Stour valley canvases, showing a workhorse ferried across the river on a flat-bottomed barge. Constable elevates everyday East Anglian labor to grand-manner scale, with broken impasto highlights and a damp, atmospheric sky.
collection-of-beauty-the-wounded-heron: A heron struck down in a hawking scene sprawls in the foreground, its wing spread on the ground. Watts, then about twenty, bought a dead heron from a poulterer to study the bird; the oil on canvas, 91.4 by 71.1 cm, was his Royal Academy debut in 1837 and now belongs to the Watts Gallery, Surrey.
collection-of-beauty-the-zuiderkerk-amst: A view up the Groenburgwal canal toward the spire of the Zuiderkerk, painted during Monet's brief Dutch sojourn. The canvas already carries the rapid, broken brushwork of nascent Impressionism, dissolving brick facades and water into vibrating coloured strokes.
collection-of-beauty-theknightatthecross: An armoured knight on a white horse halts before a moss-covered stone slab on the open steppe, ravens picking at scattered bones nearby. The stone's inscription warns that there is no return for the rider who goes straight ahead. Vasnetsov painted the nearly three-metre 1882 canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, as a free interpretation of the bylina of Ilya Muromets, sticking to ethnographically accurate armour and steppe terrain.
collection-of-beauty-theodore-gericault-: A Romantic landscape in the grand tradition, dwarfing fishermen beneath looming cliffs and gathering storm clouds. Gericault works the scene in dark earth tones, drawing on Poussin and Salvator Rosa to fuse classical composition with fervent natural drama.

One of Gericault's series of portraits depicting inmates of a Paris asylum, each suffering from a specific monomania. The unflinching, dignified treatment of the sitter and the somber palette mark a pioneering encounter between Romantic painting and clinical psychiatry.

An intimate study of two lovers locked in an embrace, modelled with the vigorous, sculptural brushwork that characterises Gericault's late work. The intense physicality and shadowed flesh tones reflect his sustained interest in bodily expression.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-carlyle-oil-: A bust portrait of the historian and essayist Thomas Carlyle, white-bearded and turned in three-quarter view. Painted by Watts in 1868 and given by the artist to the National Portrait Gallery, London, in 1895 (NPG 1002); Carlyle himself disliked the likeness.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-a-view-: Morning mist lifts off the twin Catskill lakes as the white-pillared Catskill Mountain House perches on a cliff above. Cole lived in the village of Catskill from 1836 and painted this 1844 view of the famous hotel that had drawn tourists to the Hudson Valley since 1824.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-archite: A figure reclines on a broad stone platform strewn with architectural drawings, gazing over a fantastical harbour where Gothic spires rise in the foreground and classical colonnades, a domed rotunda, and an Egyptian pyramid recede into the distance. Cole painted the canvas for architect Ithiel Town in 1840; it is now in the Toledo Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-prometh: The Titan Prometheus is chained to a crag of the Caucasus at dawn, an eagle wheeling above to tear at his liver, the sun rising behind distant snow-capped peaks. Exhibited at the National Academy of Design in 1847, Cole's late mythological piece adapts Aeschylus to the vertical drama of the Hudson River sublime.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-the-voy: An infant rides in a richly gilded ornamental boat emerging from a rocky cavern, guided by a luminous winged angel through a lush, flower-strewn landscape. This is the first of four panels in Cole's 1842 version of The Voyage of Life, a moral allegory of the soul's earthly passage, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

The traveller, now grown, clasps his hands in prayer as his rudderless boat plunges through a torrent of black rocks under storm clouds, the guardian angel watching from above. Third panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life, painted in his Catskill studio after the New York set was sold off.

The voyager, white-bearded, drifts on a glassy black sea while his angel gestures upward toward a host of celestial spirits breaking through the clouds. Fourth and final panel of the National Gallery's 1842 set, completing Cole's allegory of the Christian soul's passage from infancy to eternity.

The young traveller, now alone at the tiller, steers toward a shining cloud palace in the sky above a verdant river valley. Second panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life series at the National Gallery of Art, painted after the original 1840 set passed into private hands.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-eakins-005: Amelia Van Buren, a former Eakins pupil at the Pennsylvania Academy, sits sideways in a carved armchair with one hand against her cheek, her gaze fixed past the viewer. Painted around 1891 and now at the Phillips Collection in Washington, the portrait is one of the unflinching psychological studies of Eakins's mature American Realism.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-eakins-ameri: A monumental scene of surgeon Samuel Gross presiding over an operation before his medical students at Jefferson College. Eakins records the bloodied hand, the chloroformed patient and the rapt amphitheatre with uncompromising realism, anchoring American painting in the lecture-hall light of modern science.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-eakins-the-b: Professional oarsmen John and Barney Biglin pull in unison in their pair-oared shell on the Schuylkill River, observed by spectators on a barge and along the tree-lined shore. Eakins, an avid rower, built the composition from careful perspective studies; the painting is now at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-gage-john-si: General Thomas Gage stands in the scarlet uniform of a British commander, his left hand resting on a cane while his right gestures toward the massed troops visible in the landscape behind him. Copley's three-quarter-length oil on canvas (127 × 101 cm) is inscribed at the lower right with Gage's name and death date of 1788; it belongs to the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-gainsborough: The actress Sarah Siddons sits in profile against a red curtain, wearing a striped silk dress and a wide black plumed hat. Gainsborough painted his rival to Reynolds's celebrated Tragic Muse in 1785, complaining of the difficulty of her nose; the canvas hangs in the National Gallery, London.

Augustus Hervey, third Earl of Bristol, stands in commodore's undress uniform with a coil of rope at his hand and his ship riding at anchor offshore. Painted by Gainsborough in 1767 for Hervey's seat at Ickworth, the portrait is now in the National Trust collection.

A flock of sheep gathers near a stone trough at the foot of a dramatic rocky gorge, with a herdsman resting among them in the foreground. The scene opens onto a distant mountain valley bathed in pale light. Gainsborough presented this canvas to the Royal Academy in 1783 as his diploma work on election, and it has remained in the Academy's collection ever since.

A heavyset man identified as Mr Wood, said to have been a dancing master, is shown half-length in a pale blue coat trimmed with gold braid, against a dark neutral background. The portrait dates from around 1757, near the close of Gainsborough's Ipswich years, and is now in the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.

Richard St George Mansergh-St George stands full-length in the red uniform of the 4th Regiment of Foot, hat in hand, with ships and a coastal cliff visible in the stormy background. A dog sits at his feet. Gainsborough painted the portrait between 1776 and 1780, and it is now held at the National Gallery of Victoria.

A self-portrait painted around 1758-59, just as Gainsborough left Ipswich for the spa town of Bath. The small canvas, now NPG 4446 in the National Portrait Gallery, almost certainly hung in his studio as an advertisement of his skill; behind the loose, fluent brushwork the trees of a Suffolk landscape can still be made out.

A pastoral scene of cattle pausing at a wooded stream, painted with the feathery, scumbled foliage typical of Gainsborough's mature landscapes. The work belongs to his Suffolk-derived rural idylls, indebted to Dutch seventeenth-century models yet handled with English freshness.

Clayton Jones is shown full-length, seated beneath a tree in a parkland landscape, wearing a dark blue coat over a yellow waistcoat and holding a walking cane. Gainsborough painted the portrait between 1744 and 1745, during his early career, and it is now at the Yale Center for British Art.

A late landscape in which a shepherd and flock cross a windswept shore beneath gathering clouds. Gainsborough loosens the topography into soft, tonal silhouettes, prefiguring the atmospheric coastal scenes that would influence British Romantic painters.

Anne, Countess of Chesterfield, is shown seated in a pale blue satin gown, leaning thoughtfully against a stone balustrade with trees and a landscape behind her. Gainsborough painted the canvas in 1777–78 with the sweeping, atmospheric brushwork of his late style. The portrait is now at the J. Paul Getty Museum.

Frances Browne, later Mrs John Douglas, is shown in a silvery-white silk gown, seated against a stone balustrade in a parkland setting. Gainsborough painted the portrait in 1783–84, and it is now held at Waddesdon Manor under the care of the National Trust.

A wooded river landscape in the Dutch-influenced manner of Gainsborough's middle years, with travellers descending toward a rustic bridge. Feathered foliage and a silvery palette establish the gentle, picturesque mood that defined his Bath-period landscapes.

A wooded lane winds past a pool toward a sandy rise dotted with figures, a thatched cottage, and further structures under a dramatic cloudscape. Gainsborough painted the canvas between circa 1746 and 1750, during his early years working in East Anglia, and it is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

A broad river landscape shows cattle and sheep near a weir, with a wooden gate at the water's edge, a cliff and ruined structure at right, and a sweeping cloud-filled sky above. Gainsborough painted the work between 1750 and 1753, and it is now at the Yale Center for British Art.

A young Frenchwoman in a powdered chignon and pale gauze gown sits half-length against an indistinct landscape. Gainsborough painted the sitter, identified as Madame Lebrun, in London in 1780 with the feathery brushwork and limited palette he favoured in his late portraiture.

Mary, Countess Howe, walks through a wooded landscape in a pink silk gown lifted to show a quilted petticoat, a black ribbon at her throat. Painted in 1764 at Bath and now at Kenwood House, the portrait is among Gainsborough's most admired full-lengths, the gown rendered in feathery strokes that animate the silk.

Mary Little, later Lady Carr, is shown in a rose-pink silk gown with lace cuffs, holding a small bouquet of flowers, against a warm dark background. The portrait dates from around 1763 and is now at the Yale Center for British Art.

A double portrait of a young Suffolk landowner and his bride seated at the edge of their estate, the rolling cornfields and oak deliberately presented as part of their identity. The crisp early style fuses French rococo elegance with topographical precision unusual in English portraiture.

A portrait of Elizabeth Linley, singer and wife of the playwright Richard Brinsley Sheridan, shown seated against a windswept landscape. Gainsborough merges sitter and setting through loosely brushed foliage and the soft fall of her pink gown, characteristic of his late manner. The canvas, painted between 1785 and 1787, is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

A three-quarter-length portrait of a woman in a blue silk gown, her tall powdered wig adorned with feathers and a blue ribbon, set against a dark ground. The cool palette and freely handled brushwork are characteristic of Gainsborough's manner from the late 1770s to early 1780s. The canvas is in the Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg.

John Plampin sits informally on a mossy bank, one hand grasping a tree branch, his spaniel at his feet, the countryside spreading behind him under a cloudy sky. Painted around 1752 during Gainsborough's Ipswich period, the small canvas fuses portraiture and landscape in the intimate manner of his early career. It is now in the National Gallery, London (NG5984).

A rural landscape in which figures with laden horses return along a sunken track at the close of day. Gainsborough constructs the scene from imagined, idealised motifs, building a poetic vision of English country life in the Bath-period pastoral mode.

John Gravenor stands at the left while his wife Ann and their two daughters are seated in a wooded landscape at the edge of a field, the younger girl in white with flowers in her lap. Painted around 1754, during Gainsborough's Ipswich period, the canvas is a characteristic conversation piece combining portraiture with natural surroundings. It is now in the Yale Center for British Art, New Haven.

The Honourable Mrs Graham stands full-length in an elaborate silver-white gown with a rose-patterned skirt, a feathered hat, and one hand resting on a stone column. Gainsborough exhibited the portrait at the Royal Academy in 1777; her widower later withheld it from public view, and it entered the Scottish National Gallery in 1859. The picture, painted in 1775, is regarded as one of the grandest statements of his Bath-period portraiture.

Fashionable Londoners promenade in pairs and small groups under the avenue of trees in St James's Park, their pale dresses catching the filtered light. Gainsborough modelled the figures from a doll dressed in different gowns; the canvas of 1783 is held by the Frick Collection in New York.

The four Marsham children of Stratton Strawless play in a wooded landscape, the eldest girl gathering nuts while her brother reaches up to a sapling. Gainsborough painted the group portrait in 1787, the year before his death, combining the conversation-piece tradition with the feathery foliage and silvery palette of his late manner.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-howard-ruben: A bust-length portrait of Thomas Howard, 14th Earl of Arundel, shown in a dark fur-trimmed coat with white collar and a blue sash, a medal suspended from a ribbon at his chest. Rubens painted the Earl during his diplomatic visit to London around 1629–30, capturing the great English collector in the rich, restrained manner of his mature Flemish Baroque portraiture. The canvas is held by the National Gallery, London (NG2968).
collection-of-beauty-three-friends-of-wi: An ink album leaf bringing together the three classical scholarly emblems of resilience — pine, bamboo, and flowering plum — in spare, calligraphic brushwork that interweaves the three plants into a single composition. Zhao Mengjian, a Song-dynasty literatus, renders the trio with economy and precision, surrounded by collector seals accumulated over centuries. The leaf is in the collection of the National Palace Museum, Taipei.
collection-of-beauty-three-sisters-by-ya: A four-fold screen painted in ink and color on silk by the nihonga artist Yamakawa Shuho in 1936. Three young women in kimono are grouped around a white motor car: one leans against the front fender holding a handbag, another sits inside the open rear door, and the third looks out through the back window, a quietly modern image of well-to-do life in 1930s Japan rendered in the flat, elegant manner of traditional figure painting. The screen is in the Honolulu Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-and-lukr: A late Mannerist treatment of the Roman legend in which Tarquin's assault on Lucretia precipitates the founding of the Republic. Tintoretto stages the violence with twisting bodies, broken pearls and torn drapery, the diagonal composition lit by sharp Venetian chiaroscuro.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-depositi: The body of Christ, still bearing his wound, is lowered by several figures in an animated, brightly coloured composition set against a pale sky, with the Virgin fainting at the lower right. Tintoretto organises the scene through compressed, overlapping figures and the turbulent energy typical of his late Venetian manner, painted around 1585–90. The large canvas is in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, Venice.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-jacopo-c: A Venetian rendering of the Gospel episode in which Christ appears to the disciples on a storm-tossed sea. The dramatic torsion of the figures, raking light and turbulent green-grey waves are characteristic of the Tintoretto workshop, though the attribution has been debated in favour of Lambert Sustris.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-prayer-i: A nocturnal Agony in the Garden, with Christ kneeling in radiant spotlight while the disciples slumber and torch-bearing soldiers approach through the olive grove. The picture exemplifies Tintoretto's preference for elongated figures, plunging diagonals and theatrical chiaroscuro.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-st-mary-: A solitary image of the penitent Magdalen withdrawn in a rocky wilderness with her book and ointment jar. Tintoretto isolates the saint against a brooding twilight landscape, animating the meditation with flickering, sketch-like brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-the-bapt: A Mannerist treatment of the Baptism in which crowds press toward the Jordan beneath a luminous descent of the Holy Spirit. Tintoretto orchestrates space through deep diagonals and silvery, restless light, characteristic of his late Venetian altarpieces.
collection-of-beauty-titian-self-portrai: A late self-portrait of the Venetian master, shown in three-quarter profile with brush in hand and the gold chain of imperial favor across his black robe. The looser handling and reserved gaze typify Titian's introspective final decade.
collection-of-beauty-titian-the-flaying-: Apollo punishes the satyr Marsyas for his musical hubris, suspending him upside down to be skinned alive. Painted in the artist's final years, the canvas is built from open, almost dissolving brushwork that anticipates later European painting.
collection-of-beauty-titian-venus-with-a: Venus is depicted partially nude, turning toward a mirror held by two cupids — one also raising a wreath or crown above her head — while red drapery frames the composition behind her. Painted around 1555, the canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, and represents the prime version of a composition Titian repeated across several decades for European patrons.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-015-2: One of Titian's mythological poesie made for Philip II of Spain, depicting Diana's discovery of the pregnant nymph Callisto among her bathing companions. Diagonal drapery, a marbled fountain and richly varied flesh tones articulate the moment of accusation.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-080: A young Venetian man is shown in three-quarter view, with short dark hair and a slight beard, holding an object such as a ring or coin and resting his arm on a ledge beside a book; a cityscape is visible through a window behind him. Dated between circa 1510 and 1515, the portrait belongs to Titian's early period and is held in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-085: A late poesia for Philip II showing the Phoenician princess carried across the sea on the back of Jupiter disguised as a bull. Loose, atmospheric handling and a glowing pink-gold sky transform the abduction into a turbulent seascape.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-091: Adam and Eve beneath the Tree of Knowledge, the serpent rendered as a child clutching the fatal fruit. Titian gives the Genesis subject a sculptural, classicizing weight, drawing on Northern prototypes filtered through Venetian colorism.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-danae-receiv: Danaë reclines nude on her bed as Jupiter descends as a shower of gold, while an old nursemaid stretches up an apron to catch the falling coins. Among Titian's poesie for the Spanish court, the scene contrasts youthful flesh and wizened greed in loose, atmospheric paint.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-portrait-of-: Federico II Gonzaga, Marquis of Mantua, is shown half-length against a dark ground wearing a richly embroidered dark blue velvet doublet with gold decoration, one hand resting on a small white dog that looks up at him. Painted circa 1525, the work is held in the Museo del Prado, Madrid, and is among Titian's most celebrated court portraits.
collection-of-beauty-tokaido28-mitsuke: Mitsuke, the twenty-eighth station of the Tokaido road, depicting travelers crossing the Tenryu River by ferry. Hiroshige's woodblock design uses graded blue bokashi and a low horizon to evoke morning mist over the water.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-daiko: A small cargo boat makes its way along the Sumida River beside the Daikon vegetable wharf, while produce is piled on the near bank under willows and workers tend to the waterfront buildings above. The print belongs to Hasui's series Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō (Tōkyō jūnidai) and exemplifies his shin-hanga approach of merging traditional workshop technique with Western-influenced perspective.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-fukag: The Kaminohashi Bridge in Fukagawa, from the series Twelve Scenes of Tokyo. Hasui captures a quiet canal-side moment, using graded inks and reflective water in the shin-hanga tradition that updated ukiyo-e cityscape conventions.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-kiba-: Evening at the Kiba lumber yards, where stacked timber and floating logs catch the last light along the canal. From Twelve Scenes of Tokyo, the print exemplifies Hasui's shin-hanga blend of working-city subject and lyrical atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-samid: A lone figure shelters under a yellow umbrella and walks a dog past the vermilion gate of Hie (Sannō) Shrine in early summer rain, the surrounding trees rendered in soft greens against a muted grey sky. From the series Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō, this 1919 woodblock print is one of Kawase Hasui's earliest shin-hanga works, combining quiet atmosphere with the graphic economy of traditional printmaking.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-shina: A view of fishing boats anchored in the bay off Shinagawa, sails reflected on a tranquil sea. Part of Twelve Scenes of Tokyo, the design relies on flat planes of graded blue and economical silhouettes characteristic of shin-hanga.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-toyam: A winter moon floats above a grove of silhouetted pine trees on the Toyama Plain, their reflections catching in the still water below. Deep bands of blue and blue-green fill the composition, with the luminous disc set against a gradated night sky. From Kawase Hasui's 1920 woodblock series Twelve Scenes of Tōkyō, the print exemplifies the atmospheric restraint characteristic of the shin-hanga movement.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-niju-kei-kand: The stone-paved grounds of the Kanda Myōjin Shrine are dominated by two towering dark cedars, a stone torii gate at the end of the path, and a small shrine lantern visible to one side. Billowing summer clouds rise dramatically behind the trees, filling the upper half of the composition. The print is from Kawase Hasui's series Twenty Views of Tōkyō (Tōkyō nijū kei), published in 1926.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-niju-kei-shin: The steel girders of the Shin Ohashi bridge over the Sumida River, rendered through slanting rain and a darkening sky. Hasui treats modern Tokyo infrastructure with the lyrical atmospherics of traditional landscape woodblock printing.
collection-of-beauty-torii-kotondo-kamis: A bijin-ga showing a young woman drawing a comb through her loosened black hair, her undergarment slipping from one shoulder. Kotondo revives the intimate vanity scenes of Edo-period printmaking within the early Showa shin-hanga movement.
collection-of-beauty-torii-kotondo-woman: A bijin-ga in which a woman, her patterned kimono fallen from her upper body, raises both arms to arrange her hair before a mirror visible at the print's left edge. The richly decorated fabric — pink with floral motifs and contrasting obi — pools in the lower half of the composition. Kotondo balances flat decorative pattern against the quiet intimacy of a private dressing moment in this 1930 shin-hanga print held at the Walters Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-toshogu-shrine-5759: A colour woodblock print of the Tōshō-gū shrine at Nikkō, designed by Yoshida Hiroshi in 1937. Towering cryptomeria trunks frame the lantern-lined approach to the shrine, rendered with the soft gradations Yoshida carried from his watercolour training into woodblock. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-transfiguration-rap: Christ rises in light between Moses and Elijah above the apostles on Mount Tabor, while in the lower zone the disciples fail to heal a possessed boy. Commissioned in 1516 by Cardinal Giulio de' Medici for Narbonne Cathedral, Raphael was still completing the panel when he died in 1520 and it now belongs to the Vatican Pinacoteca.
collection-of-beauty-transfiguration-rub: Christ rises in radiant white between Moses and Elijah while the apostles below shield their eyes, a subject drawn from Matthew 17. Rubens organizes the composition around a vertical axis of light, marrying Italian disegno with Flemish painterly warmth.
collection-of-beauty-treaty-of-paris-by-: John Jay, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Henry Laurens and William Temple Franklin sit together around a table in West's unfinished oil sketch for the planned Treaty of Paris group portrait. The British commissioners refused to sit, and West abandoned the canvas; the fragment is held at the Winterthur Museum in Delaware.
collection-of-beauty-trinidad-el-greco2: God the Father supports the dead body of Christ while the dove of the Holy Spirit hovers above, attended by mourning angels. Painted between 1577 and 1579 for the high altar of Santo Domingo el Antiguo in Toledo, the composition draws directly on a Dürer engraving but elongates the figures in El Greco's emerging Mannerist idiom.
collection-of-beauty-triumphant-cupid-am: Cupid sits in triumph atop instruments of art, science and war, a Baroque allegory of love's universal sway. Willeboirts Bosschaert painted the figures and de Vos the still-life trophies, reflecting the seventeenth-century Antwerp practice of collaborative specialization.
collection-of-beauty-triumphant-entry-of: Part of the Constantine cycle designed for tapestries woven for Louis XIII, showing the emperor's victorious procession through Rome after the Battle of the Milvian Bridge. Rubens stages the parade as a ceremonial relief, packed with banners, classical architecture and rearing horses.
collection-of-beauty-tsar-nikolai: A portrait of Tsar Nicholas II in full imperial dress — red military uniform with blue ribbon and numerous orders — set against the golden-domed churches and towers of the Moscow Kremlin. The work is unsigned and held without museum attribution in the catalogue, but the physiognomy and iconographic setting identify the sitter as the last Russian emperor, reigned 1894–1917.
collection-of-beauty-tsukioka-yoshitoshi: A pale full moon rises over the windswept grasses of Musashino, where a fox glances back through the autumn pampas. The plate from One Hundred Aspects of the Moon distills a literary motif into spare silhouette and graded sky.
collection-of-beauty-tsunami-by-hokusai-: The opening sheet of Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows a towering offshore wave (okinami) breaking over fishing boats while Fuji stands small on the horizon. Hokusai's use of imported Prussian blue and his geometric treatment of foam made the print a touchstone of Edo design.
collection-of-beauty-turner-antwerp-van-: An imagined homage in which the Dutch master Jan van Goyen sketches from a small boat in Antwerp harbor, surrounded by shipping under broken cloud. Turner pays tribute to the seventeenth-century landscape tradition while asserting his own atmospheric handling of sky and water.
collection-of-beauty-turner-cologne-the-: Cologne's quayside gilds in evening light as a packet boat draws in beneath the unfinished cathedral. The vast canvas, now in the Frick Collection, pushes Rhineland topography toward Venetian-style golden atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-turner-deluge: An early biblical disaster scene depicting the universal flood, with massed bodies struggling against rising water beneath churning storm clouds. Turner builds the composition from a baroque diagonal of light, a precedent for his later sublime catastrophes.
collection-of-beauty-turner-fishermen-up: Fishermen struggle to bring a sailing vessel ashore as breaking surf and squall lines press against a steep coast. An early Royal Academy exhibit, the canvas sets Turner's lifelong concern with mariners' jeopardy in a darker, more Dutch-inflected idiom.
collection-of-beauty-turner-j-m-w-the-gr: A view down the Grand Canal toward the domes of Santa Maria della Salute, gondolas dispersed across luminous water. Turner dissolves the architecture of Venice into pale light and reflected color, characteristic of his late Romantic vedute.
collection-of-beauty-turner-joseph-mallo: Fishing boats work the swell off Hastings under a turbulent sky, the figures and rigging set against pale sea-light. Turner treats the everyday coastal labor with the atmospheric breadth of his mature marine paintings.
collection-of-beauty-turner-newark-abbey: The ruined Augustinian priory of Newark stands above the still waters of the Wey, framed by trees and scattered cattle. Turner adopts the picturesque vocabulary of the topographical watercolorists, softened by an early painterly attention to reflected light.
collection-of-beauty-turner-peace-burial: Commemorates the sea burial of the painter David Wilkie off Gibraltar, the steamer's silhouette and inky black sails set against a flaring sun. Exhibited as a pendant to Turner's fiery 'War,' the picture pairs cool nocturnal calm with the warmth of mourning.
collection-of-beauty-turner-port-rusdael: An invented harbour named in homage to the Dutch marine master Jacob van Ruisdael, with squat fishing craft straining against a grey-green swell. Turner adopts the seventeenth-century tonal vocabulary while loosening the brushwork toward atmospheric haze.
collection-of-beauty-turner-rain-steam-a: A Great Western Railway locomotive races across Maidenhead Bridge through curtains of rain, the iron viaduct dissolving into vapour and golden light. The picture is a defining statement of the modern industrial sublime, painted with palette knife and finger as much as brush.
collection-of-beauty-turner-ships-bearin: A fleet of sailing vessels bears up for anchorage in squally open water, their hulls and rigging silhouetted against a turbulent, cloud-laden sky. Turner's treatment recalls the seventeenth-century Dutch marine tradition of Willem van de Velde while asserting a broader atmospheric ambition. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1802, the work is known as 'The Egremont Seapiece' and is held by the National Trust at Petworth House.
collection-of-beauty-turner-the-banks-of: A luminous river view shows wooded cliffs rising above a broad reach of calm water, with sailing vessels in the middle distance and a seated figure in red beside a small bridge in the foreground. The warm amber and golden tones suffuse the landscape with milky riverine light. Painted around 1829, it is held by the Worcester Art Museum (inv. 1940.59).
collection-of-beauty-turner-the-bright-s: The Rhine fortress of Ehrenbreitstein rises in golden haze above the confluence with the Moselle, paired with the riverside tomb of the French general Marceau. Turner illustrates a passage from Byron's Childe Harold, fusing topography with literary elegy.
collection-of-beauty-turner-the-eruption: A volcanic eruption blazes against a night sky, the summit of the Soufrière bursting with incandescent orange and gold light that reflects across the dark water below. Small dark forms — rocks or boats — punctuate the foreground, but the composition is dominated by the eruptive column and its radiant halo. Painted in 1815 to record the eruption of 30 April 1812, the work is held by the University of Liverpool.
collection-of-beauty-turner-the-evening-: A solitary boy with a dog wades along an empty Margate beach as Venus pricks the violet dusk. Pared back to bands of damp sand, sea and sky, the canvas distils Turner's late preoccupation with thresholds of light.
collection-of-beauty-turner-the-trout-st: Several figures fish and work along the shallows of a broad river beneath an open, cloud-filled sky, with a prominent hill dominating the left background and a bridge visible in the middle distance. The expansive, unwooded landscape departs from the enclosed pastoral of Turner's Thames studies, lending the scene a grander scale. Painted in 1809, the canvas is held by the Taft Museum of Art, Cincinnati (inv. 1931.459).
collection-of-beauty-turner-the-wreck-bu: A scarlet buoy bobs above a foundered hull as a low rainbow arcs over a ruffled sea. One of Turner's last completed oils, the picture reworks an earlier seascape into a meditation on hazard and salvage.
collection-of-beauty-turner-thomson-s-ae: A pastoral elegy for the poet James Thomson, with classical figures grouped on a hillside above the Thames at Richmond. Turner pairs the picture with verses of his own, blending Claudean idyll and literary tribute.
collection-of-beauty-turner-venice-the-d: Looking across the Bacino, the Dogana's customs point and Palladio's San Giorgio Maggiore float in a wash of lagoon light. Turner reduces Venice's masonry to shimmering tints, the gondolas mere flecks against pearl water and sky.
collection-of-beauty-turner-walton-bridg: Sheep and shepherds gather on the riverbank below two bridges at Walton, one a timber lock structure in the foreground and the other a broad stone bridge spanning the Thames beyond. Turner painted the scene around 1806 during his sketching tours along the river, and the work is held by the National Gallery of Victoria.
collection-of-beauty-twee-kaketoes-op-ta: Two white cockatoos perch among the early flowers of a plum branch. Ohara Koson produced the design for Watanabe Shōzaburō's Shin-hanga programme, which translated the kachō-e tradition into a refined modern colour-print idiom.
collection-of-beauty-two-faces-expressin: Two labelled heads demonstrate contrasting emotional states after Le Brun: Veneration is shown with the face inclined downward and the eyes cast humbly low, while Rapture turns the head upward with parted lips and an open gaze. The etching, made around 1760 after Charles Le Brun, belongs to the tradition of academic physiognomic instruction and is held by the Wellcome Collection.
collection-of-beauty-two-sisters-on-the-: On a Chatou terrace above the Seine, a young woman in a plain red hat stands beside a younger girl whose blue hat is trimmed with flowers, a basket of yarn resting between them against a backdrop of broken foliage and river. Renoir painted the picture in 1881, and it is one of his most celebrated figure compositions of that year.
collection-of-beauty-udaipur-1916-woodbl: A view across the lake at Udaipur shows figures gathered on stone steps by the water's edge, with the Lake Palace reflected beyond and blue mountains rising in the distance. Designed by Charles W. Bartlett in 1916 and published in 1917 by Watanabe Shōzaburō's Tokyo workshop, the print belongs to Bartlett's series of Indian landscapes executed in the shin-hanga idiom; a fine impression is held by the Honolulu Academy of Arts.
collection-of-beauty-udaipur-by-charles-: A solitary figure in orange robes sits cross-legged within an ornate lakeside pavilion, looking out over the still water at Udaipur; a distant temple or palace is visible on the far shore, and a large tree extends its branches overhead. Charles W. Bartlett designed the woodblock print in 1916, and it was cut and published that same year in a warm palette of golden ochres and deep blues characteristic of his shin-hanga work.
collection-of-beauty-umegawa-in-sagami-p: From the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the volcano floats beyond a quiet manor pond ringed by cranes and pines. Hokusai marshals his celebrated bero-ai Prussian-blue gradients to balance domestic foreground against distant peak.
collection-of-beauty-unmatinapresledelug: A vortex of golden light spirals around the figure of Moses inscribing Genesis, with a serpent and submerged figures at its rim. Turner conceived the picture as a pendant illustrating Goethe's theory of positive, light-giving colour.
collection-of-beauty-uriel-da-costa: A bust-length imaginary portrait depicts Uriel da Costa, the seventeenth-century rationalist philosopher, in a white collar and dark doublet, his gaze directed at the viewer. Léon Bakst painted the work in 1893, early in his career and well before his association with the Ballets Russes.
collection-of-beauty-urteil-des-paris: The shepherd Paris hands the golden apple to Venus while river gods recline at the foreground edge. Known chiefly through Marcantonio Raimondi's engraving after Raphael's lost design, the composition shaped European depictions of the nude for centuries.
collection-of-beauty-utagawa-hiroshige-1: A vertical triptych charts the famed Naruto whirlpools off Awa province, the churning indigo eddies set beneath a banded sky. Hiroshige stretches the ooban format to give the tide its full vertiginous scale.
collection-of-beauty-utagawa-hiroshige-i: Tall purple irises crowd the foreground of the celebrated Horikiri garden east of Edo, dwarfing the strolling visitors beyond. The radical close-up viewpoint, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, would be admired and copied by Van Gogh.
collection-of-beauty-utagawa-kunisada-18: A triptych of women engaged in various craft trades — dyeing, lacquerwork, and painting — fills an interior workshop scene, each figure rendered in Kunisada's characteristic bijin-ga style. Designed in 1857, the print belongs to the series Modern Parodies of the Four Classes (Imayō mitate shinō kōshō), which reimagines the Confucian social hierarchy through contemporary Edo beauties at work.
collection-of-beauty-utagawa-kunisada-i-: Dawn breaks over the linked Wedded Rocks at Futami-ga-ura on the Ise coast, their sacred shimenawa rope strung between them. Kunisada renders the famous pilgrimage site in soft graded blues typical of early-1830s ukiyo-e landscape.
collection-of-beauty-v-gorakh-alatau: A view across the Alatau range of the Tien Shan, painted during Vereshchagin's Central Asian travels. The canvas belongs to the Turkestan group of works the artist produced from sketches made on his journeys of 1869 to 1870 through what is now eastern Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.
collection-of-beauty-valentin-a-serov-ku: Two boys lead a dappled horse into shallow water under a high summer sky, the animal's reflection broken across the surface. Serov painted the canvas in 1905, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. The plein-air handling and loose, light-struck water belong to his later landscape work around the Domotkanovo estate.
collection-of-beauty-valentin-serov-pokh: Europa clings to the back of a reddish-brown bull as it surges through blue-purple waves, a dolphin visible in the foreground. Serov's 1910 treatment of the mythological abduction compresses the figures into a boldly simplified composition dominated by cool sea tones and warm earth. The work is now held in a private or unrecorded collection.
collection-of-beauty-valentin-serov-port: Princess Olga Orlova is shown seated in a large feathered hat and a voluminous dark fur wrap, her pearl necklace and pale gown visible beneath. Painted by Valentin Serov in 1911, the work is a full-length formal portrait that conveys both the sitter's aristocratic bearing and an air of detached hauteur. It is now held in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.

Henriette Girshman stands at her dressing table, glancing toward the viewer as she adjusts her fur-trimmed wrap. Behind her, a mirror reflects the interior of her boudoir. Serov painted the portrait in 1907, and it now belongs to the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-valley-of-aosta-sno: Storm, avalanche and lightning converge over the Italian Val d'Aosta, tiny figures swept along the ravine floor. Drawing on Alpine sketches made with Hugh Munro of Novar, Turner orchestrates Romantic catastrophe through swirling diagonals of paint.
collection-of-beauty-van-dyck-pieter-bru: An ageing Pieter Brueghel the Younger turns toward the viewer in a quiet half-length portrait. The plate belongs to Van Dyck's Iconography, his series of etched and engraved likenesses of the leading artists, scholars and statesmen of his day.
collection-of-beauty-van-dyck-sir-anthon: Venetia, Lady Digby is shown the morning after her sudden death, propped against a pillow with a single rose shedding its petals. Commissioned by her grieving husband Sir Kenelm, the picture is a rare seventeenth-century memorial portrait painted from the corpse.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-abendstund: A lone farm labourer stands at the edge of a ploughed field at dusk, the golden sky deepening behind him; a plough and scattered tools lie at his feet. Painted at Saint-Rémy in November 1889 as a free copy after Millet's Evening Hour, Van Gogh replaces Millet's tonal restraint with dense swirling strokes of amber and grey-green. The picture is now in the Menard Art Museum, Japan.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-am-stadtra: A lone figure walks along a bright suburban road flanked by young trees, with rows of houses and a crop field stretching to the horizon. Painted in Paris in the spring of 1887, the canvas shows Van Gogh absorbing the lighter palette and broken touch of the Impressionists he was encountering in the city.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-die-brucke: Washerwomen kneel along the canal bank as a horse-cart crosses the wooden drawbridge at Arles. Van Gogh returned to the Pont de Langlois several times in 1888, drawn to its clean geometry and Provençal light reminiscent of Japanese prints.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-die-schafe: A peasant woman sits resting in a golden field, holding a long shepherd's crook, her blue shawl and white bonnet standing out against a turbulent sky. Painted in November 1889 at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy, the work is Van Gogh's free interpretation of Millet's celebrated shepherdess, transposing the original into his own vivid blues, ochres, and greens. It is now in the Tel Aviv Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-f1040-jh10: A wide industrial landscape spreads across the sheet: factory buildings, tall chimneys trailing smoke, and a lone standing figure in the foreground fill a broad, flat terrain. Made on 4 July 1879, the drawing dates to Van Gogh's time in the Borinage mining region of Belgium and reflects his early, self-taught approach to depicting the working-class environment around him.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-grunes-wei: A Provençal field rendered in surging diagonal brushstrokes, the unripe wheat treated as a tapestry of green and blue rhythms. Painted at Saint-Rémy, the canvas demonstrates the artist's habit of converting agricultural labor's quiet subjects into studies of pictorial energy.

A lush green wheat field fills the foreground, its dense, swirling stems rendered in short curved strokes of blue-green and yellow-green, while a turbulent sky of pale blue and white clouds sweeps overhead. Van Gogh painted this close-cropped view of a wheat field in 1889, most likely during his residence at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. It is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-in-the-orc: A figure bends over to dig at the foot of a bare-branched tree in an orchard, low farm buildings visible across the flat background. Made in The Hague in July 1883 and catalogued by De La Faille, the work is one of several known impressions; an example is held at the British Museum (inventory 1929,1109.4).
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-le-moulin-: Painted during the Paris years, this view of the Montmartre windmill blends the muted palette of his earlier Dutch work with the lighter tonalities he was absorbing from the Impressionists. The motif, a popular dance hall draw for Parisian painters, is treated soberly rather than festively.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-les-alysca: The Roman necropolis at Arles, lined with poplars turning autumn yellow, is rendered with thick impasto and a steeply receding perspective. The work belongs to a small series painted alongside Gauguin during their fraught Arles collaboration.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-seineufer-: A grassy riverbank slopes down to the Seine near the Pont de Clichy, with a wooden bridge visible at right and a pale grey sky overhead. The brushwork shows the stippled, broken touch Van Gogh absorbed from the Neo-Impressionists during his Paris stay of 1886–88. The palette of greens, yellows, and cool greys reflects the suburban landscape on the edge of the city. The canvas, dated summer 1887, is held at Tate Modern, London.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-wei-es-bau: A modest farmhouse glimpsed through writhing olive trunks, painted in the months at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum. The silver-green foliage is laid down in curling, comma-like strokes that turn the orchard into a continuous nervous surface.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-zwei-bauer: Two stooped laborers turning the earth, a subject the artist returned to throughout his career as homage to Millet. The Saint-Rémy treatment swaps the dark Dutch tonalities of his earlier peasant scenes for a brighter, more rhythmic handling of soil and sky.
collection-of-beauty-van-gogh-zypressen-: Two small figures stand beneath the flame-like silhouette of cypresses, trees the artist described as obsessing him for their dark sculptural force. The composition belongs to the Saint-Rémy cypress group, in which the species becomes a vehicle for swirling, vertical brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-vangogh-starry-nigh: A cypress flames upward through a sky of churning spirals above a sleeping Provençal village. Painted from memory at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in Saint-Rémy, the canvas welds observation, symbol and rhythmic impasto.
collection-of-beauty-various-objects: Letters, an engraving and a sprig of pansies arranged against a wood surface in a trompe l'oeil of pinned papers. Oil on canvas, 72.4 by 60.3 cm, at the Clark Art Institute, among Boilly's earliest illusionistic still lifes.
