Several of the letters are addressed to a Monsieur and Madame Dandré, and the pensées (French for both pansies and thoughts) suggest a dedication.
collection-of-beauty-vasily-surikov-boya: Boyarina Feodosia Morozova is conveyed through a snowy Moscow street on a wooden sledge, her emaciated hand raised in the two-fingered Old Believer sign of the cross as a dense crowd of beggars, clergy, nuns, and curious onlookers presses close. Surikov spent years preparing this monumental canvas, exhibiting it at the Peredvizhniki Travelling Exhibition of 1887. The vast composition — just under three metres high and nearly six metres wide — was acquired for the Tretyakov Gallery, where it remains one of the defining works of Russian historical painting.
collection-of-beauty-vasily-surikov-suvo: Russian troops slide down a near-vertical snowfield above the Saint Gotthard pass, the white-haired general Suvorov on horseback at the cliff edge encouraging them on. Surikov completed the canvas in 1899 for the centenary of the Italian campaign; it hangs in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-vasily-vasilevich-v: A solitary informant figure rendered with the documentary literalism for which the Russian battle painter was known. Vereshchagin's military scenes typically reject heroic convention in favor of the bleak human detail of campaign life.
collection-of-beauty-vasnetsov-acrobats: A lit fairground stage at night draws a working-class Parisian crowd; a white-costumed Pierrot stands on the steps while musicians beat drums and a horse waits in the wings behind a red canvas backdrop. Painted between 1876 and 1877 during Vasnetsov's stay in Paris, the canvas captures the louder, theatrical side of popular entertainment on the city's outskirts. The work is held in the Russian Museum, St Petersburg, and marks the years just before the artist turned decisively to Russian folklore subjects.
collection-of-beauty-vasnetsov-alenushka: A barefoot peasant girl sits hunched on a stone at the edge of a dark forest pond, her chin resting on her knees and her auburn hair loose around her. Vasnetsov drew on the fairy tale of Sister Alyonushka and Brother Ivanushka, using a local girl as model to convey the suffering of a solitary, grief-stricken orphan. Painted at Abramtsevo in 1881, the canvas is held in the Tretyakov Gallery and is widely regarded as one of the defining images of Russian Romantic painting.
collection-of-beauty-vasnetsov-ioann-4: Ivan IV stands on a stairway in elaborate gold-embroidered robes trimmed with white fur, a long staff in hand, his dark eyes fixed in watchful intensity. Vasnetsov painted this full-length imaginary portrait in 1897, drawing on chronicle sources and reconstructions of late Muscovite court regalia to give the figure archaeological specificity. The canvas is held in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-vasnetsov-moving-ho: An elderly couple shuffle across a frozen waterfront in winter, sharing the weight of a heavy sack while a small dog trots beside them; the gilded spire of the Peter and Paul Fortress rises in the mist behind them, placing the scene firmly in St Petersburg. Painted in 1876, the canvas is one of Vasnetsov's early Realist genre works, attentive to the hardship of urban poverty, and is held in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-vasnetsov-samolet: Ivan Tsarevich, the hero of Russian folklore, stands upright on a large ornate flying carpet high above a misty river landscape at dusk, a gilded cage bearing the Firebird at his side and a crescent moon on the horizon. Painted in 1880, the work is one of Vasnetsov's earliest explorations of the fairy-tale subjects that would come to define his mature career. The source describes it as a depiction of Ivan Tsarevich, the archetypal princely hero of Russian folk tradition.
collection-of-beauty-velazquez-de-breda-: Justin of Nassau hands the keys of the Dutch city to the Genoese general Ambrogio Spinola, who lays a conciliatory hand on the defeated commander's shoulder. The forest of upright Spanish pikes that gives the painting its nickname, Las Lanzas, organises the right half of the composition, painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro.
collection-of-beauty-velazquez-el-triunf: A pale, half-nude Bacchus crowns a kneeling soldier with vine leaves while a circle of weather-beaten Spanish drinkers grins out at the viewer. Painted in Madrid before Velázquez's first trip to Italy, the canvas pulls classical mythology down to tavern level with a sober, almost documentary realism.
collection-of-beauty-veld-met-klaprozen-: A green field near Arles scattered with red poppies, farm buildings with orange rooftiles visible across the middle distance. Van Gogh rendered grasses and blossoms in energetic, varied strokes of saturated red and green against a pale sky. Painted in 1888 and now in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam, it belongs to his prolific series of Provençal landscapes made during his time in the south of France.
collection-of-beauty-venice-aristotele-b: A full-length depiction of Aristotle seated in classical robes, stylus in hand, his gaze turned upward with intensity; sculpted lions on a pediment and garden foliage fill the background. Painted by Francesco Hayez and held in the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice, the work exemplifies his ability to fuse careful academic draughtsmanship with the expressive ambitions of Italian Romanticism.
collection-of-beauty-venice-la-distruzio: Hayez stages the Roman sack of Herod's Temple as operatic Romantic history painting: massive white walls from which prisoners are cast down, soldiers bearing Roman standards, and billowing smoke above the scene. The vast canvas of 1867, now in the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice, was conceived as a meditation on tyranny that resonated with Italian audiences living under Austrian rule.
collection-of-beauty-venus-and-adonis-by: Venus, seen from behind, twists to embrace the youthful hunter Adonis as he pulls away with his hounds towards the hunt that will kill him. One of the mythological poesie made for Philip II of Spain, the canvas exemplifies Titian's late, freely brushed handling of flesh and landscape.
collection-of-beauty-venus-and-mars: Mars sleeps disarmed while Venus watches, mischievous satyrs playing with his lance and helmet. The horizontal panel was likely produced as a marriage spalliera or backboard, its Neoplatonic theme contrasting feminine vigilance with the exhaustion of war.
collection-of-beauty-venus-and-mars-nati: Venus, dressed and alert, watches Mars sleep so deeply that the infant satyrs playing with his lance, helmet, and cuirass cannot rouse him — one even blows a conch shell in his ear. Love disarms war: the long horizontal panel was almost certainly a spalliera, a painted backboard for furniture in a Florentine bedchamber, and the wasps buzzing by Mars's head may pun on the Vespucci family, Botticelli's neighbors and likely patrons. Painted around 1483, the panel is now in the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-venus-and-organist-: Venus reclines nude on a draped bed, her small dog beside her, while an organist turns from his keyboard to gaze at her body. Part of a series Titian produced for European courts, the composition stages a debate between sight and sound as competing routes to the experience of beauty.
collection-of-beauty-venus-consoling-lov: Venus reclines in a lush woodland setting, attended by multiple putti — one bearing his bow and quiver leans into her, while another peers from above; white doves flutter at the pool's edge below. Signed and dated 1751, the canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington and exemplifies Boucher's characteristic synthesis of Rococo charm, soft flesh tones, and pastoral fantasy.
collection-of-beauty-vereshchagin-napole: Part of an extensive cycle the painter devoted to the 1812 French invasion of Russia, the canvas shows the emperor on the battlefield reduced to an ordinary, weary commander. The series was researched on site and built around demystifying the Napoleonic legend.
collection-of-beauty-vermeer-view-of-del: A panorama of the artist's home city seen across the Schie, rendered with the peculiar optical fidelity for which he is celebrated. Pinpoint dabs of impasto on the boats and roofs, possibly studied via a camera obscura, mimic the glint of refracted morning light.
collection-of-beauty-veronese-allegory-o: Divine Wisdom, crowned and turned upward, stands beside a brawny Hercules whose attention is fixed on the worldly riches at his feet. The pairing, painted for the Habsburg court, sets celestial contemplation against earthly power in characteristic Venetian color.
collection-of-beauty-veronese-persee-ren: Andromeda, chained to the rock, twists toward the descending hero as Perseus swoops down on the sea monster with drawn sword. The picture's silvery palette and elongated figures, long debated between Veronese and his workshop circle, exemplify late-sixteenth-century Venetian narrative painting.
collection-of-beauty-versailles-boilly-a: A self-portrait of Boilly in middle age, bust-length and turned slightly toward the viewer. Oil on canvas, about 1805, in the collection of the Château de Versailles. The painter renders his own features with the close finish he applied to his commissioned heads.
collection-of-beauty-vertumnus-arstidern: The Roman god of seasons assembled entirely from fruit, vegetables, grains and flowers, each species chosen to flatter Emperor Rudolf II as the bringer of perpetual abundance. The composite portrait is the most refined example of the painter's signature conceit, made for the Prague court.
collection-of-beauty-vesalius-fabrica-p1: A woodcut from Andreas Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica of 1543, showing the complete human skeleton standing upright in a landscape, leaning on a staff — the Latin caption identifies it as the anterior view of the assembled bones. Part of the foundational Renaissance atlas of anatomy, the plate combines scientific precision with a theatrically posed figure set against an open countryside background.

A muscle-man plate from Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, depicting progressive layers of dissection with the cadaver theatrically standing in a Paduan-style landscape. The series broke with medieval anatomical convention by presenting direct observation as the basis of medical knowledge.
collection-of-beauty-victor-vasnetsov-kn: A bogatyr in heavy armour sits on a white horse before a standing stone inscribed in Cyrillic on a darkening steppe, ravens circling above scattered bones and skulls at the stone's base. The inscription warns that the way ahead leads to death, a warning drawn from Russian epic tradition. Vasnetsov completed this composition in 1882; the painting is now in the State Russian Museum.
collection-of-beauty-view-of-constantino: Aivazovsky surveys Constantinople from an elevated hillside at sunset, the Galata Tower — still bearing its original conical roof, destroyed by storm in 1875 — rising above the Golden Horn, the city and its minarets stretching across the horizon. Figures in Ottoman dress rest in the foreground under a large tree. The oil painting dates to 1846 and is held at the Cottage Palace in Peterhof.
collection-of-beauty-view-of-the-brenta-: A late-eighteenth-century view of a canal on the Brenta waterway, with a prominent palazzo at the centre flanked by a church dome, elegantly dressed figures promenading, a horse-drawn cart, and sheep in the foreground. Attributed to Giovanni Battista Cimaroli, the canvas entered the Robert Lehman Collection at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1975 (inv. 1975.1.91).
collection-of-beauty-view-of-tiflis-from: Tiflis, modern Tbilisi, spreads along the Kura river below the bluff of Seid-Abaz, its houses stepping up the slopes toward the surrounding Caucasian ridges. Aivazovsky toured the Caucasus in 1868 and produced a series of Georgian and Armenian townscapes, of which this is one.
collection-of-beauty-vigee-lebrun-elisab: The Controller-General of Finances under Louis XVI shown at his desk, gesturing to a state document. The portrait, lavishly painted in silks and gilt, became notorious as evidence at court of the painter's alleged closeness to her Versailles sitters.
collection-of-beauty-vigee-lebrun-julie-: The painter's daughter Julie posed as the Roman flower goddess, garlanded and seen against a soft pastoral ground. The mythological costume portrait belongs to the artist's exile years following the Revolution, when she worked across the European courts.
collection-of-beauty-vigee-lebrun-marie-: Marie-Antoinette is shown in a pale blue silk court gown trimmed with lace, holding a single rose, with her powdered hair dressed high with feathers. Vigée Le Brun painted this formal version in 1783 as a replacement after the earlier informal muslin-dress portrait caused controversy at the Salon. The work is held at the Palace of Versailles.
collection-of-beauty-vigeelebrun-viewoft: A Savoyard panorama of Lake Challes with Mont Blanc rising in the distance, unusual within the painter's output for being a pure landscape rather than a portrait. The view records her travels through the Alps during her long emigration from revolutionary France.
collection-of-beauty-viktor-vasnetsov-bo: The three bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich, Ilya Muromets and Alyosha Popovich sit mounted at the edge of the steppe, scanning the horizon for enemies. Vasnetsov worked on the nearly 3 by 4 metre canvas for almost twenty years, finishing it in 1898 in the rebuilt barn-studio Savva Mamontov had given him at Abramtsevo; Pavel Tretyakov bought it for his gallery as soon as it was done.
collection-of-beauty-viktor-vasnetsov-by: The painter Viktor Vasnetsov sits in three-quarter length, his long beard and contemplative expression rendered in pastel on grey cardboard. Sergey Malyutin executed the 104 by 59 centimetre portrait in 1915 in Vyatka; it is now held by the Vyatka Art Museum named for the Vasnetsov brothers, inventory number Zh-180.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-00: A self-portrait of the painter trudging to a motif under the Provençal sun, easel and canvases on his back. The picture, formerly in the Kaiser-Friedrich-Museum in Magdeburg, was lost during the Second World War and survives only in reproduction.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-18: A nocturnal view of a yellow-awninged café on the Place du Forum in Arles, with cobblestones receding under a sky of large stars. Van Gogh painted it without using black, building the night entirely from saturated yellows, blues and greens — an early experiment in his ambition to render the south at night in pure colour.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-ba: Bathers and rowboats along the willow-fringed Oise during the artist's final summer at Auvers. The reflective water and slack figures are built from broad, ribbon-like strokes, a calmer register among the more turbulent canvases of these last weeks.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-co: A close-range, near-aerial view of a garden corner in which flowering plants — their pink and white blooms rendered in rapid directional strokes — fill almost the entire picture surface, with butterflies visible among the foliage. Van Gogh painted the work in Paris between May and July 1887, and it is held by the Van Gogh Museum.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-de: A panoramic view of the harvest on the plain of La Crau outside Arles, with stacked sheaves, a blue cart, and distant farm buildings under a Provençal sky. Van Gogh structures the composition with receding parallel bands of yellow stubble, layering complementary blues and oranges to register the heat of high summer.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-en: A walled wheatfield is shown at sunrise, the sun cresting low above distant hills while curling brushstrokes animate the grain. Painted from the window of his room at the asylum in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, it is one of a sustained series in which the same enclosed field is observed across seasons and times of day.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-ho: A cluster of village rooftops in Auvers-sur-Oise, painted during the artist's final months in the small town north of Paris. Thatched and tiled roofs press together in interlocking diagonals, the brushwork rhythmic and ribbon-like across walls, foliage, and a streaked summer sky.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-ir: A bouquet of cut irises arranged in a white vase, their violet-blue petals built from short, kinetic strokes against a pale cream ground. Van Gogh painted this still life in 1890, and the work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (accession number 58.187).

A still life of irises in a vase against a saturated yellow ground, executed at Saint-Rémy. Stems curve upward in calligraphic lines while the petals are massed in cool violets and blues, an overt complementary pairing that the artist used repeatedly during his late flower studies.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-la: A view of the wheat fields and olive groves surrounding the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, with the Alpilles ridges rising in the distance. Curling, parallel brushstrokes animate the soil, foliage, and sky alike, dissolving the topography into a continuous vibrating surface.

A wide landscape with a horse-drawn carriage on a country road and a steam train cutting across the middle distance, painted at Auvers in June 1890. Green fields, farm buildings, and a row of poplars fill the composition, while the train's smoke signals the encroachment of modern transport on the rural plain. The work is held at the Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts, Moscow.

A riverside scene along the Seine on the outskirts of Paris, painted during the artist's Asnières period with Bernard and Signac. The handling shows the impact of Neo-Impressionist contact, with broken touches of pure colour modeling the embankment, water, and screen of trees.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-le: A solitary peasant cutting grain in a sun-blanched field, a subject the artist linked in letters to Millet and to thoughts of mortality. The wheat is built from sweeping yellow strokes that engulf the figure, the reaper's body almost dissolving into the matter he harvests.

A lively view of the Moulin de Blute-Fin on the butte of Montmartre, showing a crowd of fashionably dressed figures gathered at the base of the mill, painted in 1886 during Van Gogh's Paris years. The palette is notably colourful — reds, greens, and blues animate the figures — showing the rapid lightening of his manner after his arrival in the city. The work is held at Museum de Fundatie, Zwolle.

A view of the Moulin de la Galette, the Montmartre windmill turned popular dance garden depicted by Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec. Van Gogh treats the wooden mill and surrounding fence soberly, its silhouette isolated against an overcast Paris sky.

A view of the hamlet of Vessenots near Auvers-sur-Oise, with thatched and tiled cottages set among meadows bright with yellow wildflowers, painted in May 1890. The surface is densely worked in greens and yellows, the buildings serving as compact accents within the expansive landscape. The work is held at the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-mo: A view across the allotment gardens and windmills of upper Montmartre, then still a semi-rural quarter on the northern edge of Paris. Wooden fences, vegetable plots, and the silhouettes of the mills are arranged in receding bands beneath a wide, pale sky.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-pe: Peach trees in full blossom on the plain of La Crau near Arles, their white and pale-pink flowers set against the wide Provençal plain with farmhouses and mountains in the distance, painted in April 1889. The composition is characteristic of Van Gogh's Arles period, with a mosaic of short brushstrokes building the flowering branches and the earth below. The work is held at the Courtauld Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-ro: A country road at twilight with two figures, a horse-drawn cart, a flame-like cypress, and a crescent moon and evening star above. The composition compresses earth and sky into spiraling, rhythmic strokes; it was among the last canvases finished at Saint-Rémy before the move north.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-se: A three-quarter self-portrait painted at the Saint-Rémy asylum in 1889, the face and jacket modelled in cool blue-greens against a swirling turquoise ground. The artist holds himself composed and direct-eyed, the restless spiral brushwork of the background offsetting the stillness of the figure. The work is held at the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.

A Paris-period self-portrait of 1887 in which Van Gogh applies Neo-Impressionist methods to his own features, building flesh tones and the reddish beard from small, separate dabs of colour against a mottled green-blue ground. The handling reflects the lessons absorbed from Seurat and Signac during his time in the city. The work is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.

An early self-portrait with the artist's clay pipe, painted shortly after his arrival in Paris while his palette was still close to that of his Dutch years. Sober earth tones model the bearded face against a neutral ground, before the chromatic experiments of the following year.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-th: A view of the artist's own bedroom in the Yellow House at Arles, repeated in a slightly later replica painted at Saint-Rémy. Tilted floor, paired chairs, and framed prints are arranged in flat planes of colour intended, in his words, to suggest absolute rest.

The medieval parish church of Auvers seen from the apse, its stonework leaning under a deep cobalt sky split by branching lanes. The masonry and lead roofs are worked in thick, undulating strokes that twist the Gothic structure into a single restless form.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-tu: An open garden on the slopes of Montmartre, with couples strolling along winding paths between young trees in bloom. Painted in 1887 during Van Gogh's Paris years, the canvas reflects his growing interest in the broken, complementary colour touches of his Neo-Impressionist contemporaries. The work is held at the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-ve: A field near Arles with a dense foreground of blue and purple irises, beyond which a broad yellow expanse of grass and crops stretches toward a line of trees and the rooftops of the town. Van Gogh painted this view in 1888, one of several canvases he made in and around Arles celebrating the intense colour of Provence in spring. The work is held at the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-wh: A wheat field at Saint-Rémy with twisting cypresses on the right and the Alpilles range behind, the sky churning with rolled, scroll-like clouds. The composition belongs to a small group of variants the artist regarded as among his strongest summer landscapes.

A double-square panorama of a wheat field at Auvers under a vast, lowering blue-grey sky that fills most of the canvas, painted during the artist's final weeks in July 1890. The horizon is placed low, allowing the gathering storm clouds to dominate while the green-yellow grain stretches across the entire width below. The work's wide format matches a small group of panoramic canvases Van Gogh made in the Auvers fields that summer.

A walled wheat field at Saint-Rémy with a single reaper at work in the high sun, the grain rendered as a near-uniform sheet of yellow. The artist described the figure as an image of humanity being mown down like the wheat, an idea that recurs across the late Provençal landscapes.

A late Auvers wheat field interrupted by clusters of blue cornflowers, the surface built from short, directional strokes pulling the eye across the crop. It belongs to the burst of tall double-square canvases the artist produced in the weeks before his death.

A double-square panorama of a wheat field crossed by three diverging paths, with a flock of black crows lifting against a turbulent blue sky. Painted in the Auvers fields shortly before the artist's death, the work compresses storm, harvest, and flight into a single agitated surface.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-van-gogh-ze: A seascape made during the artist's brief stay at the Mediterranean fishing village of Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, with small fishing boats riding choppy water under a wind-driven sky. Short, stabbing strokes register the swell, while patches of pure colour mark sails and reflected light.
collection-of-beauty-vincent-willem-van-: The iron lifting bridge at Trinquetaille on the Rhône at Arles, painted with a tilted, plunging perspective down its broad stone steps. Cool blues and grays mark a deliberate departure from the high-keyed yellow palette of the artist's earlier Arles canvases.

Convicts circling a stone yard under guard, copied at Saint-Rémy after a print by Gustave Doré of Newgate Prison. The artist's choice of source from his asylum bed gives the trudging round of figures a transparent autobiographical charge.

Twelve sunflowers in a cream earthenware vase, set against a pale blue-grey ground and resting on a yellow surface, painted at Arles in August 1888. Van Gogh made this canvas as decoration for the bedroom he was preparing for Gauguin's visit, and the work is among the most celebrated of the series. The vase bears his signature 'Vincent' in yellow paint.

A wheat field at Saint-Rémy seen through a downpour, the rain itself drawn as long diagonal scratches that cut across the painted surface. The device adapts a graphic shorthand from Japanese woodblock prints, which the artist collected and copied.
collection-of-beauty-virgin-and-child-wi: The Virgin cradles the infant Christ as the young John the Baptist offers a reed cross, attended by hovering angels in a soft pastel light. Painted by Boucher in 1765 and now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the canvas softens Counter-Reformation imagery into the rocaille idiom of mid-century Paris.

Seated in a garden with a basket of grapes beside her, the Virgin in a blue mantle bends her cheek to the Christ Child, while the young John the Baptist kneels in prayer at the right with his lamb, and cherubs drowse on the clouds above. The oval canvas, signed and dated 1765, shows Boucher translating his pastoral idiom into devotional imagery — sacred subject matter delivered with the powdery color and soft flesh of his mythologies. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-vladimirka: The empty Vladimirka road, the convict route to Siberia, runs through flat steppe toward a low horizon, a single pilgrim halted at the wayside cross. Levitan painted the unpopulated landscape in 1892 after walking part of the road himself; he gave the canvas to Pavel Tretyakov and it remains in the Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-vnutrennost-yurty-b: The interior of a wealthy Kyrgyz yurt, its felt walls hung with patterned textiles and the floor spread with carpets. One of Vereshchagin's ethnographic studies from his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, later worked up as part of the Turkestan series.
collection-of-beauty-vue-du-val-d-arco-d: A topographical watercolour of the Arco valley in the southern Tyrol, made during Dürer's return journey from his first Italian trip. The fortified hilltop town, terraced vineyards, and outcrops of rock are observed with surveyor's precision, an early instance of independent landscape study in Northern art.
collection-of-beauty-walentin-alexandrow: Rimsky-Korsakov sits half-turned at his desk in a dark frock coat, hand resting on a manuscript page. Serov painted the composer in 1898 for the Tretyakov Gallery during the years Rimsky-Korsakov was teaching at the St Petersburg Conservatory and orchestrating the operas of Mussorgsky.

Serov's two sons, Sasha and Yura, lean against a wooden railing with a wide coastal view behind them, their white shirts and dark trousers rendered in loose, assured brushwork. The painting dates to 1899 and is held in the Russian Museum, St Petersburg. It captures the children in the brisk, diffuse light typical of Serov's plein-air portraits of the period.
collection-of-beauty-walpurgis-night-193: Dense, swirling blue lines scratched over a near-black ground conjure half-legible figures and watchful, owl-like eyes in this 1935 panel by Paul Klee. The work evokes the German folk legend of witches gathering on the Brocken on the eve of May Day, made the year after Klee left Düsseldorf following his dismissal by the Nazi authorities. It is held at Tate (T00669).
collection-of-beauty-wang-meng-dwelling-: A towering hanging scroll in ink on paper, its densely textured peaks built from layered hemp-fibre strokes and moss dots. Wang Meng's restless, near-trembling line gives the Qingbian range a vibrating, almost airless density emblematic of late-Yuan literati landscape.
collection-of-beauty-washingtonatdorches: George Washington in Continental uniform stands beside his horse on the Boston-area hill where his artillery emplacement forced the British evacuation in March 1776. Stuart painted the full-length composition in 1806 for the Boston town fathers; it now hangs at the Museum of Fine Arts and remains the city's official Washington portrait.
collection-of-beauty-wassilij-wassiljewi: Three men stand closely together in richly patterned Central Asian robes and distinctive tall felt hats, their backs turned to the viewer. The careful ethnographic detail of their layered, multicoloured garments reflects Vereshchagin's travels in Central Asia during 1869–1870. Now in the Tretyakov Gallery, the painting exemplifies his documentary approach to the peoples and customs of Russian-administered territories.
collection-of-beauty-water-lilies-agapan: From Monet's late Giverny series, the painting abandons horizon and shoreline for a pure expanse of water surface. Lily pads and blossoms float among broken reflections of sky and trees, the brushwork loosened toward near-abstraction in shades of blue, violet, and green. Originally the left panel of a triptych titled Agapanthus, this monumental canvas — now in the Cleveland Museum of Art — was repainted by Monet before his death, leaving only water lilies on the shimmering surface.
collection-of-beauty-water-lilies-and-ja: The arched footbridge of Monet's Giverny garden hangs above a pond crowded with floating blossoms, framed by curtains of willow and iris. Painted in tightly woven greens and rose-tinted whites, the canvas turns a private water garden into an enclosed world of reflection.
collection-of-beauty-water-lilies-by-mon: An overhead view of the Giverny pond, dotted with discs of pink and white lilies. Cool blues and greens shift toward lavender where the surrounding foliage is mirrored in still water, with no sky visible above the bank.
collection-of-beauty-waterloo-bridge-lon: Part of Monet's London Thames series, Waterloo Bridge dissolves into a pale silver-grey mist, the stone arches barely distinguishable from fog and water. Tall vertical forms — factory chimneys and industrial structures — rise indistinctly beyond the river, their outlines softened by atmosphere. Completed in 1904 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the canvas exemplifies Monet's interest in the Thames as a subject of light rather than topography.
collection-of-beauty-watteau-antoine-que: A young woman crowned with a laurel wreath sits beside a large ornamental urn from which water pours, her gaze turned upward against an open sky with reeds and foliage behind her. The loose, warm handling of the figure and the pastoral setting align with the decorative mythological subjects Watteau explored in this period. Titled Nymphe de fontaine and dated 1718 in the catalogue, the painting was offered at Sotheby's New York in 2012.
collection-of-beauty-wedding-of-nicholas: An imperial ceremonial scene staged inside a Russian Orthodox chapel, with Tsar Nicholas II and Alexandra Fyodorovna at the centre of a glittering crowd of courtiers, clergy and grand dukes. Tuxen, official painter to several European royal houses, marshals the assembly into a measured, document-like composition.
collection-of-beauty-weeping-from-le-bru: An engraved head with furrowed brows, clenched eyes, and a downward-drawn mouth illustrates the passion of weeping, captioned 'WEEPING' below the image. The print reproduces Charles Le Brun's analysis of facial expression, derived from his influential lecture on the passions delivered at the French Royal Academy in 1668. This impression is held in the Wellcome Collection, where it forms part of an extensive archive relating to physiognomy and the study of human expression.
collection-of-beauty-west-benjamin-woodc: Labourers fell and trim oaks in a clearing of Windsor Great Park, the felled trunks arranged in diagonals across the foreground. West painted the scene in 1795 as part of the royal commission documenting estate work, pairing rural labour with the picturesque conventions of late eighteenth-century landscape.
collection-of-beauty-weyden-christ-on-th: A T-shaped cross holding the crucified Christ rises before a red cloth of honour and a stone wall, flanked by the white-robed Virgin and Saint John. The reduced palette and stark spatial setting strip away narrative detail, concentrating on grief and bodily presence in a manner unusual for mid-fifteenth-century devotional painting.
collection-of-beauty-weyden-deposition: The body of Christ is lowered from the cross within a shallow gilded niche, surrounded by ten mourners arranged in a tight, frieze-like rhythm. Van der Weyden's sharp drapery folds and tear-streaked faces compress the Passion into a sculpted relief of grief, a touchstone of Early Netherlandish painting.
collection-of-beauty-whaling-off-the-coa: Small whaling boats converge on a large whale at the surface of the sea off the Goto Islands of Kyushu, their crews manoeuvring amid choppy water and cresting waves. From Hokusai's Oceans of Wisdom (Chie no umi) series, the woodblock print of around 1831–33 pairs a vernacular subject with the artist's characteristic command of rhythmic line and dynamic composition.
collection-of-beauty-wheat-field-with-re: A solitary reaper bends amid blazing yellow stalks beneath a swollen sun. Painted from Van Gogh's window at the Saint-Paul asylum in Saint-Remy, the scene was for him an emblem of human labour and mortality bound to nature's cycles.
collection-of-beauty-whistler-james-symp: Joanna Hiffernan stands full-length in a flowing white dress, holding a small cluster of white flowers, before a gauze curtain backdrop. Her feet rest on a bear-skin rug laid over a patterned carpet. Whistler's emphasis on subtle gradations of cream, ivory and pale flesh tones over storytelling helped lay the ground for Aestheticism's art-for-art's-sake credo.
collection-of-beauty-whistler-nocturne-g: Westminster Bridge and the Thames vanish into a haze of grey-blue twilight, pierced by scattered gold lamplight. The painting belongs to Whistler's Nocturne series, in which musical titles signalled the priority of tonal harmony over narrative.
collection-of-beauty-whistler-nocturne-i: Showers of golden sparks fall through a smoky night sky above the Cremorne Gardens fireworks. The thinly washed, near-monochrome surface so provoked John Ruskin that his attack triggered the famous 1878 libel trial.
collection-of-beauty-whistler-selbstport: Whistler portrays himself in a broad black hat and light grey coat, holding paintbrushes against a near-uniform grey ground. The carefully tuned tonal intervals, with face and hat providing the principal points of contrast, exemplify the musical analogies for picture-making that underlie his Arrangement titles. Painted around 1872, the work is known as Arrangement in Gray: Portrait of the Painter.
collection-of-beauty-whistlers-mother-hi: Anna McNeill Whistler sits in profile in a London interior, bonneted and dressed in black against a pale grey wall hung with one of her son's etchings. The strict horizontal-vertical geometry and muted palette underscore Whistler's framing of a familial portrait as a tonal arrangement.
collection-of-beauty-wiktor-michajlowits: Viktor Vasnetsov depicted himself in this 1873 self-portrait wearing a brown coat and cravat, with auburn hair and a full beard, against a dark background with an easel partly visible at the left. The direct, quietly concentrated gaze and loose painterly handling reflect the realist training Vasnetsov received in those years.

Prince Ivan rides the grey wolf through a moonlit forest, the captured tsarevna Yelena cradled in his arms among gnarled oaks and a flowering apple tree. Painted in 1889 from the Russian folktale of Ivan Tsarevich and the Grey Wolf, the canvas hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery and helped Vasnetsov define the bylina-painting genre at the heart of Russian national Romanticism.
collection-of-beauty-wild-woman-holding-: In this circular engraving a wild woman wearing only a leafy wreath nurses her child while steadying a tilted shield emblazoned with a snarling lion's head; ragged heraldic mantling fills the edges of the roundel. The hairy 'wild folk' of medieval legend were popular shield-supporters in fifteenth-century German art, and Schongauer here turns the motif into an oddly tender domestic image. The plate is signed with his M†S monogram.
collection-of-beauty-wilhelm-alexander-w: A group of mounted officers and attendant cavalry survey a distant city from a high ridge in this 1808 painting by Wilhelm von Kobell. The work depicts the 1807 siege of Cosel in Silesia, recording the Bavarian repulse of a Prussian sortie during the Third Coalition War; the city lies in the misty valley below, framed by bare winter trees at right.
collection-of-beauty-wilhelm-von-kaulbac: Kaulbach assembled a variety of butterfly and moth species around a bare branch against a dark brown ground, recording each specimen's wing markings with finely observed detail. The composition, dated around 1860, arranges the insects in a loose arabesque rhythm across the picture surface.
collection-of-beauty-wilhelm-von-kobell-: Drovers, riders and townspeople negotiate over cattle on a rise overlooking a Bavarian lake, with a distant city silhouetted under bright clear air. Kobell's crisp draftsmanship and high-keyed Alpine light typify his Biedermeier landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-wilhelmine-sulzer: Wilhelmine Sulzer is depicted in a white off-the-shoulder dress with embroidered neckline trim and a fur stole, her auburn hair falling loosely around her shoulders against a dark ground. Stieler painted this 1838 portrait for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie in Munich, applying his characteristic porcelain finish and discreet idealisation.
collection-of-beauty-william-curtis-1775: Oil portrait of the English botanist William Curtis, demonstrator of plants at the Chelsea Physic Garden from 1771 and later author of Flora Londinensis. The picture, held in the RHS Lindley Collections, captures Curtis during the years before he launched The Botanical Magazine in 1787.
collection-of-beauty-william-holman-hunt: A garden stream runs through a series of wooden sluice boards in the foreground, bordered by irises and dense summer vegetation, while the timber gables of a building are glimpsed through the trees at upper right. Painted in 1849 and now in the Tate collection, the work displays Hunt's meticulous early Pre-Raphaelite attention to botanical and textural detail rendered in warm evening light.

Hunt meets the viewer's gaze in this large 1867 self-portrait, wearing an elaborate Eastern silk robe over red undergarments and a decorative embroidered sash, with a painter's palette in hand and brushes on the table before him. A founding member of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, he presents himself here with the intensity and meticulously observed surface detail that characterised his later career.

Edith, the artist's wife, is shown in three-quarter view wearing a dark dress with white fur collar trim, a richly patterned shawl, and a red bead necklace, holding an ornate beaded purse and a red rose. Dated 1868, the portrait's exacting detail of ornament and fabric — some acquired during Hunt's eastern travels — exemplifies his characteristic Pre-Raphaelite finish in an intimate register.

The boy Jesus is discovered among Jerusalem's elders, who recoil or peer at him in a chamber thick with embroidered textiles, scrolls and oil lamps. Hunt prepared the picture during years in the Holy Land, pursuing archaeologically researched detail as a vehicle for biblical truth.

A Pre-Raphaelite vision of Christ as a young carpenter stretching after labor, his outflung arms casting a cruciform shadow across the workshop wall. Hunt painted the scene in Jerusalem to ground every tool, shaving and textile in archaeological accuracy.
collection-of-beauty-william-m-chase-n-a: Sargent's full-length portrait of William Merritt Chase shows the older painter holding palette and brushes, his pince-nez and white cravat catching the light against a near-black ground. The fluid, broadly handled paint that reduces costume and setting to shadow exemplifies Sargent's debt to Velázquez. Painted in 1902, the canvas is now held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-william-merrit-chas: Grapes, peaches, a melon, pears and other fruit are arranged on a stone ledge before an open landscape of grass and sky. A wicker basket of red fruit and a butterfly enliven the composition. Painted in 1871 and now held at the Parrish Art Museum, the work shows Chase's early academic command of the traditional fruit-piece genre.
collection-of-beauty-william-merritt-cha: A sandy track winds through open coastal scrubland under a pale, clear sky, the dried grasses and low shrubs carrying the first warm tones of autumn. The wide, flat horizon suggests the Long Island shore near Chase's Shinnecock Hills summer school. Painted around 1898, the work belongs to Chase's sustained engagement with the American Impressionist plein-air landscape.

A young woman is shown bust-length wearing a pale blue kimono decorated with red and gold botanical motifs and an orange obi sash, her dark hair loosely arranged. Chase's fluid brushwork focuses attention on the sitter's composed gaze and the decorative surface of the Japanese garment. Painted around 1890, the work is held at the Brooklyn Museum and reflects the Aesthetic-movement taste for Japonisme in American studios of the period.

Chase's family takes breakfast in a leafy Brooklyn yard, the white tablecloth and hammock catching dappled sun. Loose brushwork and a bright outdoor palette align the scene with American Impressionism's domestic, garden-side mode.

Chase's family takes breakfast in a leafy Brooklyn yard, the white tablecloth and hammock catching dappled sun. Loose brushwork and a bright outdoor palette align the scene with American Impressionism's domestic, garden-side mode.

A hummingbird hovers at the apex of a dense floral arrangement in an ornate vase, the roses, carnations and grasses rendered against a warm ochre ground. The tightly observed bird and academic handling of the blooms reflect Chase's Munich-trained still-life manner in his earliest years. Painted in 1870, the work is held in the collection identified in museum records as Q1117704.

A woman in a white dress sits absorbed in thought on a red upholstered chair in a grand interior, leaning her head on her hand as another figure plays piano in the background. Arched ceilings, a heavy table bearing books and flower arrangements, and a distant gilded figure set an atmosphere of cultivated leisure. Chase painted the work in 1907, using his characteristic fluid handling to animate the richly appointed space.

A young woman in mourning black reclines on a red velvet settee, her auburn hair and pale face set against richly coloured red walls. Chase's confident, economical brushwork conveys both the weight of grief and the sensuous warmth of the interior. Painted in 1884, the canvas is held at the National Academy of Design, New York.
collection-of-beauty-william-turner-brid: Turner's 1833 view of Venice stretches from the Customs House at the left across the basin to the Campanile, Doge's Palace and the Bridge of Sighs, the foreground animated by gondolas, trading vessels and waterside figures. The vivid blue sky and warm stone of the buildings are rendered with relative topographical clarity, marking the work as distinct from Turner's hazier late Venetian oils. Now at Tate (inventory N00370), it was exhibited at the Royal Academy the year it was painted.
collection-of-beauty-wind-god-and-thunde: Sotatsu's pair of two-fold screens places Fujin clutching his wind sack and Raijin riding a ring of drums against expanses of unworked gold leaf. The bold negative space and tarashikomi ink pooling became a touchstone for the Rinpa school and a National Treasure of Japan.
collection-of-beauty-windmill-and-boats-: Painted during Monet's residence in the Dutch town of Zaandam, the canvas registers a working waterway under low northern light, with a windmill anchoring the moored barges. Quick, broken touches across the water anticipate the Impressionist breakthroughs of the next few years.
collection-of-beauty-windows-open-simult: A small 1912 oil in which the Eiffel Tower dissolves into a grid of translucent green, pink and ochre prisms, identifiable only by its tapering silhouette. Acquired by the Tate and measuring 45.7 by 37.5 cm, the panel belongs to Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows cycle, the founding works of Orphism.
collection-of-beauty-winners-by-vasily-v: Drawn from Vereshchagin's Balkan series, the painting confronts the aftermath of battle: victorious soldiers in red-trimmed coats move among the fallen on a grey, open field. The Russian realist refused to glamorise war, building documentary detail into a deliberately disquieting scene of defeat and death. Painted between 1878 and 1879, the large canvas exemplifies Vereshchagin's unflinching engagement with the human cost of conflict.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-after: A black sailor lies cast up beside his shattered sloop on a Bahamian beach, the sea behind still heavy from the storm. Homer's late watercolor technique uses transparent washes and reserved white paper to convey both tropical glare and human vulnerability.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-ameri: A hunter rests on a felled tree stump on an autumnal hillside, a rifle in hand and a deer carcass with antlers slung across his back, while two hounds flank him against a sky of rolling clouds. Homer sets the scene in a landscape of red-orange foliage and dead timber that speaks to the rougher economy of the wilderness. Painted in 1891, the oil is one of Homer's major late figural works in the realist mode.

A coastguardsman pulls a fainting woman across the surf on a breeches buoy, the rope line cutting taut against churning spray. Homer studied actual life-saving drills on the New Jersey coast, and the obscured rescuer's face concentrates attention on the woman's limp red scarf.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-artis: Three painters at work on an open hillside in the White Mountains, each at an easel sheltered by a large parasol umbrella, the mountain ridges and a stormy sky filling the distance behind them. The foreground figure works intently while two others are visible further along the slope. Painted in 1868, the work is held at the Portland Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-breez: A catboat heels into a stiff wind, four figures — three boys and an older man at the tiller — braced along the gunwale as spray breaks around the hull. A second vessel appears on the horizon to the right. Homer worked on this composition between 1873 and 1876, and the finished oil became one of his best-known celebrations of post-Civil-War American leisure.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-clear: Two figures stand on a rocky bank in the right foreground, watching several sailboats glide across calm, reflective water under a light sky. Homer summarises the scene with characteristic economy of wash, leaving the white paper to carry the sails' brightness. The watercolour, dated 1880, is held at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-crab-: Four figures — a fisherman in a yellow oilskin at the bow and three women amidships — ride a small open dory through choppy grey seas, a crab pot visible in the bow. Homer captures the weight of rough weather with loose washes of grey and white, the figures rendered with confident economy. The watercolour, dated 1883, is held at the Worcester Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-dad-s: A boy seated beside a beached dory stares out toward a horizon dotted with distant sails, while a woman stands a little behind him looking in the same direction. The paired figures and their mutual waiting convey the coastal anxieties that run through Homer's early shore paintings. Dated 1873, the oil is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-eagle: Three young women emerge from the surf onto the Cape Ann shore, their wet bathing dresses clinging in a way that scandalized contemporary critics. Homer treats the scene as a study of weight, wind and waterlogged fabric rather than narrative incident.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-girl-: A young woman in a white apron and close-fitting bonnet stands before a wall of flowering mountain laurel in full bloom, a basket in her hand and her gaze directed outward. The vertical composition and dense floral backdrop place the figure firmly within Homer's mid-career sequence of solitary rural women absorbed in the seasonal landscape. Dated 1879.

A woman reclines in a hammock slung between trees in a shaded garden, reading a book, a red shawl visible beside her. Light filters through the leafy canopy, and Homer's close attention to the play of sun and shadow across the foliage fills the picture with a decorative, almost flat quality. The oil, dated 1873, is held at the Colby College Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-long-: Two fashionable women in bustled dresses pause on a cliff at the Jersey Shore resort, parasols snapping in the Atlantic wind. Homer's bright, almost Impressionist palette captures the new postwar leisure culture with magazine-illustrator clarity.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-mink-: A brightly coloured sunfish and a frog face one another across a lily pad in the dark, reflective water of an Adirondack pond, a white water-lily bloom opening to the left. Homer dissolves the boundary between underwater and surface worlds, the whole scene rendered with the precise yet luminous touch he brought to his later nature watercolours. Signed and dated Mink Pond 1891.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-moonl: Two figures sit silhouetted on a dark beach as a full moon rides high above the horizon, its reflection stretching across the breaking surf. Homer uses a restricted palette of dark teal, grey and brown to evoke the stillness of a coastal night, the moon's halo and the white foam the only bright notes in the composition. Dated 1874, the work is held at the Fenimore Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-on-th: A small group of bathers in dark dress stands at the water's edge beneath a brooding overcast sky, the breaking surf occupying the centre of the canvas in powerful horizontal bands of dark wave and white foam. Homer subordinates the figures to the elemental force of sea and sky, a composition characteristic of his early Atlantic coast paintings. Circa 1869, held at the Arkell Museum.

Two young women meet at a wooden fence in a sunny pastoral setting, one seated on the stile and the other leaning against it, their hands nearly touching. The scene belongs to Homer's Houghton Farm idylls of the late 1870s, where rural leisure is rendered with the clarity of magazine illustration and a warm, unidealized light. Circa 1878, held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-shark: A shirtless man and a young child sit in a small wooden boat while two sharks circle alongside in open blue water, the larger shark occupying the full foreground. Homer painted the scene during his visits to the Bahamas in the mid-1880s, and the work anticipates the themes of human vulnerability before the sea that he would develop in The Gulf Stream. Dated 1885.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-sunli: Surf crashes against dark rocky ledges under a storm-lit sky, with a distant vessel barely visible on the horizon. No human figure appears; Homer reduces the scene to an elemental confrontation of wave, rock, and atmosphere. Painted in 1890, the work belongs to his Prouts Neck marine series and is held at the Toledo Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-the-a: A solitary woodsman paddles his canoe across a still mountain lake, the watercolor reserving the white of the paper for highlights on water and shirt. The picture distills Homer's late respect for the working backwoodsman into a quietly monumental profile.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-the-b: Two barefoot boys in straw hats stand on a sunlit hillside, one upright and gazing into the distance, the other seated below him. The landscape opens behind them to a broad sky with scattered clouds, a red barn just visible at the far right. Watercolour, dated 1873, the work is catalogued as Cow Boys and held at the David Owsley Museum of Art, Ball State University.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-the-f: A halibut fisherman in a dory pauses at the crest of a swell to gauge the schooner against a wall of advancing fog. The diagonal of the boat and the steep horizon convert a routine moment into a measured study of solitude at sea.

A young girl in a white dress sits in a cottage garden, holding a small flower and turning it in her hands before a multi-paned window framed by climbing roses. The setting is domestic and sheltered, the mood absorbed and quiet. Painted in 1873, the work is held at the Detroit Institute of Arts.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-the-g: A solitary female figure in a brown dress crouches on the sun-drenched lower slope of a gently rolling hillside, trees at the left horizon and open sky above. Homer reduces the composition to broad fields of colour — earth, grass, and cloud — with the single figure providing a quiet focal point. Painted in 1878, the work is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

A Black sailor lies on the deck of a dismasted sloop adrift on rough seas, encircled by sharks while a waterspout darkens the horizon. Homer's late marine paintings turn man-against-nature subjects into terse moral allegories, the figure's resigned posture sharpened by the painter's economical handling of pigment and salt-bleached light.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-the-h: Two fishermen work a dory laden with the silver gleam of a hauled net, the larger schooners reduced to ghosted shapes in the Atlantic mist. Painted after Homer settled at Prouts Neck, the picture distills the labor of New England's offshore fleet into a low horizon, broad tonal blocks, and a pearly fog that flattens space.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-the-r: A solitary harvester in a wide-brimmed hat swings his scythe through a field of grain under a stormy summer sky, the pale stalks filling the foreground. The upright figure and brooding clouds give the scene a quietly monumental character. Painted in 1878 and associated with Homer's Houghton Farm period, the work is held at the Art Renewal Center.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-two-b: Two boys sit side by side on low rocks at the water's edge, watching a fleet of schooners at anchor across a calm bay under an overcast sky. The watercolour pares the scene to stone, water, sail, and muted sky, characteristic of Homer's coastal subjects. Painted in 1880, the work is held at the Art Institute of Chicago.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-warm-: A woman lies stretched out on the grass in the shadow of a large tree, a sheep resting close beside her, while a flock grazes across the sunlit hillside behind them. The composition contrasts the shaded foreground with the warm, open pasture receding to a row of trees on the horizon. Painted in 1878, the work is held at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-winslow-homer-watch: Two women in dark Victorian dresses stand on a rocky shore as heavy surf breaks behind them; one carries a wicker basket, and the vivid orange-patterned hem of her companion's skirt catches against the grey rocks. Homer sets the human figures as a counterweight to the churning Atlantic, animating the Prouts Neck seascape with narrative weight. Painted in 1891, the work is held at the Gilcrease Museum, Tulsa.
collection-of-beauty-winter-night-ekely-: From Munch's late period at Ekely, his estate outside Oslo, where the ageing painter circled the same garden and orchard motifs through every season. Bare trees stand against deep blue snow in raw, scumbled strokes, the loneliness familiar from his earlier symbolist work distilled into pure landscape.
collection-of-beauty-wla-moma-monet-refl: Monet's three-panel Water-Lily triptych at the Museum of Modern Art spans roughly forty feet of canvas, carrying the Giverny pond surface in an unbroken panoramic band. Painted around 1920, the panels dissolve water, lily pads, and cloud reflections into shifting fields of blue-green and golden-amber, without horizon or sky to anchor the view. The work is held at the Museum of Modern Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-wlanl-adagio808-clo: A massive cliff face of warm ochre and rose-tinted rock fills most of the canvas, a strip of sandy beach and turquoise sea opening at its foot under a clear blue sky. Monet paints the cliff's surface in dense, broken strokes that animate the stone with light and colour. Painted in 1882, the work is held at the Rijksmuseum Twenthe, Enschede.
collection-of-beauty-wohnzimmer-des-schl: The sitting room of the Berlin locksmith C.F.A. Hauschild on Stralauer Strasse 49, with blue patterned wallpaper, a large wardrobe and mirror at left, framed pictures on the walls, and a family group at various occupations across the room. Eduard Gaertner, who trained as a porcelain painter at KPM, made a speciality of Biedermeier-era interiors and Berlin views, and painted this domestic scene in 1843.
collection-of-beauty-woman-writing-a-let: A seated lady drafts a letter at a draped table while her standing maid waits, glancing toward a sunlit window. Vermeer constructs the interior with his characteristic geometry of floor tiles, parallel walls, and a hanging picture, weaving the small domestic event into a quietly orchestrated study of light and waiting.
collection-of-beauty-xsxlt-fankuan: A monumental hanging scroll in which towering peaks rise abruptly above a thread of waterfall, while travelers and pack mules trace a path across the valley floor. A landmark of Northern Song monumental landscape, the work uses dense raindrop texture strokes and a vertiginous vertical scale to express the Confucian ideal of nature dwarfing humanity.
collection-of-beauty-yamamoto-1904: A heavily cloaked figure stands with his back to the viewer, surveying a harbour or coastal industrial scene rendered in bold gouged lines and flat tonal areas. This 1904 woodcut by Kanae Yamamoto, titled "Fisherman," is considered a founding work of the sosaku-hanga movement, in which the artist independently designed, carved, and printed each sheet.
collection-of-beauty-yermolova: The actress Maria Yermolova stands full length in a black gown, her gaze directed upward and away from the viewer, a large framed painting of an arched interior visible on the wall behind her. Painted by Valentin Serov in 1905 to mark her anniversary at the Maly Theatre, the work is now in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-yoshiclimber: A lone warrior clings to a near-vertical rock face beneath a crescent moon and windswept grasses, his body braced against the cliff as he ascends. This is plate seven of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series (1885), depicting the young Toyotomi Hideyoshi in his famous assault on the castle of Inaba Mountain.
collection-of-beauty-yoshida-hiroshi-gra: The South Rim falls away into vast layered cliffs flushed with desert light, a Japanese sensibility brought to the American Southwest. The print belongs to Yoshida's United States series, made after his sketching tour abroad, and uses successive overprintings to suggest the canyon's atmospheric haze.
collection-of-beauty-yoshida-hiroshi-rap: Powerful cascading water fills the composition in Hiroshi Yoshida's 1928 woodblock print, with white foam churning over dark rocks as the river plunges in a broad torrent. Yoshida, who trained as a Western-style oil painter before turning to woodblock printing, achieves the water's translucent force through the layered impressions characteristic of his technique.
collection-of-beauty-yoshida-hiroshi-suz: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida, dated 1935 in the margin, showing snow-capped Mount Fuji rising beyond a stand of pines and farm buildings along the Suzukawa river, the mountain and trees doubled in the still water of the foreground. Yoshida trained as a Western-style painter, and his prints join Japanese woodblock technique to a naturalist's handling of light and atmosphere, produced under his close supervision in his own studio.
collection-of-beauty-yoshida-kameido: The arched drum bridge of Kameido Tenjin shrine reflects in the still pond below, surrounded by spring wisteria. Yoshida revisits a motif made famous by Hiroshige, but rebuilds it with the soft tonal gradations and calibrated overprinting of the shin-hanga revival.
collection-of-beauty-yoshida-komagatake: From the summit of Komagatake, a vast sea of white clouds fills the composition, with the distant cone of Mount Fuji rising above the cloud layer at the left. A small shrine or refuge marks the rocky foreground ridge in this 1928 woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida, whose lifelong mountaineering informed his alpine series.
collection-of-beauty-yoshida-sailboat-mo: A single junk-rigged sailboat moves across calm, luminous water, its sails and hull mirrored in glassy reflections below. This 1921 woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida belongs to his celebrated sailboat set, in which the same composition was printed in different colorways to capture varying times of day and atmospheric conditions.
collection-of-beauty-yoshioldwoman: The aged poetess Ono no Komachi sits before a wooden gravemarker beneath a crescent moon, a woven basket on her back and a staff in her hands, her gaze lifted skyward. Plate twenty-five of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon (1886), the image evokes the courtly love legend in which Komachi's later life became a meditation on the arrogance she had shown her suitors in youth.
collection-of-beauty-yoshitoshi-100-aspe: A bearded figure in green robes stands against a vast golden moon, one hand raised pointing upward while his axe rests at his side and a fan hangs from his arm. From Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series, this design illustrates the Daoist legend of Wu Gang, condemned to chop eternally at the cassia tree on the moon.

A towering festival float, richly decorated with red and green ornaments, miniature figurines, and a tall banner, is shown against a clear blue sky. This is plate thirty-three of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series (1886), titled "Dawn Moon of the Shinto Rites," and depicts the elaborate dashi floats associated with Shinto festival processions.

A courtier in flowing light blue robes draws a yumi bow at a sika deer beneath a full moon and autumn cherry tree, fallen maple leaves scattered across the ground. From Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, this print illustrates the incident in which Minamoto no Tsunemoto killed a deer in the imperial palace grounds in the autumn of 932.
collection-of-beauty-yoshitoshi-the-ghos: A translucent female figure with long dishevelled hair drifts among climbing gourd vines bearing white flowers and fruit, the full moon glowing behind her against a blue ground. The cartouche links this image to the "Yugao" chapter of The Tale of Genji, and the print is part of Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's One Hundred Aspects of the Moon series.
collection-of-beauty-yoshitoshi-tsuki: The warrior-monk Benkei stands at the prow of a storm-tossed vessel in Daimotsu Bay, calming the vengeful spirits of fallen Taira warriors with chanted prayers. From One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, Yoshitoshi pitches the scene against rolling waves and a clouded moon to dramatize the Heike legend.
collection-of-beauty-young-spartans-exer: Four Spartan girls advance toward a group of nude boys in an open landscape, challenging them to exercise, while older citizens and women watch from the middle distance. Drawing on Plutarch's account of the legislator Lycurgus, who urged Spartan girls to engage in wrestling and physical contest with boys, Degas reworked the canvas across the 1860s and later. The picture is in the National Gallery, London (NG3860).
collection-of-beauty-young-tiger-playing: A tigress reclines on a rocky ground beneath a stormy sky while a young cub presses close and wrestles at her face and neck. Painted in 1830 by Eugène Delacroix, the canvas belongs to the Département des Peintures of the Louvre (RF 1943) and exemplifies the Romantic fascination with wild animal energy.
collection-of-beauty-yuliya-samoylova: Countess Yuliya Samoylova strides forward in a white ermine-trimmed gown before a sweeping crimson curtain, her adopted daughter Amazilia Pacini at her side. Karl Bryullov completed this life-size oil on canvas by 1842; it is held in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg (inv. Ж-5093).
collection-of-beauty-zaandam2: Dutch windmills line a low horizon while flat water carries their reflections under a wide sky. The etching belongs to Whistler's later European tours, where his economical needlework and selective wiping of the plate convert a mundane port into a tonal study close in spirit to his Nocturnes.
collection-of-beauty-zbvenigorod-savvins: A plank bridge crosses a dark stream amid lush summer trees and green undergrowth at Savvinskaya Sloboda near Zvenigorod, with wooden village buildings visible behind. Isaac Levitan painted this small canvas in 1884 while near Zvenigorod, as confirmed by the title on the work.
collection-of-beauty-zeitungsleser-im-ha: A Biedermeier gentleman absorbs himself in his newspaper amid the trellised greenery of a small private garden. Spitzweg specialized in such gently humorous bourgeois vignettes, painted in rich enamel-like color, that catalogued the introspective civic culture of mid-nineteenth-century Munich.
collection-of-beauty-zentralbibliothek-z: Anna Magdalena Schweizer, née Hess (1751–1814), is shown in a precise profile view, her hair swept up and secured with a ribbon bow. Henry Fuseli executed this pencil portrait drawing on 15 March 1779, when the sitter was 27 years old; it is preserved in the Zentralbibliothek Zürich.
collection-of-beauty-zinaida-yusupova-by: Princess Zinaida Yusupova sits on a flower-patterned sofa in a white dress with a dark velvet bodice, a large white borzoi beside her in an interior hung with paintings. Valentin Serov worked on the portrait between 1900 and 1902; it now belongs to the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg (abbreviated GRM).
collection-of-beauty-zmei-gorinich-colou: The bogatyr Dobrynya Nikitich, armoured and cloaked in crimson, confronts the towering seven-headed dragon Zmey Gorynych against a blazing red and violet sky. Viktor Vasnetsov completed the canvas in 1918, drawing on the Russian bylina cycle; it is held in the House-Museum of V. M. Vasnetsov, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-zwei-junge-seehunde: Two young harbor seals lie on a stretch of Flemish shoreline, painted with the close observation of fur, hide, and salt-damp sand for which the de Vos workshop was prized. The Antwerp painter built his career on Baroque animal subjects, often supplying livestock and game for collaborators including Rubens.
collection-of-beauty__a-garden-gate-in-c: A weathered wooden gate set into a sun-bleached adobe wall, sketched on Vereshchagin's Central Asian journey. The painter's eye for vernacular architecture turns a quiet doorway into a record of Chuguchak's domestic fabric in the wake of regional war.
collection-of-beauty__by-the-fortress-wa: From the Turkestan series, the canvas commemorates the Russian defense of Samarkand in 1868: soldiers crouch behind a defensive wall, awaiting the order to admit attackers within firing range. The terse caption carries the painting's pent-up tension.
collection-of-beauty__fakir: A solitary Indian ascetic, painted after Vereshchagin's travels through India in the early 1870s. The figure's gaunt frame and bright cloth set against a plain ground typify the artist's documentary approach to religious and ethnographic subjects abroad.
collection-of-beauty__prokhod-barskaun: A view of the Barskoon gorge in the Tian Shan mountains, painted during Vereshchagin's travels through Russian Turkestan. Rocky cliffs and a thin descending road register his documentary interest in the terrain of the empire's southern frontier.
collection-of-beauty__razvaliny-chugucha: Crumbling walls and abandoned masonry mark the ruins of Chuguchak (Tacheng), destroyed during the Dungan Revolt shortly before Vereshchagin's visit. The painter renders the desolation with a topographer's precision, treating wreckage as both landscape and historical witness.
collection-of-beauty__ruins-of-chinese-s: The shattered remains of a Chinese temple at Ak-Kent, recorded during Vereshchagin's first Turkestan expedition. Broken roof tiles and exposed beams testify to the violence of the Dungan uprising that swept the region in the 1860s.
collection-of-beauty__selling-a-child-sl: A Central Asian slave market scene, with a turbaned merchant inspecting a naked boy offered for sale. Vereshchagin's Turkestan series used such unflinching ethnographic detail as moral indictment, the cool light and tile-work setting heightening the transactional cruelty.
collection-of-beauty__snowscape-ma-yuan: A winter landscape by the Southern Song master Ma Yuan, working in the spare 'one-corner' composition for which he is named. Bare trees and rocky outcrops occupy a fraction of the silk while open mist suggests the cold expanse beyond.
collection-of-beauty__ukrainian-woman: A young Ukrainian peasant woman in embroidered dress, painted with Repin's characteristic warmth of touch and earth-toned palette. The study reflects his recurring engagement with rural Ukrainian subjects and the ethnographic realism of the Peredvizhniki circle.
collection-of-beauty__yaponka: A young Japanese woman in kimono, made during Vereshchagin's 1903 journey to Japan, his last major travel project. The bright textiles and frontal pose continue his lifelong practice of ethnographic portraiture across Asia.
kunstformen-images-assortment-of-hepatic: Plate 82 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904) presents an array of liverworts (Hepaticae) including both thalloid genera such as Marchantia and Lunularia and numerous foliose species from Scapania, Lepidozia, and Jungermannia. The coloured lithograph arranges gametophytes, archegonial heads, and sporophytes across the page to reveal the diverse architectural forms within the group.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-acanthometra: Lithographic plate gathering Acantharian protozoa whose star-shaped strontium-sulfate skeletons radiate twenty spicules from a central point. Haeckel arranged the microscopic single-celled marine organisms in a cathedral-like symmetry, advancing his argument that morphological law unites the smallest plankton with the greatest works of design.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-acanthophract: Plate 41 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904) depicts Acanthophractan radiolarians whose silica lattice shells radiate spines and form intricate polyhedral and stellate tests. Haeckel arranged several species, including Dorataspis and Diploconus, to reveal the geometric variety within the group and his conviction that microscopic marine life embodied universal laws of natural ornament.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-acephala: Plate of headless bivalve molluscs arrayed for symmetry: Venus clams, cockles, and related shells shown in opening, valve, and hinge views. Haeckel exploits the radiating ribs and growth rings to draw the eye outward from each pair, treating malacology as ornamental design.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-actiniae: Sea anemones rendered with their tentacle crowns spread in jewel-toned discs, including Cereus pedunculatus and Aiptasia mutabilis. The plate compresses several species into a single bouquet, using the column striations and radial muscle bands as decorative geometry.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-ammonitida: Fossil ammonite shells from the Mesozoic, shown in lateral and ventral views to display sutured chambers and ribbed coiling. The composition makes the logarithmic spiral and ornamentation of Cardioceras and Schloenbachia legible at a glance, treating extinct cephalopods as design specimens.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-amphoridea: Plate 95 of Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904) brings together Palaeozoic cystoid echinoderms — including Enoploura and Pleurocystites — alongside juvenile and larval forms of living echinoderms such as Ophiothrix, Luidia, and Arbacia. The juxtaposition of armoured fossil plates with delicate modern larvae underscores Haeckel's comparative approach to echinoderm morphology across geological time.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-anthomedusae: Hydromedusae of the Anthomedusae order, shown from above, below and in lateral section to expose the gonads and gastrovascular canals. Trailing tentacles fall in glassy curtains around bell-shaped umbrellas, a study in translucent radial symmetry.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-antilopina: Nine antelope and bovid species drawn full-body, including four-horned antelope, black wildebeest, sitatunga, pronghorn, waterbuck, sable antelope, addax, greater kudu, and bushbuck. The plate functions as a comparative survey of horn forms — spiral, lyrate, forked, and straight — set against lightly indicated ground. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 100.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-arachnida: Spiders and arachnids in close comparative study: orb-weavers with spiny abdomens (Gasteracantha, Micrathena), a garden spider, a lynx spider, and a tailless whipscorpion (Phrynichus reniformis), alongside four mite species of the Cepheus group. Each specimen is magnified and set against a warm ground to expose sculptural cuticle detail. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 66.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-ascidiae: Sea squirts presented as solitary forms, in section, and as colonial aggregates. Boltenia echinata is shown bristling with spicules above a longitudinal cut that reveals the U-shaped gut, while compound ascidians cluster like ripening fruit on the lower register.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-ascomycetes: Plate from Kunstformen der Natur showing a symmetrical arrangement of sac fungi, with cup-shaped fruiting bodies and powdery mildews magnified and framed like ornament. Haeckel's lithographs translated microscopic biology into decorative compositions that fed directly into Art Nouveau design.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-aspidonia: Horseshoe crabs and their extinct sea-scorpion kin, including Tachypleus gigas in adult and larval form alongside the Silurian eurypterid Eurypterus tetragonophthalmus. The plate stages a deep-time comparison between living and fossil chelicerates.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-asteridea: Adult and larval starfish across several species: bipinnaria, brachiolaria, and pentapalmar larvae of Asterias rubens arranged in the upper register, with a large mature Asterias at centre. The lower portion shows the cushion starfish Pteraster stellifer and the webbed Hymenaster echinulatus, each rendered from above and below. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 40.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-basimycetes: Stinkhorn fungi arranged on a dark ground: the latticed Clathrus ruber, the tall veiled stinkhorn (Dictyophora madonna), the starfish-armed Aseroë rubra, and Phallus impudicus with a lengthwise section of its volva. Cross-sections of egg stages appear alongside mature fruiting bodies. From Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 63.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-batrachia: Tropical tree frogs and marsupial frogs grouped for skin-pattern variety, including Hyla meridionalis, Rhacophorus pardalis, and the egg-brooding Gastrotheca. Splayed toe pads and warted backs are emphasized to register adhesive and camouflage adaptations.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-blastoidea: Extinct Paleozoic blastoids with budlike calyces drawn from above and the side, including Pentremites pyriformis. The five-petaled ambulacral fields are featured prominently, and one specimen appears with its delicate brachioles extended, folded, and removed.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-bryozoa: Freshwater and marine moss animals centered on Cristatella mucedo, traced through statoblast, juvenile, and mature colony stages. Haeckel draws the gelatinous mat with its lophophore crowns extended in a feathered ring around each zooid.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-bryozoa-33: Calcified bryozoan skeletons enlarged so that individual zooecia read as tiled honeycomb. Phaeostachys, Cribrilina, and Umbonula appear as porous lacework, with detail shifting between whole colonies and single chambered cells.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-calcispongiae: Calcareous sponges of the Leucosolenia and Guancha groups, shown as branching tubular colonies anchored by spiculate roots. Haeckel sets habitus drawings beside isolated triradiate spicules to expose the skeletal architecture beneath the soft tissue.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-campanariae: Hydroid colonies of the family Campanulariidae, slender stems bearing bell-shaped hydranths and reproductive gonophores. The plate threads the colonies like vines across the page, foregrounding the hydrothecae as cup-on-stalk ornaments.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-chaetopoda: Marine bristle worms with their feeding crowns expanded: feather duster Sabellastarte indica, the calcareous-tubed Hydroides, and the spiraled fan of Sabella spallanzanii. Tube architecture and feathered radioles are treated as the principal motif.
kunstformen-images-haeckel-chelonia: Comparative tableau of turtles and tortoises from Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 89. The plate ranges from the leatherback Dermochelys coriacea and hawksbill Eretmochelys imbricata at the top, through the Argentine snake-necked turtle Hydromedusa tectifera and mata mata Chelys fimbriata in the middle, to the geometric tortoise Psammobates geometricus and Galápagos giant tortoise at the lower register, with the common snapping turtle Chelydra serpentina completing the survey. Carapace pattern and head form serve as the organising contrast across the group.
